# Game is forced; opener has 24+, so the questions are the fit and the
# strain (BBA raises with three, else shows a suit or bids notrump). The
# raise agrees the suit, and the slam modules take over (keycards).
# Until 2026-10-07 opener had no rule here and the base 3NT ended the
# auction (Benjamin_2D: 2♦-2♥-3NT-pass on boards with a grand slam).
after 2D (P) 2y (P) | 2D (P) 3y (P) when y is not N
  cheapest(y) "Raise: three or more {y}"   shows y>=3   sets trump=y
      priority 1
  cheapest(S) "Five or more spades"        shows S>=5   when y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Five or more hearts"        shows H>=5   when y is not H
  cheapest(D) "Five or more diamonds"      shows D>=5   when y is not D
  cheapest(C) "Five or more clubs"         shows C>=5   when y is not C
  cheapest(N) "No fit, no suit to show"
      priority -1

# Responder after opener's raise of the major: with 0-5 the fast arrival
# to game (BBA: 4 of 4 with 0-6 there, two of them 3NT); more cue-bids
# (control-bids.bid) or asks.
after 2D (P) 2M (P) 3M (P)
  4M  "Weak: 0-5, game"    shows hcp<=5
      priority 2

# Opener over responder's game in the agreed major (0-5 after the raise,
# 0-6 after the negative): slam needs the playing tricks, at most two
# losers (BBA: asked on 4 of 4 with two or fewer, passed 5 of 6 with
# three or more, Benjamin_2D). With fewer the generic keycard ask
# (rkcb-1430.bid, 18 of my own) asks anyway.
after 2D (P) 2M (P) 3M (P) 4M (P) | 2D (P) 2N (P) 3M (P) 4M (P)
  P   "No slam interest"   shows losers>=3
      priority 1

# Responder after opener's suit: raise with three (agreeing it), rebid a
# six-card major or a seven-card minor, else notrump. (A six-card minor
# rebid at the four level left opener without a rule: four boards.)
after 2D (P) 2y (P) 2z (P) | 2D (P) 2y (P) 3z (P) | 2D (P) 3y (P) 3z (P) when y is not N, z is not N, z is not y
  cheapest(z) "Three or more {z}: agrees it"   shows z>=3   sets trump=z
      priority 1
  cheapest(y) "Six or more {y}"                shows y>=6
      when  y is H | y is S
  cheapest(y) "Seven or more {y}"              shows y>=7
      when  y is C | y is D
  cheapest(N) "No fit"
      priority -1

# ── Opener over the 3NT positive ─────────────────────────────────────
# 24+ facing 7+: slam is there. BBA (Benjamin_2D, 41 boards) bids slam
# on every one: mostly 5NT, which responder answers 6NT, or 7NT with a
# maximum; 6NT or 7NT directly with more.
after 2D (P) 3N (P)
  # 37 or more between us.
  7N  "Grand slam"   shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 37
      priority 3
  5N  "Slam: 6NT, or 7NT with a maximum"    shows hcp>=23
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 2
after 2D (P) 3N (P) 5N (P)
  7N  "A maximum: 12+ HCP"    shows hcp>=12
      priority 1
  6N  "6NT"

# ── Opener after the negative 2NT: natural ───────────────────────────
after 2D (P) 2N (P)
  3C  "Five or more clubs"       shows C>=5
  3D  "Five or more diamonds"    shows D>=5
  3H  "Five or more hearts"      shows H>=5
  3S  "Five or more spades"      shows S>=5
  3N  "Balanced"                 shows balanced
      priority 1
  4N  "Balanced 28+: invites 6NT"   shows balanced, hcp>=28
      sets  ask=quant
      priority 2

# Responder after opener's suit over the negative: raise with three
# (agreeing it: opener's 24+ then asks for keycards), else 3NT.
after 2D (P) 2N (P) 3z (P) when z is not N
  4z  "Three or more {z}"    shows z>=3   sets trump=z
      when  z is H | z is S
      priority 1
  3N  "No fit"
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/blackwoo:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Standard Blackwood: 4NT asks for aces once a trump suit is agreed. The
# answers count aces only; keycards(N) is aces without a trump king.

module blackwood "Blackwood (standard)"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/blackwood
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/blackwood
  param  style = bidding_conventions/control_bids:style default first_or_second_round
  param  kstyle = slam.king_ask.style default five_nt   # five_nt | next_step | none (convention-card 0.28); a card that is silent plays 5NT (2026-10-29)

# ── The ask ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Rick's ruling:
#
#   Slam asks isn't about 18 -- what has partner shown? It's more about
#   33+ combined points, where in a suit contract the player with fewer
#   trumps gets to switch to short-suit points -- 1 for a doubleton, 3
#   for a singleton, 5 for a void, capped by number of trumps held. When
#   the slam asker has unprotected suits, we will normally use control
#   bids before keycard, and stop in game if there is a suit unprotected
#   in both hands.
#
# So the test is **33 combined support points with the agreed suit as
# trump**, `we.tp(trump)`: my exact count plus the range a raise recorded
# for partner. It replaces `tp(trump) + partner.hcp.max`, which was a
# workaround from before raises showed support points. The evidence
# behind the boundaries is in slam-catch.notes.md.
#
# Two branches, because partner's range is read from a different end.
#
# 1. **Partner is limited** (a raise, a limit raise) and nothing has
#    forced us to game. Partner has shown a top as well as a bottom, and
#    the only other call on offer is game, so the ask carries the whole
#    decision and 33 is measured against partner's maximum:
#    `we.tp(trump).max >= 33`. With it, the hand must play for twelve
#    tricks opposite a minimum (`losers <= 4`) and must not have **two
#    bare side suits** -- two or more cards with neither the ace nor the
#    king, where the first two tricks can go. That last test replaces
#    `controls >= 7`: it says which suit is the problem rather than
#    counting. One bare suit is allowed, because a raise facing it will
#    usually hold something there; two is where partner cannot cover
#    both. BBA draws the same line: over `1S P 2S P` and `1S P 3S P` on
#    the Basic-Bridge card it asks with none or one bare suit (272
#    boards) and never with two.
#
# 2. **We are already forced to game.** Partner's range has no top, so
#    `we.tp(trump).max` says nothing; what is known is partner's floor.
#    33 between us on that floor is the test, and where the trump
#    agreement recorded no support points for partner the fallback is my
#    own 18, a game force being worth about 13 (`slam_values`, named in
#    slam-entry.bid with the other shared conditions). Here the
#    ask ranks *behind* the system's descriptive calls: shortness, a
#    second suit and a control bid all say more than 4NT does, and the
#    ask is what is left when they are used up.
#
# When the card plays control bids (`slam.cue_bids.play`), a hand with a
# bare suit goes to `control-bids.bid` first and comes back here only
# once partner has shown a control.

when we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked, we.forcing = none | we.forcing = round
  4N  "Blackwood: how many aces?"
      when  slam_values_limited     # 33 facing partner's maximum
      when  !two_bare_suits  # and no two bare side suits
      sets  ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 1

when we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked, we.forcing = game, !answered control   # after a control dialogue its own rules decide
  4N  "Blackwood: how many aces?"
      when  slam_values  # 33 on partner's floor, or 18 of my own
      sets  ask=aces
      artificial
      priority -1                      # after any natural 4NT

# A fit known but not agreed (docs/JUDGMENT-LAYER.md, Phase 1): partner's
# game raise, his preempt, a transfer completed. No rule set `trump`, so
# the asks above never saw it. The ask agrees the major on the way.
# Majors only for now: the sign-offs after an answer are awkward in a
# minor.
when we.trump is none, !asked, !they.bid   # uncontested for now: in competition it cost
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♠: how many aces?"
      when  shown_fit(S), we.fit(S).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(S), !two_bare_beside(S)
      sets  trump=S, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 1
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♥: how many aces?"
      when  shown_fit(H), we.fit(H).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(H), !two_bare_beside(H)
      sets  trump=H, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 1

# The keycard suit when no rule has set the one we play in (Rick,
# 2026-10-03; `kc_open`, slam-entry.bid): a suit agreed by what we have
# shown, else, with no notrump bid by us, the last suit we bid
# (1H-1S-2H-4NT asks for aces with hearts agreed). The ask sets it as
# trump. As in rkcb-1430.bid.
when we.trump is none, !asked, !they.bid
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♠: how many aces?"
      when  kc_open(S), !shown_fit(S), !shown_fit(H), we.fit(S).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(S), !two_bare_beside(S)
      sets  trump=S, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority -1
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♥: how many aces?"
      when  kc_open(H), !shown_fit(S), !shown_fit(H), we.fit(H).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(H), !two_bare_beside(H)
      sets  trump=H, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority -1
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♦: how many aces?"
      when  kc_open(D), !shown_fit(S), !shown_fit(H), we.fit(D).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(D), !two_bare_beside(D)
      when  hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 30   # a minor slam needs the high cards (rebids.test: 17 facing a preference)
      sets  trump=D, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority -1
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♣: how many aces?"
      when  kc_open(C), !shown_fit(S), !shown_fit(H), we.fit(C).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(C), !two_bare_beside(C)
      when  hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 30   # a minor slam needs the high cards (rebids.test: 17 facing a preference)
      sets  trump=C, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority -1

# A minor set as trump, and a major agreed since (Rick, 2026-10-03): the
# major is trump.
when minor_given_way, !asked
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♠: how many aces?"
      when  major_over_minor(S), fit_slam_values(S), !two_bare_beside(S)
      sets  trump=S, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 1
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♥: how many aces?"
      when  major_over_minor(H), !major_over_minor(S), fit_slam_values(H), !two_bare_beside(H)
      sets  trump=H, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 1

# After a control-bid exchange (`control-bids.bid`, when the card plays
# them). `asked control(t)` is partner's control bid; `answered control(u)`
# says partner was answering mine, so I am the hand that opened the
# dialogue and the one that takes charge. Above it, the stop-in-game rule
# at priority 20 has already ruled out a suit bare in both hands; below
# it, any control still to show outranks the ask.

# In a control-bid dialogue (control-bids.bid): ask once every side suit
# is covered -- a control of mine, one partner has cued, or one I denied
# that partner has promised by bidding on. A control bid below game still
# comes first (priority 12), the ask before one past game (10).
when we.trump is suit, asked control(t)
  4N  "Blackwood: how many aces?"
      when  all_covered
      sets  ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 11

when we.trump is suit, answered control(t), partner.last = 4{trump}
  4N  "Blackwood: how many aces?"
      when  all_covered_by_us
      sets  ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 15

when asked aces
  5C  "0 or 4 aces"                    shows keycards(N) in 0|4  artificial
  5D  "1 ace"                          shows keycards(N)=1       artificial
  5H  "2 aces"                         shows keycards(N)=2       artificial
  5S  "3 aces"                         shows keycards(N)=3       artificial

# The asker places the contract: slam with at most one ace missing,
# otherwise five of the trump suit (or pass when that is the answer).
when answered aces
  # The king ask (`slam.king_ask.style = five_nt`, 2026-10-05): all four aces
  # are ours and the grand turns on the kings.
  5N        "King ask: all the aces held"
            when kstyle is five_nt, we.keycards(N)=4
            sets ask=kings(N)
            artificial
            priority 1
  6{trump}  "Small slam"
            when we.keycards(N)>=3
  P         "To play"
            when partner.last=5{trump}, we.keycards(N).max<=2
  5{trump}  "Signoff"
            when we.keycards(N).max<=2
  # "0 or 4" facing no ace of my own is four.
  6{trump}  "Small slam"
            when maybe we.keycards(N)>=3
            priority -1

# The king ask by 5NT: the number of kings by steps from 6♣ (6NT four),
# as ACBL's SAYC booklet. Kings are controls less two for each ace.
define bw_kings = controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N)

when kstyle is five_nt, asked kings(N)
  6C  "No king"       shows bw_kings = 0   artificial
  6D  "One king"      shows bw_kings = 1   artificial
  6H  "Two kings"     shows bw_kings = 2   artificial
  6S  "Three kings"   shows bw_kings = 3   artificial
  6N  "Four kings"    shows bw_kings = 4   artificial

# The asker: the grand with every king between us, or with three and 33
# HCP on partner's floor; else six, or 6NT when the answer has passed six
# of our suit.
define partner_kings = (partner.last = 6D) + (partner.last = 6H) + (partner.last = 6H) + (partner.last = 6S) + (partner.last = 6S) + (partner.last = 6S) + (partner.last = 6N) + (partner.last = 6N) + (partner.last = 6N) + (partner.last = 6N)

when kstyle is five_nt, answered kings(N)
  7{trump}  "Grand slam"
            when bw_kings + partner_kings >= 4
  7{trump}  "Grand slam"
            when bw_kings + partner_kings >= 3, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 33
  P         "To play"
            when partner.last = 6{trump}
  6{trump}  "Small slam"
  6N        "Small slam"
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/checkbac:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Checkback Stayman: after opener's 1NT rebid, responder's 2C is
# artificial, invitational or better, and asks about three-card support
# for responder's major and four cards in an unbid major, whichever minor
# was opened. Opener: 2D denies both, two of responder's major shows
# three, two of the other major shows four. Played instead of NMF
# (new-minor-forcing.bid switches off when this is on). See
# checkback.notes.md.

module checkback "Checkback Stayman"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/checkback
  needs  responder-rebids
  skill  bidding_conventions/checkback

after 1x (P) 1M (P) 1N (P) when !tw(x)
  2C  "Checkback: invitational or better, asks about the majors"   alert
      shows M>=5 | (H>=4, S>=4), points>=11
      sets  forcing=round, ask=checkback
      artificial
      priority 1                       # ahead of a natural 2NT or 3NT
after 1C (P) 1D (P) 1N (P) when !tw(C)
  2C  "Checkback: invitational+, asks for a 4-card major"   alert
      shows H>=4 | S>=4, points>=11
      sets  forcing=round, ask=checkback
      artificial
      priority 1

# Opener's answers. Over a minor opening: three of responder's major
# first, then four hearts after a 1S response (1NT over 1H denies four
# spades). After 1H-1S-1NT: three spades or 2D.
after 1m (P) 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) when !tw(m)
  2M  "Three {M}"                          shows M=3
  2H  "Four hearts, not three spades"      shows H>=4, S<=2
      when  M is S
  2D  "No three {M}, no four-card major to show"   artificial
      priority -1
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 1N (P) 2C (P)
  2S  "Three spades"                       shows S=3
  2D  "Not three spades"                   artificial
      priority -1
after 1C (P) 1D (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) when !tw(C)
  2H  "Four hearts"                        shows H>=4
  2S  "Four spades, not four hearts"       shows S>=4, H<=3
  2D  "No four-card major"                 shows H<=3, S<=3   artificial
      priority -1

# Responder places the contract: with a fit (five opposite three, or
# four-four), invite with 3M or bid game; without one 2NT invites and 3NT
# is game.
when answered checkback
  4H  "Game in the heart fit"              shows points>=13, H>=5 | (H>=4, partner.H.min>=4)   when partner.H>=3   sets trump=H
  3H  "Invitational, heart fit"            shows points=11..12, H>=5 | (H>=4, partner.H.min>=4)   when partner.H>=3   sets trump=H, ask=invite(H)
  4S  "Game in the spade fit"              shows points>=13, S>=5 | (S>=4, partner.S.min>=4)   when partner.S>=3   sets trump=S
  3S  "Invitational, spade fit"            shows points=11..12, S>=5 | (S>=4, partner.S.min>=4)   when partner.S>=3   sets trump=S, ask=invite(S)
  3N  "Game, no fit"                       shows points>=13
      priority -1
  2N  "Invitational, no fit"               shows points=11..12   sets ask=nt_invite
      priority -1
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/control_:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Control bids: with a trump suit agreed and slam in the air, name a suit
# you can control instead of asking for keycards straight away. Rick's
# rulings:
#
#   When the slam asker has unprotected suits, we will normally use
#   control bids before keycard, and stop in game if there is a suit
#   unprotected in both hands.
#
# So this is the branch that runs *before* the ask in `blackwood.bid` /
# `rkcb-1430.bid`, whenever the card plays control bids and the asker has
# a suit it cannot control on its own. It is gated on the card:
# `slam.cue_bids.play` is BBA's own `Cue bid` key, off on Basic-Bridge
# (which is why BBA blasts 4NT there) and on for the 21GF cards.
#
# No auction patterns: like the rest of slam/, the rules key on
# `we.trump`, `we.forcing` and the control-bid dialogue itself.

module control-bids "Control bids before the keycard ask"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/control_bids
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/control_bids
  skill  partnership_bidding/slam_bidding
  param  style = style default first_or_second_round

# ── The treatment (Rick, 2026-09-25) ─────────────────────────────────
#
#   In a game force with a suit agreed, new non-jump bids below game are
#   control bids. You bid the cheapest control you can show; any suit you
#   skip over you are denying. Partner then shows the cheapest control
#   they have. If either player skips (denies) a suit and the other
#   continues control bidding, they are promising a control in the
#   skipped suit. Standard control bids are aces and voids; the
#   first-and-second-round treatment, more common now, shows an ace, king,
#   singleton or void. Control bidding past game shows first-round
#   control. A singleton or void in partner's own suit is not shown.
#
# `style` is the card's choice: `first_round` (aces and voids) or
# `first_or_second_round` (the default). "Partner's own suit" is one
# partner has shown four or more of.
#
# The engine keeps the dialogue: each ladder call (`sets ladder=control`)
# records the suits it skipped as denied by its bidder
# (`partner.denied(x)`, `me.denied(x)`) and the suit it names as cued
# (`partner.cued(x)`). `cheapest(x)` is the non-jump bid; `under_game(x)`
# says whether it is still below game; `prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(x)`
# picks the cheapest of the controls I hold.
#
# Majors only (Rick, 2026-09-25): "we don't usually use control bids for
# minors". With a minor agreed, new suits show stoppers on the way to 3NT
# (responder-rebids.bid).
#
# ── Opening the dialogue ──────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The values are the ask's own (slam-catch.notes.md): 33 support points
# between us, or 18 of my own facing a game force. What sends the hand
# here rather than straight to 4NT is a side suit I cannot control.

when we.trump is suit, !asked, !answered control, (trump is H | trump is S), we.forcing = game
  cheapest(C)  "Control bid in ♣"  alert
      when  trump is not C, !partner.cued(C), !me.cued(C), under_game(C)
      when  slam_values, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(C), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(C), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(C)
      priority 12
  cheapest(D)  "Control bid in ♦"  alert
      when  trump is not D, !partner.cued(D), !me.cued(D), under_game(D)
      when  slam_values, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(D), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(D), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(D)
      priority 12
  cheapest(H)  "Control bid in ♥"  alert
      when  trump is not H, !partner.cued(H), !me.cued(H), under_game(H)
      when  slam_values, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(H), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(H), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(H)
      priority 12
  cheapest(S)  "Control bid in ♠"  alert
      when  trump is not S, !partner.cued(S), !me.cued(S), under_game(S)
      when  slam_values, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(S), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(S), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(S)
      priority 12

# Over a limited raise: partner has shown a top as well as a bottom, so
# 33 is measured against partner's maximum, and the control bid forces
# to game itself.

when we.trump is suit, !asked, !answered control, (trump is H | trump is S), (we.forcing = none | we.forcing = round)
  cheapest(C)  "Control bid in ♣"  alert
      when  trump is not C, !partner.cued(C), !me.cued(C), under_game(C)
      when  slam_values_limited, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(C), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(C), ladder=control, forcing=game
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(C)
      priority 12
  cheapest(D)  "Control bid in ♦"  alert
      when  trump is not D, !partner.cued(D), !me.cued(D), under_game(D)
      when  slam_values_limited, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(D), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(D), ladder=control, forcing=game
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(D)
      priority 12
  cheapest(H)  "Control bid in ♥"  alert
      when  trump is not H, !partner.cued(H), !me.cued(H), under_game(H)
      when  slam_values_limited, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(H), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(H), ladder=control, forcing=game
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(H)
      priority 12
  cheapest(S)  "Control bid in ♠"  alert
      when  trump is not S, !partner.cued(S), !me.cued(S), under_game(S)
      when  slam_values_limited, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(S), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(S), ladder=control, forcing=game
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(S)
      priority 12

# ── Answering a control bid ───────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Show the cheapest control I have, promising every suit partner has
# denied; past game, first-round controls only. With no such call, sign
# off in game: that is also where a suit denied by both hands leaves us.
# When every side suit is covered the keycard ask comes first
# (blackwood.bid, rkcb-1430.bid).

when we.trump is suit, asked control(t), (trump is H | trump is S)
  cheapest(C)  "Control bid in ♣"  alert
      when  trump is not C, !partner.cued(C), !me.cued(C), under_game(C)
      when  controlled(C), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(C), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(C)
      priority 12
  cheapest(D)  "Control bid in ♦"  alert
      when  trump is not D, !partner.cued(D), !me.cued(D), under_game(D)
      when  controlled(D), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(D), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(D)
      priority 12
  cheapest(H)  "Control bid in ♥"  alert
      when  trump is not H, !partner.cued(H), !me.cued(H), under_game(H)
      when  controlled(H), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(H), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(H)
      priority 12
  cheapest(S)  "Control bid in ♠"  alert
      when  trump is not S, !partner.cued(S), !me.cued(S), under_game(S)
      when  controlled(S), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(S), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(S)
      priority 12
  cheapest(C)  "Control bid in ♣: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not C, !partner.cued(C), !me.cued(C), !under_game(C), (trump is H, cheapest_rank(C) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(C) < 28)
      when  first_round(C), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(C), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(C)
      priority 10
  cheapest(D)  "Control bid in ♦: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not D, !partner.cued(D), !me.cued(D), !under_game(D), (trump is H, cheapest_rank(D) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(D) < 28)
      when  first_round(D), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(D), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(D)
      priority 10
  cheapest(H)  "Control bid in ♥: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not H, !partner.cued(H), !me.cued(H), !under_game(H), (trump is H, cheapest_rank(H) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(H) < 28)
      when  first_round(H), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(H), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(H)
      priority 10
  cheapest(S)  "Control bid in ♠: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not S, !partner.cued(S), !me.cued(S), !under_game(S), !kb_spade_ask, (trump is H, cheapest_rank(S) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(S) < 28)
      when  first_round(S), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(S), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(S)
      priority 10
  4{trump}  "Signoff: no further control"
      sets  ladder=control
      priority -5
  5{trump}  "Signoff: no further control"
      priority -6

# ── Partner signed off in game ────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Partner bid game over my control bid, denying what it skipped. I may
# still go on past game with first-round controls, promising every suit
# partner has denied; otherwise pass.

# Not when I bypassed a suit myself: partner's sign-off says he cannot
# cover it, and no control of mine past game can (2026-09-30; the case
# surfaced when slam_values moved to 32).
when we.trump is suit, answered control(t), partner.last = 4{trump}, (trump is H | trump is S), !me.denied(C), !me.denied(D), !me.denied(H), !me.denied(S)
  cheapest(C)  "Control bid in ♣: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not C, !partner.cued(C), !me.cued(C), (trump is H, cheapest_rank(C) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(C) < 28)
      when  slam_values, first_round(C), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(C), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(C)
      priority 10
  cheapest(D)  "Control bid in ♦: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not D, !partner.cued(D), !me.cued(D), (trump is H, cheapest_rank(D) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(D) < 28)
      when  slam_values, first_round(D), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(D), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(D)
      priority 10
  cheapest(H)  "Control bid in ♥: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not H, !partner.cued(H), !me.cued(H), (trump is H, cheapest_rank(H) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(H) < 28)
      when  slam_values, first_round(H), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(H), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(H)
      priority 10
  cheapest(S)  "Control bid in ♠: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not S, !partner.cued(S), !me.cued(S), !kb_spade_ask, (trump is H, cheapest_rank(S) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(S) < 28)
      when  slam_values, first_round(S), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(S), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(S)
      priority 10
  P   "No further bid"
      priority 2
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/exclusio:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Exclusion Blackwood: with a suit agreed, a jump to the five level in a
# new suit shows a void there and asks for keycards outside it (the ace
# of the void suit does not count, so there are four). The answers are
# steps above the ask, 1430 style: first step 1 or 4, second 0 or 3,
# third 2 without the trump queen, fourth 2 with it. With
# `general.style=bba` the steps count 0, 1, 2, 3 and the ask need not be
# a jump (BBA's own treatment). Notes: exclusion.notes.md.

module exclusion "Exclusion Blackwood: a jump to five in a void asks for keycards outside it"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/exclusion_blackwood
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/exclusion_blackwood
  param  gstyle = general.style
  param  dopi   = bidding_conventions/dopi_ropi:dopi default false
  param  ropi   = bidding_conventions/dopi_ropi:ropi default false

# ── The ask ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# A void in v (not the trump suit), the slam values of the keycard ask
# (`slam_values`, `slam_values_limited`: slam-entry.bid), and keycards
# enough that every answer leaves room: three of my own, or two when the
# answer "none" is still at or below five of our suit. Above the 4NT ask
# (priority 1); control bids, when the card plays them, come first.

# A jump: the cheapest bid in v is at the four level or lower. In BBA's
# style any five-level bid in v asks.
define ex_jump(v) = (v is C, cheapest_rank(C) <= 20) | (v is D, cheapest_rank(D) <= 21) | (v is H, cheapest_rank(H) <= 22) | (v is S, cheapest_rank(S) <= 23)
define ex_level(v) = ex_jump(v) | gstyle is bba

# The answer "no keycard" is at or below five of the trump suit: 1430's
# second step, BBA's first.
define ex_zero_room(v) = (gstyle is not bba, (v is C, trump is H | trump is S) | (v is D, trump is S)) | (gstyle is bba, (v is C, trump is not C) | (v is D, trump is H | trump is S) | (v is H, trump is S))
define ex_room(v) = keycards(trump) >= 3 | (keycards(trump) >= 2, ex_zero_room(v))

define ex_values = slam_values | slam_values_limited

when we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked
  5C  "Exclusion: ♣ void, how many keycards outside ♣?"  alert
      shows C=0, ex_values
      when  trump is not C, ex_level(C), ex_room(C)
      sets  ask=exclusion(C)
      artificial
      priority 12
  5D  "Exclusion: ♦ void, how many keycards outside ♦?"  alert
      shows D=0, ex_values
      when  trump is not D, ex_level(D), ex_room(D)
      sets  ask=exclusion(D)
      artificial
      priority 12
  5H  "Exclusion: ♥ void, how many keycards outside ♥?"  alert
      shows H=0, ex_values
      when  trump is not H, ex_level(H), ex_room(H)
      sets  ask=exclusion(H)
      artificial
      priority 12
  5S  "Exclusion: ♠ void, how many keycards outside ♠?"  alert
      shows S=0, ex_values
      when  trump is not S, ex_level(S), ex_room(S)
      sets  ask=exclusion(S)
      artificial
      priority 12

# ── The answers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Keycards outside the void suit: the trump king and the other three aces.
define ex_keys(v) = keycards(trump) - has(A,v)

when asked exclusion(v), rho.last = P, gstyle is not bba
  5D  "1 or 4 keycards outside clubs"      shows ex_keys(v) in 1|4   artificial   when v is C
  5H  "0 or 3 keycards outside clubs"      shows ex_keys(v) in 0|3   artificial   when v is C
  5S  "2 keycards outside clubs, no {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, !has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is C
  5N  "2 keycards outside clubs and the {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is C
  5H  "1 or 4 keycards outside diamonds"   shows ex_keys(v) in 1|4   artificial   when v is D
  5S  "0 or 3 keycards outside diamonds"   shows ex_keys(v) in 0|3   artificial   when v is D
  5N  "2 keycards outside diamonds, no {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, !has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is D
  6C  "2 keycards outside diamonds and the {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is D
  5S  "1 or 4 keycards outside hearts"     shows ex_keys(v) in 1|4   artificial   when v is H
  5N  "0 or 3 keycards outside hearts"     shows ex_keys(v) in 0|3   artificial   when v is H
  6C  "2 keycards outside hearts, no {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, !has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is H
  6D  "2 keycards outside hearts and the {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is H
  5N  "1 or 4 keycards outside spades"     shows ex_keys(v) in 1|4   artificial   when v is S
  6C  "0 or 3 keycards outside spades"     shows ex_keys(v) in 0|3   artificial   when v is S
  6D  "2 keycards outside spades, no {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, !has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is S
  6H  "2 keycards outside spades and the {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is S

when asked exclusion(v), rho.last = P, gstyle is bba
  5D  "0 keycards outside clubs"      shows ex_keys(v) = 0   artificial   when v is C
  5H  "1 keycard outside clubs"       shows ex_keys(v) = 1   artificial   when v is C
  5S  "2 keycards outside clubs"      shows ex_keys(v) = 2   artificial   when v is C
  5N  "3 keycards outside clubs"      shows ex_keys(v) >= 3  artificial   when v is C
  5H  "0 keycards outside diamonds"   shows ex_keys(v) = 0   artificial   when v is D
  5S  "1 keycard outside diamonds"    shows ex_keys(v) = 1   artificial   when v is D
  5N  "2 keycards outside diamonds"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2   artificial   when v is D
  6C  "3 keycards outside diamonds"   shows ex_keys(v) >= 3  artificial   when v is D
  5S  "0 keycards outside hearts"     shows ex_keys(v) = 0   artificial   when v is H
  5N  "1 keycard outside hearts"      shows ex_keys(v) = 1   artificial   when v is H
  6C  "2 keycards outside hearts"     shows ex_keys(v) = 2   artificial   when v is H
  6D  "3 keycards outside hearts"     shows ex_keys(v) >= 3  artificial   when v is H
  5N  "0 keycards outside spades"     shows ex_keys(v) = 0   artificial   when v is S
  6C  "1 keycard outside spades"      shows ex_keys(v) = 1   artificial   when v is S
  6D  "2 keycards outside spades"     shows ex_keys(v) = 2   artificial   when v is S
  6H  "3 keycards outside spades"     shows ex_keys(v) >= 3  artificial   when v is S

# Over interference, DOPI and ROPI as for the keycard ask (dopi-ropi.bid):
# double or redouble the first step, pass the second; with two keycards
# or more, partner's and mine make a slam, so bid it.
when asked exclusion(v), dopi, rho_bid, rho.last <= 6S
  X   "DOPI: first step"   shows ex_keys(v) in 1|4   artificial   when gstyle is not bba   priority 5
  P   "DOPI: second step"  shows ex_keys(v) in 0|3   artificial   when gstyle is not bba   priority 5
  X   "DOPI: no keycard"   shows ex_keys(v) = 0      artificial   when gstyle is bba       priority 5
  P   "DOPI: one keycard"  shows ex_keys(v) = 1      artificial   when gstyle is bba       priority 5
when asked exclusion(v), ropi, rho.last = X
  XX  "ROPI: first step"   shows ex_keys(v) in 1|4   artificial   when gstyle is not bba   priority 5
  P   "ROPI: second step"  shows ex_keys(v) in 0|3   artificial   when gstyle is not bba   priority 5
  XX  "ROPI: no keycard"   shows ex_keys(v) = 0      artificial   when gstyle is bba       priority 5
  P   "ROPI: one keycard"  shows ex_keys(v) = 1      artificial   when gstyle is bba       priority 5
when asked exclusion(v), !rho.last = P
  6{trump}  "Small slam: two keycards outside the void"
      shows ex_keys(v) = 2
      priority 4

# ── The asker places the contract ─────────────────────────────────────
#
# The step partner answered with, by the ask's suit.
define ex_s1(v) = (v is C, partner.last = 5D) | (v is D, partner.last = 5H) | (v is H, partner.last = 5S) | (v is S, partner.last = 5N)
define ex_s2(v) = (v is C, partner.last = 5H) | (v is D, partner.last = 5S) | (v is H, partner.last = 5N) | (v is S, partner.last = 6C)
define ex_s3(v) = (v is C, partner.last = 5S) | (v is D, partner.last = 5N) | (v is H, partner.last = 6C) | (v is S, partner.last = 6D)
define ex_s4(v) = (v is C, partner.last = 5N) | (v is D, partner.last = 6C) | (v is H, partner.last = 6D) | (v is S, partner.last = 6H)

# Partner's keycards outside the void, the low count where the step
# leaves two open (1430 "1 or 4" facing none of mine, "0 or 3" facing
# one: read low, as the keycard sign-off is). Over DOPI and ROPI the
# double (redouble) is the first step and the pass the second.
define ex_d1 = partner.last = X | partner.last = XX
define ex_d2 = partner.last = P
define ex_partner(v) = (gstyle is not bba, ex_s1(v) | ex_d1) + (gstyle is not bba, ex_s3(v) | ex_s4(v)) + (gstyle is not bba, ex_s3(v) | ex_s4(v)) + (gstyle is bba, ex_s2(v) | ex_d2) + (gstyle is bba, ex_s3(v)) + (gstyle is bba, ex_s3(v)) + (gstyle is bba, ex_s4(v)) + (gstyle is bba, ex_s4(v)) + (gstyle is bba, ex_s4(v))
define ex_total(v) = keycards(trump) + ex_partner(v)

# The trump queen: mine, or 1430's fourth step.
define ex_queen(v) = has(Q,trump) | (gstyle is not bba, ex_s4(v))

when answered exclusion(v)
  7{trump}  "Grand slam"
            when  ex_total(v) >= 4, ex_queen(v)
  6{trump}  "Small slam"
            when  ex_total(v) >= 3
  P         "Defend doubled: two keycards missing"
            when  ex_d1, partner.last = X, ex_total(v) <= 2
  X         "Penalty: two keycards missing"
            when  ex_d2, rho.last = P, lho_bid, lho.last >= 5C, lho.last <= 6S, ex_total(v) <= 2
  P         "To play"
            when  partner.last = 5{trump}, ex_total(v) <= 2
  5{trump}  "Signoff"
            when  ex_total(v) <= 2
  6{trump}  "Small slam"
            priority -1
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/flannery:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Flannery 2♦ (Bridge Bum, "Flannery 2D"): an opening 2♦ shows 11-15 HCP
# with exactly four spades and five hearts, so the 1♥ opener never has to
# reverse or rebid awkwardly with the 4-5 majors. The natural weak 2♦ is
# off (preempts.bid, `weak_2d_open`). Responder:
#
#   Pass  6+ diamonds, weak          2♥/2♠  to play
#   2NT   asks (forcing)             3♣  6+ clubs, to play
#   3♦    6+ diamonds, invitational  3♥/3♠  invitational, 10-12
#   3NT   to play                    4♣/4♦  transfer to 4♥/4♠
#
# Opener's answers to 2NT: 3♣ 4-5-1-3, 3♦ 4-5-3-1, 3♥ 4-5-2-2 minimum,
# 3♠ 4-5-2-2 maximum, 3NT 4-5-2-2 maximum with the minors stopped, 4♣
# 4-5-0-4, 4♦ 4-5-4-0. See flannery.notes.md.

module flannery "Flannery 2♦"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/flannery
  needs  preempts
  skill  bidding_conventions/flannery

# ── The opening ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Ahead of 1♥ and 1NT (both would describe it less well).
when opening
  2D  "Flannery: 11-15 HCP, four spades and five hearts"   alert
      shows S=4, H=5, hcp=11..15
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Over a double the same calls (the double is usually a strong hand or
# diamonds; nothing is lost by playing the system on).
after 2D (P) | 2D (X)
  P   "Six or more diamonds, weak: to play"
      shows D>=6, hcp<=9, H<=2, S<=3
      priority 1
  2S  "To play: no game interest"
      shows hcp<=9, S>=4 | (S=3, H<=1)
  2H  "To play: no game interest"
      shows hcp<=10
      priority -1
  3C  "Six or more clubs: to play"
      shows C>=6, hcp<=9, H<=2, S<=3
      priority 1
  3D  "Six or more diamonds, invitational"
      shows D>=6, hcp=10..12, H<=2, S<=3
  3H  "Invitational: three or more hearts, 10-12"
      shows H>=3, tp(H)=10..12, S<=3
  3S  "Invitational: four or more spades, 10-12"
      shows S>=4, tp(S)=10..12
  # Game in a major: the transfer, so that opener declares.
  4C  "Transfer to 4♥: game, no slam interest"   alert
      shows H>=3, tp(H)>=13, tp(H)<=18, S<=3
      sets  trump=H
      artificial
  4D  "Transfer to 4♠: game, no slam interest"   alert
      shows S>=4, tp(S)>=13, tp(S)<=18
      sets  trump=S
      artificial
  3N  "To play: the minors held, no major fit"
      shows hcp=13..17, H<=2, S<=3, stop(C), stop(D)
  2N  "Asks opener's shape: game interest"   alert
      shows hcp>=11
      sets  forcing=round, ask=flannery
      artificial
      priority -1

# ── Opener after a sign-off or a natural game ────────────────────────
after 2D (P) 2H (P) | 2D (P) 2S (P) | 2D (P) 3C (P) | 2D (P) 3N (P)
  P   "No further bid"

after 2D (P) 3H (P)
  4H  "Accepts the invitation: 14-15"   shows hcp>=14
  P   "Declines: a minimum"
after 2D (P) 3S (P)
  4S  "Accepts the invitation: 14-15"   shows hcp>=14
  P   "Declines: a minimum"
after 2D (P) 3D (P)
  3N  "Accepts: a maximum with the clubs stopped"   shows hcp>=14, stop(C)
  P   "Declines"

after 2D (P) 4C (P)
  4H  "Completes the transfer"
after 2D (P) 4D (P)
  4S  "Completes the transfer"

# ── Opener answers 2NT ───────────────────────────────────────────────
when asked flannery
  3C  "Three clubs: 4-5-1-3"              shows D=1, C=3   artificial
  3D  "Three diamonds: 4-5-3-1"           shows D=3, C=1   artificial
  3H  "4-5-2-2, minimum, 11-13"           shows D=2, C=2, hcp<=13
  3S  "4-5-2-2, maximum, 14-15"           shows D=2, C=2, hcp>=14   artificial
  3N  "4-5-2-2, maximum, the minors held"  shows D=2, C=2, hcp>=14, stop(C), stop(D)
  4C  "Four clubs: 4-5-0-4"                shows D=0, C=4   artificial
  4D  "Four diamonds: 4-5-4-0"             shows D=4, C=0   artificial

# ── The asker places the contract ────────────────────────────────────
# 3NT with the short suit held, else game in the 5-2 heart fit; a
# fit in the minor that opener holds as a side suit is left to the
# natural rules.
when answered flannery
  P   "3NT is the contract"
      when  partner.last=3N
      priority 1
  4S  "Game in the spade fit"                shows S>=4
      priority 1
  4H  "Game in the heart fit"                shows H>=2
      when  !partner.last=3N
  3N  "To play: the short suit held"
      shows stop(C) | partner.C.min>=2, stop(D) | partner.D.min>=2
      when  partner.last <= 3S
      priority 1
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/four_nt_:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# The 4NT opening: asks for specific aces. A hand whose only losers are
# aces (a long, solid suit and kings with queens or short) needs to know
# which aces partner holds, not how many. Answers: 5♣ no ace, 5♦ 5♥ 5♠
# the ace of that suit, 6♣ the club ace, 5NT two aces. The opener then
# places the contract in his long suit. Notes: four-nt-opening.notes.md.

module four-nt-opening "4NT opening: asks for specific aces"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/four_nt_opening
  needs  base

# ── The opening ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Every loser is an ace: each suit without the ace is a singleton, K-x,
# K-Q-x, or the long suit headed by the K-Q-J (partner's ace there is a
# winner; a longer side suit could lose its small cards too), the suits
# with the ace lose nothing (`losers` equals the aces missing), and no
# void, where partner's ace would be wasted. One to three aces missing,
# and a suit of six or more to play in, the longest (spades first on a
# tie). One rule, which sets no trump: partner's answer does not depend
# on the suit, and the opener places the contract in his own.
define fna_ace_only(x) = has(A,x) | x = 1 | (has(K,x), x = 2) | (has(K,x), has(Q,x), x = 3) | (has(K,x), has(Q,x), has(J,x), x >= 6)
define fna_hand = C>=1, D>=1, H>=1, S>=1, fna_ace_only(C), fna_ace_only(D), fna_ace_only(H), fna_ace_only(S), keycards(N) >= 1, keycards(N) <= 3, losers + keycards(N) = 4
define fna_suit(x) = x>=6, x>=S, x>=H, x>=D, x>=C

when opening
  4N  "Asks for specific aces: a long suit, every loser an ace"  alert
      shows fna_hand, S>=6 | H>=6 | D>=6 | C>=6
      sets  ask=specific_aces
      artificial
      priority 2

# ── The answers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
when asked specific_aces
  5C  "No ace"                    shows keycards(N)=0                 artificial   priority 5
  5D  "The diamond ace"           shows keycards(N)=1, has(A,D)       artificial   priority 5
  5H  "The heart ace"             shows keycards(N)=1, has(A,H)       artificial   priority 5
  5S  "The spade ace"             shows keycards(N)=1, has(A,S)       artificial   priority 5
  6C  "The club ace"              shows keycards(N)=1, has(A,C)       artificial   priority 5
  5N  "Two aces"    shows keycards(N) in 2|3            artificial   priority 5

# ── The opener places the contract ────────────────────────────────────
#
# Every ace partner holds is one I lack, so each covers a loser: seven
# with none left, six with one, else five of the suit (pass when that
# was the answer).
define fna_left = losers - (we.keycards(N).min - keycards(N))

when answered specific_aces
  7S  "Grand slam"
        when fna_suit(S), fna_left <= 0
        priority 5
  6S  "Small slam"
        when fna_suit(S), fna_left <= 1
        priority 5
  P   "To play"
        when fna_suit(S), partner.last = 5S
        priority 5
  5S  "Signoff"
        when fna_suit(S)
        priority 5
  6S  "Small slam"
        when fna_suit(S)
        priority 4
  7H  "Grand slam"
        when fna_suit(H), fna_left <= 0
        priority 5
  6H  "Small slam"
        when fna_suit(H), fna_left <= 1
        priority 5
  P   "To play"
        when fna_suit(H), partner.last = 5H
        priority 5
  5H  "Signoff"
        when fna_suit(H)
        priority 5
  6H  "Small slam"
        when fna_suit(H)
        priority 4
  7D  "Grand slam"
        when fna_suit(D), fna_left <= 0
        priority 5
  6D  "Small slam"
        when fna_suit(D), fna_left <= 1
        priority 5
  P   "To play"
        when fna_suit(D), partner.last = 5D
        priority 5
  5D  "Signoff"
        when fna_suit(D)
        priority 5
  6D  "Small slam"
        when fna_suit(D)
        priority 4
  7C  "Grand slam"
        when fna_suit(C), fna_left <= 0
        priority 5
  6C  "Small slam"
        when fna_suit(C), fna_left <= 1
        priority 5
  P   "To play"
        when fna_suit(C), partner.last = 5C
        priority 5
  5C  "Signoff"
        when fna_suit(C)
        priority 5
  6C  "Small slam"
        when fna_suit(C)
        priority 4
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/french_2:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# French 2♦ (the French standard system, SEF: "2♦ forcing de manche";
# BBA's `French 2D`, probes/b2-French-*.toml): 2♦ is the artificial
# game-forcing opening, 24+ HCP of any shape, and 2♣ keeps the strong
# hands below it (strong-openings.bid caps it at 23 when this is on).
# There is no weak 2♦ (preempts.bid, `weak_2d_open`).
#
# Responder answers in aces (BBA):
#
#   2♥   no ace, 0-7, no five-card major
#   2♠   one ace, the ♥A or the ♠A
#   2NT  no ace, 8+
#   3♣   one ace, the ♣A          3♦   one ace, the ♦A
#   3♥/3♠  no ace, 0-7, a five-card suit
#   3NT  two aces or more
#
# Opener then bids naturally. See french-2d.notes.md.

module french-2d "French 2♦ (game forcing)"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/french_2d
  needs  strong-openings
  skill  bidding_conventions/french_2d

# ── The opening ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Above every 2♣ opening and the 3NT opening (BBA opens 2♦ with a
# balanced 26 too).
when opening
  2D  "French 2♦: game forcing, 24+ HCP"   alert
      shows hcp>=24
      sets  forcing=game, ask=french_2d
      artificial
      priority 2

# ── Responder: aces ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
when asked french_2d
  3N  "Two aces or more"                 shows keycards(N)>=2
      artificial
      priority 2
  2S  "One ace: the ♥A or the ♠A"        shows keycards(N)=1, has(A,H) | has(A,S)
      artificial
      priority 1
  3C  "One ace: the ♣A"                  shows keycards(N)=1, has(A,C)
      artificial
      priority 1
  3D  "One ace: the ♦A"                  shows keycards(N)=1, has(A,D)
      artificial
      priority 1
  3H  "No ace, 0-7: five or more hearts"   shows keycards(N)=0, hcp<=7, H>=5, H>=S
  3S  "No ace, 0-7: five or more spades"   shows keycards(N)=0, hcp<=7, S>=5, S>H
  2N  "No ace, 8+"                       shows keycards(N)=0, hcp>=8
      artificial
  2H  "No ace, 0-7"                      shows keycards(N)=0, hcp<=7
      artificial
      priority -1

# ── Opener: natural ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The auction is forced to game; opener shows his suit or his balanced
# hand, and the slam modules take over once a suit is agreed.
after 2D (P) 3H (P)
  4H  "Three or more hearts: agrees hearts"   shows H>=3
      sets  trump=H
      priority 2
after 2D (P) 3S (P)
  4S  "Three or more spades: agrees spades"   shows S>=3
      sets  trump=S
      priority 2
# Two aces opposite 24+: a balanced 25 bids the slam (32+ between us).
after 2D (P) 3N (P)
  6N  "Balanced: slam opposite two aces"    shows balanced, hcp>=25
      priority 1
  P   "Balanced 24: game"                    shows balanced
after 2D (P) 2H (P) | 2D (P) 2S (P) | 2D (P) 2N (P) | 2D (P) 3C (P) | 2D (P) 3D (P) | 2D (P) 3H (P) | 2D (P) 3S (P) | 2D (P) 3N (P)
  cheapest(S) "Five or more spades"       shows S>=5
  cheapest(H) "Five or more hearts"       shows H>=5
  cheapest(D) "Five or more diamonds"     shows D>=5
  cheapest(C) "Five or more clubs"        shows C>=5
  cheapest(N) "Balanced"                  shows balanced
      priority -1
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/gambling:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Gambling 3NT (ACBL SAYC booklet; Bridge Bum, "Gambling 3NT";
# convention-card bidding_conventions/gambling_3nt): a solid seven- or
# eight-card minor (AKQ at least) and no outside ace or king. The
# balanced 26-27 then opens 2♣ (strong-openings.bid reads the same field).
#
# The pass-or-correct calls are not marked artificial: a pass plays
# them. Responder: pass to play (the other suits stopped), 4♣ and 5♣ pass or
# correct to opener's minor, 4♥/4♠ to play, 6♣ pass or correct with slam
# values. See gambling-3nt.notes.md.

module gambling-3nt "Gambling 3NT: a solid minor"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/gambling_3nt
  needs  preempts
  skill  bidding_conventions/gambling_3nt

# ── The opening ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Ahead of a one-level or three-level opening of the minor.
when opening, seat<=3
  3N  "Gambling: a solid seven-card minor, no outside ace or king"   alert
      shows C>=7, has(A,C), has(K,C), has(Q,C), D<=3, S<=4, H<=4
      shows !has(A,S), !has(K,S), !has(A,H), !has(K,H), !has(A,D), !has(K,D)
      priority 2
  3N  "Gambling: a solid seven-card minor, no outside ace or king"   alert
      shows D>=7, has(A,D), has(K,D), has(Q,D), C<=3, S<=4, H<=4
      shows !has(A,S), !has(K,S), !has(A,H), !has(K,H), !has(A,C), !has(K,C)
      priority 2

# ── Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Opener brings seven tricks: pass with the other three suits covered.
after 3N (P)
  P   "To play: the other suits stopped"
      shows stop(S), stop(H), stop(C) | stop(D)
      shows hcp>=10
  4C  "Pass or correct: to play in your minor"   alert
      priority -5
  5C  "Pass or correct: game in your minor"   alert
      shows S<=1 | H<=1, C>=3, D>=3
      priority -4
  6C  "Pass or correct: slam in your minor"   alert
      shows hcp>=16, quick_tricks>=4
  4H  "To play: a long heart suit"            shows H>=7 | (H>=6, hcp>=10)
  4S  "To play: a long spade suit"            shows S>=7 | (S>=6, hcp>=10)

after 3N (P) 4C (P) | 3N (P) 5C (P) | 3N (P) 6C (P)
  P   "My minor is clubs"                     shows C>=7
  cheapest(D)  "My minor is diamonds"         shows D>=7

after 3N (P) 4H (P) | 3N (P) 4S (P)
  P   "Partner's suit: to play"

# Responder after the correction: the contract is placed.
after 3N (P) 4C (P) 4D (P) | 3N (P) 5C (P) 5D (P) | 3N (P) 6C (P) 6D (P)
  P   "To play in opener's diamonds"
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/gazzilli:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Gazzilli: after 1♥/1♠ and a 1NT response (or 1♥-1♠), opener's 2♣ is
# artificial: either natural, 11-15 with four or more clubs, or any
# strong hand (16+). Responder's 2♦ says 8+ and asks; anything else is
# 5-7 and natural.
#
#   1M-1NT-2♣-2♦:  2M the natural minimum with clubs (NF); 2NT 16-17
#                  balanced; 3♣/3♦ 16+ with the minor, 3M 16+ with six or
#                  more, the other major 16+ with four (all game forcing)
#
# The classic form (Wikipedia, "Gazzilli"; BBA plays it: every 2♣ in the
# PBS scenario Gazzilli holds clubs or 16+). Todd's modern form ("Modern
# Gazzilli", Adventures in Bridge TWiB 488) moves the minimum six-card
# one-suiter into 2♣ and the 5-4 with clubs into 2M; not played. Partial:
# the artificial relays after 2♦ and opener's 5-5 jumps are not played;
# see gazzilli.notes.md.

module gazzilli "Gazzilli 2♣ after 1M-1NT and 1♥-1♠"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/gazzilli
  needs  rebids
  skill  bidding_conventions/gazzilli

# A strong hand for the relay: 16+, but not 18-19 balanced (2NT at once)
# or six of the major and 16-18 (the jump rebid, as BBA).
define gazzilli_strong(M) = hcp>=16, !(balanced, hcp=18..19), !(M>=6, hcp<=18)

# ── Opener ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1M (P) 1N (P)
  2C  "Gazzilli: 11-15 with four or more clubs, or any 16+"  alert
      shows gazzilli_strong(M) | (hcp<=15, C>=4)
      sets  forcing=round, ask=gazzilli(M)
      artificial
      priority 2                       # ahead of the natural rebids (rebids.bid)
  3x  "Five-five, 13-15: {M} and {x}"
      shows M>=5, x>=5, hcp=13..15
      when  x is not M, M is S | x is not S
      priority 3                       # the jump in a new suit (PBS Gazzilli; Todd)
after 1H (P) 1S (P)
  3x  "Five-five, 13-15: hearts and {x}"
      shows H>=5, x>=5, hcp=13..15, S<=3
      when  x is C | x is D
      priority 3
  2C  "Gazzilli: 11-15 with four or more clubs, or any 16+"  alert
      shows gazzilli_strong(H) | (hcp<=15, C>=4), S<=3
      sets  forcing=round, ask=gazzilli(H)
      artificial
      priority 2                       # a spade fit raises (rebids.bid)

# Responder after the 5-5 jump (13-15, not forcing).
after 1M (P) 1N (P) 3x (P) when x is not M, M is S | x is not S
  4M  "Game in {M}: two or more and 9+"
      shows M>=2, points>=9
      priority 3
  3M  "Preference for {M}"
      shows M>=2
      priority 2
  3N  "No fit for {M}, 10+"
      shows points>=10
      priority 2
  P   "Weak: plays {x}"
      priority 1
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 3x (P) when x is C | x is D
  4H  "Game in hearts: two or more and 9+"
      shows H>=2, points>=9
      priority 3
  3H  "Preference for hearts"
      shows H>=2
      priority 2
  3N  "No fit for hearts, 10+"
      shows points>=10
      priority 2
  P   "Weak: plays {x}"
      priority 1

after 1M (P) 1N (P) 3x (P) 3M (P) | 1M (P) 1N (P) 3x (P) 3N (P) when x is not M
  P   "No further bid"
      priority 2
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 3x (P) 3H (P) | 1H (P) 1S (P) 3x (P) 3N (P) when x is C | x is D
  P   "No further bid"
      priority 2

# ── Responder after 2♣ ───────────────────────────────────────────────
when asked gazzilli(M), rho.last=P, partner.last=2C
  2D  "Gazzilli: 8+, asks"  alert
      shows hcp>=8
      sets  forcing=round
      artificial
      priority 3                       # ahead of responder's natural rebids
  2M  "5-7, two or more {M}"
      shows hcp<=7, M>=2
      priority 3
  2H  "5-7, five or more hearts, no spade fit"
      shows hcp<=7, H>=5, S<=1
      when  M is S
      priority 2
  2S  "5-7, five or more spades, no heart fit"
      shows hcp<=7, S>=5, H<=1
      when  M is H, me.last=1S
      priority 2
  3C  "5-7, six or more clubs"
      shows hcp<=7, C>=6, M<=1
      priority 2
  3D  "5-7, six or more diamonds"
      shows hcp<=7, D>=6, M<=1
      priority 2
  2N  "5-7, no fit for {M}"
      shows hcp<=7, M<=1
      priority 1

# ── Opener after 2♦ (8+) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
when answered gazzilli(M), rho.last=P, partner.last=2D
  2M  "Gazzilli: the natural minimum, four or more clubs"
      shows hcp<=15
      priority 3                       # ahead of opener's natural rebids
  2N  "Gazzilli: 16-17, balanced"
      shows hcp=16..17, balanced
      priority 3
  3N  "Gazzilli: 20-21, balanced"
      shows hcp>=20, balanced
      priority 3
  3M  "Gazzilli: 16+, six or more {M}"
      shows hcp>=16, M>=6
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 3
  3C  "Gazzilli: 16+, four or more clubs"
      shows hcp>=16, C>=4, C>=D, M<=6
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 3
  3D  "Gazzilli: 16+, four or more diamonds"
      shows hcp>=16, D>=4, D>C, M<=6
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 3
  3H  "Gazzilli: 16+, four or more hearts"
      shows hcp>=16, H>=4
      when  M is S
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 3
  # Anything else strong: game in the major.
  4M  "Gazzilli: 16+, game"
      shows hcp>=16
      priority 1

after 1H (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P)
  2S  "Gazzilli: 16+, four or more spades"
      shows hcp>=16, S>=4
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 3
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2D (P)
  2S  "Gazzilli: 16+, three spades"
      shows hcp>=16, S=3
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 3

# ── Responder after opener's minimum (2M, not forcing) ───────────────
after 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 2M (P)
  4M  "Game opposite a minimum: 12+ with two or more {M}"
      shows points>=12, M>=2
      priority 3
  3M  "Invites opposite a minimum: 10-11"
      shows points=10..11, M>=2
      priority 3
  2N  "No fit for {M}, 8-10"
      shows M<=1, points<=10
      priority 3
  3N  "No fit for {M}, 11+"
      shows M<=1, points>=11
      priority 3
  P   "No game opposite a minimum"
      priority 2
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 2H (P)
  2S  "Five or more spades, no heart fit: to play"
      shows S>=5, H<=1, points<=10
      priority 3
  2N  "No fit for hearts, 8-10"
      shows H<=1, S<=4, points<=10
      priority 3
  3N  "No fit for hearts, 11+"
      shows H<=1, points>=11
      priority 3
  4H  "Game opposite a minimum: 12+ with two or more hearts"
      shows points>=12, H>=2
      priority 3
  3H  "Invites opposite a minimum: 10-11"
      shows points=10..11, H>=2
      priority 3
  P   "No game opposite a minimum"
      priority 2

# ── Responder after opener's strong rebids ───────────────────────────
after 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 2N (P)
  3N  "Game opposite 16-17: 9+"
      shows points>=9
      priority 3
  P   "No game opposite 16-17"
      priority 2
after 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 3M (P)
  4M  "Game in the six-card major"
      priority 3
after 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 3x (P) | 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 2x (P) when x is not M, we.forcing = game
  4M  "Game in the major: three of them"
      shows M>=3
      priority 3
  3N  "Game: no fit for {M}"
      priority 2
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 2N (P)
  3N  "Game opposite 16-17: 9+"
      shows points>=9
      priority 3
  P   "No game opposite 16-17"
      priority 2
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 3H (P)
  4H  "Game in the six-card major"
      priority 3
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 2S (P)
  4S  "Game in the 4-3 or better spade fit"
      priority 3
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 3x (P) when x is C | x is D
  4H  "Game in hearts: three of them"
      shows H>=3
      priority 3
  3N  "Game: no fit for hearts"
      priority 2

# Opener after responder's no-fit 2NT or 2♠: the minimum stops.
after 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 2M (P) 2N (P) | 1H (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 2H (P) 2N (P)
  3C  "Five or more clubs: to play"
      shows C>=5
      priority 3
  P   "Minimum: no game"
      priority 2
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 2H (P) 2S (P)
  P   "Minimum: partner's spades"
      priority 2

# Opener after responder's 3NT: a six-card major plays there.
after 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 3x (P) 3N (P) when x is not M
  4M  "Six or more {M}: game in the major"
      shows M>=6
      priority 3
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 3x (P) 3N (P) when x is C | x is D
  4H  "Six or more hearts: game in the major"
      shows H>=6
      priority 3

# ── Opener after a weak answer (5-7) ─────────────────────────────────
when answered gazzilli(M), rho.last=P
  P   "Gazzilli: no game opposite 5-7"
      shows hcp<=18
      when  !partner.last=2D
      priority 2
  3M  "Invites with six or more {M}: 19-20"
      shows hcp=19..20, M>=6
      when  !partner.last=2D
      priority 3
  4M  "Game: 21+ with six or more {M}"
      shows hcp>=21, M>=6
      when  !partner.last=2D
      priority 3
  3N  "Game: 19+, no six-card {M}"
      shows hcp>=19, M<=5
      when  !partner.last=2D
      priority 3
  3C  "Natural clubs, minimum: to play"
      shows hcp<=15, C>=5
      when  partner.last=2N
      priority 3
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/gerber/g:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Gerber: 4♣ asks for aces over partner's natural notrump, where no suit
# has been agreed. Answers by steps (4♦ 0 or 4, 4♥ 1, 4♠ 2, 4NT 3); 5♣
# then asks for kings the same way. The asker places the contract; 4NT
# after an answer is a sign-off. Notes: gerber.notes.md.
#
# Where it applies (card `slam.gerber.*`):
# - directly over partner's 1NT or 2NT where systems are on (2NT opening,
#   2♣–2♦–2NT, Kokish's 2NT ...: one-nt.bid, `systems on`);
# - over interference to our 1NT opening (a double, a two-level overcall);
# - after 1NT–2♣–2♦ (Stayman, no major; not with the bba treatment);
# - over partner's 1NT or 2NT rebid after 1x–1y, and by opener over a
#   natural 2NT response (1m–2NT, 2♣–2NT), unless the card says
#   `gerber.only_over_nt_openings` (BBA's "Gerber only for NT openings")
#   or not `gerber.over_nt_seq`;
# - brill: over a 3NT opening and opener's 3NT rebid after 2♣.
# Never where clubs are natural or a suit is agreed: after a transfer, a
# major Stayman answer, or a minor raise, 4♣ keeps its other meanings.
#
# 4♣ over 1NT is a transfer to diamonds with `transfers.texas_4c`, and
# then Gerber is off there. Over 2NT the 4♣ slam try in clubs
# (two-nt-responses.bid) is off when Gerber is on: those hands ask for
# aces and bid 6♣ (gerber.notes.md, "Decisions").

module gerber "Gerber: 4♣ asks for aces over partner's notrump"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/gerber
  needs  notrump-base
  skill  bidding_conventions/gerber
  param  only_openings = only_over_nt_openings default false
  param  nt_seq = over_nt_seq default true   # not in the .bbsa map: true unless a card JSON says no
  param  texas_4c = bidding_conventions/texas:bid_4c default false
  param  tu = bidding_conventions/texas:two_under default false   # 2-under Texas: 4C transfers
  param  style = general.style
  param  system = general.system   # `brill`: the Brill card's treatments (over 3NT)

# ── The ask ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The hands that would bid 6NT directly (one-nt.bid, two-nt-responses.bid)
# check the aces first; priority 1 puts the ask ahead of 6NT. BBA asks a
# point lower, 31 HCP between the hands (probes/gerber-resp-1N.toml,
# gerber-resp-2N.toml), and then bids 6NT only with three aces between
# the hands: that is the bba treatment. Our default keeps Rick's 4NT
# invitation with 16 opposite 15-17 (one-nt.bid).
after 1N (P) when !texas_4c, !tu
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, points>=32-partner.hcp.min, H<=4, S<=4   # a major goes through Stayman or a transfer
      when  style is not bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1                         # ahead of 6NT: check the aces first
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, hcp>=31-partner.hcp.min, H<=4, S<=4
      when  style is bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# Over 2NT a long club suit asks too, and plays in 6♣ (BBA from 9 HCP
# with six clubs; our threshold is the old 4♣ slam try's).
after nt2 when !tu
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows H<=4, S<=4, (balanced, strength>=slam) | (C>=6 | (C>=5, !balanced), strength>=slam_invite)
      when  style is not bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows H<=4, S<=4, (balanced, hcp>=31-partner.hcp.min) | (C>=6, hcp>=29-partner.hcp.min)
      when  style is bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# brill (the Brill card): Gerber over a 3NT opening too (25-27), where
# our default reads 4C as a club slam try (over-3nt.bid). Brill /explain,
# 2026-10-15, after 3N P: "Gerber" `slammish`. Slam values: 31 between
# the hands, as over-3nt.bid counts.
after 3N (P) when system is brill
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows hcp>=31-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# Brill: also over opener's 3NT rebid after 2♣ (2♣–2♦–3NT, and after
# their overcall, 2♣ (2♥) P (P) 3NT, 2♣ P 2♦ (2♥) 3NT). Our default reads
# 4♣ after 2♣–2♦–3NT as the club slam try, as over the 3NT opening
# (over-3nt.bid), and has no rule after interference (notes, "Gaps").
after 2C (*) P (P) 3N (P) | 2C (P) 2D (*) 3N (P) when system is brill
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows hcp>=31-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# Over interference to our 1NT opening (a double or a suit overcall at
# the two level) the jump to 4♣ is still Gerber, the same hands as
# without it: 4♣ is not a sensible cue-bid or natural call there.
after 1N (X) when !texas_4c, !tu
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, points>=32-partner.hcp.min
      when  style is not bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, hcp>=31-partner.hcp.min
      when  style is bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1
after 1N (2y) when y is not N, !texas_4c, !tu
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, points>=32-partner.hcp.min
      when  style is not bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, hcp>=31-partner.hcp.min
      when  style is bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# After Stayman's 2♦ (no major) the jump to 4♣ is Gerber: no suit is
# agreed and clubs are not natural. The hands that bid 6NT there
# (stayman.bid) check the aces first. The bba treatment keeps BBA's 4♣
# minor slam try (stayman.bid).
after 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) when style is not bba
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, points>=32-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# Over a notrump rebid or response (the card's "over NT sequence";
# BBA's "Gerber only for NT openings" turns it off).
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 1N (P) | 1x (P) 1y (P) 2N (P) when !only_openings, nt_seq
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, points>=32-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# Gerber by opener over responder's natural 2NT: 1♣–2NT and 1♦–2NT
# (Bridge Bum: 4♣ over any natural notrump; PBS Gerber_By_Opener), and
# 2♣–2NT, the balanced positive. After 1♣ too: clubs are not agreed, and
# opener with long clubs shows them at the three level first. Slam
# values against responder's minimum; over 2♣–2NT the balanced hands
# that bid 6NT (strong-openings.bid) ask first.
after 1m (P) 2N (P) when !only_openings, nt_seq
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows H<=4, S<=4, strength>=slam
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1
after 2C (P) 2N (P) when !only_openings, nt_seq
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, points>=33-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── The answers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
when asked gerber
  4D  "0 or 4 aces"   shows keycards(N) in 0|4   artificial
  4H  "1 ace"         shows keycards(N)=1        artificial
  4S  "2 aces"        shows keycards(N)=2        artificial
  4N  "3 aces"        shows keycards(N)=3        artificial

# ── The asker places the contract ─────────────────────────────────────
# we.keycards(N) is my aces plus partner's answer, four in the deck, so
# "0 or 4" resolves against my own. Rules without `shows` rank by
# priority, then file order: the grand before the king ask before six.
# The thresholds (my points plus opener's minimum) were set on the
# corpus: 7NT from 35 with all the aces, the king ask at 33-34
# (gerber.notes.md, "Grand slam and the king ask"; the textbook 37 for
# 7NT scored 400 IMPs worse).
when answered gerber
  7N  "Grand slam"
      when  we.keycards(N)=4, points + partner.hcp.min >= 35
      priority 3
  5C  "Gerber: how many kings?"  alert
      when  we.keycards(N)=4, points + partner.hcp.min >= 33, points + partner.hcp.min <= 34
      when  C<=5                         # a long club suit settles for six
      sets  ask=gerber_kings
      artificial
      priority 2
  6C  "Small slam"
      when  we.keycards(N)>=3, C>=6, imps       # at matchpoints 6NT scored better (notes)
      priority 1
  6N  "Small slam"
      when  we.keycards(N)>=3
  4N  "Signoff"
      when  we.keycards(N).max<=2
  # "0 or 4" facing no ace of my own is four.
  6N  "Small slam"
      when  maybe we.keycards(N)>=3
      priority -1

when asked gerber_kings
  5D  "0 or 4 kings"  shows (controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) = 0) | (controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) = 4)   artificial
  5H  "1 king"        shows controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) = 1   artificial
  5S  "2 kings"       shows controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) = 2   artificial
  5N  "3 kings"       shows controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) = 3   artificial

# All four aces are ours (the king ask needs them): seven with all four
# kings as well, else six. Kings are controls less two for each ace.
when answered gerber_kings
  7N  "Grand slam"
      when  (partner.last=5N, controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) >= 1) | (partner.last=5S, controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) >= 2) | (partner.last=5H, controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) >= 3) | (partner.last=5D, controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) >= 4)
      priority 1
  6N  "Small slam"
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/impossib:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# The Impossible 2♠ (Robert Todd, "The Impossible ♠ Bid", Adventures in
# Bridge TWiB 269; GIB's "Impossible spade"): after 1♥–1NT, responder has
# denied four spades, so a later 2♠ over opener's 2♣ or 2♦ cannot be
# natural. It shows a good raise of opener's minor: four or more, the top
# of the 1NT response, and forcing to three of the minor. The plain raise
# to 3m stays the lesser raise (responder-rebids.bid). Only after a 1♥
# opening (over 1♠, 2♠ is a preference) and only over a minor rebid: our
# 1NT denies three hearts, so Todd's 1♥–1NT–2♥–2♠ (a three-card limit
# raise) has no hand here. See impossible-2s.notes.md.

module impossible-2s "Impossible 2♠"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/impossible_2s
  needs  responder-rebids
  skill  bidding_conventions/impossible_2s

# ── Responder: the good raise ────────────────────────────────────────
# Our 1NT is 6-10 HCP, so the raise to 3m (9-10 points) is the courtesy
# raise and 2♠ takes the 11+ hands (10 HCP and a fifth trump, or a
# sixth). Without the convention they raise to 3m (responder-rebids.bid).
# Priority 1: the 6-12 1NT of the 2/1 cards brought a natural 11-12 HCP
# raise to 3m (responder-rebids.bid, 2026-09-30) that outranked 2♠ on
# description and took every hand, so switching the convention off
# changed nothing (convention score, 2026-10-07).
after 1H (P) 1N (P) 2m (P)
  2S  "Impossible 2♠: good raise of {m}, 4+ {m}, 11+ points"  alert
      shows m>=4, H<=2, points>=11
      sets  trump=m, forcing=round
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── Opener answers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Responder has 11-13 with the fit, so opener goes to game with 15+
# support points (HCP and shortness: a 5-4-3-1 twelve-count, a 5-4-2-2
# thirteen; GIB's minimum is 12-13 total points): 3NT with both unbid suits stopped, otherwise the
# stopper he has (up the line, looking for 3NT, with the minor as the
# fallback; responder answers in responder-rebids.bid), otherwise five
# of the minor. With a minimum he signs off in three of the minor.
after 1H (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2S (P)
  3C  "Minimum: no game opposite the good raise"
      shows tp(C)<=14
      sets  ask=signoff
  3N  "Game: 15+, spades and diamonds stopped"
      shows tp(C)>=15, stop(S), stop(D)
  3D  "Diamond stopper, not spades: looking for 3NT"
      shows tp(C)>=15, stop(D), !stop(S)
      sets  ask=stoppers, ladder=stopper, forcing=game
  3S  "Spade stopper, not diamonds: looking for 3NT"
      shows tp(C)>=15, stop(S), !stop(D)
      sets  ask=stoppers, ladder=stopper, forcing=game
  5C  "Game in clubs: 15+, neither suit stopped"
      shows tp(C)>=15
      priority -1
after 1H (P) 1N (P) 2D (P) 2S (P)
  3D  "Minimum: no game opposite the good raise"
      shows tp(D)<=14
      sets  ask=signoff
  3N  "Game: 15+, spades and clubs stopped"
      shows tp(D)>=15, stop(S), stop(C)
  3C  "Club stopper, not spades: looking for 3NT"
      shows tp(D)>=15, stop(C), !stop(S)
      sets  ask=stoppers, ladder=stopper, forcing=game
  3S  "Spade stopper, not clubs: looking for 3NT"
      shows tp(D)>=15, stop(S), !stop(C)
      sets  ask=stoppers, ladder=stopper, forcing=game
  5D  "Game in diamonds: 15+, neither suit stopped"
      shows tp(D)>=15
      priority -1

# ── Responder after opener's minimum ─────────────────────────────────
after 1H (P) 1N (P) 2m (P) 2S (P) 3m (P)
  P   "Opener is minimum: play three of {m}"

# ── Responder after opener's game ────────────────────────────────────
after 1H (P) 1N (P) 2m (P) 2S (P) 3N (P) | 1H (P) 1N (P) 2m (P) 2S (P) 5m (P)
  P   "No further bid"
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/ingberma:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Ingberman 2NT (Lebensohl over opener's reverse; convention-card
# bidding_conventions/ingberman; Robert S. Todd, Adventures in Bridge #417,
# "Lebensohl over Reverses"): after 1x-1y-2z, a reverse (17+, forcing one
# round), responder's 2NT is artificial and weak and asks opener for 3♣;
# responder then passes with clubs or signs off in three of a suit. Every
# other call above 2NT is natural and game forcing; responder's rebid of
# his own suit at the two level is five or more and forcing one round.
# Not played over interference. See ingberman.notes.md.

module ingberman "Ingberman 2NT after opener's reverse"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/ingberman
  needs  responder-rebids
  skill  bidding_conventions/ingberman

# A reverse is the one two-level new suit that forces one round: a jump
# shift forces to game, and a new suit below the first does not force.
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) when z is not x, z is not y, we.forcing = round, !tw(x)
  2N  "Ingberman: weak, relay to 3♣"   alert
      shows points<=8
      sets  ask=ingberman
      artificial
      priority 2
  2y  "Five or more {y}, forcing one round"
      shows y>=5, points>=6
      sets  forcing=round, ask=ing_suit
      priority 3
  3x  "Three or more {x}: game forcing"
      shows x>=3, points>=9
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 2
  3z  "Four or more {z}: game forcing"
      shows z>=4, points>=9
      sets  forcing=game, trump=z
      priority 3
  3y  "Six or more {y}: game forcing"
      shows y>=6, points>=9
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 2
  3N  "Game: no fit, 9+"
      shows points>=9, z<=3
      priority 1

when asked ingberman
  3C  "Forced: 3♣ as asked"   alert
      artificial

# Responder signs off: pass with clubs, else three of a suit.
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) when answered ingberman
  3z  "Weak, four or more {z}: invitational"   shows z>=4   sets trump=z, ask=invite(z)
      priority 3
  3y  "Weak, six or more {y}: to play"         shows y>=6   sets ask=signoff
      priority 2
  P   "Weak: to play in clubs"                 shows C>=2
      when  x is C
      priority 1
  3x  "Weak: to play in {x}"                   shows x>=2   sets ask=signoff
      when  x is not C
      priority 1
  P   "Weak: to play in clubs"                 shows C>=5
      when  x is not C
      priority 2

# Opener over the forcing 2y: support, a longer suit, or 2NT without.
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) 2y (P) when asked ing_suit
  3y  "Three-card support for {y}"         shows y>=3
      sets  trump=y
      priority 2
  3x  "Six or more {x}"                    shows x>=6, y<=2
      priority 1
  3z  "Five or more {z}"                   shows z>=5, y<=2
      priority 1
  3N  "19+, no fit"                        shows hcp>=19, y<=2
  2N  "No fit for {y}"       shows y<=2
      priority -1
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) 2y (P) 2N (P) when answered ing_suit
  P   "Weak: no game"                      shows points<=8
      priority -5
  3y  "Six or more {y}: to play"           shows y>=6, points<=8   sets ask=signoff
  3N  "Game: 9+"                           shows points>=9
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) 2y (P) 3y (P) when answered ing_suit
  P   "Weak: no game"                      shows points<=7
      priority -5
  4y  "Game"                               shows points>=8
      when  y is H | y is S
  3N  "Game"                               shows points>=8
      when  y is C | y is D
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) 2y (P) 3x (P) | 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) 2y (P) 3z (P) when answered ing_suit
  P   "Weak: no game"                      shows points<=7
      priority -5
  3N  "Game"                               shows points>=8
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/inverted:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Inverted minors, as BBA plays them on 21GF-DEFAULT (probed 2026-09-25,
# probes/minor-resp-inv-*.toml, inv-opener-*.toml; inverted-minors.notes.md):
#
# - 1m-2m is 10+ HCP, four or more of the minor, no four-card major,
#   forcing one round; 1m-3m is weak, 5-9 with five or more.
# - Opener: 2NT 12-14 balanced; 3NT 18-19 balanced; 3m a minimum,
#   unbalanced; a new suit at the two level shows a stopper and extras
#   (15+) or shape; a jump in a new suit is a splinter (four trumps).
# - Responder then places the contract: 3NT with game values and the
#   suits held, 3m/pass with a minimum, 5m with shape.
#
# BBA's stopper-showing bids are up the line and more detailed; this is a
# first cut that keeps the auction going to the right level.

module inverted-minors "Inverted minor raises"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/inverted_minors
  needs  responses
  skill  bidding_conventions/inverted_minors

after 1m (P)
  2m  "Inverted raise: 10+, 4+ {m}, no 4-card major, forcing"  shows m>=4, hcp>=10, H<=3, S<=3
      sets  forcing=round, trump=m
  3m  "Weak raise: 5-9, 5+ {m}, no 4-card major"  shows m>=5, hcp=5..9, H<=3, S<=3
      sets  trump=m

# Opener over the weak raise (5-9): game needs about 18 (rebids.bid's
# 14+ is for the limit raise without inverted minors; conv-ab 2026-10-07
# found 14-counts bidding 3NT opposite 5-9).
after 1m (P) 3m (P)
  3N  "Game opposite the weak raise: 18+, balanced"   shows hcp>=18, balanced | semibalanced
      priority 1
  5m  "Game opposite the weak raise: 18+, unbalanced"  shows hcp>=18
      priority 1
  P   "No game opposite the weak raise"              shows hcp<=17
      priority 1

# ── 1C-2C ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1C (P) 2C (P)
  2N  "12-14 balanced"                        shows balanced, hcp<=14
  3N  "18-19 balanced"                        shows balanced, hcp>=18
  3C  "Minimum, unbalanced"                   shows !balanced, hcp<=14
  2D  "Extras or shape, a diamond stopper"    shows stop(D), hcp>=15 | !balanced
      priority -1
