  2H  "Extras or shape, a heart stopper"      shows stop(H), hcp>=15 | !balanced, !stop(D)
      priority -1
  2S  "Extras or shape, a spade stopper"      shows stop(S), hcp>=15 | !balanced, !stop(H), !stop(D)
      priority -1
  3H  "Splinter: heart shortness, four clubs"  shows H<=1, C>=4, hcp>=13
      priority 1
  3S  "Splinter: spade shortness, four clubs"  shows S<=1, C>=4, hcp>=13
      priority 1
  4C  "Slam try, extras and a fit"            shows C>=4, hcp>=16, !balanced
# Opposite 12-14 and a nine-card minor fit, game from 12 (11 with a
# fifth trump): 3NT makes about half the time there (conv-ab, 2026-10-07).
after 1C (P) 2C (P) 2N (P)
  3N  "Game values"                           shows hcp>=12 | (hcp>=11, C>=5)
  3C  "Minimum, to play"                      shows hcp<=11, hcp<=10 | C<=4, !balanced
  P   "Minimum, balanced"      shows hcp<=11, hcp<=10 | C<=4, balanced
after 1C (P) 2C (P) 2N (P) 3C (P)
  P   "No further bid"
      priority -1
after 1C (P) 2C (P) 3C (P)
  3N  "Game values, the majors held"          shows hcp>=12, stop(S), stop(H)
  5C  "Game values"                           shows hcp>=13
      priority -1
  P   "Minimum"                               shows hcp<=12
      priority -2
# Opener's slam try: responder declines in game; with more, the slam
# rules (keycards) come first.
after 1C (P) 2C (P) 4C (P)
  5C  "Declines the slam try"
      priority -1
after 1C (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) | 1C (P) 2C (P) 2H (P) | 1C (P) 2C (P) 2S (P)
  2N  "10-12, balanced"                       shows hcp<=12, balanced
  3N  "Game values"                           shows hcp>=13
  3C  "10-12, unbalanced"                     shows hcp<=12
      priority -1
after 1C (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 2N (P) | 1C (P) 2C (P) 2H (P) 2N (P) | 1C (P) 2C (P) 2S (P) 2N (P)
  3N  "Game"                                  shows hcp>=15
  3C  "Minimum, unbalanced"                   shows hcp<=14
      priority -1
after 1C (P) 2C (P) 3H (P)
  3N  "A heart stopper"                           shows hcp>=10, stop(H)
  5C  "Game in clubs"                        shows hcp>=12
      priority -1
  4C  "Minimum"                               shows hcp<=11
      priority -1
after 1C (P) 2C (P) 3S (P)
  3N  "A spade stopper"                           shows hcp>=10, stop(S)
  5C  "Game in clubs"                        shows hcp>=12
      priority -1
  4C  "Minimum"                               shows hcp<=11
      priority -1

# ── 1D-2D ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1D (P) 2D (P)
  2N  "12-14 balanced"                        shows balanced, hcp<=14
  3N  "18-19 balanced"                        shows balanced, hcp>=18
  3D  "Minimum, unbalanced"                   shows !balanced, hcp<=14
  2H  "Extras or shape, a heart stopper"      shows stop(H), hcp>=15 | !balanced
      priority -1
  2S  "Extras or shape, a spade stopper"      shows stop(S), hcp>=15 | !balanced, !stop(H)
      priority -1
  3H  "Splinter: heart shortness, four diamonds"  shows H<=1, D>=4, hcp>=13
      priority 1
  3S  "Splinter: spade shortness, four diamonds"  shows S<=1, D>=4, hcp>=13
      priority 1
  4D  "Slam try, extras and a fit"            shows D>=4, hcp>=16, !balanced
# Opposite 12-14 and a nine-card minor fit, game from 12 (11 with a
# fifth trump): 3NT makes about half the time there (conv-ab, 2026-10-07).
after 1D (P) 2D (P) 2N (P)
  3N  "Game values"                           shows hcp>=12 | (hcp>=11, D>=5)
  3D  "Minimum, to play"                      shows hcp<=11, hcp<=10 | D<=4, !balanced
  P   "Minimum, balanced"      shows hcp<=11, hcp<=10 | D<=4, balanced
after 1D (P) 2D (P) 2N (P) 3D (P)
  P   "No further bid"
      priority -1
after 1D (P) 2D (P) 3D (P)
  3N  "Game values, the majors held"          shows hcp>=12, stop(S), stop(H)
  5D  "Game values"                           shows hcp>=13
      priority -1
  P   "Minimum"                               shows hcp<=12
      priority -2
# Opener's slam try: responder declines in game; with more, the slam
# rules (keycards) come first.
after 1D (P) 2D (P) 4D (P)
  5D  "Declines the slam try"
      priority -1
after 1D (P) 2D (P) 2H (P) | 1D (P) 2D (P) 2S (P)
  2N  "10-12, balanced"                       shows hcp<=12, balanced
  3N  "Game values"                           shows hcp>=13
  3D  "10-12, unbalanced"                     shows hcp<=12
      priority -1
after 1D (P) 2D (P) 2H (P) 2N (P) | 1D (P) 2D (P) 2S (P) 2N (P)
  3N  "Game"                                  shows hcp>=15
  3D  "Minimum, unbalanced"                   shows hcp<=14
      priority -1
after 1D (P) 2D (P) 3H (P)
  3N  "A heart stopper"                           shows hcp>=10, stop(H)
  5D  "Game in diamonds"                        shows hcp>=12
      priority -1
  4D  "Minimum"                               shows hcp<=11
      priority -1
after 1D (P) 2D (P) 3S (P)
  3N  "A spade stopper"                           shows hcp>=10, stop(S)
  5D  "Game in diamonds"                        shows hcp>=12
      priority -1
  4D  "Minimum"                               shows hcp<=11
      priority -1


# Opener after responder's minimum over the splinter.
after 1C (P) 2C (P) 3x (P) 4C (P) when x is H | x is S
  P   "No further bid"
      priority -1
after 1D (P) 2D (P) 3x (P) 4D (P) when x is H | x is S
  P   "No further bid"
      priority -1
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/jacoby_t:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.

module jacoby-transfers "Jacoby Transfers"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers default true
  needs  notrump-base
  skill  bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers
  param  systems_on = nt_overcalls.direct.systems_on default true
  param  vs_double = vs_double default false
  param  vs_2c = vs_2c default false
  param  style = general.style
  param  system = general.system   # `brill`: the Brill card's treatments

# The transfer is a question: "bid my suit". Opener's next call answers it,
# whether a plain completion or a super-accept.
after nt1 when !they.bid | systems_on
  2D  "Transfer to hearts"  announce "Transfer"  shows H>=5  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(H)  artificial
  2H  "Transfer to spades"  announce "Transfer"  shows S>=5  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(S)  artificial
  2H  "Transfer to spades, 5-5 in the majors"  announce "Transfer"  shows S>=5, H>=5
      when  style is bba                  # BBA transfers to spades first with 5-5
      sets  forcing=round, ask=transfer(S)
      artificial

# Opener completes the transfer. Super-accepts are separate modules
# (super-accept.bid, superaccept-doubleton.bid), switched on by the card.
after nt1 2D (P)
  2H  "Completes transfer"
      when  system is not brill
after nt1 2H (P)
  2S  "Completes transfer"
      when  system is not brill

# brill (the Brill card): the plain completion denies four trumps, except
# with 4-3-3-3 and a minimum. Brill /explain, 2026-10-15, "No superaccept":
# `hearts < 4 or (not max and ExplicitShape == '3=4=3=3')` (spades:
# `spades < 4 or (not max and ExplicitShape == '4=3=3=3')`). The other
# four-trump hands super-accept: super-accept.bid, superaccept-doubleton.bid.
after nt1 2D (P) when system is brill
  2H  "Completes transfer: 2-3 ♥, or a minimum 3=4=3=3"
      shows H<=3 | (H=4, shortest=3, hcp<=15)
after nt1 2H (P) when system is brill
  2S  "Completes transfer: 2-3 ♠, or a minimum 4=3=3=3"
      shows S<=3 | (S=4, shortest=3, hcp<=15)

# Responder's second call, once opener has answered. There is no auction
# pattern: `answered transfer(M)` holds after any auction where partner
# answered my transfer, and binds M to the major.
#
# `strength` bands are measured against what opener has shown: after a
# 15-17 1NT, invite is 8-9 and game 10-15; after a maximum super-accept the
# invitational band shrinks, so invitational hands bid game. Notrump
# decisions use `strength`, total points (HCP + ½ per ten + 1 per card
# beyond four, so the fifth card of the major counts); playing in the major
# uses `suit_strength` (HCP + ½ per card beyond four).
when answered transfer(M)
  3M  "Sign off in the known fit"              shows suit_strength=signoff
      when partner.M>=4, !(partner.last=2{M})  # after a 2S or 2NT super-accept, not Brill's plain 4-card completion
  4M  "Game: in the fit, opposite a super-accept"  shows suit_strength=invite
      when partner.M>=4                        # the super-accept is for thin games
  P   "Weak: to play, {signoff} total points"  shows strength=signoff
      when maybe partner.M<=3 | partner.last=3{M}   # never pass an artificial super-accept (2S, 2NT)
      when !passes_out_artificial                   # nor my own transfer, doubled and passed back (base.bid)
  2N  "Invitational: {invite} total points, exactly 5 {M}"  shows M=5, balanced | shortest>=2, strength=invite
      sets ask=invite(M)
  3M  "Invitational: {invite} total points, 6+ {M}"  shows M>=6, suit_strength=invite
      when partner.last=2{M}                   # after a super-accept 3M is the sign-off
      sets ask=invite(M)
  # Six cards and a count between the two measures: too much to pass in
  # total points (the sixth card counts two), too little to invite in
  # suit points (it counts one). J85.KJ9754.6.J52 (6 HCP) had no call at all
  # (convention score, 2026-10-07: 6 no-rule boards with Texas, 26
  # without; 13 without super-accepts, whose plain completion is then
  # the whole 1NT range). HCP decide, as for the five-card hands below.
  3M  "Invitational: 6+ {M}"                   shows M>=6, strength>=invite, suit_strength=signoff, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max
      when partner.last=2{M}
      sets ask=invite(M)
      priority -1
  P   "Weak in HCP: play here"                 shows M>=6, strength>=invite, suit_strength=signoff, hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max
      when partner.last=2{M}
      priority -1
  3N  "Choice of games: 5 {M}, {game} total points"  shows M=5, balanced, strength=game
      when maybe partner.M<=2                  # only while the fit is unknown
      sets ask=choice                          # opener corrects with 3+ {M}
  4M  "Game: {game} total points, 6+ {M}"      shows M>=6, suit_strength=game
      when !texas_1nt                              # with Texas, game-only hands use it
  4M  "Game: 6+ {M}, mild slam interest"             shows M>=6, suit_points>=31-partner.points.max, suit_points<=32-partner.points.min
      when texas_1nt                               # 14-17 opposite 15-17: slam if opener has
                                               # the right hand; Texas is for 18+
      sets ask=slam_try(M)
  4M  "Game: {game} total points, 6+ {M}"      shows M>=6, suit_strength=game
      when texas_1nt                               # game-only hands normally use Texas
      priority -1                              # a fallback: 4M still reads as the slam try
  4M  "Game: in the known fit"                  shows suit_strength=game
      when partner.M>=3                        # known, e.g. after a super-accept
  # Without Texas the slam hands with six come through the transfer too
  # (convention score, 2026-10-07: 39 had no rule). Five of the major
  # invites six; six bids it.
  5M  "Slam invitation: 6+ {M}"                shows M>=6, suit_strength=slam_invite
      when !texas_1nt, partner.last=2{M}
      sets ask=major_slam_invite(M)
  6M  "Slam: 6+ {M}"                           shows M>=6, suit_strength>=slam
      when !texas_1nt, partner.last=2{M}
  3m  "Second suit, game forcing"              shows m>=4, strength>=game
      sets forcing=game, ask=new_suit(M)
  4N  "Quantitative, 5 {M}"                    shows M=5, balanced, strength=slam_invite
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      sets ask=quant_major(M)
  6N  "Slam: {slam} total points, 5 {M}"       shows M=5, balanced, strength=slam
  # Invitational in total points only through length (5-5 with a
  # singleton, 6 HCP): no natural invitation fits. BBA passes.
  P   "Weak in HCP: play here"                 shows M=5, strength=invite, hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max
      when maybe partner.M<=3 | partner.last=3{M}
      priority -1
  # With a singleton and a real invitation in HCP, BBA bids 2NT anyway
  # (Basic_Openers_Rebid 172, KT432.Q32.2.QJ93).
  2N  "Invitational, exactly 5 {M}, a singleton"   shows M=5, strength=invite, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max
      sets ask=invite(M)
      priority -1

# Opener's answer to the invitation (`when asked invite(M)`) is a base
# rule in rebids.bid: it answers any invitation in a major, transfers or
# not.

# Opener answers the quantitative 4NT with five in the major: slam with
# 32 combined. Double dummy on dealt hands (probes/dd/quant-4nt-hearts.toml,
# jacoby-transfers.notes.md, 2026-10-03): the doubleton is what makes the
# major worth playing. A fit and a doubleton count the doubleton (`tp`),
# so a minimum with one accepts in the major; 4-3-3-3 has no ruffing value
# and plays notrump, or passes with a minimum. At IMPs the major with
# four trumps, or three below a maximum; 6NT otherwise and at matchpoints.
# 5M (to play, a minimum) never beat the better of pass and slam.
when asked quant_major(M)
  6M  "Accepts in {M}: four trumps, a doubleton"
      shows M>=4, shortest=2, points>=32-partner.points.min
      when  imps
  6M  "Accepts in {M}: three trumps, a doubleton, not a maximum"
      shows M=3, shortest=2, points>=32-partner.points.min, hcp<=shown.hcp.max-1
      when  imps
  6M  "Accepts in {M}: a fit and a doubleton"
      shows M>=3, shortest=2, points<=31-partner.points.min, tp(M)>=32-partner.points.min
  6N  "Accepts the slam invitation"     shows points>=32-partner.points.min
  P   "Declines"                        shows points<=31-partner.points.min

# Opener after responder's second suit (game forcing): rebid the major with
# three-card support, which agrees it below game so that responder can look
# for slam; otherwise 3NT.
when asked new_suit(M)
  3M  "3+ {M}: support"             shows M>=3   sets trump=M
  3N  "No fit: 2 {M}"               shows M<=2

# Responder over opener's 3NT, with the 5-4 shown (Rick, 2026-11-06,
# bridge-classroom #85: AKT76.A95.9.AJ94 passed 3NT opposite 17 and
# 6NT made; "Rusty should invite slam here"). over-3nt.bid counts HCP
# for a balanced hand; this hand has shown its shape, and its fifth
# major card is a trick in notrump too, so it counts total points:
# 32 on opener's floor invites with a quantitative 4NT, 34 bids six.
# This 4NT takes over over-3nt.bid's (which counts HCP) in this auction,
# so opener reads one meaning. He accepts in points, one more than the
# textbook 32 on responder's floor (17 shown: a 16-count with two tens
# or a fifth card accepts, a flat 15 declines), in the minor with four
# of it (a 4-4 fit takes a ruff), else 6NT.
when answered new_suit(M), partner.last=3N, !they.bid
  6N  "Small slam: 5-4 shown, {slam} total points"
      shows points + partner.hcp.min >= 34
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT, 5-4 shown"
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      shows points + partner.hcp.min >= 32, points + partner.hcp.min <= 33
      sets  ask=quant_two_suits

when asked quant_two_suits
  6C  "Accepts, in clubs: four clubs"     shows C>=4, points>=33-partner.points.min
      when  partner.C>=4
      priority 1
  6D  "Accepts, in diamonds: four diamonds"  shows D>=4, points>=33-partner.points.min
      when  partner.D>=4
      priority 1
  6N  "Accepts the slam invitation"       shows points>=33-partner.points.min
  P   "Declines"                          shows points<=32-partner.points.min

# Opener after the jump to game with mild slam interest: bid on with a good
# fit and a maximum, even without having super-accepted.
when asked slam_try(M)
  4N  "Keycard ask: good fit and a maximum"   shows M>=3, points>=31-partner.suit_points.min
      sets ask=keycards(M)
      artificial
  P   "No slam: plays game"

# Opener answers five of the major: six unless minimum.
when asked major_slam_invite(M)
  6M  "Accepts the slam invitation: not a minimum"   shows hcp>=shown.hcp.max-1
  P   "Declines: a minimum"           shows hcp<=shown.hcp.max-2

# BBA's treatment (probed 2026-09-24, jacoby-transfers.notes.md), our
# default since Rick's ruling the same day: with five hearts, four spades
# and 7-9 HCP transfer rather than bid Stayman, then show the spades. The 2S is not forcing: opener passes
# with three spades and two hearts. He prefers hearts: game with four,
# or with three and 17; with four spades (two hearts) game from 16.
after 1N (P) 2D (P) 2H (P)
  2S  "5 hearts and 4 spades, invitational, not forcing"
      shows H=5, S=4, hcp>=24-partner.hcp.max, hcp<=24-partner.hcp.min

after 1N (P) 2D (P) 2H (P) 2S (P)
  4H  "Accepts, in the heart fit"      shows H>=4 | (H=3, points>=24-partner.hcp.min)
  3H  "Declines, in the heart fit"     shows H=3, points<=23-partner.hcp.min
  4S  "Accepts, in the spade fit"      shows S>=4, H<=2, points>=23-partner.hcp.min
  3S  "Declines, in the spade fit"     shows S>=4, H<=2, points<=22-partner.hcp.min
  P   "No eight-card fit: play 2S"     shows H<=2, S<=3

# Responder bids game over the decline with the top of the range.
after 1N (P) 2D (P) 2H (P) 2S (P) 3H (P)
  4H  "Game: the top of the invitation"  shows hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max
  P   "Minimum: play 3H"                 shows hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max
after 1N (P) 2D (P) 2H (P) 2S (P) 3S (P)
  4S  "Game: the top of the invitation"  shows hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max
  P   "Minimum: play 3S"                 shows hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max

# ── Under interference ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# `transfers.vs_double` and `transfers.vs_2c` say the transfers survive
# RHO's double or 2♣ overcall. They keep their own calls in both cases:
# 2♦ for hearts and 2♥ for spades. Opener completes as usual; the
# super-accepts are not written for these auctions, so he simply bids
# the major. One `after` line takes one `when`, so the double and the
# 2♣ overcall are two contexts.

# With both majors, transfer to the longer, and to spades when they are
# equal: that is what BBA does under interference, and the higher suit
# leaves us better placed if they bid again. (Uncontested, Stayman comes
# first with 5-4 for Smolen; here it does not.)
after 1N (X) when vs_double
  2H  "Transfer to spades"  announce "Transfer"  shows S>=5  when S>=H  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(S)  artificial
  2D  "Transfer to hearts"  announce "Transfer"  shows H>=5  when H>S   sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(H)  artificial

# Over the 2♣ overcall the transfer has a floor of five HCP: below that
# BBA leaves the auction alone rather than push to the two level with
# nothing. (Over the double there is no floor — running is the point.)
after 1N (2C) when vs_2c
  2H  "Transfer to spades"  announce "Transfer"  shows S>=5, hcp>=5  when S>=H  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(S)  artificial
  2D  "Transfer to hearts"  announce "Transfer"  shows H>=5, hcp>=5  when H>S   sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(H)  artificial

after 1N (X) 2D (P) when vs_double
  2H  "Completes transfer"
after 1N (X) 2H (P) when vs_double
  2S  "Completes transfer"
after 1N (2C) 2D (P) when vs_2c
  2H  "Completes transfer"
after 1N (2C) 2H (P) when vs_2c
  2S  "Completes transfer"
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/kokish/k:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# The Kokish relay (Bridge Bum, "Kokish Relay"): after 2♣–2♦, opener's
# 2♥ shows either hearts (five or more, unbalanced) or the balanced hand
# that would have rebid 3NT (24-25 on our ladder, strong-openings.bid).
# Responder must bid 2♠, and opener says which:
#
#   2NT  24-25 balanced (game forcing, below 3NT)
#   3♣/3♦/3♠  five or more hearts and four or more of that suit
#   3♥   six or more hearts, one-suited
#
# A balanced hand with five hearts rebids 2NT (22-23) or goes through the
# relay (24-25). See kokish.notes.md.

module kokish "Kokish relay after 2♣–2♦"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/kokish
  needs  strong-openings
  skill  bidding_conventions/kokish

# ── Opener's 2♥: the relay ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Priority 1: it replaces the natural 2♥ and the 3NT rebid of
# strong-openings.bid for the hands it takes.
after 2C (P) 2D (P)
  2H  "Kokish: hearts, or 24-25 balanced"   alert
      shows (H>=5, !balanced) | (balanced, hcp=24..25)
      sets  ask=kokish
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── Responder completes the relay ────────────────────────────────────
when asked kokish
  2S  "Completes the relay"   alert
      artificial
      priority 2

# ── Opener says which ────────────────────────────────────────────────
when answered kokish
  2N  "24-25 balanced"                        shows balanced, hcp=24..25
      priority 1
  3H  "Six or more hearts, one-suited"        shows H>=6, S<=3, D<=3, C<=3
      priority 1
  3C  "Five or more hearts, four or more clubs"     shows H>=5, C>=4
      priority 1
  3D  "Five or more hearts, four or more diamonds"  shows H>=5, D>=4
      priority 1
  3S  "Five or more hearts, four or more spades"    shows H>=5, S>=4
      priority 1

# ── Responder after the two-suiter: support hearts, raise the second
# suit, or 3NT. Game forcing (the 2♣ opening), so a cheap raise leaves
# room for the slam modules.
after 2C (P) 2D (P) 2H (P) 2S (P) 3x (P) when x is not H
  3H  "Three or more hearts: agrees hearts"   shows H>=3
      sets  trump=H
      priority 1
  4x  "Four or more {x}: agrees {x}"          shows x>=4, H<=2
      when  x is S
      sets  trump=x
      priority 1
  4x  "Four or more {x}: agrees {x}"          shows x>=4, H<=2
      when  x is C | x is D
      sets  trump=x
  3N  "No fit: notrump"                        shows H<=2
after 2C (P) 2D (P) 2H (P) 2S (P) 3H (P)
  4H  "Two or more hearts: game in hearts"     shows H>=2
      sets  trump=H
  3N  "A singleton or void in hearts"          shows H<=1
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/mccabe/m:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# The McCabe adjunct (Robert S. Todd, "McCabe Responses to Preempts",
# Adventures in Bridge; PBS `McCabe_After_Weak_2`): after our weak two is
# doubled for takeout, responder's new suit below three of opener's suit
# is a raise that names the lead, and the redouble shows a long suit of
# responder's own:
#
#   3♣/3♦/3♥  a raise to three of opener's suit with a good holding in
#             the suit bid (two of the top three): opener bids 3 of his suit
#   XX        a long suit of my own, no fit: opener bids the next step,
#             responder passes it or bids his suit
#   2NT       the ask, as without the double (weak-two-responses.bid)
#
# The direct raises and pass are unchanged. See mccabe.notes.md.

module mccabe "McCabe adjunct"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/mccabe
  needs  weak-two-responses
  skill  bidding_conventions/mccabe

# ── Responder over the double ────────────────────────────────────────
after 2x (X) when weak_two_suit(x), x is D | x is H | x is S
  3y  "McCabe: a raise, lead {y}"   alert
      shows x>=3, quality(y)>=good, hcp<=14
      when  y is not x, y is C | (y is D, x is not D) | (y is H, x is S)
      artificial
      priority 1
  2N  "Asks: how good is the weak two?"   alert
      shows hcp>=15, x>=2
      sets  forcing=round, ask=weak_two(x)
      artificial
  XX  "McCabe: own long suit, asks for the next step"   alert
      shows x<=1, longest>=6, hcp<=14
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── Opener after the lead-directing raise: back to his suit ──────────
after 2x (X) 3y (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is D | x is H | x is S, y is not x
  3x  "Back to my suit"
      priority 1

# ── The redouble: opener bids the next step, responder places it ────
after 2D (X) XX (P)
  2H  "Next step, as asked"   artificial   priority 1
after 2H (X) XX (P)
  2S  "Next step, as asked"   artificial   priority 1
after 2S (X) XX (P)
  2N  "Next step, as asked"   artificial   priority 1
after 2D (X) XX (P) 2H (P) | 2H (X) XX (P) 2S (P) | 2S (X) XX (P) 2N (P)
  P   "My suit: to play"           shows H>=6
      when  partner.last=2H
      priority 1
  P   "My suit: to play"           shows S>=6
      when  partner.last=2S
      priority 1
  2S  "My suit: to play"           shows S>=6
  3C  "My suit: to play"           shows C>=6
  3D  "My suit: to play"           shows D>=6
  3H  "My suit: to play"           shows H>=6
# They bid over the redouble: opener has nothing more to say.
after 2D (X) XX (*) | 2H (X) XX (*) | 2S (X) XX (*)
  P   "No further bid"
      priority -5
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/mini_rom:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Mini-Roman 2♦ (Bridge Hands, "Mini Roman",
# https://www.bridgehands.com/M/Mini_Roman.htm; ACBL Unit 390,
# "Mini-Roman"; the slam continuations are Rick Wilson's additions):
# an opening 2♦ shows 11-15 HCP and a three-suited hand, 4-4-4-1 or
# 5-4-4-0. The five-card suit of a 5-4-4-0 is a minor (with five in a
# major the hand opens 1M). The weak 2♦ is off (preempts.bid).
#
# Responder:
#
#   Pass  five or more diamonds, weak
#   2♥ 2♠ 3♣  to play, weak: opener passes, or with a singleton or void
#            there bids his next four-card suit up the line
#   2NT   11+, game forcing, asks for the short suit:
#         3♣ short clubs, 3♦ short diamonds, 3♥ short hearts, 3♠ short spades
#   3♥/3♠ invitational, five or more
#   4♥/4♠ to play
#
# See mini-roman.notes.md.

module mini-roman "Mini-Roman 2♦"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/mini_roman_2d
  needs  preempts
  skill  bidding_conventions/mini_roman_2d

define three_suiter = (longest=4, shortest=1) | (longest=5, second_longest=4, shortest=0, S<=4, H<=4)

# ── The opening ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Priority 1: it takes these hands from the one-level openings.
when opening
  2D  "Mini-Roman: 11-15, 4-4-4-1 or 5-4-4-0"   alert
      shows hcp=11..15, three_suiter
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The weak calls: the cheapest four-card suit, which opener holds unless
# it is his short suit; a diamond pass needs five.
after 2D (P) | 2D (X)
  2N  "Asks for the short suit: 11+, game forcing"   alert
      shows hcp>=11
      sets  forcing=game, ask=mini_roman
      artificial
  4H  "To play"                         shows H>=6, hcp=8..14
  4S  "To play"                         shows S>=6, hcp=8..14
  3H  "Invitational: five or more hearts"   shows H>=5, hcp=9..10
  3S  "Invitational: five or more spades"   shows S>=5, hcp=9..10
  P   "Five or more diamonds: to play"    shows D>=5, hcp<=10
      priority 1
  2H  "To play: four or more hearts"     shows H>=4, hcp<=10
  2S  "To play: four or more spades"     shows S>=4, hcp<=10, H<=3
  3C  "To play: five or more clubs"      shows C>=5, hcp<=10, H<=3, S<=3
  2H  "Weak: pass or correct"            shows hcp<=10
      priority -2

# ── Opener: pass, or correct from the short suit ─────────────────────
after 2D (P) 2H (P) | 2D (X) 2H (P)
  P   "Four or more hearts"              shows H>=4
  2S  "Short in hearts: four spades"     shows H<=1, S>=4
  3C  "Short in hearts, no four spades: clubs"   shows H<=1, C>=4
after 2D (P) 2S (P) | 2D (X) 2S (P)
  P   "Four or more spades"              shows S>=4
  3C  "Short in spades: clubs"           shows S<=1, C>=4
after 2D (P) 3C (P) | 2D (X) 3C (P)
  P   "Four or more clubs"               shows C>=4
  3D  "Short in clubs: diamonds"         shows C<=1, D>=4
# Responder accepts the correction.
after 2D (P) 2H (P) 2S (P) | 2D (P) 2H (P) 3C (P) | 2D (P) 2S (P) 3C (P) | 2D (P) 3C (P) 3D (P)
  P   "Partner's suit: to play"
      priority -1

# Opener over the invitation: game with a maximum and support.
after 2D (P) 3H (P)
  4H  "Accepts: 14-15 with four hearts"  shows H>=4, hcp>=14
  P   "Declines"
      priority -1
after 2D (P) 3S (P)
  4S  "Accepts: 14-15 with four spades"  shows S>=4, hcp>=14
  P   "Declines"
      priority -1

# ── Opener answers 2NT: the short suit ───────────────────────────────
when asked mini_roman
  3C  "Short clubs"       shows C<=1
  3D  "Short diamonds"    shows D<=1
  3H  "Short hearts"      shows H<=1
  3S  "Short spades"      shows S<=1

# ── Responder places the contract ────────────────────────────────────
# Game in a major with four (opener holds four of it unless short there),
# 3NT with the short suit stopped, else five of a minor.
after 2D (P) 2N (P) 3x (P)
  4S  "Game in spades"     shows S>=4    when x is not S
      priority 2
  4H  "Game in hearts"     shows H>=4    when x is not H
      priority 1
  3N  "Game in notrump: the short suit held"   shows x>=4 | stop(x)
  5C  "Game in clubs"      shows C>=4    when x is not C
      priority -1
  5D  "Game in diamonds"   shows D>=4    when x is not D
      priority -1
  3N  "Game in notrump"
      priority -2

# ── They overcall the 2♦ (2026-10-05) ───────────────────────────────
# The self A/B against the weak 2♦ found responder passing every
# overcall, 13 HCP and a fit included (2♦ (2♥) P P P on 32 boards). With
# game values: 3NT with their suit stopped, four of a major with five
# (four when they bid the other major: opener is then likely short in
# theirs and holds four of ours), else a double, values for defence
# or for opener to describe. Weaker hands pass. Standard practice for a
# three-suited opening, not yet cited.
after 2D (2y) | 2D (3y) when y is not D
  4S  "Game: 11+ and spades"           shows S>=5 | (S>=4, y is H), hcp>=11
      when  y is not S
      priority 2
  4H  "Game: 11+ and hearts"           shows H>=5 | (H>=4, y is S), hcp>=11
      when  y is not H
      priority 2
  3N  "Game: 11+, {y} stopped"         shows hcp>=11, stop(y)
      priority 1
  X   "11+: values, defence or a game for opener to choose"   shows hcp>=11
  P   "Not enough to act"
      priority -3

# Opener after the double: defend with three or more of their suit;
# short there, bid the cheapest four-card suit, a major first.
after 2D (2y) X (P) | 2D (3y) X (P)
  P   "Defend: three or more {y}"      shows y>=3
      priority 1
  cheapest(S) "Short in {y}: four spades"    shows S>=4, y<=1   when y is not S   priority 3
  cheapest(H) "Short in {y}: four hearts"    shows H>=4, y<=1   when y is not H   priority 2
  cheapest(C) "Short in {y}: four clubs"     shows C>=4, y<=1   when y is not C   priority 1
  cheapest(D) "Short in {y}: four diamonds"  shows D>=4, y<=1   when y is not D

# Responder places the game: four of opener's major with four, 3NT with
# their suit stopped, else five of opener's minor.
after 2D (2y) X (P) 2z (P) | 2D (2y) X (P) 3z (P) | 2D (3y) X (P) 3z (P) | 2D (3y) X (P) 4z (P)
  4{z} "Game in {z}"                    shows z>=4
      when  z is H | z is S
      priority 2
  3N  "Game in notrump: {y} stopped"   shows stop(y)
      priority 1
  5{z} "Game in {z}"                    shows z>=3
      when  z is C | z is D
  P   "Partner's suit: to play"
      priority -2

# They come in over the weak response: opener passes (responder may act).
after 2D (P) 2H (*) | 2D (P) 2S (*) | 2D (P) 3C (*)
  P   "No further bid"
      priority -5
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/minor_su:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Minor Suit Stayman over 1NT (`notrump.minor_suit_stayman.play`), as
# GIB and BBA play it (minor-suit-stayman.notes.md): 2♠ asks for a
# four-card minor with five-four or better in the minors and game
# values. Opener bids 3♣ with four or more clubs, 3♦ with four or more
# diamonds and not four clubs, 2NT with neither.
#
# The minor-suit transfers that go with it on 21GF-MSTandMSS (2NT to
# clubs, 3♣ to diamonds) are `notrump.minor_transfers.style = two_nt_three_c`,
# in minor-transfers.bid.

module minor-suit-stayman "Minor Suit Stayman over 1NT"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/minor_suit_stayman
  card   over_1nt
  needs  notrump-base
  skill  bidding_conventions/minor_suit_stayman
  param  systems_on = nt_overcalls.direct.systems_on default true
  param  rkcb   = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard default false

after nt1_undoubled when !they.bid | systems_on
  2S  "Minor Suit Stayman: 5-4+ in the minors, game values"  alert
      shows C>=4, D>=4, C+D>=9, H<=3, S<=3, strength>=game
      sets  forcing=game
      artificial
      priority 1                         # ahead of 3NT and the minor slam tries

# Opener answers Minor Suit Stayman. With a maximum BBA jumps: 4♣/4♦
# with the minor, 3NT without (corpus, 2026-10-07: every 17-count of
# 15-17 and no other; minimums bid 3♣/3♦/2NT). The jump leaves
# responder the room for keycard below game in the minor.
after nt1_undoubled 2S (P)
  4C  "Four or more clubs, a maximum"        alert  shows C>=4, hcp>=shown.hcp.max
      artificial
      priority 1
  4D  "Four or more diamonds, not four clubs, a maximum"  alert  shows D>=4, C<=3, hcp>=shown.hcp.max
      artificial
      priority 1
  3N  "No four-card minor, a maximum"        shows C<=3, D<=3, hcp>=shown.hcp.max
      priority 1
  3C  "Four or more clubs"                   alert  shows C>=4
      artificial
  3D  "Four or more diamonds, not four clubs"  alert  shows D>=4, C<=3
      artificial
  2N  "No four-card minor"                   alert  shows C<=3, D<=3
      artificial

# Responder. With a fit and slam values (33 total points between the
# hands): keycard for the minor when the card plays it (BBA asks there,
# "Blackwood 1430, for ♣/♦"), else six. With game values only and a
# singleton or void in a major, three of that major: shortness, asking
# for a stopper (BBA's "artificial" 3♥/3♠, read from its auctions);
# opener bids 3NT with it, else four of the
# minor, and responder bids five. Otherwise 3NT. Without a fit: 3NT,
# 4NT quantitative or 6NT, on HCP (a notrump slam takes high cards;
# the long minors' length points sent 13-counts to 6NT).
after nt1_undoubled 2S (P) 3m (P) | nt1_undoubled 2S (P) 4m (P)
  4N  "Keycard ask in {m}"                   alert
      when  rkcb
      shows tp(m)>=33-partner.hcp.min
      sets  trump=m, ask=keycards(m)
      artificial
      priority 1
  6m  "Slam in the minor fit"                shows tp(m)>=33-partner.hcp.min
      sets  trump=m
  3H  "Short hearts: asks for a heart stopper"  alert
      shows H<=1
      artificial
      priority -1
  3S  "Short spades: asks for a spade stopper"  alert
      shows S<=1, H>=2
      artificial
      priority -1
  3N  "Game in notrump"
      priority -2
after nt1_undoubled 2S (P) 3m (P) 3M (P)
  3N  "A stopper in {M}: game in notrump"    shows stop(M)
  4m  "No stopper in {M}"                    shows !stop(M)
      priority -1
after nt1_undoubled 2S (P) 3m (P) 3M (P) 4m (P)
  5m  "Game in the minor fit"
      sets  trump=m
after nt1_undoubled 2S (P) 3m (P) 3M (P) 3N (P)
  P   "Game in notrump"
after nt1_undoubled 2S (P) 4m (P)
  5m  "Game in the minor fit"
      sets  trump=m
      priority -1
after nt1_undoubled 2S (P) 2N (P) | nt1_undoubled 2S (P) 3N (P)
  6N  "No fit: slam values"                  shows hcp>=33-partner.hcp.min
  4N  "No fit: quantitative, invites 6NT"    shows hcp>=31-partner.hcp.min, hcp<=32-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=quant
  3N  "No fit: game"
      priority -1
after nt1_undoubled 2S (P) 3N (P)
  P   "No fit: 3NT"
      priority -2
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/modified:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Modified Jacoby 2NT (Larry Cohen, "Modified Jacoby 2NT",
# https://www.larryco.com/bridge-articles/modified-jacoby-2nt):
# responder's 2NT is the same game-forcing raise (jacoby-2nt.bid), but
# opener's rebids sort the hand by strength first and shape second, and
# responder relays for more:
#
#   4M   the worst minimum: 5-3-3-2, nothing extra
#   3♣   any other minimum              3♦ asks: 3♥ short, 3♠ 5-4-2-2,
#                                       3NT 6+ trumps, 4M 5-3-3-2, 4x a side suit
#   3♦   non-minimum, a singleton or void      3♥ asks which
#   3♥   non-minimum, 5-4-2-2                  3♠ asks for the four-card suit
#   3♠   non-minimum, 6+ trumps, no shortness
#   3NT  non-minimum, 5-3-3-2
#   4x   a good five-card side suit
#
# The suits are fixed: over 1♥ too, 3♥ is the 5-4-2-2 and 3♠ the six
# trumps (Cohen writes one schedule for both majors). Minimum is 14 HCP or
# fewer, the standard module's line. See modified-jacoby-2nt.notes.md.

module modified-jacoby-2nt "Modified Jacoby 2NT"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/modified_jacoby_2nt
  needs  jacoby-2nt
  skill  bidding_conventions/modified_jacoby_2nt
  param  rkcb  = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard default false
  param  bw    = bidding_conventions/blackwood default false
  param  cue   = bidding_conventions/control_bids default false

# ── Opener's rebid ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1M (P) 2N (P)
  4M  "Minimum, 5-3-3-2, nothing extra"
      shows hcp<=12, shape 5-3-3-2, M=5
      priority 1                       # ahead of 3♣, which these hands also fit
  3C  "Minimum, 14 HCP or less: 3♦ asks"  alert
      shows hcp<=14
      artificial
  3D  "15+, a singleton or void: 3♥ asks where"  alert
      shows hcp>=15, shortest<=1
      artificial
  3H  "15+, 5-4-2-2: 3♠ asks for the four-card suit"  alert
      shows hcp>=15, shape 5-4-2-2, M=5
      artificial
  3S  "15+, six or more trumps, no singleton or void"  alert
      shows hcp>=15, M>=6, shortest>=2
      artificial
  3N  "15+, 5-3-3-2"
      shows hcp>=15, shape 5-3-3-2, M=5
  4x  "15+, a good five-card side suit"
      shows hcp>=15, x>=5, quality(x)>=good
      when  x is not M, M is S | x is not S

# ── They bid over the 2NT ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Cohen: double shows shortness in their suit, a new suit is natural or
# a control, 3NT a balanced maximum with the ace or king of their suit,
# the jump to 4M a dead minimum with 6-3-2-2, and pass a flat hand. The pass is forcing (Rick, 2026-10-28): we are in a game
# force, so responder must act, by doubling them for penalty or bidding
# on. It is marked artificial because the engine otherwise drops a pass
# below game in a game force.
after 1M (P) 2N (2x) | 1M (P) 2N (3x) when x is not M
  X   "Short in {x}: a singleton or void"  alert
      shows x<=1
      artificial
      priority 16                      # ahead of everything else here, as the shortness is the news
  3N  "15+, balanced, the ace or king of {x}"
      shows hcp>=15, balanced, has(A,x) | has(K,x)
      priority 15
  4M  "Dead minimum, 6-3-2-2"
      shows hcp<=12, shape 6-3-2-2, M=6
      priority 15
  3y  "Natural or a control in {y}"
      shows (y>=5, quality(y)>=good) | has(A,y) | has(K,y)
      when  y is not M, y is not x
      priority 15
  4y  "Natural or a control in {y}"
      shows (y>=5, quality(y)>=good) | has(A,y) | has(K,y)
      when  y is not M, y is not x, M is S | y is not S
      priority 15
  P   "Forcing pass: a flat hand"  alert
      artificial
      priority 14                      # below the descriptions, above the generic competitive calls

# Responder after the forcing pass (Cohen: "after which, responder's
# X = penalty"; Rick, 2026-10-28): opener is flat, perhaps an awful
# 5-3-3-2, so with their suit held responder doubles them, whatever his
# strength. Else game; with slam interest the slam modules act.
after 1M (P) 2N (2x) P (P) | 1M (P) 2N (3x) P (P) when x is not M
  X   "Penalty: {x} held"
      shows x>=4 | (x>=3, has(A,x) | has(K,x))
      priority 15
  4M  "Game: no slam interest"
      shows !slam_interest(M)
      priority 14

# ── They double or bid over an ask ───────────────────────────────────
# Cohen: "If they double Asks or re-asks: XX = business, Pass = S1, etc.
# If they bid after Ask or re-ask: X = Penalty, Pass = S1, etc." Pass is
# the first step and the bids follow in order from the cheapest
# (`step(1)` the second step). The pass is artificial, so the game force
# keeps it legal and makes responder bid again. 2NT is the first ask:
# over their double of it the steps hold; over their bid, the schedule
# above (X short there, as Cohen says).

define mj_business(a) = a>=4, has(A,a) | has(K,a)

after 1M (P) 2N (X)
  XX  "Business: 15+, balanced, to play 2NT redoubled"
      shows hcp>=15, balanced
      priority 16
  P   "Step 1: a minimum, 14 or less"  alert
      shows hcp<=14
      artificial
      priority 15
  step(1)  "Step 2: 15+, a singleton or void"  alert
      shows hcp>=15, shortest<=1
      artificial
      priority 15
  step(2)  "Step 3: 15+, 5-4-2-2"  alert
      shows hcp>=15, shape 5-4-2-2, M=5
      artificial
      priority 15
  step(3)  "Step 4: 15+, six or more trumps, no singleton or void"  alert
      shows hcp>=15, M>=6, shortest>=2
      artificial
      priority 15
  step(4)  "Step 5: 15+, 5-3-3-2"  alert
      shows hcp>=15, shape 5-3-3-2, M=5
      artificial
      priority 15

# The 3♦ ask after a minimum.
after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (X)
  XX  "Business: good diamonds"
      shows mj_business(D)
      priority 16
after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (3z) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (4z)
  X   "Penalty: good {z}"
      shows mj_business(z)
      priority 16
after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (*) when !rho.last=P
  P   "Step 1: a singleton or void"  alert
      shows shortest<=1
      artificial
      priority 15
  step(1)  "Step 2: 5-4-2-2"  alert
      shows shape 5-4-2-2, M=5
      artificial
      priority 15
  step(2)  "Step 3: six or more trumps, no singleton or void"  alert
      shows M>=6, shortest>=2
      artificial
      priority 15
  step(3)  "Step 4: 5-3-3-2"  alert
      shows shape 5-3-3-2, M=5
      artificial
      priority 15

# The 3♥ ask after shortness.
after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (X)
  XX  "Business: good hearts"
      shows mj_business(H)
      when  M is S
      priority 16
after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (3z) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (4z)
  X   "Penalty: good {z}"
      shows mj_business(z)
      priority 16
after 1S (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (*) when !rho.last=P
  P   "Step 1: a void"  alert
      shows C=0 | D=0 | H=0
      artificial
      priority 15
  step(1)  "Step 2: a singleton club"  alert
      shows C=1, D>=1, H>=1
      artificial
      priority 15
  step(2)  "Step 3: a singleton diamond"  alert
      shows D=1, C>=2, H>=1
      artificial
      priority 15
  step(3)  "Step 4: a singleton heart"  alert
      shows H=1, C>=2, D>=2
      artificial
      priority 15
after 1H (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (*) when !rho.last=P
  P   "Step 1: a void"  alert
      shows C=0 | D=0 | S=0
      artificial
      priority 15
  step(1)  "Step 2: a singleton club"  alert
      shows C=1, D>=1, S>=1
      artificial
      priority 15
  step(2)  "Step 3: a singleton diamond"  alert
      shows D=1, C>=2, S>=1
      artificial
      priority 15
  step(3)  "Step 4: a singleton spade"  alert
      shows S=1, C>=2, D>=2
      artificial
      priority 15

# The 3♠ ask after 5-4-2-2.
after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3H (P) 3S (X)
  XX  "Business: good spades"
      shows mj_business(S)
      when  M is H
      priority 16
after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3H (P) 3S (3z) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3H (P) 3S (4z)
  X   "Penalty: good {z}"
      shows mj_business(z)
      priority 16
after 1S (P) 2N (P) 3H (P) 3S (*) when !rho.last=P
  P        "Step 1: four clubs"     alert  shows C=4  artificial  priority 15
  step(1)  "Step 2: four diamonds"  alert  shows D=4  artificial  priority 15
  step(2)  "Step 3: four hearts"    alert  shows H=4  artificial  priority 15
after 1H (P) 2N (P) 3H (P) 3S (*) when !rho.last=P
  P        "Step 1: four clubs"     alert  shows C=4  artificial  priority 15
  step(1)  "Step 2: four diamonds"  alert  shows D=4  artificial  priority 15
  step(2)  "Step 3: four spades"    alert  shows S=4  artificial  priority 15

# The 3NT re-ask: where is the void?
after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) 3N (4z)
  X   "Penalty: good {z}"
      shows mj_business(z)
      priority 16
after 1S (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) 3N (*) when !rho.last=P
  P        "Step 1: club void"     alert  shows C=0  artificial  priority 15
  step(1)  "Step 2: diamond void"  alert  shows D=0  artificial  priority 15
  step(2)  "Step 3: heart void"    alert  shows H=0  artificial  priority 15
after 1H (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) 3N (*) when !rho.last=P
  P        "Step 1: club void"     alert  shows C=0  artificial  priority 15
  step(1)  "Step 2: diamond void"  alert  shows D=0  artificial  priority 15
  step(2)  "Step 3: spade void"    alert  shows S=0  artificial  priority 15

# ── Responder: the relays ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Over the minimum (Rick, 2026-11-07): "modified jacoby 2nt is mostly
# useful because responder can jump to game with no slam interest,
# after a 3C rebid by opener. the main advantage is that it doesn't
# give the defenders any clues to opener's distribution. so we don't
# want to always ask. but with say 15+ HCP, responder should probably
# ask." So 3♦ with 15+ HCP, else 4M at once. This overrides the
# double-dummy measurement, which cannot see what the relays tell the
# defenders (notes, "Ask over 3♣ only with 15+").
#
# Over the non-minimum answers (3♦ short, the void) the relays stay
# wide: responder relays whenever slam is possible with everything
# working, his support points and opener's top HCP 27 or more
# (`mj_relay_floor`). Cohen: "If responder still has slam interest, he
# can ask further".
define mj_relay_floor = 27
define mj_try(t) = slam_interest(t) | tp(t) + partner.hcp.max >= mj_relay_floor

after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3C (P)
  3D  "Asks opener to describe the minimum"  alert
      shows hcp >= 15
      sets  ask=mj_relay
      artificial
      priority 15                      # the relay, ahead of the control bids (12-14)
  4M  "Game: no slam interest opposite a minimum"
      shows hcp <= 14
      priority 15                      # Rick 2026-11-07: tell the defenders nothing

after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3D (P)
  3H  "Asks where the singleton or void is"  alert
      shows mj_try(M)
      sets  ask=mj_relay
      artificial
      priority 15

after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3H (P)
  3S  "Asks for opener's four-card side suit"  alert
      shows slam_interest(M)
      sets  ask=mj_relay
      artificial
      priority 15

# ── Opener answers the 3♦ ask (a minimum) ────────────────────────────
after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P)
  3H  "Minimum, a singleton or void"  alert
      shows shortest<=1
      artificial
      priority 15
  3S  "Minimum, 5-4-2-2"  alert
      shows shape 5-4-2-2, M=5
      artificial
      priority 15
  3N  "Minimum, six or more trumps, no singleton or void"  alert
      shows M>=6, shortest>=2
      artificial
      priority 15
  4M  "Minimum, 5-3-3-2"
      shows shape 5-3-3-2, M=5
      priority 15
  4x  "Minimum, a good five-card side suit"
      shows x>=5, quality(x)>=good, shortest>=1
      when  x is not M, M is S | x is not S
      priority 16                      # ahead of a singleton most such hands also hold; a void goes first (3♥)

# The next step asks again (Cohen: "After opener's 3♥ or 3♠ answer to
# 3♦, next step asks, using same schedule"), one step up from the
# non-minimum schedule: over 3♥ (short), 3♠ asks: 3NT a void (4♣ asks
# where: 4♦ clubs, 4♥ diamonds, 4♠ the other major), 4♣/4♦/4♥ a
# singleton club, diamond, other major. Over 3♠ (5-4-2-2), 3NT asks:
# 4♣ clubs, 4♦ diamonds, 4♥ the other major. Over 1♥ the singleton or
# four spades lands on 4♥, the spade void on 4♠: past game, and
# responder still has 4NT.
after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3H (P)
  3S  "Asks where the singleton or void is"  alert
      shows mj_try(M)
      sets  ask=mj_relay
      artificial
      priority 15
# Responder does not make the 3NT ask himself: nothing below reads the
# four-card suit, and relaying cost 53 IMPs on 34 boards against going
# on at once (notes). Opener still answers a partner who asks.
after 1S (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P)
  3N  "A void: 4♣ asks where"  alert   shows C=0 | D=0 | H=0     artificial  priority 15
  4C  "A singleton club"  alert        shows C=1, D>=1, H>=1     artificial  priority 15
  4D  "A singleton diamond"  alert     shows D=1, C>=2, H>=1     artificial  priority 15
  4H  "A singleton heart"  alert       shows H=1, C>=2, D>=2     artificial  priority 15
after 1H (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P)
  3N  "A void: 4♣ asks where"  alert   shows C=0 | D=0 | S=0     artificial  priority 15
  4C  "A singleton club"  alert        shows C=1, D>=1, S>=1     artificial  priority 15
  4D  "A singleton diamond"  alert     shows D=1, C>=2, S>=1     artificial  priority 15
  4H  "A singleton spade"  alert       shows S=1, C>=2, D>=2     artificial  priority 15
after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) 3N (P)
  4C  "Asks where the void is"  alert
      sets  ask=mj_relay
      artificial
      priority 15
after 1S (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) 3N (P) 4C (P)
  4D  "Club void"  alert       shows C=0  artificial  priority 15
  4H  "Diamond void"  alert    shows D=0  artificial  priority 15
  4S  "Heart void"  alert      shows H=0  artificial  priority 15
after 1H (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) 3N (P) 4C (P)
  4D  "Club void"  alert       shows C=0  artificial  priority 15
  4H  "Diamond void"  alert    shows D=0  artificial  priority 15
  4S  "Spade void"  alert      shows S=0  artificial  priority 15
after 1S (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3S (P) 3N (P)
  4C  "Four clubs"  alert      shows C=4  artificial  priority 15
  4D  "Four diamonds"  alert   shows D=4  artificial  priority 15
  4H  "Four hearts"  alert     shows H=4  artificial  priority 15
after 1H (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3S (P) 3N (P)
  4C  "Four clubs"  alert      shows C=4  artificial  priority 15
  4D  "Four diamonds"  alert   shows D=4  artificial  priority 15
  4H  "Four spades"  alert     shows S=4  artificial  priority 15

# ── Opener answers the 3♥ ask (non-minimum, short somewhere) ─────────
# Steps: a void (3♠), then a singleton in clubs, diamonds, the other
# major. After the void, 3NT asks where: clubs, diamonds, the other major.
after 1S (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (P)
  3S  "A void: 3NT asks where"  alert
      shows C=0 | D=0 | H=0
      artificial
      priority 15
  3N  "A singleton club"  alert
      shows C=1, D>=1, H>=1
      artificial
      priority 15
  4C  "A singleton diamond"  alert
      shows D=1, C>=2, H>=1
      artificial
      priority 15
  4D  "A singleton heart"  alert
      shows H=1, C>=2, D>=2
      artificial
      priority 15
after 1H (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (P)
  3S  "A void: 3NT asks where"  alert
      shows C=0 | D=0 | S=0
      artificial
      priority 15
  3N  "A singleton club"  alert
      shows C=1, D>=1, S>=1
      artificial
      priority 15
  4C  "A singleton diamond"  alert
      shows D=1, C>=2, S>=1
      artificial
      priority 15
  4D  "A singleton spade"  alert
      shows S=1, C>=2, D>=2
      artificial
      priority 15

after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P)
  3N  "Asks where the void is"  alert
      shows mj_try(M)
      sets  ask=mj_relay
      artificial
      priority 15
after 1S (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) 3N (P)
  4C  "Club void"  alert       shows C=0  artificial  priority 15
  4D  "Diamond void"  alert    shows D=0  artificial  priority 15
  4H  "Heart void"  alert      shows H=0  artificial  priority 15
after 1H (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) 3N (P)
  4C  "Club void"  alert       shows C=0  artificial  priority 15
  4D  "Diamond void"  alert    shows D=0  artificial  priority 15
  4H  "Spade void"  alert      shows S=0  artificial  priority 15

# ── Opener answers the 3♠ ask (non-minimum, 5-4-2-2) ─────────────────
after 1S (P) 2N (P) 3H (P) 3S (P)
  3N  "Four clubs"  alert      shows C=4  artificial  priority 15
  4C  "Four diamonds"  alert   shows D=4  artificial  priority 15
  4D  "Four hearts"  alert     shows H=4  artificial  priority 15
after 1H (P) 2N (P) 3H (P) 3S (P)
  3N  "Four clubs"  alert      shows C=4  artificial  priority 15
  4C  "Four diamonds"  alert   shows D=4  artificial  priority 15
  4D  "Four spades"  alert     shows S=4  artificial  priority 15

# ── Responder: keycard once the relays have placed opener's shape ────
# (Rick, 2026-11-06, bridge-classroom #83/#84: "ask about south shape
# and learn of spade void then try keycard"; 2026-11-07: "keycard
# should be the stronger hand. the idea of the relays is it will allow
# us to find low HCP slams when there is a good fit.") Once a relay
# answer has placed opener's singleton or void (`shown_short`),
# responder counts his working values (slam-entry.bid, `working_count`:
# support points less the honours wasted opposite the shortness, plus
# opener's floor; `working_slam`, 26). With that, slam: the stronger hand
# by what has been shown (`stronger_hand`: responder's HCP at least
# opener's floor; always opposite a minimum) asks for keycards; the
# weaker, opposite a non-minimum, bids the cheapest suit below game
# ("my values work: you ask") and opener asks. Where there is no room
# below game responder asks himself. Or 14 HCP with an honour in
# opener's good five-card side suit (the 4x answer). Less is left to
# the slam modules (game, mostly). Not after the 5-4-2-2's four-card
# suit: that branch lost 223 IMPs on 46 boards (notes). The keycard
# answers and the placement are rkcb-1430.bid's (blackwood.bid's
# without RKCB). The asks are `mj_relay`, not `relay`: minor-
# transfers.bid's `when answered relay` (pass with clubs) read our
# relays and passed a 4♥ answer.
define mj_slam(t) = working_slam(t)
define mj_side_fits(x) = x is not trump, partner.x >= 5, has(A,x) | has(K,x) | has(Q,x), hcp >= 16
define mj_room = (trump is not C, under_game(C)) | (trump is not D, under_game(D)) | (trump is not H, under_game(H)) | (trump is not S, under_game(S))
define mj_fits = (mj_slam(trump), stronger_hand | !mj_room) | mj_side_fits(C) | mj_side_fits(D) | mj_side_fits(H) | mj_side_fits(S)

when answered mj_relay, we.trump is H | we.trump is S, we.forcing = game
  4N  "Keycard ask in {trump}: opener's shape fits"
      when  rkcb
      shows mj_fits
      sets  ask=keycards(trump)
      artificial
      priority 14
  4N  "Blackwood: opener's shape fits"
      when  bw, !rkcb
      shows mj_fits
      sets  ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 14
  cheapest(C)  "Slam values opposite your shape: you ask"  alert
      shows mj_slam(trump), !stronger_hand
      when  rkcb | bw, trump is not C, under_game(C), shown_short   # public: read only where it can be the signal
      sets  ask=mj_captain
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(C)
      priority 14
  cheapest(D)  "Slam values opposite your shape: you ask"  alert
      shows mj_slam(trump), !stronger_hand
      when  rkcb | bw, trump is not D, under_game(D), shown_short   # public: read only where it can be the signal
      sets  ask=mj_captain
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(D)
      priority 14
  cheapest(H)  "Slam values opposite your shape: you ask"  alert
      shows mj_slam(trump), !stronger_hand
      when  rkcb | bw, trump is not H, under_game(H), shown_short   # public: read only where it can be the signal
      sets  ask=mj_captain
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(H)
      priority 14
  cheapest(S)  "Slam values opposite your shape: you ask"  alert
      shows mj_slam(trump), !stronger_hand
      when  rkcb | bw, trump is not S, under_game(S), shown_short   # public: read only where it can be the signal
      sets  ask=mj_captain
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(S)
      priority 14

# Opener, the stronger hand, asks over responder's "you ask".
when asked mj_captain, we.trump is H | we.trump is S
  4N  "Keycard ask in {trump}: the stronger hand asks"
      when  rkcb
      sets  ask=keycards(trump)
      artificial
      priority 15
  4N  "Blackwood: the stronger hand asks"
      when  bw, !rkcb
      sets  ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 15

# With a side suit open, the asker bids a control instead of asking
# (Rick, 2026-11-10, Bridge-Classroom report: 1H 2N 3D 3H 3NT 4C 4S with
# AK.QJ8653.JT97.A). Past game it is first-round, and only 4♠ over
# hearts: a control above 4NT would take the keycard ask away (five-level
# ones cost 13-26 IMPs on the Jacoby scenarios). A suit skipped is
# denied, so partner goes on only if he covers it. A new suit here has
# no natural meaning, so these do not wait for `bidding_conventions/control_bids`.
when asked mj_captain, we.trump is H | we.trump is S
  cheapest(C)  "Control bid in ♣"  alert
      when  trump is not C, under_game(C)
      when  side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(C)
      sets  ask=control(C), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(C)
      priority 16
  cheapest(D)  "Control bid in ♦"  alert
      when  trump is not D, under_game(D)
      when  side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(D)
      sets  ask=control(D), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(D)
      priority 16
  cheapest(H)  "Control bid in ♥"  alert
      when  trump is not H, under_game(H)
      when  side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(H)
      sets  ask=control(H), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(H)
      priority 16
  cheapest(S)  "Control bid in ♠"  alert
      when  trump is not S, under_game(S)
      when  side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(S)
      sets  ask=control(S), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(S)
      priority 16
  cheapest(S)  "Control bid in ♠: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is H, !under_game(S), !kb_spade_ask
      when  side_suit_uncontrolled, first_round(S)
      sets  ask=control(S), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(S)
      priority 16

# Past game, without the suit partner skipped: back to five of the
# trump suit (control-bids.bid has this when the card plays them).
when asked control(t), !cue, we.trump is H, partner.last = 4S
  5{trump}  "No slam: a suit is open"
      priority -6

# Over 1♥ the spade void is shown with 4♠, past game: without the
# values for keycard, back to five hearts.
after 1H (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) 3N (P) 4C (P) 4S (P)
  5H  "No slam: back to hearts"
      priority 13

# ── Opener after responder declines (Rick, 2026-11-07) ───────────────
# "normally opener doesn't continue for slam exploration after
# responder chooses not to try, unless opener has 19+ points." When
# responder bids 4M over any of opener's answers or relay answers,
# opener passes with 18 points or fewer; with 19+ the slam modules
# decide as before. Above the keycard ask and the control bids.
after 1M (P) 2N (P) 3x (P) 4M (P) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3N (P) 4M (P) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 4x (P) 4M (P) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3x (P) 4M (P) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3N (P) 4M (P) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 4x (P) 4M (P) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) 3N (P) 4x (P) 4M (P) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) 3N (P) 4M (P) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) 4x (P) 4M (P) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3x (P) 4M (P) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3N (P) 4M (P) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 4x (P) 4M (P) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) 3N (P) 4M (P) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) 4x (P) 4M (P) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) 3N (P) 4C (P) 4x (P) 4M (P) | 1M (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3S (P) 3N (P) 4x (P) 4M (P)
  P   "Responder declined: no slam without 19+"
      shows points <= 18
      priority 16
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/multi_2d:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Multi 2♦ (Bridge Bum, "Multi 2D"): an opening 2♦ shows a weak two in
# one of the majors. The strong options (a 4-4-4-1 or a 20-21 notrump,
# Lars Multi) are not written: the card has no field for them and BBA
# opens those hands naturally (probes/multi-openings.toml). With Multi on,
# the natural weak twos are off (preempts.bid): every weak two in a major
# opens 2♦, as BBA does.
#
# Responder bids "pass or correct":
#
#   2♥   happy in 2♥ or 2♠: opener passes with hearts, bids 2♠ with spades
#   2♠   three or more hearts: opener passes with spades, bids 3♥ with hearts
#   2NT  asks: 3♣ maximum hearts, 3♦ maximum spades, 3♥ minimum hearts,
#        3♠ minimum spades
#   3♥   preemptive, three or more in both majors: pass or correct
#   4♦   game: opener bids his major
#   4♥   preemptive game, four or more in both: pass or correct
#   3♣   to play
#
# See multi.notes.md.

module multi "Multi 2♦"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/multi_2d
  needs  preempts
  skill  bidding_conventions/multi_2d

# ── The opening ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The weak two of preempts.bid, either major: 5-10 HCP and a six-card
# suit, vulnerable a good one. A ten-count with the ace-king of the suit,
# or its ace and a side ace, opens at the one level (BBA, as in
# preempts.bid's default).
when opening, seat<=3
  2D  "Multi: a weak two in hearts or spades"   alert
      shows hcp=5..10, (H=6, S<=3, hcp<=9 | !has(A,H) | (!has(K,H), !has(A,S), !has(A,D), !has(A,C))) | (S=6, H<=3, hcp<=9 | !has(A,S) | (!has(K,S), !has(A,H), !has(A,D), !has(A,C)))
      when  !vul | (H=6, quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3) | (S=6, quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3)
      artificial

# ── Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 2D (P) | 2D (X)
  2H  "Pass or correct: no game interest"   alert
      shows hcp<=14
      priority -1
  2S  "Pass or correct: three or more hearts, short spades"   alert
      shows H>=3, S<=2, hcp=6..14
  3H  "Pass or correct, preemptive: three or more in both majors"   alert
      shows H>=3, S>=3, H+S>=8, hcp<=10
  4H  "Pass or correct to game: 4+ in both majors"   alert
      shows H>=4, S>=4, hcp<=12
  4D  "Game: bid your major"   alert
      shows hcp>=15, H>=3, S>=3
      artificial
  3C  "Six or more clubs: to play"
      shows C>=6, H<=2, S<=2, hcp<=14
  2N  "Asks: which major, minimum or maximum?"   alert
      shows hcp>=15
      sets  forcing=round, ask=multi
      artificial

# ── Opener: pass or correct ──────────────────────────────────────────
after 2D (P) 2H (P) | 2D (X) 2H (P)
  P   "My suit is hearts"     shows H=6
  2S  "My suit is spades"     shows S=6
after 2D (P) 2S (P) | 2D (X) 2S (P)
  P   "My suit is spades"     shows S=6
  3H  "My suit is hearts"     shows H=6
after 2D (P) 3H (P) | 2D (X) 3H (P)
  P   "My suit is hearts"     shows H=6
  3S  "My suit is spades"     shows S=6
after 2D (P) 4H (P) | 2D (X) 4H (P)
  P   "My suit is hearts"     shows H=6
  4S  "My suit is spades"     shows S=6
after 2D (P) 4D (P) | 2D (X) 4D (P)
  4H  "My suit is hearts"     shows H=6
  4S  "My suit is spades"     shows S=6
after 2D (P) 3C (P) | 2D (X) 3C (P)
  P   "Partner's suit: to play"

# They come in over the pass-or-correct response: opener passes (the
# auction is theirs; responder may still act).
after 2D (P) 2H (*) | 2D (P) 2S (*)
  P   "No further bid"
      priority -5

# Responder after the correction: the contract is placed.
after 2D (P) 2H (P) 2S (P) | 2D (P) 2S (P) 3H (P) | 2D (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) | 2D (P) 4H (P) 4S (P) | 2D (X) 2H (P) 2S (P) | 2D (X) 2S (P) 3H (P) | 2D (X) 3H (P) 3S (P) | 2D (X) 4H (P) 4S (P)
  P   "Partner's major: to play"

# Opener after the asker's sign-off: pass.
after 2D (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3H (P) | 2D (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) 3S (P)
  P   "No further bid"

# ── Opener answers 2NT ───────────────────────────────────────────────
when asked multi
  3C  "Maximum with hearts: 8-10"   shows H=6, hcp>=8   artificial
  3D  "Maximum with spades: 8-10"   shows S=6, hcp>=8   artificial
  3H  "Minimum with hearts"          shows H=6, hcp<=7
  3S  "Minimum with spades"          shows S=6, hcp<=7

# ── The asker places the contract ────────────────────────────────────
after 2D (P) 2N (P) 3C (P)
  4H  "Game opposite a maximum"   shows H>=2 | hcp>=18
  3H  "No game: sign off"
      priority -1
after 2D (P) 2N (P) 3D (P)
  4S  "Game opposite a maximum"   shows S>=2 | hcp>=18
  3S  "No game: sign off"
      priority -1
after 2D (P) 2N (P) 3H (P)
  4H  "Game opposite a minimum"   shows H>=2, hcp>=18 | (H>=3, hcp>=16)
  P   "No game: play 3♥"
      priority -1
after 2D (P) 2N (P) 3S (P)
  4S  "Game opposite a minimum"   shows S>=2, hcp>=18 | (S>=3, hcp>=16)
  P   "No game: play 3♠"
      priority -1
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/namyats/:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Namyats (Bridge Bum, "Namyats"): 4♣ shows a strong four-level preempt
# in hearts, 4♦ the same in spades: a good seven- or eight-card major and
# eight or nine playing tricks, too good for a plain 4♥/4♠ and not
# strong enough for 2♣. The direct 4♥/4♠ stays the weaker preempt
# (preempts.bid).
#
# Responder: the next step (4♦ over 4♣, 4♥ over 4♦) is a relay with slam
# interest; the major is the sign-off. After the relay opener bids his
# major without a side shortness, or shows a singleton or void.
# See namyats.notes.md.

module namyats "Namyats: 4♣/4♦ strong major preempts"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/namyats
  needs  preempts
  skill  bidding_conventions/namyats

# ── The opening ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Exactly seven cards headed by the ace-king-queen, 9-13 HCP, no side
# ace or king: the hand BBA opens 4♣/4♦ (nine times in the whole corpus,
# all of them this hand, 21GF-GIB; with eight such cards and 9-10 it
# opens 4M, with a side ace or king 1M). Bridge Bum's "8-9 tricks" alone took 1M openings
# (the first version, 10-15 HCP with five losers, changed ~70 boards
# where BBA opened 1M; namyats.notes.md). Ahead of the one-level opening.
when opening, seat<=3
  4C  "Namyats: a strong preempt in hearts, 8-9 tricks"   alert
      shows H=7, has(A,H), has(K,H), has(Q,H), hcp=9..13, S<=3
      shows !has(A,S), !has(K,S), !has(A,D), !has(K,D), !has(A,C), !has(K,C)
      artificial
      priority 1
  4D  "Namyats: a strong preempt in spades, 8-9 tricks"   alert
      shows S=7, has(A,S), has(K,S), has(Q,S), hcp=9..13, H<=3
      shows !has(A,H), !has(K,H), !has(A,D), !has(K,D), !has(A,C), !has(K,C)
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 4C (P) | 4C (X)
  4H  "Sign-off: no slam interest"
      priority -1
  4D  "Relay: slam interest in hearts"   alert
      shows controls>=5 | hcp>=15, quick_tricks>=3
      sets  trump=H, ask=namyats(H)
      artificial
after 4D (P) | 4D (X)
  4S  "Sign-off: no slam interest"
      priority -1
  4H  "Relay: slam interest in spades"   alert
      shows controls>=5 | hcp>=15, quick_tricks>=3
      sets  trump=S, ask=namyats(S)
      artificial

# Opener after the sign-off: pass.
after 4C (P) 4H (P) | 4D (P) 4S (P)
  P   "No further bid"

# ── Opener after the relay ───────────────────────────────────────────
when asked namyats(t)
  4{t}  "No side shortness: back to my suit"
        priority -1
  4S    "A singleton or void in spades"     shows S<=1
        when  t is H
  5C    "A singleton or void in clubs"      shows C<=1
  5D    "A singleton or void in diamonds"   shows D<=1
  5H    "A singleton or void in hearts"     shows H<=1
        when  t is S
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/new_mino:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# New Minor Forcing: after 1m-1M-1NT, two of the other minor is artificial,
# invitational or better, and asks opener about support for responder's
# major (and four cards in the other major). Without it, that bid is natural
# and not forcing (responder-rebids.bid).

module new-minor-forcing "New Minor Forcing"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/new_minor_forcing
  card   after_1nt_rebid
  needs  responder-rebids
  skill  bidding_conventions/new_minor_forcing
  param  checkback = bidding_conventions/checkback default false
  param  roudi = bidding_conventions/roudi default false
  param  twoway = bidding_conventions/two_way_nmf default false
  param  xyz = bidding_conventions/xyz default false

# Checkback, Roudi and two-way NMF each replace NMF when the card has
# both (no PBS card does).
after 1C (P) 1M (P) 1N (P) when !checkback, !roudi, !twoway, !xyz, !tw(C)
  2D  "New Minor Forcing: invitational+, 5+ {M} or both majors"  alert
      shows M>=4, nt_rebid_invite | nt_rebid_game
      sets  forcing=round, ask=nmf
      artificial
      priority 1                       # ahead of a natural 2NT or 3NT
after 1D (P) 1M (P) 1N (P) when !checkback, !roudi, !twoway, !xyz
  2C  "New Minor Forcing: invitational+, 5+ {M} or both majors"  alert
      shows M>=4, nt_rebid_invite | nt_rebid_game
      sets  forcing=round, ask=nmf
      artificial
      priority 1                       # ahead of a natural 2NT or 3NT

# Opener answers: three cards in responder's major first, then four hearts
# after a 1S response (1NT over 1S can hide four hearts; over 1H it denies
# four spades), else notrump by strength.
when asked nmf
  2H  "Three hearts"                       shows H=3        when partner.H>=4
  2S  "Three spades"                       shows S=3        when partner.S>=4
  2H  "Four hearts, not three spades"      shows H>=4, S<=2  when partner.S>=4
  2N  "No fit, minimum"            shows hcp<=shown.hcp.max-1
      priority -1
  3N  "No fit, maximum"               shows hcp>=shown.hcp.max
      priority -1

# Responder places the contract: with a fit, invite (3M) or bid game (4M);
# without one, 2NT invites and 3NT is game.
when answered nmf
  4H  "Game in the heart fit"              shows points+partner.hcp.min>=25, H>=5 | (H>=4, partner.H.min>=4)   when partner.H>=3
  3H  "Invitational, heart fit"            shows points+partner.hcp.min>=23, points+partner.hcp.min<=24, H>=5 | (H>=4, partner.H.min>=4)   when partner.H>=3   sets ask=invite(H)
  4S  "Game in the spade fit"              shows points+partner.hcp.min>=25, S>=5   when partner.S>=3
  3S  "Invitational, spade fit"            shows points+partner.hcp.min>=23, points+partner.hcp.min<=24, S>=5   when partner.S>=3   sets ask=invite(S)
  3N  "Game, no fit"                       shows points+partner.hcp.min>=25
  2N  "Invitational, no fit"               shows points+partner.hcp.min>=23, points+partner.hcp.min<=24   sets ask=nt_invite
  P   "Accepts the notrump game"           when partner.last=3N
  P   "No game: opener is minimum"         shows points+partner.hcp.min<=24   when partner.last=2N
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/pick_a_s:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Pick-a-slam 5NT: a jump to 5NT, not after a keycard ask, says "we
# belong in slam, choose where" (1♠-2♣-3♣-3♠-5NT: 6♣, 6♠ or 6NT).
# Partner bids six of the suit he likes best, or 6NT with no preference.
# Notes: pick-a-slam.notes.md.

module pick-a-slam "Pick-a-slam 5NT: choose among the slams"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/pick_a_slam_5nt
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/pick_a_slam_5nt

# ── The ask ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# A jump (4NT was available), no ask pending (a stopper ask aside), slam values on partner's
# floor (33 total points), and two eight-card fits known, so there is a
# real choice. Without the two fits the keycard ask or a direct slam
# says more.
define pas_fit(x) = we.fit(x).min >= 8
define pas_two_fits = (pas_fit(S), pas_fit(H)) | (pas_fit(S), pas_fit(D)) | (pas_fit(S), pas_fit(C)) | (pas_fit(H), pas_fit(D)) | (pas_fit(H), pas_fit(C)) | (pas_fit(D), pas_fit(C))

when !asked | asked stoppers, partner_bid, partner.last <= 4S, rho.last = P | (rho_bid, rho.last <= 4S)
  5N  "Pick a slam: choose the strain"  alert
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 33, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 30, pas_two_fits
      sets  ask=pick_slam
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── The answer ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Six of the suit where we hold the most cards between us (the
# higher suit on a tie), or 6NT with no eight-card fit of mine to show.
when asked pick_slam
  6S  "Pick a slam: spades"     when we.fit(S).min >= 8   prefer we.fit(S).min   priority 5
  6H  "Pick a slam: hearts"     when we.fit(H).min >= 8   prefer we.fit(H).min   priority 5
  6D  "Pick a slam: diamonds"   when we.fit(D).min >= 8   prefer we.fit(D).min   priority 5
  6C  "Pick a slam: clubs"      when we.fit(C).min >= 8   prefer we.fit(C).min   priority 5
  6N  "Pick a slam: notrump"    priority 4

# The asker accepts partner's choice.
when answered pick_slam
  P   "To play"   priority 5
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/polish_t:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Polish two-suiters (Wikipedia, "Polish Club": "Polish two-suiters,
# 6-11 HCP. Opening 2♥ = any 5-5 with hearts (spades possible). Opening
# 2♠ = 5 spades and 5 of a minor"). The natural weak 2♥/2♠ are off
# (preempts.bid). Responder:
#
#   over 2♥  pass to play; 2♠ pass or correct (opener passes with
#            spades, else bids his minor); 2NT asks (3♥ = spades,
#            3♣/3♦ = that minor); 3♥ preemptive; 4♥ to play
#   over 2♠  pass to play; 3♣ pass or correct to the minor; 2NT asks
#            (3♣/3♦); 3♠ preemptive; 4♠ to play
#
# Ranges and responder's choices follow BBA (probes/polish-openings.toml,
# polish-resp-2H.toml, polish-resp-2S.toml). See
# polish-two-suiters.notes.md.

module polish-two-suiters "Polish two-suiters: 2♥ and 2♠"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/polish_two_suiters
  needs  preempts
  skill  bidding_conventions/polish_two_suiters

# ── The openings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
when opening, seat<=3
  2H  "Polish: five hearts and another five-card suit, 5-11"   alert
      shows H>=5, S>=5 | D>=5 | C>=5, hcp=5..11
      priority 1
  2S  "Polish: five spades and a five-card minor, 5-11"   alert
      shows S>=5, H<=4, D>=5 | C>=5, hcp=5..11
      priority 1

# ── Responder to 2♥ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 2H (P) | 2H (X)
  P   "Hearts: to play"                        shows H>=3, hcp<=14
  2S  "Pass or correct: no heart fit"   alert  shows H<=2, hcp<=14
      artificial
  3H  "Preemptive raise: four or more hearts"  shows H>=4, hcp<=9
  4H  "Game in hearts"                         shows H>=3, hcp>=15
      priority 1
  2N  "Asks for the second suit: game interest"   alert
      shows hcp>=15
      sets  forcing=round, ask=polish(H)
      artificial

# ── Responder to 2♠ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 2S (P) | 2S (X)
  P   "Spades: to play"                        shows S>=2, hcp<=14
  3C  "Pass or correct: no spade fit"   alert  shows S<=1, hcp<=14
      artificial
  3S  "Preemptive raise: four or more spades"  shows S>=4, hcp<=9
  4S  "Game in spades"                         shows S>=3, hcp>=15
      priority 1
  2N  "Asks for the minor: game interest"   alert
      shows hcp>=15
      sets  forcing=round, ask=polish(S)
      artificial

# ── Opener: pass or correct ──────────────────────────────────────────
after 2H (P) 2S (P) | 2H (X) 2S (P)
  P   "My second suit is spades"     shows S>=5
  3C  "My second suit is clubs"      shows C>=5
  3D  "My second suit is diamonds"   shows D>=5
after 2S (P) 3C (P) | 2S (X) 3C (P)
  P   "My minor is clubs"            shows C>=5
  3D  "My minor is diamonds"         shows D>=5
after 2H (P) 3H (P) | 2S (P) 3S (P) | 2H (P) 4H (P) | 2S (P) 4S (P)
  P   "No further bid"

# Responder after the correction to a minor: pass.
after 2H (P) 2S (P) 3x (P) | 2S (P) 3C (P) 3D (P)
  P   "Partner's suit: to play"

# ── Opener answers 2NT ───────────────────────────────────────────────
when asked polish(t)
  3C  "My second suit is clubs"      shows C>=5
  3D  "My second suit is diamonds"   shows D>=5
  3H  "My second suit is spades"     shows S>=5
      when  t is H
      artificial

# ── The asker places the contract ────────────────────────────────────
when answered polish(t)
  4{t}  "Game in the major"                     shows t>=3
        priority 1
  4S    "Game in spades: opener's second suit"  shows S>=3
        when  t is H, partner.last=3H
        priority 2
  3N    "Game in notrump"                        shows hcp>=16
  5C    "Game in clubs"                          shows C>=3
        when  partner.last=3C
  5D    "Game in diamonds"                       shows D>=3
        when  partner.last=3D
        priority -1
files.conventions/bidding_conventions/precisio:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Precision 2♦ (Bridge Bum, "Precision 2D"): 11-15 HCP, short in
# diamonds, 4-4-1-4 or 4-4-0-5; 4-3-1-5 or 3-4-1-5 when the clubs are
# too weak for a Precision 2♣ (here: fewer than two of the top three).
# Written as an opening on its own; it does not need the forcing 1♣.
# The weak 2♦ is off (preempts.bid).
#
# Responder:
#
#   Pass        six or more diamonds, no interest in the other suits
#   2♥ 2♠ 3♣    natural, sign-off
#   2NT         11+, game forcing, asks:
#               3♣ 3-4-1-5   3♦ 4-3-1-5
#               3♥ 4-4-1-4 11-13   3♠ 4-4-1-4 14-15
#               3NT 4-4-1-4 14-15 with the ♦A or ♦K
#               4♣ 4-4-0-5 11-13   4♦ 4-4-0-5 14-15
#   3♦          six or more diamonds, invites 3NT
#   3♥ 3♠       preemptive
#
# Responder's rebids are natural. See precision-2d.notes.md.

module precision-2d "Precision 2♦"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/precision_2d
  needs  preempts
  skill  bidding_conventions/precision_2d

define prec_2d_shape = (S=4, H=4, D=1, C=4) | (S=4, H=4, D=0, C=5) | (S=4, H=3, D=1, C=5, quality(C)<=fair) | (S=3, H=4, D=1, C=5, quality(C)<=fair)

# ── The opening ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Priority 1: it takes these hands from the one-level openings.
when opening
  2D  "Precision 2♦: 11-15, short diamonds"   alert
      shows hcp=11..15, prec_2d_shape
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 2D (P) | 2D (X)
  2N  "Asks for shape and strength: 11+, game forcing"   alert
      shows hcp>=11
      sets  forcing=game, ask=precision_2d
      artificial
  P   "Six or more diamonds: to play"     shows D>=6, hcp<=10
      priority 1
  3D  "Six or more diamonds: invites 3NT"   shows D>=6, hcp=9..10, quality(D)>=good
      priority 1
  3H  "Preemptive: six or more hearts"    shows H>=6, hcp<=8
  3S  "Preemptive: six or more spades"    shows S>=6, hcp<=8
  2S  "Sign-off"                          shows S>=3, S>H, hcp<=10
  2H  "Sign-off"                          shows H>=3, hcp<=10
  3C  "Sign-off"                          shows C>=4, hcp<=10, S<=2, H<=2
  # The best of a bad lot.
  2H  "Sign-off"   shows hcp<=10
      priority -2

# Opener passes the sign-offs.
after 2D (P) 2H (P) | 2D (P) 2S (P) | 2D (P) 3C (P) | 2D (P) 3H (P) | 2D (P) 3S (P) | 2D (X) 2H (P) | 2D (X) 2S (P) | 2D (X) 3C (P)
  P   "No further bid"
# The invitation: 3NT with a maximum and the diamond singleton an honour.
after 2D (P) 3D (P)
  3N  "Accepts: 14-15"     shows hcp>=14
  P   "Declines"
      priority -1

# ── Opener answers 2NT ───────────────────────────────────────────────
when asked precision_2d
  3C  "3-4-1-5"                       shows S=3, H=4, C=5
  3D  "4-3-1-5"                       shows S=4, H=3, C=5
  3H  "4-4-1-4, 11-13"                shows S=4, H=4, D=1, hcp<=13
  3S  "4-4-1-4, 14-15"                shows S=4, H=4, D=1, hcp>=14
  3N  "4-4-1-4, 14-15, the ♦A or ♦K"  shows S=4, H=4, D=1, hcp>=14, has(A,D) | has(K,D)
      priority 1
  4C  "4-4-0-5, 11-13"                shows S=4, H=4, D=0, hcp<=13
  4D  "4-4-0-5, 14-15"                shows S=4, H=4, D=0, hcp>=14

# ── Responder places the contract ────────────────────────────────────
# Opener's shape is known: game in a major with a 4-4 fit (or five
# opposite three), 3NT with diamonds held, else five clubs.
after 2D (P) 2N (P) 3x (P) | 2D (P) 2N (P) 4x (P) | 2D (P) 2N (P) 3N (P)
