# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Wolff sign-off (Rick, 2026-09-30: "there is a convention where 3C there
# is to stop in part score"). After 1x-1y-2NT (18-19), responder's 3C
# asks opener to bid 3D; responder passes with diamonds or signs off in
# his major. Every other call but pass forces to game (game-force.bid).

module wolff "Wolff sign-off after opener's 2NT rebid"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/wolff_signoff
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/wolff_signoff

after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2N (P) when !tw(x)
  3C  "Wolff: relay to 3♦, to sign off"   alert
      shows points<=6, D>=6 | (y>=6, y is H) | (y>=6, y is S)
      when  y is not C
      sets  ask=wolff
      artificial
      priority 1

when asked wolff
  3D  "Wolff: the forced 3♦"   alert
      artificial

when answered wolff, partner.last=3D
  P   "To play in 3♦"                  shows D>=6
  3y  "To play in {y}"                 shows y>=6
      when  y is H | y is S
files.conventions/competitive_bidding/dont/don:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# DONT (Disturb Opponents' No Trump, Marty Bergen) over their 1NT, direct
# and balancing (vs-1nt.notes.md has the sources).
#
#   X    one long suit, six or more, not spades: partner relays 2♣
#   2♣   clubs and a higher suit, 5-4 either way
#   2♦   diamonds and a major, 5-4 either way
#   2♥   hearts and spades, 5-4 either way
#   2♠   six or more spades, one-suited
#
# DONT is meant to be light: shape before points. We count HCP plus a
# point a card beyond four in each suit and ask for 10 (8 HCP with a
# six-card suit or 5-5, 9 with 5-4), with a 15 HCP ceiling: DONT has no
# penalty double, and a stronger hand passes and comes in later. There
# is no BBA reference (BBA has no DONT; scenario DONT is bba-works:
# false).
#
# It is on when DONT is the convention the card plays for
# `defence_to_1nt.strong`.

module dont "DONT over their 1NT"
  kind   convention
  convention  competitive_bidding/dont
  needs  vs-1nt
  skill  competitive_bidding/dont
  skill  competitive_bidding/defense_vs_1nt
  param  def = defence_to_1nt.strong

# The ceiling: 15 HCP, or 19 with a shapely hand (5-5 or longer, or a
# seven-card suit). 2026-10-05, the self A/B against the card's default
# defence: 16-19 with 6-5 passed "to wait" and partner passed it out,
# about -100 IMPs on DONT's own deals. A balanced or 5-4 strong hand
# still passes.
define dont_strength = hcp<=15 | (hcp<=19, longest+second_longest>=10 | longest>=7)

after (1N) | (1N) P (P) when def is competitive_bidding/dont
  X   "DONT: one long suit, not spades"   alert
      shows (C>=6 | D>=6 | H>=6), second_longest<=3, hcp+length_points>=10, dont_strength
      sets  ask=dont_one
  2C  "DONT: clubs and a higher suit"            alert
      shows (C>=5, (D>=4 | H>=4 | S>=4)) | (C>=4, (D>=5 | H>=5 | S>=5))
      shows hcp+length_points>=10, dont_strength
      sets  ask=nt_pc(C)
  2D  "DONT: diamonds and a major"               alert
      shows (D>=5, (H>=4 | S>=4)) | (D>=4, (H>=5 | S>=5))
      shows hcp+length_points>=10, dont_strength
      sets  ask=nt_pc(D)
  2H  "DONT: hearts and spades"                  alert
      shows H>=4, S>=4, H+S>=9, hcp+length_points>=10, dont_strength
      sets  ask=nt_majors
  2S  "DONT: six or more spades"
      shows S>=6, second_longest<=4, hcp+length_points>=10, dont_strength
      sets  ask=nt_one(S)

# Advancer over the double: 2♣ asks for the suit (partner passes with
# clubs); a six-card suit of my own is to play.
when asked dont_one, rho.last=P | rho.last=X | rho.last=XX
  2C  "Relay: bid your suit"                      alert
      sets  ask=dont_relay
  2D  "Six or more diamonds: to play"             shows D>=6
  2H  "Six or more hearts: to play"               shows H>=6
  2S  "Six or more spades: to play"               shows S>=6

when asked dont_relay, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P   "My suit is clubs"                          shows C>=6
  2D  "My suit is diamonds"                       shows D>=6
      sets  ask=nt_one(D)
  2H  "My suit is hearts"                         shows H>=6
      sets  ask=nt_one(H)
files.conventions/competitive_bidding/fit_show:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Fit-showing jumps (`competitive.fit_showing_jumps.play`): a jump in a
# new suit by a hand that has a fit for partner shows four or more of
# partner's suit, a five-card side suit with a top honour, and about a
# limit raise (Todd, "Fit-Showing Jumps"; Robinson in "25 More Bridge
# Conventions You Should Know", ch. 14). Partner then judges the double
# fit: honours in the side suit work, shortness there does not.
#
# Where they apply here (fit-showing-jumps.notes.md):
#
# - a passed hand's jump shift over partner's opening, with or without
#   an overcall on the right (the scenario Fit_Showing_Jumps);
# - responder's jump shift over their takeout double (Fit_Jumps_after_
#   1M_Double; BBA plays them there on the 21GF-GIB card);
# - advancer's jump shift after partner's overcall.
#
# An unpassed responder's jump shift over their *overcall* is not one:
# the card has its own field for it (`competitive.jump_shift_after_
# overcall`, after-interference.bid).

module fit-showing-jumps "Fit-showing jumps"
  kind   convention
  convention  competitive_bidding/fit_showing_jumps
  needs  base
  needs  overcalls
  skill  competitive_bidding/fit_showing_jumps

# ── A passed hand's jump shift ───────────────────────────────────────
# 10-12 support points (a passed hand), four of partner's suit, five of
# the side suit with an ace, king or queen.
after 1x (P) | 1x (X) | 1x (1N) when passed_hand
  jump(S) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {x}, 5+ ♠ with an honour, 10-12"  alert
      shows x>=4, S>=5, quality(S)>=fair, hcp+length_points=10..12, hcp<=11
      when  x is not S
      sets  trump=x, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(x)
      priority 2
  jump(H) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {x}, 5+ ♥ with an honour, 10-12"  alert
      shows x>=4, H>=5, quality(H)>=fair, hcp+length_points=10..12, hcp<=11
      when  x is not H
      sets  trump=x, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(x)
      priority 2
  jump(D) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {x}, 5+ ♦ with an honour, 10-12"  alert
      shows x>=4, D>=5, quality(D)>=fair, hcp+length_points=10..12, hcp<=11
      when  x is not D
      sets  trump=x, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(x)
      priority 2
  jump(C) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {x}, 5+ ♣ with an honour, 10-12"  alert
      shows x>=4, C>=5, quality(C)>=fair, hcp+length_points=10..12, hcp<=11
      when  x is not C
      sets  trump=x, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(x)
      priority 2
after 1x (1y) | 1x (2y) when passed_hand, y is not x
  jump(S) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {x}, 5+ ♠ with an honour, 10-12"  alert
      shows x>=4, S>=5, quality(S)>=fair, hcp+length_points=10..12, hcp<=11
      when  x is not S, y is not S
      sets  trump=x, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(x)
      priority 2
  jump(H) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {x}, 5+ ♥ with an honour, 10-12"  alert
      shows x>=4, H>=5, quality(H)>=fair, hcp+length_points=10..12, hcp<=11
      when  x is not H, y is not H
      sets  trump=x, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(x)
      priority 2
  jump(D) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {x}, 5+ ♦ with an honour, 10-12"  alert
      shows x>=4, D>=5, quality(D)>=fair, hcp+length_points=10..12, hcp<=11
      when  x is not D, y is not D
      sets  trump=x, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(x)
      priority 2
  jump(C) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {x}, 5+ ♣ with an honour, 10-12"  alert
      shows x>=4, C>=5, quality(C)>=fair, hcp+length_points=10..12, hcp<=11
      when  x is not C, y is not C
      sets  trump=x, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(x)
      priority 2

# ── Responder over their takeout double ──────────────────────────────
# A limit raise or better with the side suit: it replaces the redouble
# or the Jordan 2NT for this shape.
after 1x (X) when !passed_hand
  jump(S) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {x}, 5+ ♠ with an honour, 10+"  alert
      shows x>=4, S>=5, quality(S)>=fair, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not S
      sets  trump=x, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(x)
      priority 2
  jump(H) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {x}, 5+ ♥ with an honour, 10+"  alert
      shows x>=4, H>=5, quality(H)>=fair, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not H
      sets  trump=x, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(x)
      priority 2
  jump(D) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {x}, 5+ ♦ with an honour, 10+"  alert
      shows x>=4, D>=5, quality(D)>=fair, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not D
      sets  trump=x, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(x)
      priority 2
  jump(C) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {x}, 5+ ♣ with an honour, 10+"  alert
      shows x>=4, C>=5, quality(C)>=fair, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not C
      sets  trump=x, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(x)
      priority 2

# ── Advancer after partner's one-level overcall ──────────────────────
# Partner's overcall is five cards, so four-card support is nine trumps.
# Forcing one round; a passed advancer is limited to 12.
after (1x) 1y (P) | (1x) 1y (X) | (1x) P (P) 1y (P)
  jump(S) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {y}, 5+ ♠ with an honour, 10+"  alert
      shows y>=4, S>=5, quality(S)>=fair, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not S, y is not S
      when  !passed_hand | hcp<=11
      sets  trump=y, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(y)
      priority 2
  jump(H) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {y}, 5+ ♥ with an honour, 10+"  alert
      shows y>=4, H>=5, quality(H)>=fair, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not H, y is not H
      when  !passed_hand | hcp<=11
      sets  trump=y, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(y)
      priority 2
  jump(D) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {y}, 5+ ♦ with an honour, 10+"  alert
      shows y>=4, D>=5, quality(D)>=fair, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not D, y is not D
      when  !passed_hand | hcp<=11
      sets  trump=y, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(y)
      priority 2
  jump(C) "Fit-showing jump: 4+ {y}, 5+ ♣ with an honour, 10+"  alert
      shows y>=4, C>=5, quality(C)>=fair, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not C, y is not C
      when  !passed_hand | hcp<=11
      sets  trump=y, forcing=round, ask=fit_jump(y)
      priority 2

# ── Partner judges the double fit ────────────────────────────────────
# Opener (or the overcaller) counts the side suit: an honour there, or
# length, makes the hands fit; a singleton or void there is wasted
# opposite partner's length. Game with a fitting maximum, else the
# cheapest bid in the trump suit, which partner passes.
#
# In a major the jump is at least a limit raise with four trumps, so
# opener accepts it as he accepts Jordan's 2NT (14+ total points), and
# with 12+ when the side suit fits (2026-10-09: with HCP alone opener
# signed off on 5-5 hands opposite the over-double jump, where the off
# auction 1M (X) 2NT reached a making game; notes).
# In a minor a passed hand's 10-12 needs more: four of the side suit
# when it is a major and three cards there make the major the game;
# 3NT needs 16+ with the side suit covered (a balanced 1m opener is
# 12-14 or 18-19, so in practice the strong notrump hand), or 18+ with
# any shape (2026-10-09: 14 balanced bid 3NT opposite 8-11 HCP).
after 1x (P) 2z (P) | 1x (P) 3z (P) | 1x (X) 2z (P) | 1x (X) 3z (P) | 1x (1y) 2z (P) | 1x (1y) 3z (P) | 1x (2y) 2z (P) | 1x (2y) 3z (P) | (1y) 1x (P) 2z (P) | (1y) 1x (P) 3z (P) | (1y) 1x (X) 2z (P) | (1y) 1x (X) 3z (P) | (1y) P (P) 1x (P) 2z (P) | (1y) P (P) 1x (P) 3z (P) when asked fit_jump(t), z is not t
  4{t} "Game: 14+ total points, or 12+ with a fit in {z}"
      shows tp(t)>=14 | (hcp>=12, z>=3 | quality(z)>=fair, z>=2)
      when  t is H | t is S
      priority 2
  4{z} "Game in {z}: three or more, 14+ total points"
      shows z>=3, tp(z)>=14
      when  t is C | t is D, z is H | z is S
      priority 3
  3N  "Game in notrump: 16+ with {z} covered, or 18+"
      shows (hcp>=16, z>=2, balanced) | hcp>=18
      when  t is C | t is D
      priority 2
  5{t} "Game in {t}: 16+, a fit in {z}"
      shows hcp>=16, z>=3 | quality(z)>=fair, !balanced
      when  t is C | t is D
      priority 2
  cheapest(t) "No game: sign off in {t}"
      priority 1

# ── The jumper after partner's sign-off ──────────────────────────────
# The jump described the hand; partner has judged. Pass, unless an
# unlimited jump (over their double, or advancer's) holds 13+ for game
# in a major. The pass outranks the base rules' rebids after a two-over-
# one (2026-10-09: 1D-2H-3D read as a two-over-one, and the passed hand
# bid 3NT over the sign-off).
after 1x (P) 2z (P) 3x (P) | 1x (P) 3z (P) 3x (P) | 1x (P) 3z (P) 4x (P) | 1x (X) 2z (P) 3x (P) | 1x (X) 3z (P) 3x (P) | 1x (X) 3z (P) 4x (P) | 1x (1y) 2z (P) 3x (P) | 1x (1y) 3z (P) 3x (P) | 1x (1y) 3z (P) 4x (P) | 1x (2y) 3z (P) 3x (P) | 1x (2y) 3z (P) 4x (P) | (1y) 1x (P) 2z (P) 3x (P) | (1y) 1x (P) 3z (P) 3x (P) | (1y) 1x (P) 3z (P) 4x (P) when answered fit_jump(x), z is not x
  4{x} "Game: 13+"                 shows hcp+length_points>=13
      when  x is H | x is S, !passed_hand
      priority 4
  P   "No further bid"               priority 3
files.conventions/competitive_bidding/ghestem/:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Ghestem (`competitive.ghestem.play`; Wikipedia, "Ghestem"): over their
# one-level opening on our right, three two-suited overcalls, each naming
# one pair of the three unbid suits, five-five or longer:
#
# - 2NT: the two lowest unbid suits (the Unusual 2NT of
#   two-suited-overcalls.bid, which this switch also turns on);
# - 3♣: the two highest unbid suits (over 1♣ it is the jump cue bid);
# - the cue bid: the highest and the lowest unbid suits.
#
#   over 1♣: 2NT ♦+♥, 3♣ ♥+♠, 2♣ ♦+♠
#   over 1♦: 2NT ♣+♥, 3♣ ♥+♠, 2♦ ♣+♠
#   over 1♥: 2NT ♣+♦, 3♣ ♦+♠, 2♥ ♣+♠
#   over 1♠: 2NT ♣+♦, 3♣ ♦+♥, 2♠ ♣+♥
#
# It replaces Michaels over a one-level opening (two-suited-overcalls.bid
# steps aside when the card plays Ghestem). Strength as our Michaels:
# 9+ total points, 11+ vulnerable, up to 17 HCP (stronger hands double
# first). The natural 3♣ jump overcall is lost (Wikipedia's first
# disadvantage). Advancer: preference for the longer of partner's suits
# at the cheapest level, the jump in a major to invite, game in a major
# with a fit and an opening hand. After the cue bid of a major
# the Michaels advances of two-suited-overcalls.bid apply (they read
# partner's shown major). Notes: ghestem.notes.md.

module ghestem "Ghestem two-suited overcalls"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  needs  two-suited-overcalls
  skill  competitive_bidding/ghestem
  convention  competitive_bidding/ghestem

after (1C)
  2C  "Ghestem: five or more diamonds and spades"
      alert
      shows D>=5, S>=5, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp<=17
      when  !vul
      priority 1
  2C  "Ghestem: five or more diamonds and spades"
      alert
      shows D>=5, S>=5, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      when  vul
      priority 1
  3C  "Ghestem: five or more hearts and spades"
      alert
      shows H>=5, S>=5, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp<=17
      when  !vul
      priority 1
  3C  "Ghestem: five or more hearts and spades"
      alert
      shows H>=5, S>=5, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      when  vul
      priority 1

after (1D)
  2D  "Ghestem: five or more clubs and spades"
      alert
      shows C>=5, S>=5, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp<=17
      when  !vul
      priority 1
  2D  "Ghestem: five or more clubs and spades"
      alert
      shows C>=5, S>=5, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      when  vul
      priority 1
  3C  "Ghestem: five or more hearts and spades"
      alert
      shows H>=5, S>=5, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp<=17
      when  !vul
      priority 1
  3C  "Ghestem: five or more hearts and spades"
      alert
      shows H>=5, S>=5, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      when  vul
      priority 1

after (1H)
  2H  "Ghestem: five or more clubs and spades"
      alert
      shows C>=5, S>=5, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp<=17
      when  !vul
      priority 1
  2H  "Ghestem: five or more clubs and spades"
      alert
      shows C>=5, S>=5, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      when  vul
      priority 1
  3C  "Ghestem: five or more diamonds and spades"
      alert
      shows D>=5, S>=5, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp<=17
      when  !vul
      priority 1
  3C  "Ghestem: five or more diamonds and spades"
      alert
      shows D>=5, S>=5, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      when  vul
      priority 1

after (1S)
  2S  "Ghestem: five or more clubs and hearts"
      alert
      shows C>=5, H>=5, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp<=17
      when  !vul
      priority 1
  2S  "Ghestem: five or more clubs and hearts"
      alert
      shows C>=5, H>=5, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      when  vul
      priority 1
  3C  "Ghestem: five or more diamonds and hearts"
      alert
      shows D>=5, H>=5, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp<=17
      when  !vul
      priority 1
  3C  "Ghestem: five or more diamonds and hearts"
      alert
      shows D>=5, H>=5, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      when  vul
      priority 1

# ── Advancer ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# After the cue bid of a minor and after 3♣ (the cue bid of a major is
# advanced as Michaels, above). Partner's two suits are known.
after (1m) 2m (P) | (1m) 2m (X) | (1x) 3C (P) | (1x) 3C (X)
  4S  "Game: three or more spades, 12+"
      shows S>=3, S>=H, hcp+length_points>=12
      when  partner.S>=5
      priority 3
  4H  "Game: three or more hearts, 12+"
      shows H>=3, hcp+length_points>=12
      when  partner.H>=5
      priority 3
  jump(S) "Invitational: four or more spades, 10-11"
      shows S>=4, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp+length_points<=11
      when  partner.S>=5, cheapest_rank(S) <= 13
      priority 2
  jump(H) "Invitational: four or more hearts, 10-11"
      shows H>=4, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp+length_points<=11
      when  partner.H>=5, cheapest_rank(H) <= 13
      priority 2
  cheapest(S) "Preference: spades"
      prefer S + 0
      when  partner.S>=5
      priority 1
  cheapest(H) "Preference: hearts"
      prefer H + 0
      when  partner.H>=5
      priority 1
  cheapest(D) "Preference: diamonds"
      prefer D + 0
      when  partner.D>=5
      priority 1
  cheapest(C) "Preference: clubs"
      prefer C + 0
      when  partner.C>=5
      priority 1
files.conventions/competitive_bidding/lead_dir:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Lead-directing doubles (`competitive.lead_directing_double.play`;
# convention-card competitive_bidding/lead_directing_doubles; Bridge
# Bum, "Lead Directing Double"; PBS btn/Lead_Directing_Double.btn):
# a double of an artificial bid asks partner to lead that suit. The
# hand: five cards with three of the top five honours, or six with two
# of the top three (the scenario's standard; Bridge Bum: a good suit).
#
# Written for the artificial bids the engine marks as such (`!rho.named(x)`:
# RHO has not bid the suit naturally), when it is RHO's call and our
# side has not bid:
#
# - responder's artificial bids over their 1NT or 2NT opening (Stayman,
#   transfers, minor-suit and other relays);
# - the 2♦ response to their strong 2♣;
# - an answer to their 4NT (keycard or ace ask).
#
# Not written: the Lightner double of a slam, doubles of their cue bids
# and of control bids (the engine marks few of those artificial), and
# the opening leader's actual lead (the engine does not play the cards).
# Notes: lead-directing-doubles.notes.md.

module lead-directing-doubles "Lead-directing doubles of artificial bids"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  skill  competitive_bidding/lead_directing_doubles
  convention  competitive_bidding/lead_directing_doubles

define ldd_suit(x) = x>=5, top5(x)>=3 | (x>=6, quality(x)>=good)

after (1N) P (2x) | (1N) P (3x) | (2N) P (3x) | (4N) P (5x) when !rho.named(x)
  X   "Lead-directing: a good {x} suit, lead it"
      alert
      shows ldd_suit(x)
      priority 1
after (2C) P (2D) when !rho.named(D)
  X   "Lead-directing: a good diamond suit, lead it"
      alert
      shows ldd_suit(D)
      priority 1
files.conventions/competitive_bidding/lebensoh:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Lebensohl after a natural two-level overcall of our 1NT (2♦, 2♥, 2♠),
# "slow shows" (Larry Cohen, "Lebensohl"; lebensohl.notes.md):
#
# - two of a suit: natural, to play (nt-interference.bid);
# - 2NT: a relay to 3♣. Then pass or a suit below theirs is to play, a
#   suit above theirs invites, their suit is Stayman with a stopper and
#   3NT is game with a stopper;
# - a new suit at the three level directly: natural, forcing to game;
# - their suit directly: Stayman without a stopper;
# - 3NT directly: game without a stopper.
#
# The double stays what the card says it is (nt-interference.bid), and
# so do the calls over their 2♣, their double and their conventional
# two-suited overcalls: Lebensohl reads only a natural overcall.

module lebensohl "Lebensohl after they overcall our 1NT"
  kind   convention
  convention  competitive_bidding/lebensohl
  card   over_1nt_interference
  needs  nt-interference
  skill  competitive_bidding/lebensohl
  param  rub = competitive_bidding/rubensohl:over_1nt_interference default false

# Responder. The context is the natural-overcall one of nt-interference.bid.
after 1N (2y) when y is not C, rho.y>=4, (maybe rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3), !rub
  # Game values with four of an unbid major: Stayman, fast without a
  # stopper, slow (through 2NT) with one. Ahead of the negative double.
  3y  "Stayman, no stopper in {y}: a four-card major"  alert
      shows hcp>=10, !stop(y), H=4 | S=4, H<=4, S<=4
      when  y is D
      sets  forcing=game
      artificial
      priority 2
  3y  "Stayman, no stopper in {y}: four spades"  alert
      shows hcp>=10, !stop(y), S=4
      when  y is H
      sets  forcing=game
      artificial
      priority 2
  3y  "Stayman, no stopper in {y}: four hearts"  alert
      shows hcp>=10, !stop(y), H=4
      when  y is S
      sets  forcing=game
      artificial
      priority 2
  2N  "Lebensohl: relays to 3♣, then Stayman with a stopper in {y}"  alert
      shows hcp>=10, stop(y), H=4 | S=4, H<=4, S<=4
      when  y is D
      sets  ask=leb_relay
      artificial
      priority 2
  2N  "Lebensohl: relays to 3♣, then Stayman with a stopper in {y}"  alert
      shows hcp>=10, stop(y), S=4
      when  y is H
      sets  ask=leb_relay
      artificial
      priority 2
  2N  "Lebensohl: relays to 3♣, then Stayman with a stopper in {y}"  alert
      shows hcp>=10, stop(y), H=4, S<=4
      when  y is S
      sets  ask=leb_relay
      artificial
      priority 2
  # Game in notrump: fast denies a stopper, slow shows one.
  3N  "Game: 10+ HCP, no stopper in {y}"        shows hcp>=10, !stop(y)
  2N  "Lebensohl: relays to 3♣, then 3NT with a stopper in {y}"  alert
      shows hcp>=10, stop(y)
      sets  ask=leb_relay
      artificial
  # Weak with a long suit that cannot be bid at the two level: through
  # 2NT, to sign off at three.
  2N  "Lebensohl: relays to 3♣, to play three of a long minor"  alert
      shows hcp>=4, points<=9, C>=6 | D>=6, H<=4, S<=4
      when  y is not D
      sets  ask=leb_relay
      artificial
  2N  "Lebensohl: relays to 3♣, to play three clubs"  alert
      shows hcp>=4, points<=9, C>=6, H<=4, S<=4
      when  y is D
      sets  ask=leb_relay
      artificial
  2N  "Lebensohl: relays to 3♣, to play three hearts"  alert
      shows hcp>=4, points<=9, H>=5, H>=S
      when  y is S
      sets  ask=leb_relay
      artificial
      priority -1                        # the negative double first (5 hearts, weak)
  # Invitational with a five-card major above their suit: through 2NT,
  # then three of the major.
  2N  "Lebensohl: relays to 3♣, then invites in spades"  alert
      shows S>=5, S>=H, hcp=8..9
      when  y is D | y is H
      sets  ask=leb_relay
      artificial
      priority 1                         # ahead of the natural two of the suit
  2N  "Lebensohl: relays to 3♣, then invites in hearts"  alert
      shows H>=5, H>S, hcp=8..9
      when  y is D
      sets  ask=leb_relay
      artificial
      priority 1
  # A jump to three of a major is natural and forcing to game (the
  # non-jump new suits are in nt-interference.bid).
  3S  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more spades"   shows S>=5, S>=H, points>=10
      when  y is D | y is H
      sets  forcing=game
  3H  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more hearts"   shows H>=5, H>S, points>=10
      when  y is D
      sets  forcing=game

# Opener: the relay is forced.
after 1N (2y) 2N (P) when y is not C, lho.y>=4, (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3), !rub
  3C  "Completes the Lebensohl relay"  alert
      artificial

# Responder after the relay.
after 1N (2y) 2N (P) 3C (P) when y is not C, rho.y>=4, (maybe rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3), !rub
  P   "To play: clubs"                           shows C>=6, points<=9
  3D  "To play: diamonds"                        shows D>=6, points<=9
      when  y is not D
  3H  "To play: hearts"                          shows H>=5, points<=9
      when  y is S
  3H  "Invitational: five or more hearts"        shows H>=5, hcp=8..9
      when  y is D
      sets  ask=leb_invite(H)
  3S  "Invitational: five or more spades"        shows S>=5, hcp=8..9
      when  y is D | y is H
      sets  ask=leb_invite(S)
  3y  "Stayman, a stopper in {y}: a four-card major"  alert
      shows hcp>=10, stop(y), H=4 | S=4, H<=4, S<=4
      when  y is D
      sets  forcing=game
      artificial
      priority 1                                 # ahead of 3NT with the major
  3y  "Stayman, a stopper in {y}: four spades"  alert
      shows hcp>=10, stop(y), S=4
      when  y is H
      sets  forcing=game
      artificial
      priority 1
  3y  "Stayman, a stopper in {y}: four hearts"  alert
      shows hcp>=10, stop(y), H=4
      when  y is S
      sets  forcing=game
      artificial
      priority 1
  3N  "Game with a stopper in {y}"               shows hcp>=10, stop(y)

# Opener after the invitation: game with a maximum.
when asked leb_invite(M)
  4M  "Accepts: a maximum and three or more {M}"   shows M>=3, hcp>=16
  3N  "Accepts: a maximum, two {M}"                shows M<=2, hcp>=16
  P   "Declines: a minimum"                        shows hcp<=15

# Opener answers Stayman: a four-card unbid major, else 3NT with their
# suit stopped (partner's slow cue-bid has one already), else four of
# his longer minor. Responder then places the contract.
after 1N (2y) 3y (P) | 1N (2y) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3y (P) when y is not C, lho.y>=4, (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3), !rub
  3H  "Four hearts"                              shows H>=4
      when  y is D
  3S  "Four spades"                              shows S>=4, H<=3 | y is H
      when  y is D | y is H
  4H  "Four hearts"                              shows H>=4
      when  y is S
after 1N (2y) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3y (P) when y is not C, lho.y>=4, (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3), !rub
  3N  "No four-card major: game in notrump"
      priority -1
after 1N (2y) 3y (P) when y is not C, lho.y>=4, (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3), !rub
  3N  "No four-card major, a stopper in {y}"     shows stop(y)
  4C  "No four-card major, no stopper in {y}: clubs"     shows C>=D, !stop(y)
      priority -2
  4D  "No four-card major, no stopper in {y}: diamonds"  shows D>C, !stop(y)
      when  y is not D
      priority -2
after 1N (2y) 3y (P) 4m (P) when y is not C, rho.y>=4, (maybe rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3), !rub
  # Neither hand stops their suit: game in the minor, not 3NT.
  5m  "Game in {m}"
files.conventions/competitive_bidding/meckwell:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Meckwell (Meckstroth-Rodwell) over their strong 1NT, direct and
# balancing (vs-1nt.notes.md has the sources).
#
#   X    a long minor (six or more), or both majors: partner relays 2♣
#   2♣   clubs and a major, 5-4 either way
#   2♦   diamonds and a major, 5-4 either way
#   2♥/2♠ natural: six or more, or a good five without a four-card minor
#   2NT  both minors, 5-5 or longer
#
# This is the scheme against a strong notrump. Against a weak notrump
# Meckwell players double for penalties and change the other calls
# (bridgebum); our card has one field, for the strong notrump, so the
# same scheme is played against any range. A passed hand plays it
# anyway. Strength as in Cappelletti (cappelletti.bid): HCP plus a point
# a card beyond four, 10 for a two-suiter and 12 for a one-suiter. No
# BBA reference: BBA has no Meckwell, and played Multi-Landy in the
# Meckwell scenario.

module meckwell "Meckwell over their 1NT"
  kind   convention
  convention  competitive_bidding/meckwell
  needs  vs-1nt
  skill  competitive_bidding/meckwell
  skill  competitive_bidding/defense_vs_1nt
  param  def = defence_to_1nt.strong

after (1N) | (1N) P (P) when def is competitive_bidding/meckwell
  X   "Meckwell: a long minor, or both majors"   alert
      shows ((C>=6 | D>=6), second_longest<=3, hcp+length_points>=12) | (H>=4, S>=4, H+S>=9, hcp+length_points>=10)
      shows hcp<=17
      sets  ask=meck_one
  2C  "Meckwell: clubs and a major"              alert
      shows (C>=5, (H>=4 | S>=4)) | (C>=4, (H>=5 | S>=5))
      shows hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_pc(C)
  2D  "Meckwell: diamonds and a major"           alert
      shows (D>=5, (H>=4 | S>=4)) | (D>=4, (H>=5 | S>=5))
      shows hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_pc(D)
  2H  "Natural: six or more hearts, or a good five"
      shows H>=6 | (H>=5, quality(H)>=good, C<=3, D<=3), S<=3, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_one(H)
  2S  "Natural: six or more spades, or a good five"
      shows S>=6 | (S>=5, quality(S)>=good, C<=3, D<=3), H<=3, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_one(S)
  2N  "Meckwell: both minors, 5-5 or longer"     alert
      shows C>=5, D>=5, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_minors

# Advancer relays over the double; the doubler passes with clubs, bids
# 2♦ with diamonds and 2♥ with both majors (then partner picks the major,
# vs-1nt.bid).
when asked meck_one, rho.last=P | rho.last=X | rho.last=XX
  2C  "Relay: bid your suit"                      alert
      sets  ask=meck_relay

when asked meck_relay, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P   "My suit is clubs"                          shows C>=6
  2D  "My suit is diamonds"                       shows D>=6
      sets  ask=nt_one(D)
  2H  "Both majors"                               alert
      shows H>=4, S>=4
      sets  ask=nt_majors
files.conventions/competitive_bidding/raptor/r:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Raptor 1NT (`competitive.raptor_1nt.play`; convention-card
# competitive_bidding/raptor; Wikipedia, "Raptor (bridge)"): the direct
# 1NT overcall of a one-level suit opening shows a four-card major and a
# longer minor instead of a strong balanced hand:
#
# - over 1♣: five or more diamonds and four of a major;
# - over 1♦: five or more clubs and four of a major;
# - over 1♥: four spades and five or more of a minor;
# - over 1♠: four hearts and five or more of a minor.
#
# 8-15 HCP (10+ vulnerable); a stronger hand doubles. The natural 1NT
# overcall is off (overcalls.bid); a strong balanced hand doubles or
# passes. Advancer: the known suit at the cheapest level, 2♣
# pass-or-correct over a major (partner's minor unknown), the cue bid
# with 11+ asks for the unknown suit. Notes: raptor.notes.md.

module raptor "Raptor 1NT: a four-card major and a longer minor"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  needs  overcalls
  skill  competitive_bidding/raptor
  convention  competitive_bidding/raptor

after (1x)
  1N  "Raptor: five or more diamonds and four of a major"
      alert
      shows D>=5, H=4 | S=4, hcp>=8, hcp<=15
      when  !vul | hcp>=10, x is C
      priority 1
  1N  "Raptor: five or more clubs and four of a major"
      alert
      shows C>=5, H=4 | S=4, hcp>=8, hcp<=15
      when  !vul | hcp>=10, x is D
      priority 1
  1N  "Raptor: four spades and five or more of a minor"
      alert
      shows S=4, C>=5 | D>=5, hcp>=8, hcp<=15
      when  !vul | hcp>=10, x is H
      priority 1
  1N  "Raptor: four hearts and five or more of a minor"
      alert
      shows H=4, C>=5 | D>=5, hcp>=8, hcp<=15
      when  !vul | hcp>=10, x is S
      priority 1

# ── Advancer ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Over a minor: partner's minor is known, the major is not.
after (1m) 1N (P) | (1m) 1N (X)
  cheapest(m) "Cue bid: 11+, asks for partner's major"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp+length_points>=11
      sets  forcing=round, ask=raptor_major
      priority 3
  2H  "To play: five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, H>=S, hcp+length_points<=10
      priority 2
  2S  "To play: five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, S>H, hcp+length_points<=10
      priority 2
  2D  "To play: diamonds"
      when  partner.D>=5
      priority 1
  2C  "To play: clubs"
      when  partner.C>=5
      priority 1
  3D  "Invitational in diamonds: four or more, 9-10"
      shows D>=4, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  partner.D>=5
      priority 2
  3C  "Invitational in clubs: four or more, 9-10"
      shows C>=4, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  partner.C>=5
      priority 2

# Over a major: partner's major is known, the minor is not.
after (1M) 1N (P) | (1M) 1N (X)
  cheapest(M) "Cue bid: 11+, asks for partner's minor"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp+length_points>=11
      sets  forcing=round, ask=raptor_minor
      priority 3
  2S  "To play: three or more spades"
      shows S>=3, hcp+length_points<=10
      when  partner.S>=4
      priority 3
  2H  "To play: three or more hearts"
      shows H>=3, hcp+length_points<=10
      when  partner.H>=4
      priority 3
  3S  "Invitational: four or more spades, 9-10"
      shows S>=4, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  partner.S>=4
      priority 3
  2C  "Pass or correct: to play in partner's minor"
      alert
      shows C>=3, D>=3
      priority 3                         # above the Unusual 1NT's preference
  2D  "To play: six or more diamonds"
      shows D>=6
      when  partner.H>=4
      priority 2

# The overcaller answers.
when asked raptor_major
  cheapest(H) "Four hearts"                         shows H=4
  cheapest(S) "Four spades"                         shows S=4
      priority 1
when asked raptor_minor
  3C  "Clubs"                                       shows C>=5
  3D  "Diamonds"                                    shows D>=5
after (1M) 1N (P) 2C (P)
  P   "Clubs: to play"                              shows C>=5
  2D  "Diamonds"                                    shows D>=5
files.conventions/competitive_bidding/responsi:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Responsive doubles (Rick, 2026-09-22): when partner has doubled or
# overcalled and RHO raises, our double is for takeout, not penalty.
#
# - after partner's takeout double it shows both majors when they have
#   bid a minor, and both minors when they have bid a major;
# - after partner's overcall it shows the other two suits, with
#   tolerance (usually Hx) for partner's suit;
# - advancer needs 6+ total points at the two level, 8+ at the three and
#   10+ at the four.
#
# The card switches them on (`doubles.responsive.play`): the 21GF cards
# play them, Basic-Bridge does not.

module responsive-doubles "Responsive doubles"
  kind   convention
  convention  competitive_bidding/responsive_doubles
  needs  base
  skill  competitive_bidding/responsive_doubles

# ── After partner's takeout double ───────────────────────────────────
# Partner has the other three suits, so the double picks the two he can
# hold four of: the majors over a minor, the minors over a major.
after (1x) X (2x) when x is C | x is D
  X   "Responsive: both majors, 6+ total points"
      alert  artificial
      shows  S>=4, H>=4, hcp+length_points>=6
      sets   ask=responsive
      priority 1
after (1x) X (3x) when x is C | x is D
  X   "Responsive: both majors, 8+ total points"
      alert  artificial
      shows  S>=4, H>=4, hcp+length_points>=8
      sets   ask=responsive
      priority 1
after (1x) X (4x) when x is C | x is D
  X   "Responsive: both majors, 10+ total points"
      alert  artificial
      shows  S>=4, H>=4, hcp+length_points>=10
      sets   ask=responsive
      priority 1

after (1x) X (2x) when x is H | x is S
  X   "Responsive: both minors, 6+ total points"
      alert  artificial
      shows  D>=4, C>=4, hcp+length_points>=6
      sets   ask=responsive
      priority 1
after (1x) X (3x) when x is H | x is S
  X   "Responsive: both minors, 8+ total points"
      alert  artificial
      shows  D>=4, C>=4, hcp+length_points>=8
      sets   ask=responsive
      priority 1
after (1x) X (4x) when x is H | x is S
  X   "Responsive: both minors, 10+ total points"
      alert  artificial
      shows  D>=4, C>=4, hcp+length_points>=10
      sets   ask=responsive
      priority 1

# ── After partner's overcall ─────────────────────────────────────────
# The two unbid suits and a doubleton in partner's, which is tolerance
# enough for him to pass or rebid it. With three we raise instead.
after (1x) 1y (2x) | (1x) 2y (3x) | (1x) P (P) 1y (2x)
  X   "Responsive: the two unbid suits, 6+ total points"
      alert  artificial
      shows  (S>=4 | x is S | y is S), (H>=4 | x is H | y is H)
      shows  (D>=4 | x is D | y is D), (C>=4 | x is C | y is C)
      shows  y=2, x<=3, hcp+length_points>=10
      sets   ask=responsive
after (1x) 1y (3x) | (1x) 2y (4x)
  X   "Responsive: the two unbid suits, 8+ total points"
      alert  artificial
      shows  (S>=4 | x is S | y is S), (H>=4 | x is H | y is H)
      shows  (D>=4 | x is D | y is D), (C>=4 | x is C | y is C)
      shows  y=2, x<=3, hcp+length_points>=11
      sets   ask=responsive

# ── Answering a responsive double ────────────────────────────────────
# Partner named two suits; pick the one we are longer in, at the
# cheapest level. Written against the question, so it is the same rule
# after a double of their raise at any level.
when asked responsive
  cheapest(S) "Preference: spades"
      shows S>=3, S>=H
      when  partner.S>=4
  cheapest(H) "Preference: hearts"
      shows H>=3, H>S
      when  partner.H>=4
  cheapest(D) "Preference: diamonds"
      shows D>=3, D>=C
      when  partner.D>=4
  cheapest(C) "Preference: clubs"
      shows C>=3, C>D
      when  partner.C>=4
files.conventions/competitive_bidding/sandwich:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Sandwich 1NT (`competitive.sandwich_nt.play`; convention-card
# competitive_bidding/sandwich_nt, Robert S. Todd, Adventures in Bridge
# 194; Wikipedia, "Unusual notrump"): when they have bid two suits,
# (1x) P (1y) 1NT shows the two unbid suits instead of a strong
# balanced hand, which is unlikely between an opener and a responder.
#
# The passed hand's version is the Unusual 1NT of two-suited-overcalls.bid
# (`competitive.unusual_1nt.play`); when that is on it keeps the passed
# hand and this module covers the hand that has not passed. Five-four or
# better (five-five preferred), 8-15 HCP: with more, double first. The
# advances are the Unusual 1NT's (two-suited-overcalls.bid, which reads
# this switch too). Notes: sandwich-nt.notes.md.

module sandwich-nt "Sandwich 1NT: the two unbid suits"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  needs  two-suited-overcalls
  skill  competitive_bidding/sandwich_nt
  convention  competitive_bidding/sandwich_nt
  param  u1n = competitive_bidding/unusual_notrump:at_1nt default false

after (1x) P (1y) when y is not x, !passed_hand | !u1n
  1N  "Sandwich 1NT: the two unbid suits, hearts and spades"
      alert
      shows H>=4, S>=4, H>=5 | S>=5, hcp>=8, hcp<=15
      when  x is C, y is D
      priority 1
  1N  "Sandwich 1NT: the two unbid suits, diamonds and spades"
      alert
      shows D>=4, S>=4, D>=5 | S>=5, hcp>=8, hcp<=15
      when  x is C, y is H
      priority 1
  1N  "Sandwich 1NT: the two unbid suits, diamonds and hearts"
      alert
      shows D>=4, H>=4, D>=5 | H>=5, hcp>=8, hcp<=15
      when  x is C, y is S
      priority 1
  1N  "Sandwich 1NT: the two unbid suits, clubs and spades"
      alert
      shows C>=4, S>=4, C>=5 | S>=5, hcp>=8, hcp<=15
      when  x is D, y is H
      priority 1
  1N  "Sandwich 1NT: the two unbid suits, clubs and hearts"
      alert
      shows C>=4, H>=4, C>=5 | H>=5, hcp>=8, hcp<=15
      when  x is D, y is S
      priority 1
  1N  "Sandwich 1NT: the two unbid suits, both minors"
      alert
      shows C>=4, D>=4, C>=5 | D>=5, hcp>=8, hcp<=15
      when  x is H, y is S
      priority 1
files.conventions/competitive_bidding/scrambli:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Scrambling 2NT (`competitive.scrambling_2nt.play`; convention-card
# competitive_bidding/scrambling_2nt; Robert S. Todd, Advancing in
# Bridge 555; PBS btn/Scrambling_2NT.btn): when advancer must bid
# after partner's takeout double of their raise, (1M) P (2M) X (P) 2NT
# is not natural: it shows two places to play, both minors, and asks
# the doubler to bid his lower four-card suit; advancer passes or
# corrects. A free 2NT (RHO has bid) would be good/bad, not written.
#
# Here: four or more in each minor, no five-card suit and no four-card
# unbid major (that is bid instead), 0-10 HCP (with more, game or a
# jump). Notes: scrambling-2nt.notes.md.

module scrambling-2nt "Scrambling 2NT"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  needs  takeout-double
  skill  competitive_bidding/scrambling_2nt
  convention  competitive_bidding/scrambling_2nt

after (1M) P (2M) X (P) | (1M) P (2M) P (P) X (P)
  2N  "Scrambling: both minors, pick one"
      alert  artificial
      shows C>=4, D>=4, C<=5, D<=5, C+D>=8, hcp<=10, S<=3 | M is S, H<=3 | M is H
      sets  ask=scramble
      priority 1

# The doubler: his lower four-card minor.
when asked scramble
  3C  "Four or more clubs"                         shows C>=4
      priority 1
  3D  "Diamonds: fewer than four clubs"            shows D>=4
after (1M) P (2M) X (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) | (1M) P (2M) P (P) X (P) 2N (P) 3C (P)
  P   "Clubs will do"                              shows C>=D
      priority 1
  3D  "Diamonds: longer"                           shows D>C
      priority 1
files.conventions/competitive_bidding/snapdrag:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Snapdragon doubles (`competitive.snapdragon.play`; Bridge Bum,
# "Snapdragon Double"; PBS btn/Snapdragon_Double.btn): they open, partner
# overcalls, RHO bids a new suit; three suits have been bid, one by each
# of three players, and advancer's double shows five or more of the
# fourth suit with tolerance for partner's (two or three cards), 8+ HCP.
# Forcing for one round (the scenario's definition).
#
# The overcaller then bids the fourth suit with three-card support (a
# jump with 15+), rebids a six-card suit, bids notrump with RHO's suit
# stopped, or else returns to his own suit. Notes: snapdragon.notes.md.

module snapdragon "Snapdragon doubles"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  needs  advances
  skill  competitive_bidding/snapdragon
  convention  competitive_bidding/snapdragon

after (1x) 1y (1z) | (1x) 1y (2z) | (1x) 2y (2z) | (1x) 2y (3z) when y is not x, z is not x, z is not y
  X   "Snapdragon: five or more clubs, tolerance for {y}, 8+"
      alert
      shows C>=5, y>=2, hcp>=8
      when  x is not C, y is not C, z is not C
      sets  forcing=round
      priority 1
  X   "Snapdragon: five or more diamonds, tolerance for {y}, 8+"
      alert
      shows D>=5, y>=2, hcp>=8
      when  x is not D, y is not D, z is not D
      sets  forcing=round
      priority 1
  X   "Snapdragon: five or more hearts, tolerance for {y}, 8+"
      alert
      shows H>=5, y>=2, hcp>=8
      when  x is not H, y is not H, z is not H
      sets  forcing=round
      priority 1
  X   "Snapdragon: five or more spades, tolerance for {y}, 8+"
      alert
      shows S>=5, y>=2, hcp>=8
      when  x is not S, y is not S, z is not S
      sets  forcing=round
      priority 1

# The overcaller. Over opener's redouble too (2026-10-05, self A/B:
# without it the overcaller passed and the redouble was left to play,
# 1♥XX made with overtricks on 30-odd boards).
after (1x) 1y (1z) X (P) | (1x) 1y (2z) X (P) | (1x) 2y (2z) X (P) | (1x) 2y (3z) X (P) | (1x) 1y (1z) X (XX) | (1x) 1y (2z) X (XX) | (1x) 2y (2z) X (XX) | (1x) 2y (3z) X (XX) when y is not x, z is not x, z is not y
  jump(C) "Fit for clubs and 15+"        shows C>=3, hcp+length_points>=15   when partner.C>=5   priority 3
  jump(D) "Fit for diamonds and 15+"     shows D>=3, hcp+length_points>=15   when partner.D>=5   priority 3
  jump(H) "Fit for hearts and 15+"       shows H>=3, hcp+length_points>=15   when partner.H>=5   priority 3
  jump(S) "Fit for spades and 15+"       shows S>=3, hcp+length_points>=15   when partner.S>=5   priority 3
  cheapest(C) "Three or more clubs"      shows C>=3                          when partner.C>=5   priority 2
  cheapest(D) "Three or more diamonds"   shows D>=3                          when partner.D>=5   priority 2
  cheapest(H) "Three or more hearts"     shows H>=3                          when partner.H>=5   priority 2
  cheapest(S) "Three or more spades"     shows S>=3                          when partner.S>=5   priority 2
  cheapest(y) "Six or more {y}"          shows y>=6                                              priority 1
  cheapest(N) "{z} stopped, no fit"      shows stop(z), hcp+length_points<=14
  cheapest(y) "Back to {y}: no fit"
      priority -2
files.conventions/competitive_bidding/sos_redo:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# SOS redouble (`other_conventions.sos_redouble.play`; convention-card
# competitive_bidding/sos_redouble; "25 More Bridge Conventions You
# Should Know", chapter 22): when a low-level contract of ours is
# doubled for penalty, a redouble asks partner to choose another suit
# rather than showing strength.
#
# Written for the one place where the engine knows the double has
# become a penalty double: our one-level opening doubled for takeout and
# passed round by the doubler's partner, 1x (X) P (P). Opener redoubles
# with three cards or fewer in his suit (a short minor opening); with
# four or more he passes and plays it. Responder then bids his longest
# other suit, the cheapest of equals. Notes: sos-redouble.notes.md.

module sos-redouble "SOS redouble"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  skill  competitive_bidding/sos_redouble
  convention  competitive_bidding/sos_redouble

after 1x (X) P (P)
  XX  "SOS: {x} is short, pick another suit"
      alert  artificial
      shows x<=3
      sets  ask=sos
      priority 1
  P   "To play: four or more {x}"
      shows x>=4
      priority 1

# Responder: his longest suit other than opener's, cheapest of equals.
after 1x (X) P (P) XX (P)
  cheapest(C) "Rescue: clubs"     shows C>=D | x is D, C>=H | x is H, C>=S | x is S
      when  x is not C
      priority 1
  cheapest(D) "Rescue: diamonds"  shows D>C | x is C, D>=H | x is H, D>=S | x is S
      when  x is not D
      priority 1
  cheapest(H) "Rescue: hearts"    shows H>C | x is C, H>D | x is D, H>=S | x is S
      when  x is not H
      priority 1
  cheapest(S) "Rescue: spades"    shows S>C | x is C, S>D | x is D, S>H | x is H
      when  x is not S
      priority 1
files.conventions/competitive_bidding/suction/:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Suction over their 1NT, direct and balancing (Bridge Bum, "Suction";
# convention-card competitive_bidding/suction). Each two-level suit bid
# shows the next suit up, or the two suits above that:
#
#   X    clubs and hearts
#   2♣   diamonds, or hearts and spades
#   2♦   hearts, or spades and clubs
#   2♥   spades, or clubs and diamonds
#   2♠   clubs, or diamonds and hearts
#   2NT  diamonds and spades
#
# A one-suiter is a good five or six or more; a two-suiter 5-4 or longer,
# 5-5 when it may end at the three level (2♥, 2♠, 2NT). Strength as the
# other defences (cappelletti.bid): HCP plus a point a card beyond four,
# 10 or more, at most 17. Advancer assumes the one-suiter and bids the
# next suit; the overcaller passes with it or shows the two-suiter, which
# advancer passes or corrects. See suction.notes.md.

module suction "Suction over their 1NT"
  kind   convention
  convention  competitive_bidding/suction
  needs  vs-1nt
  skill  competitive_bidding/suction
  skill  competitive_bidding/defense_vs_1nt
  param  def = defence_to_1nt.strong

define suction_one(x) = x>=6, second_longest<=4 | (x=5, quality(x)>=good, second_longest<=3)

after (1N) | (1N) P (P) when def is competitive_bidding/suction
  X   "Suction: clubs and hearts"                       alert
      shows C>=4, H>=4, C+H>=9, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=suc_pick(C, H)
  2C  "Suction: diamonds, or hearts and spades"         alert
      shows suction_one(D) | (H>=4, S>=4, H+S>=9), hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=suc_relay(D)
      artificial
  2D  "Suction: hearts, or spades and clubs"            alert
      shows suction_one(H) | (S>=4, C>=4, S+C>=9), hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=suc_relay(H)
      artificial
  2H  "Suction: spades, or clubs and diamonds"          alert
      shows suction_one(S) | (C>=5, D>=5), hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=suc_relay(S)
      artificial
  2S  "Suction: clubs, or diamonds and hearts"          alert
      shows suction_one(C) | (D>=5, H>=5), hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=suc_relay(C)
      artificial
  2N  "Suction: diamonds and spades"                    alert
      shows D>=5, S>=5, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=suc_pick(D, S)

# ── Advancer ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Assume the one-suiter: bid it, the overcaller passes or shows the rest.
when asked suc_relay(x), rho.last=P | rho.last=X | rho.last=XX
  cheapest(x)  "Suction relay: pass or correct"   alert
      sets  ask=suc_correct(x)

# A two-suiter shown directly: preference, the longer (the higher when equal).
when asked suc_pick(a, b), rho.last=P | rho.last=X | rho.last=XX
  cheapest(a)  "Preference: {a}"                      shows a>b
  cheapest(b)  "Preference: {b}"                      shows b>=a

# ── The overcaller after the relay ───────────────────────────────────
# Over their double too, and advancer over their redouble (2026-10-05,
# the self A/B: 1NT 2D X 2H X left in with spades and clubs, -1400; 1NT
# X XX passed out).
when asked suc_correct(x), rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P   "My suit is {x}"                                shows x>=5
      priority 1
when asked suc_correct(D), rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  2H  "Hearts and spades"                             shows H>=4, S>=4
      sets  ask=nt_majors
when asked suc_correct(H), rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  2S  "Spades and clubs"                              shows S>=4, C>=4
      sets  ask=suc_keep(S, C)
when asked suc_correct(S), rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  2N  "Clubs and diamonds"                            shows C>=5, D>=5
      sets  ask=nt_minors
when asked suc_correct(C), rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  3D  "Diamonds and hearts"                           shows D>=5, H>=5
      sets  ask=suc_keep(D, H)

# Advancer: keep the first suit, or correct to the second.
when asked suc_keep(a, b), rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P            "Keeps {a}"                            shows a>=b
  cheapest(b)  "Prefers {b}"                          shows b>a

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Support doubles and redoubles. We open, partner responds one of a
# major, and RHO comes in: opener's double (redouble over their double)
# shows exactly three cards in partner's major, and a raise shows four.
# The strength is not limited: opener shows extras at his next turn.
#
# The card switches them on (`doubles.support.play`; the redouble is
# `doubles.support.rdbl`). `doubles.support.through` is the highest call
# by RHO over which the double still shows support ("2♥" on Rick's card);
# a card that leaves it unset plays them through two of responder's major,
# which is where BBA stops (probes/support-x-1C-1H-2S.toml,
# support-x-1D-1H-3C.toml). Above it opener's double keeps whatever
# meaning it had.
#
# Notes: support-doubles.notes.md.

module support-doubles "Support doubles and redoubles"
  kind   convention
  convention  competitive_bidding/support_doubles
  needs  rebids
  skill  competitive_bidding/support_doubles
  param  rdbl = rdbl default false
  param  through = through

# ── Opener: the double shows three, the raise four ───────────────────
# BBA doubles on every hand with three of partner's major, 11 to 21, and
# with a six-card minor too (probes/support-x-*.toml: 490 of 490), so the
# double comes before every other rebid. The raise with four is
# unchanged (rebids.bid, `1x (*) 1z (*)`: it already shows four).
after 1x (*) 1M (1z) | 1x (*) 1M (2z) | 1x (*) 1M (3z) when M is not x, z is not M
  when (through is none, rho.last <= 2{M}) | rho.last <= through
    X   "Support double: exactly three {M}"
        alert  artificial
        shows  M=3
        sets   ask=support(M, x, z)
        priority 1                 # before any other rebid, as BBA (above)
    # After their takeout double of our opening the double was the 18+
    # hand (rebids.bid, ticket b6), which gives way to the support double
    # here. The strong hands without three of the major still need a
    # call: BBA bids 2NT or 3NT with 18 (probes/support-x-1C-X-1H-1S.toml).
    jump(N) "18-19 balanced with a stopper in {z}"
        when  nt_jump_to_game                  # 3NT at most (rebids.bid)
        shows  balanced, hcp=18..19, M<=2, stop(z)
        when   lho.last=X
    3N  "20+ with a stopper in {z}"
        shows  hcp>=20, M<=2, stop(z)
        when   lho.last=X
        priority -1
    cheapest(z) "Cue bid: 18+, forcing to game"
        alert  artificial
        shows  hcp>=18, M<=2
        when   lho.last=X
        sets   forcing=game
        priority -3

after 1x (*) 1M (X) when M is not x, rdbl
  XX  "Support redouble: exactly three {M}"
      alert  artificial
      shows  M=3
      sets   ask=support(M, x)
      priority 1                   # before any other rebid (probes/support-xx-1C-1H-X.toml)

# ── Responder after the support double, when they pass ───────────────
# Partner has exactly three of my major. With five it is an eight-card
# fit, bid to the level the hand is worth; with four it is a 4-3 fit, and
# notrump with their suit held, or a minor, comes first (BBA: 2C or 2D
# rather than the 4-3 fit on 100 of 100 minimum hands with four,
# probes/support-x-resp-1C-1H-1S.toml).
when asked support(M, x, z), rho.last=P, partner.last=X
  cheapest(M) "Five or more {M}, minimum"
      shows M>=5, points<=9
      sets  trump=M, ask=signoff
  jump(M) "Five or more {M}, 10-11, invitational"
      shows M>=5, points=10..11
      sets  trump=M, ask=invite(M)
  4M  "Five or more {M}, 12+: game"
      shows M>=5, points>=12
      sets  trump=M
  1N  "Four {M}, 6-10 balanced with a stopper in {z}"
      shows M=4, balanced, points=6..10, stop(z)
      sets  ask=signoff
  2N  "Four {M}, 11-12, a stopper in {z}, invitational"
      shows M=4, semibalanced, points=11..12, stop(z)
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  3N  "Four {M}, 13+ with a stopper in {z}"
      shows M=4, semibalanced, points>=13, stop(z)
  # The minor bids only at the two level, and never in a suit LHO has
  # shown (2026-09-28: 1C (1D) 1S (2H) X (P) 3D left us in a 5-card fit).
  cheapest(x) "Raise: four or more {x}, minimum"
      shows x>=4, M=4, points<=10
      when  x is C | x is D, z is not x, cheapest_rank(x)<=14
      sets  ask=signoff
  cheapest(D) "Four or more diamonds, minimum"
      shows D>=4, M=4, points<=10
      when  x is C, z is not D, cheapest_rank(D)<=14
      when  maybe lho.D<=4
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -1
  cheapest(C) "Four or more clubs, minimum"
      shows C>=4, M=4, points<=10
      when  x is not C, z is not C, cheapest_rank(C)<=14
      when  maybe lho.C<=4
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -1
  cheapest(z) "Cue bid: four {M}, 13+, no stopper in {z}"
      alert  artificial
      shows M=4, points>=13
      sets  forcing=game, ask=support_cue(M, z)
      priority -1
  jump(M) "Four {M}, 11-12, invitational"
      shows M=4, points=11..12
      sets  trump=M, ask=invite(M)
      priority -2
  # BBA converts the double on 30 of 184 hands with four of partner's
  # major and four or more of theirs (probes/support-x-resp-1D-1S-2C.toml).
  P   "Penalty: four or more {z} with two of the top five"
      shows z>=4, top5(z)>=2, M<=4, hcp>=7
      priority 1                   # before the notrump and minor bids it outranks
  cheapest(M) "Four {M}, no better bid"
      shows M>=4
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -5

# After the redouble, their pass leaves us in one of the major
# redoubled with seven trumps: BBA passes (216 of 250,
# probes/support-xx-resp-1C-1H-X.toml).
when asked support(M), rho.last=P, partner.last=XX
  P   "Plays one {M} redoubled"
  4M  "Five or more {M}, 13+: game"
      shows M>=5, points>=13
      sets  trump=M
      priority -1

# ── Responder after the support double, when they bid again ──────────
# The double is no longer to be answered: compete with the eight-card
# fit, bid game with it and 12+, and otherwise leave it to partner.
when asked support(M), rho.last!=P
  cheapest(M) "Competes: five or more {M}"
      shows M>=5, points<=11
      sets  trump=M, ask=signoff     # opener goes on only with 19+ (rebids.bid)
  4M  "Five or more {M}, 12+: game"
      shows M>=5, points>=12
      sets  trump=M
  P   "No further bid"
      priority -10

# ── Opener answers the cue bid ───────────────────────────────────────
# Responder has four of the major, 13+ and nothing in their suit; the
# cue bid asks for a stopper. With none, the 4-3 fit is the game.
when asked support_cue(M, z)
  3N  "A stopper in {z}"             shows stop(z)
  4M  "Game: no stopper in {z}"
      priority -1
files.rules/base/base.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Natural opening bids. The 1-level suit openings are written to be mutually
# exclusive (longest suit; higher of two 5-card suits; 1C with 3-3 in the
# minors, 1D with 4-4), so ranking only has to choose between a suit opening
# and something more descriptive such as 1NT.
#
# Not yet covered: 2-level and higher openings, and anything above 21 HCP.

module base "Natural opening bids"
  kind   system
  skill  basic_bidding/major_suit_openings
  skill  basic_bidding/minor_suit_openings
  param  min_open = general.min_hcp_open default 12
  param  style = general.style
  # 1m with a five-card major and a longer minor (off: open the major)
  param  may5 = minor_openings.may_hold_5_card_major default true
  # 2C is the strong opening (off: no 2C, a strong hand opens at one;
  # but a forcing 1C card keeps 2C until 1C is built, strong-openings.bid)
  param  forcing_2c = general.forcing_opening_2c default true
  param  forcing_1c = general.forcing_opening_1c default false

# An opening needs 12 total points: HCP plus one for each card beyond four
# in every suit (12 flat, 11 with a five-card suit, 10 with a six-card one).
# The rule of 20 was tried as an extra requirement without a six-card suit
# (it rules out 11 HCP with 5-3-3-2). BBA opens those hands far more often
# than it passes them: it cost 2,939 agreeing calls and gained 225, so we
# keep the 12 total points alone.
# That leaves no gap between a weak two and a one-level opening.
#
# bba (probed 2026-09-24, preempts.notes.md): a ten-count with a six-card
# suit opens at the one level only when the weak two is out (two aces, a
# major with the ace-king, or a side four-card major with an honour), and
# then, with the side major, only with two aces or kings among its honours
# (controls 3+, or two kings). Six clubs and ten HCP pass.
when opening
  1S  "Major opening: 5+ spades"
      shows hcp>=10, hcp+length_points>=min_open, hcp<=21 | (!forcing_2c, !forcing_1c), S>=5, S>=H, (S>=D, S>=C) | !may5
      when  style is standard
  1H  "Major opening: 5+ hearts"
      shows hcp>=10, hcp+length_points>=min_open, hcp<=21 | (!forcing_2c, !forcing_1c), H>=5, H>S, (H>=D, H>=C) | !may5
      when  style is standard
  1D  "3+ diamonds"
      shows hcp>=10, hcp+length_points>=min_open, hcp<=21 | (!forcing_2c, !forcing_1c), D>=3, D>C | D>=4, D>=C, H<=4 | (H<D, may5), S<=4 | (S<D, may5)
      when  style is standard
  1C  "3+ clubs"
      shows hcp>=10, hcp+length_points>=min_open, hcp<=21 | (!forcing_2c, !forcing_1c), C>D | (C=3, D=3), H<=4 | (H<C, may5), S<=4 | (S<C, may5)
      when  style is standard
  1S  "Major opening: 5+ spades"
      shows hcp>=10, hcp+length_points>=min_open, hcp<=21 | (!forcing_2c, !forcing_1c), S>=5, S>=H, (S>=D, S>=C) | !may5, hcp>=11 | S<=5 | H<=3 | controls>=3 | (controls=2, !has(A,S), !has(A,H), !has(A,D), !has(A,C))
      when  style is not standard
  1H  "Major opening: 5+ hearts"
      shows hcp>=10, hcp+length_points>=min_open, hcp<=21 | (!forcing_2c, !forcing_1c), H>=5, H>S, (H>=D, H>=C) | !may5, hcp>=11 | H<=5 | S<=3 | controls>=3 | (controls=2, !has(A,S), !has(A,H), !has(A,D), !has(A,C))
      when  style is not standard
  1D  "3+ diamonds"
      shows hcp>=10, hcp+length_points>=min_open, hcp<=21 | (!forcing_2c, !forcing_1c), D>=3, D>C | D>=4, D>=C, H<=4 | (H<D, may5), S<=4 | (S<D, may5), hcp>=11 | D<=5 | (H<=3, S<=3) | controls>=3 | (controls=2, !has(A,S), !has(A,H), !has(A,D), !has(A,C))
      when  style is not standard
  1C  "3+ clubs"
      shows hcp>=10, hcp+length_points>=min_open, hcp<=21 | (!forcing_2c, !forcing_1c), C>D | (C=3, D=3), H<=4 | (H<C, may5), S<=4 | (S<C, may5), hcp>=11 | C<=5
      when  style is not standard
  P   "No opening bid"
      shows hcp<=min_open-1, hcp+length_points<=min_open-1 | hcp<=9
      priority -10
  P   "No opening bid"
      shows hcp=10, longest=6
      when  style is not standard
      priority -10

# Third seat may open light with a good four-card major; fourth seat opens
# by the rule of 15 (HCP plus spade length), and passes otherwise.
when opening, seat=3
  1S  "Major opening: 4+ good spades, 10-11 HCP"
      shows S>=4, hcp=10..11, quality(S)>=good
  1H  "Major opening: 4+ good hearts, 10-11 HCP"
      shows H>=4, hcp=10..11, quality(H)>=good, S<=3
when opening, seat=4
  P   "No opening bid: HCP and spades under 15"
      shows hcp<=14
      when  hcp + S <= 14
      priority 1

# Once our side has bid game, a player with nothing more to add passes.
# Slam tries and corrections are separate rules that outrank this.
when game_reached
  P   "No further bid"
      when  !passes_out_artificial
      priority -50

# Partner bid at game or above, in a suit other than our agreed one, and
# our system gives the call no meaning (a 5NT king ask the card does not
# play, a convention we do not know): passing may leave us in a contract
# nobody chose. Bid the agreed suit at the cheapest level, five, six or
# seven (Rick, 2026-10-29).
when game_reached, we.trump is suit, partner.unread, rho.last=P, !(partner.last=P | partner.last=X | partner.last=XX | partner.last=4{trump} | partner.last=5{trump} | partner.last=6{trump} | partner.last=7{trump})
  cheapest(trump) "Back to the agreed suit"
      priority -40

# Partner answered my quantitative 4NT with a five-level suit our system
# gives no meaning: below slam it is never a place to stop (Rick,
# 2026-11-06, bridge-classroom-bug-artifacts #94: 4NT, 5♣ unread, passed
# in a 4-0 fit with thirteen tricks in four strains). Read it as an
# acceptance with a suit to offer: slam in notrump. The keycard asks
# have their own continuations (rkcb-1430.bid, `answered keycards`).
when answered quant, partner.unread, partner.last >= 5C, partner.last <= 5S, rho.last=P
  6N  "Slam: partner accepted the invitation"
      priority -40
when answered quant_major(M), partner.unread, partner.last >= 5C, partner.last <= 5S, rho.last=P
  6N  "Slam: partner accepted the invitation"
      priority -40

# ── Never pass out our own artificial bid ────────────────────────────
# Brill round robin 2026-10-09, board 90000102: 1S 2S X 3S X P P P, a
# doubled Michaels cue bid passed out for -1,700. The catch-all passes
# (this file's "Game reached", advances.bid's "Defending: nothing more
# to say", after-interference.bid's "nothing new to say", and two
# transfer fallbacks) do not apply when our side's last bid is
# artificial (a cue bid, a transfer, Stayman, a relay; not an answer to
# partner's question, which the asker may choose to play) and RHO has
# passed it: my pass would leave LHO to end the auction, or end it
# (partner's game-forcing cue of their preempt, 3S X P 4S P, was passed
# out by the doubler 67 times on the corpus). After RHO's double, a pass
# that gives partner another turn may mean something (opener's pass of a
# doubled Stayman 2C), and partner, the hand that knows what the bid
# meant, runs at his turn.
#
# With no real rule left, the hand to call bids its best known fit
# naturally (its own length plus partner's shown length) at the cheapest
# level, never in a suit they have bid naturally. A fallback below every
# real rule.
define passes_out_artificial = artificial_contract, rho.last=P
when passes_out_artificial
  cheapest(S) "Runout: our best known fit"
      prefer we.fit(S).min
      when  !lho.named(S), !rho.named(S)
      priority -60
  cheapest(H) "Runout: our best known fit"
      prefer we.fit(H).min
      when  !lho.named(H), !rho.named(H)
      priority -60
  cheapest(D) "Runout: our best known fit"
      prefer we.fit(D).min
      when  !lho.named(D), !rho.named(D)
      priority -60
  cheapest(C) "Runout: our best known fit"
      prefer we.fit(C).min
      when  !lho.named(C), !rho.named(C)
      priority -60

# A game force must not be passed below game. When no better rule applies,
# bid game: in the agreed suit, or in notrump without one.
when we.forcing = game, !game_reached
  4{trump}  "Game in the agreed suit"   when we.trump is H | we.trump is S
            priority -40
  5{trump}  "Game in the agreed suit"   when we.trump is C | we.trump is D
            priority -40
  3N        "Game in notrump"           when we.trump is none
            priority -40
  # A fit shown but not agreed (2026-09-27, ticket b455: 1H X P 2H 3H 4D,
  # where the doubler's three spades met five and nobody bid 4S): game in
  # the known eight-card fit, a major first, above the 3NT fallback.
  4S        "Game in the spade fit"     shows S + partner.S.min >= 8
            when  we.trump is none
            priority -38
  4H        "Game in the heart fit"     shows H + partner.H.min >= 8
            when  we.trump is none
            priority -38
  5D        "Game in the diamond fit"   shows D + partner.D.min >= 8
            when  we.trump is none
            priority -41
  5C        "Game in the club fit"      shows C + partner.C.min >= 8
            when  we.trump is none
            priority -41
files.rules/base/fit.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# A major-suit fit, whatever the path (Rick, 2026-10-02): suit agreement,
# which both hands know, and a fit that only one hand can see yet. The
# conditions are named here for every module to read; the rules below are
# the judgment for the second: the hand that sees the fit places the
# contract in it. fit.notes.md has the ruling, the survey and the
# measurements.

module fit "A major-suit fit: agreed, or seen by one hand"
  kind   judgement
  needs  base
  skill  basic_bidding/fit_and_level
  param  tu    = bidding_conventions/texas:two_under default false

# ── The two concepts ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Suit agreement (public): what each hand has shown makes eight cards
# (1NT-4D Texas: two facing six), or a rule has set the trump suit. Both
# hands know it, so it makes x trump: 4NT asks for keycards in x, control
# bids refer to x.
define agreed_fit(x) = trump is x | shown.x.min + partner.x.min >= 8

# A private fit: my own length and what partner has shown make eight,
# what I have shown does not (1NT-2D-2H with six hearts; a doubleton
# facing opener's six-card rebid). Partner does not know it yet, so it
# changes nothing about what 4NT means; it tells me where to play.
define private_fit(x) = x + partner.x.min >= 8, shown.x.min + partner.x.min <= 7

# ── The count, by role (Rick, 2026-10-01) ─────────────────────────────
#
# The long-trump hand counts declarer points (HCP + length), the short
# hand support points (HCP + shortness, capped by its trumps), each on
# partner's floor (`longer`, slam-entry.bid). Game at 25.
define fit_game_values(t)   = (longer(t), hcp + length_points + partner.points.min >= 25) | (!longer(t), tp(t) + partner.points.min >= 25)

# A slam call the slam modules would make in the fit instead: the direct
# slam on a card with no ask, the keycard ask agreeing it on one with
# (slam-entry.bid, rkcb-1430.bid, blackwood.bid).
define fit_slam_call(t) = (no_ask, direct_count(t)) | (!no_ask, shown_fit(t), fit_slam_values(t), !two_bare_beside(t))

# In a game force, a fit in partner's own suit (three or more shown) with
# slam interest is agreed slowly (slam-entry.bid, "Fast arrival"): the
# jump to game would deny the interest.
define fit_slow_agree(t) = we.forcing = game, partner.t.min >= 3, under_game(t), t + partner.t.min >= 8, slam_interest(t)
define slam_route = fit_slow_agree(S) | fit_slow_agree(H) | fit_slam_call(S) | fit_slam_call(H)

# Slam interest in the fit below 3NT leaves room for the forcing calls
# that explore it (new minor forcing, a jump shift, a raise below game);
# over partner's 3NT, slam values in notrump (32 HCP on his floor, the
# quantitative 4NT and 6NT of over-3nt.bid) go there.
define fit_slam_room(t) = (slam_interest(t), !partner.last=3N) | (partner.last=3N, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 32)

# Four cards in the other major, which partner may hold four of: look for
# that fit first (1D-1S-1NT-3H with six spades and four hearts).
define other_major_open(x) = x >= 4, partner.x.max >= 4

# Partner's last bid was in x: raising it is the sequence modules' job
# (a Stayman answer, opener's suit), and their raises say more.
define partner_named(x) = partner.last=1{x} | partner.last=2{x} | partner.last=3{x} | partner.last=4{x}

# ── Placing the contract in a fit only I can see ──────────────────────
#
# Rick (2026-10-02): the hand that knows the fit places the contract in
# it, by strength, rather than in notrump. Game in the fit with 25
# between us (`fit_game_values`), ahead of the notrump calls at the same
# point (priority 1: the sequence rules are at 0). Bidding the suit this
# way shows the fit, so partner knows it too.
#
# Where, measured (fit.notes.md): at my second call or later, with
# nothing asked of me and no suit agreed, uncontested or with the
# opponents silent since (RHO passed: 1S X P 2S P 3NT P), when partner's
# last call was notrump (his 1NT, 2NT or 3NT rebid: balanced, so two or
# more in the major; over his 3NT, four of the major is the correction;
# his notrump answer to a question of mine too: a stopper ask, the
# fourth suit), or when he has answered my new minor forcing or Stayman
# in a suit. Elsewhere a
# priority-1 4M would claim how partner reads the sequence modules' own
# 4M (a jump raise's range: slam-entry.test), and an invitation at the
# three level would claim their forcing three-level bids, so neither is
# written. Not when partner's last bid was the suit (raising it is the
# sequence modules' job), not over the strong 2NT (transfers may be on) nor the 24+ 3NT rebid
# when the card plays Texas (texas-transfers.bid),
# not when a slam call or slam exploration applies (`slam_route`,
# `fit_slam_room`), and not with four cards in the other major that
# partner may share (`other_major_open`).
#
# `private_fit(x)` is the rule's condition written out: the hand part in
# `shows`, so that partner reads my length from it, the public part in
# `when`. `partner.x.min >= 2` keeps the rule from claiming partner's
# reading of a call it never made (1S-1NT-3H, a jump shift).
when !asked, we.trump is none, !game_reached | partner.last=3N, !they.bid | rho.last=P, me.has_bid, !(partner.last=2N, partner.hcp.min>=20), !(partner.last=3N, partner.hcp.min>=24, texas_2nt | tu), partner.last=1N | partner.last=2N | partner.last=3N | answered nmf | answered majors
  4S  "Game in the spade fit"
      shows S + partner.S.min >= 8, fit_game_values(S)
      when  shown.S.min + partner.S.min <= 7 | partner.last=3N, partner.S.min >= 2, !partner_named(S), !slam_route, !fit_slam_room(S), !other_major_open(H)
      when  maybe lho.S<=4, maybe rho.S<=4     # not their suit (1D P 1H (2S) 2NT)
      priority 1
  4H  "Game in the heart fit"
      shows H + partner.H.min >= 8, fit_game_values(H)
      when  shown.H.min + partner.H.min <= 7 | partner.last=3N, partner.H.min >= 2, !partner_named(H), !slam_route, !fit_slam_room(H), !other_major_open(S)
      when  maybe lho.H<=4, maybe rho.H<=4     # not their suit (1D P 1H (2S) 2NT)
      priority 1
files.rules/base/fourth-suit-forcing.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Fourth suit forcing (2026-09-30; Rick: the game-force state is
# triggered by "2/1, or 4th suit forcing, or xyz 2d"). After three suits
# have been bid, responder's cheapest bid in the fourth, at the two level,
# is artificial: values and no clear call (no fit, no stopper, no long
# suit to rebid). It forces to game when the card says so
# (`fourth_suit_forcing.game_force`, 21GF-DEFAULT), otherwise one round.
#
# BBA (probe 2026-09-30, 1D P 1H P 1S P, responder 4-4 in hearts and
# clubs): on the game-forcing card 12 HCP bids 2NT and 14-15 bid 2C, a
# club stopper or not; on the one-round card 2C from 12.
#
# The fourth suit at the one level (1C 1D 1H 1S) stays natural.
#
# It ranks with the natural calls, not above them: with a stopper and game
# values 3NT comes first. Preferring the fourth suit as BBA does scored
# -79 on random deals and -686 on the corpus against this (notes).

module fourth-suit-forcing "Fourth suit forcing"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/fourth_suit_forcing
  param  fsf_play  = bidding_conventions/fourth_suit_forcing default false
  param  fsf_round = bidding_conventions/fourth_suit_forcing:one_round default false
  param  fsf_gf    = bidding_conventions/fourth_suit_forcing:game_force default false

# Played at all; and whether it forces to game (the card's game_force, or
# Bridge-Classroom's plain `play` without one_round).
define fsf_on = fsf_play | fsf_round | fsf_gf
define fsf_game = fsf_gf | (fsf_play, !fsf_round)


after 1x (P) 1y (P) 1z (P) | 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) when y is not x, z is not x, z is not y, !tw(x)
  cheapest(w)  "Fourth suit forcing: game values"  alert
      shows points>=13
      when  fsf_on, fsf_game, w is not x, w is not y, w is not z, cheapest_rank(w) <= 13, !passed_hand
      sets  ask=fsf(x, y, z, w), forcing=game
      artificial
  cheapest(w)  "Fourth suit forcing: 12+"  alert
      shows points>=12
      when  fsf_on, !fsf_game, w is not x, w is not y, w is not z, cheapest_rank(w) <= 13, !passed_hand
      sets  ask=fsf(x, y, z, w), forcing=round
      artificial

# Opener describes, in this order: three cards in responder's suit, a
# stopper in the fourth suit, a longer first suit, a five-card second
# suit, four cards in the fourth suit.
when asked fsf(x, y, z, w)
  cheapest(y)  "Three-card support for {y}"      shows y>=3
      priority 4
  cheapest(N)  "A stopper in {w}"                shows stop(w), y<=2
      priority 3
  cheapest(x)  "Five or more {x}"                 shows x>=5, y<=2, !stop(w)
      priority 2
  cheapest(z)  "Five or more {z} as well"         shows z>=5, y<=2, !stop(w)
      priority 1
  cheapest(w)  "Four cards in {w}"                shows w>=4, y<=2, !stop(w)
  cheapest(x)  "No support, no stopper in {w}"
      priority -5

# Responder places the contract.
when answered fsf(x, y, z, w)
  4y  "Game in the {y} fit"                       shows we.fit(y).min >= 8, points>=12
      when  y is H | y is S
  3N  "Game in notrump"                           shows points>=12
      priority -1
  P   "No game: invitational values"   shows points<=12
      when  !we.gf
      priority -5
files.rules/base/game-force.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# When the auction itself forces to game (Rick, 2026-09-30): "we should
# have a state 'in game force' that 2/1 triggers, or 4th suit forcing,
# or XYZ 2D, etc." The state is `we.forcing = game`. A rule whose call
# creates it says so with `sets forcing=game` (the two-over-one on a 2/1
# card, a strong jump shift); the declarations here are the forces that
# belong to the shape of the auction rather than to one rule's meaning,
# and apply whichever rule made or explains the call.

module game-force "When the auction forces to game"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/two_over_one
  param  wolff = bidding_conventions/wolff_signoff default false

# Responder's third bid at the three level, below game: "a 3rd bid by
# responder at the 3 level or higher is usually considered a GF" (Rick).
# 3NT and higher are game themselves. Three of a suit already agreed is
# a sign-off, not a force: 1♠-2♠-2NT-3♣-3♦-3♠ declines a game try
# (majors/game-tries.bid).
force game when partner.opened, !they.bid, me.bids = 2, call >= 3C, call <= 3S, !(we.trump is suit, call = 3{trump})

# After opener's 2NT rebid (18-19), anything but pass forces to game,
# except Wolff's 3C, which is there to stop in a part score.
force game after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2N (P) when !call = P, !(wolff, call = 3C)
files.rules/base/nmf-after-2nt.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# New Minor Forcing after opener's 2NT rebid (18-19): after 1m-1M-2NT,
# three of the other minor asks for three cards in responder's major or
# four in the other major; after 1H-1S-2NT, 3C asks for three spades. The
# auction is already game forcing (game-force.bid). BBA plays it on its
# own switch, with or without NMF after 1NT (21GF-SPECIALS2 has only this
# one). With Wolff on, 3C after 1D-1M-2NT stays Wolff's.

module nmf-after-2nt "New Minor Forcing after a 2NT rebid"
  kind   convention
  card   bidding_conventions/new_minor_forcing:after_2nt_rebid
  needs  responder-rebids
  skill  bidding_conventions/new_minor_forcing
  param  wolff = bidding_conventions/wolff_signoff default false

after 1C (P) 1M (P) 2N (P) when !tw(C)
  3D  "New Minor Forcing: three {M}? four of the other major?"   alert
      shows M>=5 | (H>=4, S>=4), M<=5, points>=7
      sets  ask=nmf2n
      artificial
      priority 1
after 1D (P) 1M (P) 2N (P) when !wolff
  3C  "New Minor Forcing: three {M}? four of the other major?"   alert
      shows M>=5 | (H>=4, S>=4), M<=5, points>=7
      sets  ask=nmf2n
      artificial
      priority 1
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 2N (P)
  3C  "New Minor Forcing: three spades?"   alert
      shows S=5, points>=7
      sets  ask=nmf2n
      artificial
      priority 1

# Opener: three of responder's major first, then four of the other major,
# else 3NT.
when asked nmf2n
  3H  "Three hearts"                       shows H=3        when partner.H>=4
  3S  "Three spades"                       shows S=3        when partner.S>=4
  3S  "Four spades, not three hearts"      shows S>=4, H<=2  when partner.H>=4
  3H  "Four hearts, not three spades"      shows H>=4, S<=2  when partner.S>=4
  3N  "No fit"                             priority -1

# Responder places the contract: game in a fit (five opposite three, or
# four-four), else 3NT. Slam tries go through the agreed suit (slam/).
when answered nmf2n
  4H  "Game in the heart fit"              shows H>=5 | (H>=4, partner.H.min>=4)   when partner.H>=3
