      when  x is H | x is S
  3N  "Game in notrump: 20+, no fit"               shows hcp>=20
      when  x is D
  P   "No game"          shows hcp<=19

after 2x (P) 2y (P) 3x (P) 3y (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is not C | two_c is natural, style is not standard, y is H | y is S
  4y  "A doubleton: game in partner's suit"        shows y>=2
  3N  "A singleton or void: 3NT"                   shows y<=1

# ── Opener's answer to 2NT ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Standard (Rick, 2026-09-24): with a maximum show a feature, an ace or
# king; without one a queen; a jack only with AK of the suit. 3NT is kept for AKQ in the
# suit. The minimum, or a maximum with nothing outside, rebids the suit.
# (bba: 3NT is a maximum with no side honour; below.)
when asked weak_two(t), ask2nt is feature, style is not bba
  3N  "Solid suit: AKQ"                            shows has(A,t), has(K,t), has(Q,t)
      priority 1
  3C  "Feature: the club ace or king, maximum"     shows has(A,C) | has(K,C), hcp>=8   when t is not C
  3D  "Feature: the diamond ace or king, maximum"  shows has(A,D) | has(K,D), hcp>=8   when t is not D
  3H  "Feature: the heart ace or king, maximum"    shows has(A,H) | has(K,H), hcp>=8   when t is not H
  3S  "Feature: the spade ace or king, maximum"    shows has(A,S) | has(K,S), hcp>=8   when t is not S
  3C  "Maximum: the club queen, no side ace or king"      shows has(Q,C), hcp>=8   when t is not C
      priority -1
  3D  "Maximum: the diamond queen, no side ace or king"   shows has(Q,D), hcp>=8   when t is not D
      priority -1
  3H  "Maximum: the heart queen, no side ace or king"     shows has(Q,H), hcp>=8   when t is not H
      priority -1
  3S  "Maximum: the spade queen, no side ace or king"     shows has(Q,S), hcp>=8   when t is not S
      priority -1
  3C  "Maximum: AK of the suit and the club jack"     shows has(A,t), has(K,t), has(J,C), hcp>=8   when t is not C
      priority -2
  3D  "Maximum: AK of the suit and the diamond jack"  shows has(A,t), has(K,t), has(J,D), hcp>=8   when t is not D
      priority -2
  3H  "Maximum: AK of the suit and the heart jack"    shows has(A,t), has(K,t), has(J,H), hcp>=8   when t is not H
      priority -2
  3S  "Maximum: AK of the suit and the spade jack"    shows has(A,t), has(K,t), has(J,S), hcp>=8   when t is not S
      priority -2
  3{t}  "Minimum, or nothing outside the suit"     shows hcp<=10
        priority -3

# bba: a maximum is 8-10; it shows a side ace, king (not singleton) or
# queen third, and bids 3NT without one. A minimum (5-7) rebids the suit.
when asked weak_two(t), ask2nt is feature, style is bba
  3C  "Feature: 8-10, A, Kx or Qxx in clubs"      shows hcp>=8, has(A,C) | (has(K,C), C>=2) | (has(Q,C), C>=3)   when t is not C
  3D  "Feature: 8-10, A, Kx or Qxx in diamonds"   shows hcp>=8, has(A,D) | (has(K,D), D>=2) | (has(Q,D), D>=3)   when t is not D
  3H  "Feature: 8-10, A, Kx or Qxx in hearts"     shows hcp>=8, has(A,H) | (has(K,H), H>=2) | (has(Q,H), H>=3)   when t is not H
  3S  "Feature: 8-10, A, Kx or Qxx in spades"     shows hcp>=8, has(A,S) | (has(K,S), S>=2) | (has(Q,S), S>=3)   when t is not S
  3N  "Maximum: 8-10, no side feature"               shows hcp>=8
  3{t}  "Minimum, 5-7"                                      shows hcp<=7

# Ogust (bridgebum.com/ogust.php): a minimum is 5-7, a maximum 8-10
# (the feature answers' maximum too); a good suit two of the top three
# honours; 3NT all three. Until 2026-10-07 the split was 6/7, which sent
# every 7-count to the maximum answers (BBA: 7 is a minimum on all 77
# corpus boards) and game opposite it (notes).
when asked weak_two(t), ask2nt is ogust
  3C  "Ogust: minimum, poor suit"   shows hcp<=7, quality(t)<=1   artificial
  3D  "Ogust: minimum, good suit"   shows hcp<=7, quality(t)>=2   artificial
  3H  "Ogust: maximum, poor suit"  shows hcp>=8, quality(t)<=1   artificial
  3S  "Ogust: maximum, good suit"  shows hcp>=8, quality(t)>=2   artificial
  3N  "Ogust: the top three honours"      shows quality(t)=3
      priority 1

after 2x (P) 2N (P) 3N (P) 4x (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is C | x is D, style is bba
  5x  "A shortness: game in the minor"   shows shortest<=1
  P   "No shortness: play four"          shows shortest>=2

# ── Responder after the answer: place the contract, never pass an
# artificial answer.
# bba: facing a maximum (anything but three of the suit) the 2NT asker
# bids game: four of a major, 3NT over a minor-suit feature. Over a 3NT
# answer to 2D it passes with 17+ and bids 4D with 15-16; opener then
# bids 5D with a singleton or void, and passes without.
when answered weak_two(t), style is bba, !partner.last=3{t}
  4{t}  "Game: to play"   shows hcp>=13
        when  t is H | t is S
        priority 1
  3N    "Game: to play"   shows hcp>=13
        when  t is C | t is D, !partner.last=3N
        priority 1
  P     "To play: 3NT"          shows hcp>=17
        when  t is C | t is D, partner.last=3N
        priority 1
  4{t}  "Doubt about 3NT: 15-16"         shows hcp<=16
        when  t is C | t is D, partner.last=3N
        priority 1

# Slam values with opener's suit as trump: 33 HCP on partner's floor
# (2026-09-27), or slam-entry's count with no two bare side suits.
define w2_slam(t) = hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 33 | (fit_slam_values(t), !two_bare_beside(t))

# Partner's 3NT answer showed AKQ of the suit (Ogust, or the standard
# feature answers; bba's 3NT is a maximum with no side honour).
define w2_solid = partner.last=3N, ask2nt is ogust | style is not bba

# The ask: two trumps and the values, or a singleton opposite AKQ with
# 21 of mine and no five-card major of my own (Ogust 45, 271: a minor
# slam one trick short where my major or notrump made twelve).
define w2_fit_slam(t) = (t>=2, w2_slam(t)) | (w2_solid, t>=1, hcp>=21, S<=4 | t is S, H<=4 | t is H)

when answered weak_two(t)
  # Slam values opposite the answer (2026-09-27, ticket b201: 26 HCP
  # opposite a maximum with a feature stopped in 4H): agree the suit and
  # ask for keycards, with 33 HCP between us counting partner at the
  # floor of his answer.
  #
  # Slam after the answer (2026-10-09, notes "Slam after the answer"):
  # the 2NT ask is artificial, so no notrump has been bid, and opener's
  # six-card suit is the public fit: 4NT is keycard in it (Rick,
  # 2026-10-03: 4NT with no notrump bid is keycard, for the last suit
  # bid). The values are slam-entry's count (`fit_slam_values`) with two
  # or more trumps; opposite the AKQ answer (3NT, Ogust or the standard
  # feature treatment) a singleton is fit enough, and 21 of mine with the
  # 9 of AKQ make the 30 a minor slam needs.
  4N    "Keycard ask in {t}"          shows w2_fit_slam(t)
        when  rkcb
        sets  trump=t, ask=keycards(t)
        artificial
        priority 2
  4N    "Blackwood: aces, {t} agreed"  shows w2_fit_slam(t)
        when  aces, !rkcb
        sets  trump=t, ask=aces
        artificial
        priority 2
  # My own major, with no fit for partner's suit and slam interest
  # (2026-10-09): natural and forcing at the three level, below 3NT
  # (bridgebum: "rebids by the Ogust bidder are natural"). 27 between us
  # on partner's floor: 22 facing a minimum, 19 facing a maximum.
  # Opener raises with three; the raise agrees it and the keycard ask
  # follows (rkcb-1430.bid).
  3S    "Natural: five or more spades, slam interest"   shows S>=5, S>=H, t<=1, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 27
        when  t is not S, partner.last=3C | partner.last=3D | partner.last=3H
        sets  forcing=game
        priority 3
  3H    "Natural: five or more hearts, slam interest"   shows H>=5, H>S, t<=1, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 27
        when  t is not H, partner.last=3C | partner.last=3D
        sets  forcing=game
        priority 3
  4{t}  "Game in the weak two suit"   shows hcp>=17
        when  t is H | t is S
  3N    "Game in notrump"             shows hcp>=17
        when  t is C | t is D
  # Opposite a maximum game needs less (Rick, 2026-09-28, ticket
  # basic-weak-2-b278: 16 opposite 3C, a maximum with a club feature,
  # signed off in 3H). The answers record partner's range: counting him
  # at its floor, game with 21 between us, so every asker (13+) facing
  # a feature or an Ogust maximum (both 8-10); facing a minimum (4)
  # the 17 above still rules. 21 beat 22 and 23 on both
  # yardsticks (notes).
  4{t}  "Game: to play"   shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 21
        when  t is H | t is S
        priority 1
  3N    "Game: to play"   shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 21
        when  t is C | t is D
        priority 1
  P     "To play"
        when  partner.last=3{t}
  4{t}  "Sign off in {t}"    shows hcp<=16
        when  partner.last=3N, t is H | t is S
  3{t}  "Sign off in {t}"             shows hcp<=16
  3N    "To play in 3NT"   shows hcp<=16
        priority -1
  4{t}  "Sign off in {t}"       shows hcp<=16
        when  t is H | t is S
        priority -2
  P     "No game"                     shows hcp<=16
        priority -5

# Opener after responder's three of the suit over a higher answer: a
# sign-off, passed. BBA bid on over 2♦-2NT-3♣-3♦ in four Basic_Weak_2
# boards (3NT twice, 4♦, 5♦); passing was closer to par in three of them
# (notes, 2026-09-25).
after 2x (P) 2N (P) 3y (P) 3x (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is not C | two_c is natural, y is not x
  P   "No further bid"

# Opener after responder's own major over the answer (2026-10-09): raise
# with three, which agrees it; else 3NT.
after 2x (P) 2N (P) 3y (P) 3z (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is not C | two_c is natural, z is H | z is S, z is not x, y is not z
  4z  "Three-card support: agrees {z}"   shows z>=3
      sets  trump=z
  3N  "No support for {z}"               shows z<=2

# Responder after opener's 3NT, no support for my major: slam in
# notrump on 33 between us, game in my suit with six, else pass.
after 2x (P) 2N (P) 3y (P) 3z (P) 3N (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is not C | two_c is natural, z is H | z is S, z is not x, y is not z
  6N  "Slam in notrump"   shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 33
  4z  "Six-card suit: game in it"        shows z>=6
  P   "To play"

# Opener after the preemptive raise: pass.
after 2x (P) 3x (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is not C | two_c is natural
  P   "No further bid"
files.rules/base/xyz.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# XYZ (Robert S. Todd, Adventures in Bridge #587; convention-card
# bidding_conventions/xyz): after three one-level bids, 1x-1y-1z,
# responder's 2♣ relays to 2♦ (every invitational hand starts here, and a
# weak hand with diamonds passes 2♦), 2♦ is an artificial game force, and
# 2NT relays to 3♣ (weak with clubs). Other calls are natural and weak or
# as before (responder-rebids.bid). After 1x-1y-1NT the same structure is
# two-way New Minor Forcing, which two-way-nmf.bid plays when this card
# field is on. The relay and game-force answers are two-way-nmf.bid's
# (`xy_relay`, `xy_clubs`, `xy_gf`). See xyz.notes.md.

module xyz "XYZ: 2♣ relay and 2♦ game force after three one-level bids"
  kind   convention
  card   bidding_conventions/xyz
  needs  two-way-nmf
  skill  bidding_conventions/xyz

after 1x (P) 1y (P) 1z (P) when !tw(x)
  2C  "XYZ: relay to 2♦, invitational or a diamond sign-off"   alert
      shows points=11..12 | (points<=10, D>=6 | (x is D, D>=4, z<=2))
      sets  forcing=round, ask=xy_relay
      artificial
      priority 2
  2D  "XYZ: artificial game force"   alert
      shows points>=13
      sets  forcing=game, ask=xy_gf
      artificial
      priority 2
  2N  "XYZ: relay to 3♣, a club sign-off"   alert
      shows points<=10, C>=6 | (x is C, C>=5, z<=2)
      sets  forcing=round, ask=xy_clubs
      artificial
      priority 2

# ── After the 2♦ relay: weak with diamonds passes, every other call invites
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 1z (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) when !tw(x)
  P   "To play in 2♦"                      shows points<=10
  2y  "Invitational: five {y}"             shows y=5, points=11..12   sets ask=invite(y)
      when  y is H | y is S
  3y  "Invitational: six {y}"              shows y>=6, points=11..12   sets ask=invite(y)
  3z  "Invitational raise: four {z}"       shows z>=4, tp(z)=11..12   sets ask=invite(z)
  2N  "Invitational, balanced"             shows points=11..12, z<=3   sets ask=nt_invite
      priority -1
  3x  "Invitational: four {x}"             shows x>=4, points=11..12, z<=3   sets ask=invite(x)
      when  x is C | x is D
      priority -2
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 1z (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) when !tw(x)
  P   "To play in 3♣"                      shows C>=4
files.rules/competitive/advances.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Advancer: partner has overcalled, and it is our turn.
#
# Ranges follow BBA's Basic-Bridge meanings, which are the usual ones.
# Over a one-level overcall a raise is 7-11 total points with three-card
# support, a new suit 8+ with four cards at the one level and 9+ with
# five at the two, 1NT 8-11 balanced with a stopper in their suit, and
# the cue bid of their suit a limit raise or better (12+ with three).
# The jump raise is weak. With `overcalls.responses.jump_cuebid_mixed`
# the jump cue bid is a mixed raise: four trumps, 7-9 support points.
#
# An overcall is not forcing, so advancer passes with less; there is no
# forced bid here as there is after a takeout double.
#
# The file then covers, in order: advancer when RHO does not pass, the
# balancing overcall (partner is 8-15 there, so everything costs about
# two points more), the two-level overcall — simple or a weak jump, and
# they need different answers — advancer over RHO's 1NT, and the
# overcaller's reply to the cue-bid raise.
#
# Not written yet (beyond the rebid after a new suit, at the end):
# advancer's continuations once the overcaller has
# rebid, and the support cue bid.
#
# Advancing a 1NT overcall needs nothing here: systems are on, and the
# notrump modules carry the `(1x) 1N (P)` spelling of their patterns.

module advances "Advancing partner's overcall"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  needs  overcalls
  skill  competitive_bidding/advancing_overcalls
  skill  competitive_bidding/support_cuebids
  skill  competitive_bidding/mixed_raise
  param  jump_raise = overcalls.responses.jump_raise default weak
  param  mixed      = competitive_bidding/mixed_raise default false

after (1x) 1y (P)
  2{y} "Raise: 8-11 with three {y}, up to 11 with four"
      shows y>=3, hcp+length_points<=11, hcp+length_points>=8 | y>=4
  3{y} "Preemptive raise: five {y}, four at favourable; under 8 points"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points<=7
      shows weak_jump_raise(y)          # one trump more than the Law for a weak hand (total-tricks.bid)
      priority 1                        # before the raise to two, which a weak four-card hand also fits
      when  jump_raise is weak
  1S  "8+ total points, four or more spades"
      shows S>=4, hcp+length_points>=8
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  1N  "8-11 total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp+length_points<=11
      when  stop(x)
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
      when  y<=2 | y is C | y is D
  cheapest(C) "9+ total points, five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  x is not C, y is not C
  cheapest(D) "9+ total points, five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(H) "9+ total points, five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  2{x} "Cue bid: limit raise or better in {y}"
      alert  artificial
      shows  y>=3, hcp+length_points>=12
      sets   forcing=round, ask=cue_raise(y)
  # A five-card major that can be shown at the one level comes first
  # (Rick, 2026-11-09: the Brill field bid 1H, 8 of 8, with
  # QT6.A8643.J9.KJ5 over 1C 1D Pass). Over a 1S overcall 2NT stays:
  # 2H there measured worse (3 boards, -24 IMPs).
  2N  "12-15 total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp+length_points<=15, H<=4 | y is S, S<=4
      when  stop(x), y<=2
  3{x} "Mixed raise: 4+ {y}, 7-9 support points"
      alert  artificial
      shows  y>=4, tp(y)=7..9
      when   mixed, !vul
      sets   ask=mixed_raise(y)
      priority 2                        # ahead of the raise to two and the preemptive raise, which these hands also fit
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# ── Advancing a balancing overcall ───────────────────────────────────
# Partner reopened, so he is 8-15 rather than 8-17 and some of his values
# are borrowed from us: everything costs about two points more than in
# the direct seat. BBA's Balancing meanings: the raise 9-11, 1NT 10-11,
# a new suit at the one level 7-9, the cue bid 13+.
after (1x) P (P) 1y (P)
  2{y} "Raise: 9-11 total points, three-card support"
      shows y>=3, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp+length_points<=11
  3{y} "Preemptive raise: four-card support, under 9 points"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points<=8
      when  jump_raise is weak
  1S  "7+ total points, four or more spades"
      shows S>=4, hcp+length_points>=7
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  1N  "10-11 total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp+length_points<=11
      when  stop(x)
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
      when  y<=2 | y is C | y is D
  cheapest(C) "11+ total points, five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, hcp+length_points>=11
      when  x is not C, y is not C
  cheapest(D) "11+ total points, five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, hcp+length_points>=11
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(H) "11+ total points, five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, hcp+length_points>=11
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  2{x} "Cue bid: limit raise or better in {y}"
      alert  artificial
      shows  y>=3, hcp+length_points>=13
      sets   forcing=round, ask=cue_raise(y)
  2N  "13-15 total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=13, hcp+length_points<=15
      when  stop(x), y<=2
  P   "Not enough to advance a reopening bid"  priority -10

# ── Advancer when RHO does not pass ──────────────────────────────────
# RHO has doubled or bid over the overcall. Support is still the first
# thing to show, and raising at once takes bidding room from them.
after (1x) 1y (X) | (1x) P (P) 1y (X)
  2{y} "Raise: 8-11 with three {y}, up to 11 with four"
      shows y>=3, hcp+length_points<=11, hcp+length_points>=8 | y>=4
  3{y} "Preemptive raise: five {y}, four at favourable; under 8 points"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points<=7
      shows weak_jump_raise(y)          # one trump more than the Law for a weak hand (total-tricks.bid)
      priority 1                        # before the raise to two, which a weak four-card hand also fits
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

after (1x) 1y (1z) | (1x) P (P) 1y (1z)
  2{y} "Raise: 8-11 with three {y}, up to 11 with four"
      shows y>=3, hcp+length_points<=11, hcp+length_points>=8 | y>=4
  3{y} "Preemptive raise: five {y}, four at favourable; under 8 points"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points<=7
      shows weak_jump_raise(y)          # one trump more than the Law for a weak hand (total-tricks.bid)
      priority 1                        # before the raise to two, which a weak four-card hand also fits
  1N  "8-11 total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp+length_points<=11
      when  stop(x), y<=2
  cheapest(S) "Free bid: 9+ total points, five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  x is not S, y is not S, z is not S
  cheapest(H) "Free bid: 9+ total points, five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, S<=4, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  x is not H, y is not H, z is not H
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# The mixed raise holds over RHO's double or one-level bid too (BBA's
# `Mixed raise` switch plays it there and only there: advances.notes.md,
# "Mixed raise"). The direct seat only: a balancing
# overcall's ranges are two points higher. Not vulnerable only, in both
# places: BBA's limit, and the jump to three vulnerable drew the
# penalty doubles (contract errors -100 -> +4 in the self A/B).
after (1x) 1y (X) | (1x) 1y (1z)
  3{x} "Mixed raise: 4+ {y}, 7-9 support points"
      alert  artificial
      shows  y>=4, tp(y)=7..9
      when   mixed, !vul
      sets   ask=mixed_raise(y)
      priority 2                        # ahead of the raise to two and the preemptive raise, which these hands also fit

after (1x) 1y (2z) | (1x) P (P) 1y (2z)
  2{y} "Raise: 7-11 total points, three-card support"
      shows y>=3, hcp+length_points>=7, hcp+length_points<=11
  3{y} "Raise: four-card support, 8-11 total points"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp+length_points<=11
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# ── Advancing a two-level overcall ───────────────────────────────────
# `(*)` is any call by RHO, so this covers the seat however he has
# answered the overcall, and passing is much the commonest advance.
#
# `y is not x` throughout: their opening bid repeated by partner would
# be a cue bid (Michaels), not an overcall.
after (1x) 2y (*) | (1x) P (P) 2y (*) when y is not x
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# Advancer bids only while RHO has left him room: his pass, his double,
# or his simple raise of their own suit. Once RHO has bid a suit of his
# own, or notrump, or jumped, BBA's advancer passes, and so do we — the
# context above is then the only one that matches. A two-level overcall
# in the balancing seat is passed out for the same reason.

# A weak jump overcall is a six-card suit, so three-card support is nine
# trumps and the raise is a further preempt: partner is not invited to
# do anything. The `when` is the complement of the simple-overcall one
# below: "y could have been bid at the one level over x".
after (1x) 2y (P) | (1x) 2y (X) | (1x) 2y (2x) when y is not x, x is C | (x is D, y is not C) | (x is H, y is S)
  4{y} "Raise to game: four-card support, 11+"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points>=11
      when  y is H | y is S
  3{y} "Preemptive raise: three-card support, under 11 points"
      shows y>=3, hcp+length_points<=10
      when  y is H | y is S
  3{y} "Preemptive raise: four-card support, under 11 points"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points<=10
      when  y is C | y is D

# The rest only when the overcall was a *simple* two-level overcall,
# where partner has 12-17 and an opening hand to go with it. The `when`
# spells out "y could not have been bid at the one level over x": over
# 1C every two-level suit is a jump, over 1D only clubs is simple, over
# 1H everything but spades, and over 1S all three.
after (1x) 2y (P) | (1x) 2y (X) | (1x) 2y (2x) when y is not x, x is S | (x is H, y is not S) | (x is D, y is C)
  4{y} "Raise to game in partner's major: four-card support, 13+"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points>=13
      when  y is H | y is S
  3{y} "Raise: 7-10 total points, four-card support"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points>=7, hcp+length_points<=10
  cheapest(x) "Cue bid: limit raise or better in {y}"
      alert  artificial
      shows  y>=3, hcp+length_points>=11
      sets   forcing=round, ask=cue_raise(y)
  2N  "11-12 total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp+length_points<=12
      when  stop(x), y<=2
  3N  "13+ total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=13
      when  stop(x), y<=2
  cheapest(S) "10+ total points, five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "10+ total points, five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, S<=4, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(D) "12+ total points, five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=12
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(C) "12+ total points, five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=12
      when  x is not C, y is not C

# ── Advancer over RHO's 1NT ──────────────────────────────────────────
# `after (1x) 1y (1z)` binds a suit, so RHO's 1NT left advancer with no
# rule at all. Support is still the first thing to show.
after (1x) 1y (1N) | (1x) P (P) 1y (1N)
  2{y} "Raise: 9-11 total points, three-card support"
      shows y>=3, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp+length_points<=11
  cheapest(x) "Cue bid: limit raise or better in {y}"
      alert  artificial
      shows  y>=3, hcp+length_points>=12
      sets   forcing=round, ask=cue_raise(y)
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# ── The overcaller answers advancer's cue bid ────────────────────────
# The cue showed three-card support and a limit raise or better, so the
# overcall's own range decides: a minimum signs off in the suit, and
# 13+ total points bids the game. Written against the question, so it is
# the same rule whatever level the cue was made at.
when asked cue_raise(t)
  4{t} "Accepts: game in {t}"
      shows hcp+length_points>=13
      when  t is H | t is S
  3N  "Accepts: 13+ balanced, game in notrump"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=13
      when  t is C | t is D
  cheapest(t) "Minimum: signs off"
      priority -1

# Over the mixed raise (7-9 support points, four trumps): game wants
# about 25, so 16 or more bids it; else three of the suit, which the jump
# cuebid always leaves room for over a one-level overcall.
after (1x) 1y (P) 3x (P) | (1x) 1y (X) 3x (P) | (1x) 1y (1z) 3x (P)
  4{y} "Accepts: game in {y}"
      shows hcp+length_points>=16
      when  mixed, y is H | y is S
  3N  "Accepts: 16+ balanced, game in notrump"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=16, stop(x)
      when  mixed, y is C | y is D
  3{y} "Minimum: signs off"
      when  mixed
      priority -1

# ── The overcaller's rebid after a new suit (2026-09-25) ──────────────
# Advancer's new suit is not forcing. No rules existed (~90 corpus
# boards where BBA bid). BBA: raise with four, rebid a six-card suit,
# 1NT with 11-14 balanced and their suit held; otherwise pass.
after (1x) 1y (P) 1z (P)
  2{z} "Four-card support"                   shows z>=4
  2{y} "Six or more {y}"                     shows y>=6, z<=3
      priority -1
  1N  "11-14 balanced, {x} held"             shows balanced, hcp>=11, hcp<=14, stop(x), z<=3
  P   "No further bid"                  priority -5
after (1x) 1y (P) 2z (P)
  3{z} "Four-card support"                   shows z>=4, hcp>=11
  2{y} "Six or more {y}"                     shows y>=6, z<=3
      when  y is not C
      priority -1
  P   "No further bid"                  priority -5

# The overcaller again after (1x) 1y (2x) P (P): BBA rebids a six-card
# suit with 12+ (2026-09-25). It also doubles for takeout with a
# singleton in their suit and 13+; that double cost IMPs against par.
# The rebid is at the two level: a one-level overcall outranks their
# suit, so 2{y} is always there, and 3{y} was a jump. On bare SAYC BBA
# rebids 2{y} with six from 10 HCP (2026-10-02, 88 hands).
after (1x) 1y (2x) P (P)
  2{y} "Competes: six or more {y}"           shows y>=6, hcp>=10
  P   "No further bid"                          priority -5

# ── Advancing from the sandwich seat ─────────────────────────────────
# Partner came in after (1x) P (1y) (overcalls.bid, 2026-10-07). I have
# passed once, and both of them have bid: raise with support, compete to
# the three level with four, preempt with four and a weak hand. A new
# suit or notrump is not written: a passed hand with neither support
# nor a fit passes.
after (1x) P (1y) 1z (*) | (1x) P (1y) 2z (*) when z is not x, z is not y
  cheapest(z) "Raise: three-card support, 7+ total points"
      shows z>=3, hcp+length_points>=7
      when  cheapest_rank(z)<=13                 # the two level
  cheapest(z) "Competitive raise to three: four-card support"
      shows z>=4, hcp+length_points>=6
      when  cheapest_rank(z)>=15, cheapest_rank(z)<=18
  jump(z) "Preemptive raise: four-card support, weak"
      shows z>=4, hcp+length_points<=7
      shows weak_jump_raise(z)                   # total-tricks.bid
      when  cheapest_rank(z)<=13, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
      priority 1
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# Partner's takeout double of the two suits they have not bid: answer in
# the longer (a major with equal length), a jump with 9-11 and four
# cards, 1NT with both their suits stopped and nothing to bid, else the
# longer unbid suit however short.
after (1x) P (1y) X (P) when y is not x
  cheapest(S) "Answers the double: four or more spades"
      shows S>=4, S>=H | x is H | y is H, S>=D | x is D | y is D, S>=C | x is C | y is C, hcp<=8
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Answers the double: four or more hearts"
      shows H>=4, H>S | x is S | y is S, H>=D | x is D | y is D, H>=C | x is C | y is C, hcp<=8
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(D) "Answers the double: four or more diamonds"
      shows D>=4, D>S | x is S | y is S, D>H | x is H | y is H, D>=C | x is C | y is C, hcp<=8
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(C) "Answers the double: four or more clubs"
      shows C>=4, C>S | x is S | y is S, C>H | x is H | y is H, C>D | x is D | y is D, hcp<=8
      when  x is not C, y is not C
  jump(S) "Jump answer: four or more spades, 9-11"
      shows S>=4, S>=H | x is H | y is H, hcp>=9
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  jump(H) "Jump answer: four or more hearts, 9-11"
      shows H>=4, H>S | x is S | y is S, hcp>=9
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  jump(D) "Jump answer: four or more diamonds, 9-11"
      shows D>=4, D>S | x is S | y is S, D>H | x is H | y is H, hcp>=9
      when  x is not D, y is not D, cheapest_rank(D)<=13
  jump(C) "Jump answer: four or more clubs, 9-11"
      shows C>=4, C>S | x is S | y is S, C>H | x is H | y is H, C>D | x is D | y is D, hcp>=9
      when  x is not C, y is not C, cheapest_rank(C)<=13
  1N  "6-10, both their suits stopped"
      shows hcp>=6, hcp<=10, stop(x), stop(y)
      priority -1
  # The forced answer without four cards: the longer unbid suit.
  cheapest(S) "Answers the double: three spades"
      shows S>=3, S>=H | x is H | y is H, S>=D | x is D | y is D, S>=C | x is C | y is C
      when  x is not S, y is not S
      priority -2
  cheapest(H) "Answers the double: three hearts"
      shows H>=3, H>=D | x is D | y is D, H>=C | x is C | y is C
      when  x is not H, y is not H
      priority -3
  cheapest(D) "Answers the double: the longer unbid suit"
      when  x is not D, y is not D
      priority -4
  cheapest(C) "Answers the double: the longer unbid suit"
      when  x is not C, y is not C
      priority -5

after (1x) P (1y) X (*) when y is not x, !rho.last=P
  cheapest(S) "Free bid: four or more spades"
      shows S>=4, hcp+length_points>=7
      when  x is not S, y is not S, cheapest_rank(S)<=13
  cheapest(H) "Free bid: four or more hearts"
      shows H>=4, S<=H | x is S | y is S, hcp+length_points>=7
      when  x is not H, y is not H, cheapest_rank(H)<=13
  cheapest(D) "Free bid: five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, hcp+length_points>=7
      when  x is not D, y is not D, cheapest_rank(D)<=13
  cheapest(C) "Free bid: five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, hcp+length_points>=7
      when  x is not C, y is not C, cheapest_rank(C)<=13
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# ── Advancer after partner's overcall of their 1NT ───────────────────
# The overcall is five cards and 12+ total points (overcalls.bid); RHO
# has 15-17. Advancer passes (added 2026-09-25: no rule matched).
# Competitive raises were tried and lost 26 IMPs to the advancing side
# over the corpus, par neutral (nt-interference.notes.md).
after (1N) 2y (*) | (1N) 3y (*)
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# ── The defending side once the opening side bids on ─────────────────
# They opened; we have overcalled, advanced or raised, and they have bid
# again. Each of us has described his hand once, so with nothing new to
# say the call is a pass. A fallback below every real rule (2026-09-25:
# 63 no-rule positions in the Basic_* N/S boards came from here, e.g.
# 1S (2D) 2S (P) 4S and 1S (2D) X (3D) 3H). Positions where the
# defending side has more to say need rules of their own above this.
when lho.opened | rho.opened
  P   "No further bid"
      when  !passes_out_artificial   # never pass out our own artificial bid (base.bid)
      priority -20
files.rules/competitive/after-interference.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Responder's call when RHO has overcalled or doubled partner's one-level
# opening (Rick, 2026-09-22): negative doubles through 3S, and natural
# bids otherwise.
#
# The uncontested rules in responses.bid are written as `after 1x (P)`
# patterns, so none of them fire once the opponents come in; everything
# responder needs over interference is here.
#
# Negative double: 6+ total points with four or more cards in each unbid
# major, so a suit bid in the only unbid major promises five. Where both
# majors are bid (1H-(1S)) the double shows the minors instead.
#
# Opener's answer to the negative double is written once with relative
# calls, so it is right at every level they push us to, and there is a
# separate block for the auctions where they compete over the double.
#
# Not written yet: their 1NT overcall, jump shifts, opener's rebid after
# anything but a negative double, and responder's second call once the
# auction has been contested.

module after-interference "Our side once the opponents come in"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  skill  competitive_bidding/after_their_overcall
  skill  competitive_bidding/negative_doubles
  skill  competitive_bidding/support_cuebids
  param  neg = competitive_bidding/negative_doubles default true
  param  cue_raise = competitive_bidding/support_cuebids default true
  param  new_suit_forcing = competitive.new_suit_after_overcall_forcing default true
  param  js = competitive.jump_shift_after_overcall default weak
  param  fsj = competitive_bidding/fit_showing_jumps default false
  param  tfr = bidding_conventions/transfers_after_double default false

# ── They overcalled at the one level ─────────────────────────────────
after 1x (1y) when neg
  X   "Negative double: 6+ total points, the unbid suits"
      alert  artificial
      shows  hcp+length_points>=6
      shows  (S>=4 | x is S | y is S), (H>=4 | x is H | y is H)
      shows  ((D>=4 | x is D | y is D), (C>=4 | x is C | y is C)) | S>=4 | H>=4
      when   (S<=4 | x is S | y is S), (H<=4 | x is H | y is H | (y is S, hcp<=7))
      when   x<=2 | x is C | x is D     # support for a major: raise first (2026-09-25)
      priority 1
  # (the y-is-S clause) Five hearts over 1S and too weak for 2H: BBA
  # doubles (probes/free-bid-1D-1S.toml: 12 of 12 with 6 HCP).

# ── Trap pass ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# With negative doubles on, responder cannot double their overcall for
# penalty. With length and strength in their suit he passes instead and
# hopes opener reopens with a double (rebids.bid), which he then passes
# (responder-rebids.bid). The holding: four or more with two of the top
# three or three of the top five (Rick's penalty-double standard,
# 2026-09-23), and 8+ HCP. The condition is `when`, not `shows`: a pass
# still says nothing, so opener does not read every pass as a trap. Not
# disclosed as a possible trap either: it is the same "No suitable bid" as
# every other pass here, and usually is one (Rick, 2026-10-29).
after 1x (1y) | 1x (2y) when y is not x, neg
  P   "No suitable bid"
      when  y>=4, quality(y)>=good | top5(y)>=3, hcp>=8, x<=2
      priority 2

after 1x (1y)
  1S  "6+ total points, four or more spades"
      shows S>=4, hcp+length_points>=6
      when  x is not S, y is not S
      when  S>=5 | (x is not H, y is not H, H<=3)
  1H  "6+ total points, four or more hearts"
      shows H>=4, hcp+length_points>=6
      when  x is not H, y is not H, y is not S
      when  H>=5 | (x is not S, y is not S, S<=3)
  1N  "6-10 total points, balanced, a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=6, hcp+length_points<=10
      when  stop(y)
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
  2{x} "Raise: 6-9 total points, support for partner's suit"
      shows x>=3, hcp+length_points>=6, hcp+length_points<=9
      shows minor_raise(x)                # eight trumps: five over a minor (total-tricks.bid)
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
  # BBA's 1C (1S) 3C (2026-09-27, ticket b469): the jump raise over an
  # overcall is preemptive, as over the double.
  jump(x) "Preemptive raise: five-card support, six in a minor, under 8"
      shows x>=5, hcp+length_points<=7
      shows minor_preempt(x)              # nine trumps: six over a minor (total-tricks.bid)
  cheapest(C) "8+ total points, five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, hcp+length_points>=8
      when  x is not C, y is not C, new_suit_forcing
      sets  forcing=round
  cheapest(D) "8+ total points, five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, hcp+length_points>=8
      when  x is not D, y is not D, new_suit_forcing
      sets  forcing=round
  2H  "8+ total points, five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, hcp+length_points>=8
      when  y is S, x is not H, new_suit_forcing
      sets  forcing=round
  # Not forcing (Basic-Bridge): limited to 12, and 13+ jumps, forcing to
  # game, as over a two-level overcall (below).
  cheapest(C) "8-12 total points, five or more clubs, not forcing"
      shows C>=5, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp<=12
      when  x is not C, y is not C, !new_suit_forcing
  cheapest(D) "8-12 total points, five or more diamonds, not forcing"
      shows D>=5, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp<=12
      when  x is not D, y is not D, !new_suit_forcing
  2H  "8-12 total points, five or more hearts, not forcing"
      shows H>=5, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp<=12
      when  y is S, x is not H, !new_suit_forcing
  jump(C) "13+ total points, five or more clubs: forcing to game"
      shows C>=5, hcp>=13
      when  x is not C, y is not C, !new_suit_forcing, js is strong
      when  H<=4 | y is not S | x is H     # 5-5 with hearts: the higher suit
      sets  forcing=game
  jump(D) "13+ total points, five or more diamonds: forcing to game"
      shows D>=5, hcp>=13
      when  x is not D, y is not D, !new_suit_forcing, js is strong
      when  H<=4 | y is not S | x is H     # 5-5 with hearts: the higher suit
      sets  forcing=game
  3H  "13+ total points, five or more hearts: forcing to game"
      shows H>=5, hcp>=13
      when  y is S, x is not H, !new_suit_forcing, js is strong
      sets  forcing=game
  # Limit raise or better, and the notrump responses (2026-09-26: over a
  # one-level overcall these existed only over two-level ones, so 11-16
  # counts with a fit or a stopper passed; 40 corpus boards with 25+ HCP
  # and game on).
  cheapest(y) "Cue bid: limit raise or better in {x}"
      alert  artificial
      shows  x>=3, hcp+length_points>=11
      when   cue_raise, x is H | x is S | x>=4
      sets   forcing=round
      priority 1
  2N  "11-12 total points, balanced, a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp+length_points<=12
      when  stop(y)
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  3N  "13+ total points, balanced, a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=13
      when  stop(y)
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
  P   "No suitable bid"  priority -10

# Opener when they raise over the one-level cue bid: game in a major
# with 16+, else let it go (the cue bid is no longer forcing).
after 1x (1y) 2y (3y) when y is not x
  4{x} "Game: 16+"   shows hcp>=16
       when  x is H | x is S
  3N   "Game: 16+ with a stopper in {y}"       shows hcp>=16, stop(y)
       when  x is C | x is D
  5{x} "Game: 16+, no stopper in {y}"          shows hcp>=16
       when  x is C | x is D
       priority -1
  # The minor cue bid promised four, so a fifth card is nine trumps:
  # compete at the four level (2026-09-27: these hands passed once the
  # round force ended with their raise, -159 IMPs by side on 57 boards).
  4{x} "Competes: five or more {x}"
       shows x>=5
       when  x is C | x is D
       priority -4
  P    "No game"
       priority -5

# Responder once opener has passed their raise, or competed in his
# minor: the cue bid was 11+ with no upper limit, so with 13+ responder
# bids the game himself.
after 1x (1y) 2y (3y) P (P) when y is not x
  4{x} "Game: 13+"   shows hcp+length_points>=13
       when  x is H | x is S
  3N   "Game: 13+ with a stopper in {y}"       shows hcp+length_points>=13, stop(y)
       when  x is C | x is D
  5{x} "Game in the minor: 14+"                shows hcp+length_points>=14
       when  x is C | x is D
       priority -1
  P    "Limit raise only"
       priority -5
after 1x (1y) 2y (3y) 4x (P) when x is C | x is D, y is not x
  5{x} "Game in the minor: 13+"  shows hcp+length_points>=13
  P    "Limit raise only"
       priority -5

# ── Weak jump shifts over their one-level overcall ───────────────────
# `competitive.jump_shift_after_overcall` = weak (the 21GF cards): a
# jump in a new suit is preemptive, a six-card suit and little else
# (ACBL convention card, "Jump shift in competition: weak"; BBA alerts
# it "1X-(1Y)-2Z weak", 1-10 HCP, median 6, six cards, and only at the
# two level: a three-level jump it never makes, it passes). With
# support for partner's major a raise comes first. A passed hand's jump
# is fit-showing when the card plays those (fit-showing-jumps.bid).
# With `strong`, the 13+ jumps above (when a new suit is not forcing).
after 1x (1y) when y is not x, js is weak, !passed_hand | !fsj
  jump(S) "Weak jump shift: six or more spades, 2-7 HCP"
      shows S>=6, hcp=2..7
      when  x is not S, y is not S, cheapest_rank(S) <= 8
      when  x<=2 | x is C | x is D
      priority 2
  jump(H) "Weak jump shift: six or more hearts, 2-7 HCP"
      shows H>=6, hcp=2..7
      when  x is not H, y is not H, cheapest_rank(H) <= 8
      when  x<=2 | x is C | x is D
      priority 2
# Opener passes the weak jump unless something else fits better.
after 1x (1y) 2z (P) when partner.jumped, js is weak, z is not x, z is not y
  P   "No further bid"             priority -5

# ── They overcalled at the two level or jumped ───────────────────────
# Rick: over a two-level overcall a new suit is 10+ total points with five
# cards and forcing, and the negative double is 8+ with four. At the three
# level the free bid needs another point.
after 1x (2y) | 1x (3y) when y is not x
  X   "Negative double: 8+ total points, the unbid suits"
      alert  artificial
      shows  hcp+length_points>=8
      shows  (S>=4 | x is S | y is S), (H>=4 | x is H | y is H)
      shows  ((D>=4 | x is D | y is D), (C>=4 | x is C | y is C)) | S>=4 | H>=4
      when   (S<=4 | x is S | y is S), (H<=4 | x is H | y is H)
      when   neg
      priority 1
  cheapest(y) "Cue bid: limit raise or better in {x}"
      alert  artificial
      shows  x>=3, hcp+length_points>=11
      when   cue_raise
      sets   forcing=round
      priority 1
  cheapest(x) "Raise: 7-10, three-card support, five in a minor"
      shows x>=3, hcp+length_points>=7, hcp+length_points<=10
      shows minor_raise(x)                # eight trumps: five over a minor (total-tricks.bid)
  cheapest(S) "10+ total points, five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not S, y is not S, new_suit_forcing
      sets  forcing=round
  cheapest(H) "10+ total points, five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, S<=4, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not H, y is not H, new_suit_forcing
      sets  forcing=round
  cheapest(D) "10+ total points, five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not D, y is not D, new_suit_forcing
      sets  forcing=round
  cheapest(C) "10+ total points, five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not C, y is not C, new_suit_forcing
      sets  forcing=round

# The same bids where the card says a new suit is not forcing
# (Basic-Bridge sets `1X-(Y)-2Z forcing` off). The free bid is then
# limited, up to 12 HCP (BBA: 8-13 total points), and with 13+ HCP
# responder jumps,
# forcing to game (BBA: 13-21; probes/free-bid-1D-1S.toml, 2026-09-25).
# Before, a 14-count made the non-forcing bid and was passed.
after 1x (2y) | 1x (3y) when y is not x, !new_suit_forcing
  cheapest(S) "10+ total points, five or more spades, not forcing"
      shows S>=5, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=12
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "10+ total points, five or more hearts, not forcing"
      shows H>=5, S<=4, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=12
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(D) "10+ total points, five or more diamonds, not forcing"
      shows D>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=12
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(C) "10+ total points, five or more clubs, not forcing"
      shows C>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=12
      when  x is not C, y is not C
  jump(S) "13+ total points, five or more spades: forcing to game"
      shows S>=5, hcp>=13
      when  x is not S, y is not S
      sets  forcing=game
  jump(H) "13+ total points, five or more hearts: forcing to game"
      shows H>=5, S<=4, hcp>=13
      when  x is not H, y is not H
      sets  forcing=game
  jump(D) "13+ total points, five or more diamonds: forcing to game"
      shows D>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp>=13
      when  x is not D, y is not D
      sets  forcing=game
  jump(C) "13+ total points, five or more clubs: forcing to game"
      shows C>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp>=13
      when  x is not C, y is not C
      sets  forcing=game

# Opener after the forcing jump: game in a major with three-card support,
# else 3NT with their suit stopped; the game force does the rest.
after 1x (1y) 2z (P) | 1x (1y) 3z (P) | 1x (2y) 3z (P) when partner.jumped, z is not x, z is not y, we.forcing = game
  4{z}  "Three-card support: game"         shows z>=3
        when  z is H | z is S
  3N    "No fit, a stopper in {y}"         shows stop(y)
        priority -1

after 1x (2y) | 1x (3y) when y is not x
  2N  "11-12 total points, balanced, a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp+length_points<=12
      when  stop(y)
  3N  "13+ total points, balanced, a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=13
      when  stop(y)
  P   "No suitable bid"  priority -10

# ── They doubled for takeout ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Redouble shows the balance of the strength; everything else is what it
# would have been, a level lower in ambition.
after 1x (X)
  XX  "Redouble: 10+ total points"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp+length_points>=10
      when  S<=4 | x is S | hcp>=12        # BBA: a five-card spade suit with 10-11 bids 1S
      when  H<=4 | x is H | x is S | hcp>=12   # and five hearts over a minor bid 1H
      priority 1
  cheapest(S) "6-9 total points, four or more spades, or 10-11 with five"
      shows S>=4, S>H, hcp+length_points>=6, hcp+length_points<=9 | (S>=5, hcp<=11)
      when  x is not S
  cheapest(H) "6-9 total points, four or more hearts, or 10-11 with five"
      shows H>=4, H>=S, hcp+length_points>=6, hcp+length_points<=9 | (H>=5, hcp<=11)
      when  x is not H, x is not S
  cheapest(D) "6-9 total points, four or more diamonds"
      shows D>=4, S<=3, H<=3, hcp+length_points>=6, hcp+length_points<=9
      when  x is not D, x is not H, x is not S
  2{x} "Raise: 4-9 total points, support for partner's suit"
      shows x>=3, hcp+length_points>=4, hcp+length_points<=9
      when  x is H | x is S | x>=5
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | x is H), (H<=3 | x is H | x is S)   # over a major, support first (BBA)
  3{x} "Preemptive raise: five-card support for a major, less than 8"
      shows x>=5, hcp+length_points<=7
      when  x is H | x is S
  1N  "6-9 total points, balanced"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=6, hcp+length_points<=9
      when  (S<=3 | x is S), (H<=3 | x is H)
      when  x<=2 | x is C | x is D
      when  !tfr | x is C | x is D          # a transfer to clubs (transfers-after-double.bid)
  P   "No suitable bid"  priority -10

# ── Opener answers a negative double ─────────────────────────────────
# Partner has shown four or more cards in each unbid major and 6+ total
# points (8+ over a two-level overcall), so opener names the major he
# has (counted in support points, as an uncontested raise is: with a
# singleton, 16 HCP and four trumps is game, 2026-09-25), bids notrump with a stopper, or rebids his own suit. A negative
# double is forcing: opener always bids something, and jumps with 16-18.
# Relative calls keep one set of rules right at every level.
after 1x (1y) X (P) | 1x (2y) X (P) | 1x (3y) X (P)
  cheapest(S) "Four spades, minimum"
      shows S>=4, tp(S)<=15
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Four hearts, minimum"
      shows H>=4, tp(H)<=15
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  jump(S) "Four spades, 16-18"
      shows S>=4, tp(S)=16..18
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  jump(H) "Four hearts, 16-18"
      shows H>=4, tp(H)=16..18
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(N) "12-14 balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp<=14
      when  stop(y), !weak_nt
  # With a weak notrump the balanced hands above it, up to 17 (Rick,
  # 2026-11-07; one-nt.bid, `weak_nt`).
  cheapest(N) "Balanced, above the weak notrump: up to 17, a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, above_weak_nt
      when  stop(y), weak_nt
  jump(N) "18-19 balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      when  nt_jump_to_game                  # 3NT at most (rebids.bid)
      shows balanced, hcp=18..19
      when  stop(y)
  # A major rebid is read as six or more (Rick, 2026-10-16, Brill daily
  # board 8): the five-card rebid below with nothing better to say is the
  # least lie and is read by this rule (a read-as call by design). A
  # minor's rebid stays five or more (2026-10-09, read as the hand holds).
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: six or more, minimum"
      shows x>=6, hcp<=15
      when  x is H | x is S
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: five or more, minimum"
      shows x>=5, hcp<=15
      when  x is C | x is D
      when  x>=6
  jump(x) "Six cards in {x}, 16-18"
      shows x>=6, hcp=16..18
  # Partner promised four, so three is an eight-card fit and BBA bids it:
  # `1D (1S) X (P) 2H` on KQ6.832.KT84.A64. Below the four-card bids and
  # the notrump rebid, above naming a minor.
  4S  "Game: four spades, 19+"
      shows S>=4, tp(S)>=19
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  4H  "Game: four hearts, 19+"
      shows H>=4, tp(H)>=19
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  # Where both majors are bid the double showed the minors, and where
  # opener has no major, no stopper and no six-card suit he still has to
  # bid. An unbid four-card minor comes before rebidding his own suit,
  # which is what BBA does: `1D (1S) X (P) 2C` on 754.AQ.AQ52.QT74.
  cheapest(D) "Four diamonds, minimum"
      shows D>=4, hcp<=15
      when  x is not D, y is not D
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
      priority -1
  cheapest(C) "Four clubs, minimum"
      shows C>=4, C>=D, hcp<=15
      when  x is not C, y is not C
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
      priority -1
  # Partner promised four, so three is an eight-card fit and BBA bids it
  # once it has nothing else: `1D (1S) X (P) 2H` on KQ6.832.KT84.A64.
  cheapest(S) "Three spades, minimum"
      shows S>=3, hcp<=15
      when  x is not S, y is not S, partner.S>=4
      priority -2
  cheapest(H) "Three hearts, minimum"
      shows H>=3, hcp<=15
      when  x is not H, y is not H, partner.H>=4
      priority -2
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: five cards, minimum"
      shows x>=5, hcp<=15
      priority -2
  # Strong hands with no fit and no balanced notrump (2026-09-25: 19-20
  # counts rebid their suit as "nothing better" and were passed). From
  # 17 since 2026-09-26: 19/17/16 tried, 17 best (+192 by par distance).
  # Not over a three-level overcall: there it lost (-131 IMPs over 1S (3H)).
  3N  "Game: 17+ with a stopper in {y}"
      shows hcp>=17, stop(y)
      when  lho.last=1{y} | lho.last=2{y}
      priority -1
  cheapest(y) "Cue bid: 17+, forcing to game"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp>=17
      when  lho.last=1{y} | lho.last=2{y}
      sets  forcing=game
      priority -2
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: no better bid"
      priority -5

# ── Opener answers the cue-bid raise ─────────────────────────────────
# The cue bid showed three-card support and 11+ total points, so opener
# accepts with more than a minimum and signs off otherwise.
after 1x (1y) 2y (P) | 1x (2y) 3y (P) | 1x (3y) 4y (P) when y is not x   # their bid in our suit is a two-suiter (two-suited-overcalls.bid)
  # In support points (2026-09-26): 16 HCP left 14-15 with shortness in
  # a partscore. 14/15/16 support points: +750/+697/+519 by par distance.
  4{x} "Accepts: game in {x}"
      shows tp(x)>=14
      when  x is H | x is S
  # With a minor, 3NT is the game: from 14 with their suit held, any
  # shape, else five of the minor from 16 (2026-09-25: 16-20 counts
  # signed off, 668 corpus boards with 25+ HCP between us and 3NT on).
  3N  "Accepts: 14+ with a stopper in {y}"
      shows hcp>=14
      when  stop(y), x is C | x is D
  5{x} "Accepts: 16+, no stopper in {y}"
      shows hcp>=16
      when  x is C | x is D
      priority -1
  cheapest(x) "Minimum: signs off"
      priority -2

# Responder after opener's sign-off: the cue bid was 11+ with no upper
# limit, so with 13+ responder bids the game himself.
after 1x (1y) 2y (P) 3x (P) | 1x (2y) 3y (P) 3x (P) | 1x (2y) 3y (P) 4x (P) when x is C | x is D, y is not x
  3N  "Game: 13+ with a stopper in {y}"   shows hcp+length_points>=13, stop(y)
  5{x} "Game in the minor: 14+"          shows hcp+length_points>=14
      priority -1
  P   "Limit raise only"
      priority -5
after 1x (2y) 3y (P) 4x (P) when x is H | x is S, y is not x
  P   "Game reached"
after 1x (1y) 2y (P) 2x (P) | 1x (1y) 2y (P) 3x (P) | 1x (2y) 3y (P) 3x (P) when x is H | x is S, y is not x
  4{x} "Game: 13+"  shows hcp+length_points>=13
  P   "Limit raise only"
      priority -5

# ── Opener when they compete over the negative double ────────────────
# They have bid again, so the double is no longer forcing and opener may
# pass. He still names a four-card major at the cheapest level, bids
# notrump with a stopper, or rebids a six-card suit with extras; with a
# minimum and nothing to say he lets them have it, which is what BBA
# does on most of these hands. Only where they have merely competed to
# the next level: over a jump by them BBA passes almost always, and we
# leave that to the pass below.
after 1x (1y) X (2z) | 1x (2y) X (3z) when y is not x
  cheapest(S) "Four spades, minimum"
      shows S>=4, tp(S)<=15
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Four hearts, minimum"
      shows H>=4, tp(H)<=15
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  jump(S) "Four spades, 16-18"
      shows S>=4, tp(S)=16..18
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  jump(H) "Four hearts, 16-18"
      shows H>=4, tp(H)=16..18
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(N) "12-15 balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp<=15
      when  stop(y)
  jump(N) "18-19 balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      when  nt_jump_to_game                  # 3NT at most (rebids.bid)
      shows balanced, hcp=18..19
      when  stop(y)
  cheapest(x) "Six or more {x}, 13+"
      shows x>=6, hcp>=13
  P   "No further bid"  priority -10

# They jumped over the double. Most of these hands pass in the corpus,
# so opener only bids on with real extras: a four-card major for the one
# partner promised, or a stopper, and 13+ HCP to go with it.
after 1x (1y) X (3z) | 1x (1y) X (4z) | 1x (2y) X (4z) | 1x (3y) X (4z) when y is not x
  cheapest(S) "Four spades, 13+"
      shows S>=4, hcp>=13
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Four hearts, 13+"
      shows H>=4, hcp>=13
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(N) "13+ balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp>=13
      when  stop(y)
  P   "No further bid"  priority -10

# ── Fallback: a player on the opening side who passed last time ──────
# They have come in, and I passed at my last turn: with nothing new to
# say I pass again. Below every real rule (2026-09-25: six no-rule
# positions in Basic_* N/S boards, e.g. 1C P P X P 2N and
# 1D (2C) P (2S) 3D (P), where responder had passed with 0-5 or 8).
when they.bid, !lho.opened, !rho.opened, me.last=P   # our side opened
  P   "No further bid"
      when  !passes_out_artificial   # never pass out our own artificial bid (base.bid)
      priority -20
# And when partner passed at his last turn: he has nothing more, and I
# have described my hand (2026-09-25: 1S (X) 2S (3C) P (P), the raiser).
when they.bid, !lho.opened, !rho.opened, partner.last=P
  P   "No further bid"
      when  !passes_out_artificial   # never pass out our own artificial bid (base.bid)
      priority -20

# ── Opener after partner answered the reopening double ───────────────
# Partner was forced to bid; opener goes on only with game values.
after 1x (1y) P (P) X (P) 2z (P) | 1x (1y) P (P) X (P) 3z (P) | 1x (2y) P (P) X (P) 2z (P) | 1x (2y) P (P) X (P) 3z (P) | 1x (3y) P (P) X (P) 3z (P) | 1x (3y) P (P) X (P) 4z (P) when y is not x, z is not y
  3N  "Game: 18+ with a stopper in {y}"    shows hcp>=18, stop(y)
  P   "No game"
      priority -10
files.rules/competitive/balancing.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# The balancing seat: they opened, partner passed, and RHO passed too.
# Partner is marked with values, so everything is lighter than in the
# direct seat (Rick, 2026-09-22, following BBA's Basic-Bridge meanings):
#
# - the reopening double is 8+ total points with three or more cards in
#   every unbid suit, or 18+ with any shape;
# - a suit at the one level is 8-15 total points with five cards, at the
#   two level 10-15;
# - 1NT is 12-15 balanced with a stopper, not the 15-18 of the direct
#   seat, and 2NT is 19-21.
#
# Systems are on over the balancing 1NT: the notrump modules carry the
# `(1x) P (P) 1N (P)` spelling of their patterns.

module balancing "The balancing seat"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  needs  overcalls
  skill  competitive_bidding/balancing
  param  one_min = overcalls.one_level_min default 8
  param  two_min = overcalls.two_level_min default 12
  param  nt_min  = nt_overcalls.balance.range_min default 12
  param  nt_max  = nt_overcalls.balance.range_max default 15
  param  oc_max  = overcalls.one_level_max default 17

# ── Reopening ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after (1x) P (P)
  X   "Reopening double: 8+ total points and the unbid suits"
      shows hcp+length_points>=8
      shows ((S>=3 | x is S), (H>=3 | x is H), (D>=3 | x is D), (C>=3 | x is C)) | hcp+length_points>=oc_max+1
  1S  "Reopening: five spades, 8-15 total points"
      shows S>=5, S>=H, S>=D, S>=C, hcp+length_points>=one_min, hcp+length_points<=15
      when  x is not S
  1H  "Reopening: five hearts, 8-15 total points"
      shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D, H>=C, hcp+length_points>=one_min, hcp+length_points<=15
      when  x is not H
  1D  "Reopening: five diamonds, 8-15 total points"
      shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C, hcp+length_points>=one_min, hcp+length_points<=15
      when  x is not D
  2C  "Reopening: five clubs, 10-15 total points"
      shows C>=5, C>S, C>H, C>D, hcp+length_points>=two_min-2, hcp+length_points<=15
      when  x is not C
  2D  "Reopening: five diamonds, 10-15 total points"
      shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C, hcp+length_points>=two_min-2, hcp+length_points<=15
      when  x is not D, x is not C
  2H  "Reopening: five hearts, 10-15 total points"
      shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D, H>=C, hcp+length_points>=two_min-2, hcp+length_points<=15
      when  x is not H, x is not D, x is not C
  1N  "Balancing notrump: {nt_min}-{nt_max} balanced with a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp>=nt_min, hcp<=nt_max
      when  stop(x)
  2N  "19-21 balanced with a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp=19..21
      when  stop(x)
  P   "Nothing to reopen with"  priority -10
files.rules/competitive/cappelletti.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Cappelletti (Hamilton) and Modified Cappelletti over their 1NT, direct
# and balancing (vs-1nt.notes.md has the sources and the BBA probes).
#
#   X    penalty, 15+ HCP                     (both)
#   2♣   one long suit, six or more            (Cappelletti)
#        a long minor, or a major and a minor  (Modified)
#   2♦   both majors, 5-4 or longer            (both)
#   2♥/2♠ that major (5) and a minor (4)       (Cappelletti)
#        that major, six or more, one-suited   (Modified)
#   2NT  both minors, 5-5 or longer            (both)
#
# Strength (BBA on 21GF-DEFAULT, probes/vs-1N-capp.toml, 1,500 hands):
# BBA doubles from 15 HCP, shows a six-card suit from 9-10 HCP and a
# two-suiter from 9; it passes a 5-4 major-minor hand whose four-card
# minor has no top honour. We count HCP plus a point a card beyond four
# in each suit: 12 for a one-suiter (10 HCP with six cards, 9 with
# seven), 10 for a two-suiter (9 HCP with 5-4, 8 with 5-5), 8 for the
# minors (6 HCP with 5-5 minors, as BBA at 6-7 with 6-5). With 18+ HCP
# the double comes first whatever the shape.

module cappelletti "Cappelletti and Modified Cappelletti over their 1NT"
  kind   convention
  needs  vs-1nt
  skill  competitive_bidding/cappelletti
  skill  competitive_bidding/modified_cappelletti
  skill  competitive_bidding/defense_vs_1nt
  param  def = defence_to_1nt.strong
  param  system = general.system   # `brill`: the Brill card's treatments (below)

# ── Direct and balancing: the calls both versions share ──────────────
after (1N) | (1N) P (P) when def is competitive_bidding/cappelletti | def is competitive_bidding/modified_cappelletti
  X   "Penalty: 15+ HCP"
      shows hcp>=15
      sets  ask=nt_penalty
  2D  "Cappelletti: both majors, 5-4 or longer"   alert
      shows H>=4, S>=4, H+S>=9, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      when  system is not brill
      sets  ask=nt_majors
  2N  "Cappelletti: both minors, 5-5 or longer"   alert
      shows C>=5, D>=5, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp<=17
      when  system is not brill
      sets  ask=nt_minors

# brill (the Brill card): every Cappelletti bid has 10+ HCP, and 2D is
# 5-5 in the majors. Brill /explain, 2026-10-15, "Cappelletti - majors":
# `H >= 5 and S >= 5 and hcp >= 10`; "Cappelletti - minors": `C >= 5 and
# D >= 5 and totalpoints >= 15 and hcp >= 10`; "Cappelletti - single
# suited": `totalpoints >= 10 and lengthlongestsuit >= 6 and singlesuited
# and hcp >= 10`; "Cappelletti - S and a minor": `S >= 5 and (C >= 4 or D
# >= 4) and loserlevel >= 2 and totalpoints >= 12 and hcp >= 10`.
after (1N) | (1N) P (P) when def is competitive_bidding/cappelletti | def is competitive_bidding/modified_cappelletti, system is brill
  2D  "Cappelletti: both majors, 5-5 or longer, 10+ HCP"   alert
      shows H>=5, S>=5, hcp>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_majors
  2N  "Cappelletti: both minors, 5-5 or longer, 10+ HCP"   alert
      shows C>=5, D>=5, hcp>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_minors

# ── Cappelletti ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after (1N) | (1N) P (P) when def is competitive_bidding/cappelletti
  2C  "Cappelletti: one long suit, six or more"   alert
      shows longest>=6, second_longest<=4, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17 | (system is brill, hcp<=18)
      shows hcp>=10 | system is not brill
      sets  ask=capp_one
  2H  "Cappelletti: five hearts and a four-card minor"   alert
      shows H>=5, S<=3, ((C>=4, quality(C)>=fair) | (D>=4, quality(D)>=fair))
      shows hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      shows hcp>=10 | system is not brill
      sets  ask=nt_mm(H)
  2S  "Cappelletti: five spades and a four-card minor"   alert
      shows S>=5, H<=3, ((C>=4, quality(C)>=fair) | (D>=4, quality(D)>=fair))
      shows hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      shows hcp>=10 | system is not brill
      sets  ask=nt_mm(S)

# Advancer over 2♣: the 2♦ relay asks for the suit. BBA and GIB pass with
# six clubs and bid a six-card major of their own, not forcing
# (probes/vs-1N-capp-2C-adv.toml: 526 relays, 32 2♥, 21 2♠, 21 passes).
when asked capp_one, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  2D  "Relay: bid your suit"                      alert
      sets  ask=capp_relay
  P   "Long clubs: to play"                       shows C>=6
  2H  "Six or more hearts: to play"               shows H>=6, hcp<=12
  2S  "Six or more spades: to play"               shows S>=6, hcp<=12

when asked capp_relay, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P   "My suit is diamonds"                       shows D>=6
  2H  "My suit is hearts"                         shows H>=6
      sets  ask=nt_one(H)
  2S  "My suit is spades"                         shows S>=6
      sets  ask=nt_one(S)
  3C  "My suit is clubs"                          shows C>=6
      sets  ask=nt_one(C)

# ── Modified Cappelletti ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 2♣ is a long minor or a major-minor two-suiter; 2♥/2♠ one-suited.
after (1N) | (1N) P (P) when def is competitive_bidding/modified_cappelletti
  2C  "Modified Cappelletti: a long minor, or a major and a minor"   alert
      shows ((C>=6 | D>=6), second_longest<=4, hcp+length_points>=12) | (((H>=5, S<=3) | (S>=5, H<=3)), (C>=4 | D>=4), hcp+length_points>=10)
      shows hcp<=17
      sets  ask=mcapp_one
  2H  "Modified Cappelletti: six or more hearts"  alert
      shows H>=6, second_longest<=4, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_one(H)
  2S  "Modified Cappelletti: six or more spades"  alert
      shows S>=6, second_longest<=4, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_one(S)

# Advancer relays: 2♣ may be diamonds or a major, so it is not passed.
when asked mcapp_one, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  2D  "Relay: show your hand"                     alert
      sets  ask=mcapp_relay

when asked mcapp_relay, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P   "Long diamonds"                             shows D>=6
  2H  "Hearts and a minor"                        shows H>=5, C>=4 | D>=4
      sets  ask=nt_mm(H)
  2S  "Spades and a minor"                        shows S>=5, C>=4 | D>=4
      sets  ask=nt_mm(S)
  3C  "Long clubs"                                shows C>=6
files.rules/competitive/maximal-doubles.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Maximal doubles (`doubles.maximal`). We have bid and raised a major,
# 1M .. 2M, and they bid three of the suit directly below ours (3D under
# hearts, 3H under spades): there is no room left for a game try, so the
# double is the game try and three of our major is only competitive.
# Partner signs off in 3M with a minimum or bids game with a maximum.
# (Bridge Bum, "Maximal Double"; Todd, "Non-Takeout Doubles", Advancing
# in Bridge 357.) Alertable.
#
# Applies to the opener after 1M (any) 2M and to the overcaller after
# (1x) 1M (any) 2M. Against any other three-level bid (not the suit just
# below ours) the double stays what it was.

module maximal-doubles "Maximal doubles"
  kind   convention
  card   competitive_bidding/maximal_doubles
  needs  base
  needs  overcalls
  skill  competitive_bidding/maximal_doubles

# ── The opener or the overcaller ─────────────────────────────────────
# The game try is the opener's usual invitation over a single raise,
# 17-18 support points (rebids.bid); 3M competes with six trumps (five and
# a shape) and no game interest.
after 1M (*) 2M (3x) | (1y) 1M (*) 2M (3x) when (M is H, x is D) | (M is S, x is H)
  X   "Maximal double: a game try in {M}"
      alert  artificial
      shows  tp(M)=17..18
      sets   trump=M, ask=maximal(M)
      priority 2
  3{M} "Competitive: no game interest"
      shows M>=6 | (M>=5, !balanced), tp(M)<=16
      sets  trump=M
      priority 1
  4{M} "Game: 19+"
      shows tp(M)>=19
      sets  trump=M
      priority 1
  P   "No further bid"  priority -5

# ── Partner answers the game try ─────────────────────────────────────
# The raise was 6-10: the top of it (9+ support points) accepts.
when asked maximal(t)
  4{t} "Accepts the game try: a maximum raise"
      shows tp(t)>=9
      priority 1
  3{t} "Declines: a minimum raise"
      priority 1

# ── Partner after the competitive 3M ─────────────────────────────────
after 1M (*) 2M (3x) 3M (P) | (1y) 1M (*) 2M (3x) 3M (P) when (M is H, x is D) | (M is S, x is H)
  P   "No further bid"  priority 1
files.rules/competitive/multi-landy.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Landy and Multi-Landy over their 1NT, direct and balancing
# (vs-1nt.notes.md). BBA plays Multi-Landy on seven cards (21GF-Multi,
# 21GF-SPECIALS2 and others) as Woolsey describes it; its meanings,
# from probes/vs-1N-mlandy.toml (1,000 hands, 21GF-Multi):
#
#   X    a four-card major and a longer minor, 12+ HCP
#   2♣   both majors
#   2♦   one major, six or more (the "multi")
#   2♥/2♠ that major (5) and a minor (4)
#   2NT  both minors
#
# Landy is 2♣ for the majors, everything else natural (overcalls.bid).

module multi-landy "Landy and Multi-Landy over their 1NT"
  kind   convention
  needs  vs-1nt
  skill  competitive_bidding/multi_landy
  skill  competitive_bidding/landy
  skill  competitive_bidding/defense_vs_1nt
  param  def = defence_to_1nt.strong

after (1N) | (1N) P (P) when def is competitive_bidding/multi_landy | def is competitive_bidding/landy
  2C  "Landy: both majors, 5-4 or longer"          alert
      shows H>=4, S>=4, H+S>=9, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_majors

after (1N) | (1N) P (P) when def is competitive_bidding/multi_landy
  X   "Multi-Landy: a four-card major and a longer minor"   alert
      shows H=4 | S=4, C>=5 | D>=5, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=ml_x
  2D  "Multi-Landy: six or more in one major"      alert
      shows H>=6 | S>=6, second_longest<=4, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=ml_multi
  2H  "Multi-Landy: five hearts and a four-card minor"   alert
      shows H>=5, S<=3, ((C>=4, quality(C)>=fair) | (D>=4, quality(D)>=fair))
      shows hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_mm(H)
  2S  "Multi-Landy: five spades and a four-card minor"   alert
      shows S>=5, H<=3, ((C>=4, quality(C)>=fair) | (D>=4, quality(D)>=fair))
      shows hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_mm(S)
  2N  "Multi-Landy: both minors, 5-5 or longer"    alert
      shows C>=5, D>=5, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_minors

# Advancer over the double bids 2♣, pass or correct to the minor.
when asked ml_x, rho.last=P | rho.last=X | rho.last=XX
  2C  "Pass or correct: bid your minor"            alert
      sets  ask=ml_minor
when asked ml_minor, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P   "My minor is clubs"                          shows C>=5
  2D  "My minor is diamonds"                       shows D>=5

# Advancer over the multi 2♦ bids 2♥, pass or correct.
when asked ml_multi, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  2H  "Pass or correct: bid your major"            alert
      sets  ask=ml_major
when asked ml_major, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P   "My major is hearts"                         shows H>=6
  2S  "My major is spades"                         shows S>=6
      sets  ask=nt_one(S)
files.rules/competitive/overcalls.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Overcalls of a one-level opening on our right (Rick, 2026-09-22):
#
# - a simple overcall is always a five-card suit: 8-17 total points at the
#   one level, 12-17 at the two level (BBA's Basic-Bridge meanings, which
#   Rick adopted). No four-card overcalls on this card;
# - too strong to overcall (18+ total points) is a takeout double first and
#   the suit afterwards, whatever the shape (takeout-double.bid); the
#   overcall's own ceiling is 16 HCP (17 from 2026-09-25, 16 from
#   2026-09-27 so that 17+ is the power double), so a six-card suit with
#   16 still overcalls, as BBA does;
# - a jump overcall follows the weak-two rules: six cards, 4-10 HCP (10
#   as BBA, 2026-09-25), and vulnerable two of the top three or three of
#   the top five honours;
# - a direct 1NT overcall is 15-18 balanced with a stopper in their suit,
#   a point wider than our 1NT opening.
#
# With two five-card suits the higher-ranking one is bid, as in base.bid:
# each rule requires its suit to be at least as long as the suits above it
# and longer than the suits below it, so only one of them can fire.

module overcalls "Suit and notrump overcalls"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  skill  competitive_bidding/notrump_overcalls
  skill  competitive_bidding/overcalls
  param  one_min = overcalls.one_level_min default 8
  param  one_max = overcalls.one_level_max default 16
  param  two_min = overcalls.two_level_min default 12
  param  two_max = overcalls.two_level_max default 17
  param  jump    = overcalls.jump default weak
  param  nt_min  = nt_overcalls.direct.range_min default 15
  param  nt_max  = nt_overcalls.direct.range_max default 18
  param  system  = general.system   # `brill`: the Brill card's treatments (1NT overcall)
  param  nt_def  = defence_to_1nt.strong
  param  raptor  = competitive_bidding/raptor default false
  param  sandwich = competitive_bidding/sandwich_nt default false

# ── Simple overcalls at the one level ────────────────────────────────
# `(1x)` binds x to the suit they opened; the rules below never bid it.
#
# The suit has to be worth bidding (Rick, 2026-09-23): two of the top
# three or three of the top five honours, **or else an opening hand** --
# it takes 12 total points to overcall on a ten-high suit. Without that
# we overcalled 1♠ on J8753 with 10 HCP and pushed the auction up for
# the opponents.
after (1x)
  1S  "Overcall: five spades, {one_min}-{one_max} total points"
      shows S>=5, S>=H, S>=D, S>=C
      shows hcp+length_points>=one_min, hcp<=one_max
      when  x is not S
      when  quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3 | hcp+length_points>=12
  1H  "Overcall: five hearts, {one_min}-{one_max} total points"
      shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D, H>=C
      shows hcp+length_points>=one_min, hcp<=one_max
      when  x is not H
      when  quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3 | hcp+length_points>=12
  1D  "Overcall: five diamonds, {one_min}-{one_max} total points"
      shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C
      shows hcp+length_points>=one_min, hcp<=one_max
      when  x is not D
      when  quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=3 | hcp+length_points>=12

# ── Simple overcalls at the two level ────────────────────────────────
# Only where the suit cannot be shown at the one level: clubs over any
# opening, diamonds over a major, hearts over 1S. A two-level bid in a
# suit that could have been shown more cheaply is a jump, below.
# Up to the one-level maximum in HCP as well (ticket b400, 2026-10-02):
# a 16-count with a good six-card suit is 18 total points, over the
# two-level maximum but short of the power double's 17 HCP, and it used
# to pass. Now no direct-seat pass holds more than 16 HCP.
# The minimum is in HCP, a point less with six cards (ticket b238,
# 2026-10-04; probes/oc-2C-over-1D.toml): BBA overcalls 2C over 1D from
# 12 HCP with five clubs, 11 with six or seven, never on less (a weak
# hand with seven clubs preempts at 3C). 12 total points let 10 HCP and
# six clubs overcall, and partner read the overcall as 3+ HCP.
after (1x)
  2C  "Overcall: five clubs, {two_min}-{two_max} total points"
      shows C>=5, C>S, C>H, C>D
      shows hcp>=two_min | (C>=6, hcp>=two_min-1), hcp+length_points<=two_max | hcp<=one_max
      when  x is not C
      when  C>=6 | quality(C)>=good | top5(C)>=4
  2D  "Overcall: five diamonds, {two_min}-{two_max} total points"
      shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C
      shows hcp>=two_min | (D>=6, hcp>=two_min-1), hcp+length_points<=two_max | hcp<=one_max
      when  x is not D, x is not C
      when  D>=6 | quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=4
  2H  "Overcall: five hearts, {two_min}-{two_max} total points"
      shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D, H>=C
      shows hcp>=two_min | (H>=6, hcp>=two_min-1), hcp+length_points<=two_max | hcp<=one_max
      when  x is not H, x is not D, x is not C
      when  H>=6 | quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=4

# ── Notrump overcall ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# With a five-card major we show the major instead, which is what BBA
# does: every 1NT overcall in the corpus had four cards or fewer in both.
after (1x)
  1N  "{nt_min}-{nt_max} balanced with a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp>=nt_min, hcp<=nt_max, S<=4, H<=4
      when  stop(x), !raptor             # Raptor 1NT shows two suits (raptor.bid)
      when  system is not brill
# brill (the Brill card, 15-17): balanced or semi-balanced, so a five-card
# major will do. Brill /explain, 2026-10-15, "Overcalling 1Mi with 1N" and
# "Overcalling 1Ma with 1N", "15-17": `stopper('C') and hcp>= 15 and hcp<=
# 17 and (balanced or semibalanced)`.
after (1x) when system is brill
  1N  "{nt_min}-{nt_max} balanced or semi-balanced with a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced | semibalanced, C=2..5, D=2..5, H=2..5, S=2..5, hcp>=nt_min, hcp<=nt_max
      when  stop(x), !raptor

# Advancer when their partner raises over our 1NT overcall: nothing was
# written (~160 corpus boards). BBA, 2026-09-25: a five-card suit at the
# two level to play; a six-card minor at the three level; 3NT with 9+
# and their suit held. BBA also doubles for takeout short in their suit;
# the double cost 449 IMPs against par here, so it is left out.
after (1x) 1N (2x)
  2S  "To play: five or more spades"          shows S>=5, hcp<=8
      when  x is H
  3C  "To play: six or more clubs"            shows C>=6, hcp<=8, H<=3 | x is H, S<=3 | x is S
  3D  "To play: six or more diamonds"         shows D>=6, D>C, hcp<=8, H<=3 | x is H, S<=3 | x is S
  3N  "Game: 9+, {x} held"                    shows hcp>=9, stop(x)
  P   "Not enough to advance"                        shows hcp>=0
      priority -5

# ── Over their 1NT, natural (2026-09-25, probes/vs-1N.toml) ───────────
# No rules existed. BBA on Basic-Bridge (no conventional defence): a
# five-card suit at the two level with 12+ total points (six cards from
# about 10 HCP), the longest suit and the higher of two equal; a
# preemptive three-level bid with seven cards and 4-10. (BBA also doubles
# with 13+ and 4-3-3-3; neutral, left out.) Judged from the overcalling
# side: +1,007 IMPs over 237 changed boards (par distance says -825, but
# par distance counts a successful overcall against us: overcalls.notes.md).
# The pass is shared by every defence, and the conventional defences
# preempt in a narrower range (vs-1nt.bid). Landy keeps the natural 2♦/2♥/2♠ and uses 2♣ for the majors
# (multi-landy.bid).
# `natural` is the card's explicit word for it (convention-card 0.43; it used to load as `other`).
after (1N) when nt_def is none | nt_def is competitive_bidding/landy
  2S  "Natural: five spades, 12+ total points"    shows S>=5, S>=H, S>=D, S>=C, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
  2H  "Natural: five hearts, 12+ total points"    shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D, H>=C, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
  2D  "Natural: five diamonds, 12+ total points"  shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
after (1N) when nt_def is none
  2C  "Natural: five clubs, 12+ total points"     shows C>=5, C>S, C>H, C>D, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
  3S  "Preemptive: seven spades, 4-10"            shows S>=7, hcp=4..10
      priority 1
  3H  "Preemptive: seven hearts, 4-10"            shows H>=7, hcp=4..10
      priority 1
  3D  "Preemptive: seven diamonds, 4-10"          shows D>=7, hcp=4..10
