      when  y is D | y is H
  cheapest(C) "Natural, forcing to game: five or more clubs"      shows C>=5, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
  cheapest(D) "Natural, forcing to game: five or more diamonds"   shows D>=5, points>=10
      when  y is not D
      sets  forcing=game
  3H  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more hearts"   shows H>=5, points>=10
      when  y is S
      sets  forcing=game
  4H  "Game: six or more hearts"   shows H>=6, hcp>=10
      when  y is not H, !texas_1nt
      priority 1
  4S  "Game: six or more spades"   shows S>=6, hcp>=10
      when  y is not S, !texas_1nt
      priority 1
  2N  "Invitational: 8-9 HCP, a stopper in {y}"   shows hcp=8..9, stop(y)
      when  !leb, !rub                  # 2NT is a relay or a transfer
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  3N  "Game: 10+ HCP"                           shows hcp>=10
      when  !leb
  P   "No bid over their overcall"
      priority -10

# Opener answers the negative double: a four-card major at the cheapest
# level, 2NT with a stopper, a four-card minor, or a pass for penalties
# with four of their suit.
after 1N (2y) X (P) when y is not C, lho.y>=4, (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3)
  cheapest(H) "Four hearts for partner's double"   shows H>=4   when y is not H
  cheapest(S) "Four spades for partner's double"   shows S>=4   when y is not S
  2N  "No four-card major, a stopper in {y}"       shows stop(y)
      priority -1
  P   "Four of their suit: defends"                shows y>=4
      priority -2
  cheapest(C) "No major, no stopper: four clubs"   shows C>=4
      priority -3
  cheapest(D) "No major, no stopper: four diamonds"   shows D>=4
      when  y is not D
      priority -3
  cheapest(N) "No four-card major"
      priority -5

# Responder after opener's answer: game with 10+, an invitation in the
# major with 8-9, else pass.
after 1N (2y) X (P) 2M (P) | 1N (2y) X (P) 3M (P) when y is not C, rho.y>=4, (maybe rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3)
  4M  "Game in the fit: 10+"          shows M>=4, points>=10
  3M  "Invitational in the fit: 8-9"  shows M>=4, points=8..9
      when  partner.last=2M
  3N  "Game, no fit: 10+"             shows M<=3, points>=10
  P   "No game"                       shows points<=9
      priority -5
after 1N (2y) X (P) 2M (P) 3M (P) when y is not C, lho.y>=4, (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3)
  4M  "Accepts the invitation: a maximum"        shows hcp>=16
  P   "Declines: a minimum"                      shows hcp<=15
after 1N (2y) X (P) 2N (P) | 1N (2y) X (P) 3C (P) | 1N (2y) X (P) 3D (P) when y is not C, rho.y>=4, (maybe rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3)
  3N  "Game: 10+"                     shows points>=10
  P   "No game"                       shows points<=9
      priority -5

# Opener after responder's other calls.
after 1N (2y) 3z (P) when y is not C, z is not y, z is not N, lho.y>=4, (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3)
  4{z}  "Three-card support: game in the major"   shows z>=3
        when  z is H | z is S
  3N    "Game in notrump"
        priority -1
after 1N (2y) 2z (P) when y is not C, z is not N, lho.y>=4, (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3)
  P   "Partner's suit, to play"
after 1N (2y) 2N (P) when !leb, !rub, y is not C, lho.y>=4, (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3)
  3N  "Accepts: a maximum"             shows hcp>=16
      priority 1                       # ahead of one-nt.bid's answer to the invitation
  P   "Declines: a minimum"            shows hcp<=15
      priority 1

# ── Their natural 2♣, transfers off (2026-09-30) ─────────────────────
# With `vs_2c` off there is no Stayman by double and no transfer, and a
# natural 2♣ (five or more clubs: `rho.C>=5`, which DONT, Meckwell,
# Cappelletti and Landy 2♣ never show) is met as BBA meets it on bare
# SAYC (nt-interference.notes.md, probes/nt-2C-nat-resp.toml): no
# negative double. A five-card suit at the two level is to play, 2NT
# invites with a club stopper, 3NT is game with one. A weak hand with
# four of a major passes and leaves it to opener's reopening double.
# Game values are ours, not BBA's (which passes some 13-16 counts): a
# five-card suit at the three level forces to game, and the cue-bid is
# Stayman forcing to game, with a four-card major or no club stopper.
after 1N (2C) when !vs_2c, rho.C>=5
  2S  "Natural, to play: five or more spades"     shows S>=5, S>=H, hcp>=4, points<=9
  2H  "Natural, to play: five or more hearts"     shows H>=5, H>S, hcp>=4, points<=9
  2D  "Natural, to play: five or more diamonds"   shows D>=5, H<=4, S<=4, hcp>=4, points<=9
  2N  "Invitational: 8-9 HCP, a club stopper"     shows hcp=8..9, stop(C), H<=4, S<=4
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  3N  "Game: 10+ HCP, a club stopper"             shows hcp>=10, stop(C), H<=3, S<=3
  3C  "Stayman cue-bid: a four-card major or no club stopper"
      alert  artificial
      shows  hcp>=10, H<=4, S<=4, H=4 | S=4 | !stop(C)
      sets   forcing=game
      priority 1
  3D  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more diamonds"   shows D>=5, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 2
  3H  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more hearts"     shows H>=5, H>S, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 2
  3S  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more spades"     shows S>=5, S>=H, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 2
  4H  "Game: six or more hearts"   shows H>=6, H>S, points>=9
      when  !texas_1nt
      priority 3
  4S  "Game: six or more spades"   shows S>=6, S>=H, points>=9
      when  !texas_1nt
      priority 3
  P   "No bid over their 2♣: weak, or length in clubs"
      priority -10

# Opener after responder's call.
after 1N (2C) 2z (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5, z is not N
  P   "Partner's suit, to play"
after 1N (2C) 2N (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  3N  "Accepts: a maximum"             shows hcp>=16
      priority 1                       # ahead of one-nt.bid's answer to the invitation
  P   "Declines: a minimum"            shows hcp<=15
      priority 1
after 1N (2C) 3z (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5, z is not C
  4{z}  "Three-card support: game in the major"   shows z>=3
        when  z is H | z is S
  3N    "Game in notrump"
        priority -1
# The cue-bid: a four-card major, else 3NT with a club stopper, else 3♦.
after 1N (2C) 3C (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  3H  "Four hearts"                         shows H>=4
  3S  "Four spades, not four hearts"        shows S>=4, H<=3
  3N  "No four-card major, a club stopper"  shows H<=3, S<=3, stop(C)
  3D  "No four-card major, no club stopper" shows H<=3, S<=3
      priority -1
after 1N (2C) 3C (P) 3M (P) when !vs_2c, rho.C>=5
  4M  "Game in the fit"                     shows M>=4
  3S  "Four spades, not four hearts"        shows S>=4
      when  M is H
  3N  "No fit: game in notrump"
      priority -1
after 1N (2C) 3C (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  4S  "Four spades too: game in the fit"    shows S>=4
  3N  "Game in notrump"                     priority -1
after 1N (2C) 3C (P) 3D (P) when !vs_2c, rho.C>=5
  3N  "Game in notrump"
after 1N (2C) 3C (P) 3N (P) | 1N (2C) 3C (P) 3H (P) 3N (P) | 1N (2C) 3C (P) 3S (P) 3N (P) when !vs_2c
  P   "No further bid"

# They raised their clubs: compete in partner's major with four, accept
# the invitation with a maximum, otherwise pass.
after 1N (2C) 2M (3C) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  3M  "Four-card support: competing"   shows M>=4
  P   "No further bid"            priority -5
after 1N (2C) 2N (3C) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  3N  "Accepts: a maximum"             shows hcp>=16
  P   "Declines: a minimum"            priority -5
# Any other raise of their clubs over partner's two-level call, and
# their next club bid after we compete: we have said what we have.
after 1N (2C) 2z (3C) | 1N (2C) 2z (4C) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  P   "No further bid"   priority -10
after 1N (2C) 2M (3C) 3M (4C) when !vs_2c, rho.C>=5
  P   "No further bid"         priority -10

# Responder passed: with two clubs opener reopens with a double (BBA,
# 32 of 32 two-club openers in the vanilla corpus; none with three).
# Responder passes for penalties with four clubs, else names a suit.
after 1N (2C) P (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  X   "Reopening double: two clubs or fewer"   shows C<=2
      priority 1
after 1N (2C) P (P) X (P) when !vs_2c, rho.C>=5
  P   "Four or more clubs: defends"             shows C>=4
      priority 1
  2N  "8-9 HCP, a club stopper"                 shows hcp>=8, stop(C), H<=3, S<=3
  2H  "Four or more hearts"                     shows H>=4, H>=S
  2S  "Four or more spades"                     shows S>=4, S>H
  2D  "Four or more diamonds"                   shows D>=4
      priority -1
  2D  "Nothing better"                          priority -5
after 1N (2C) P (P) X (P) 2z (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5, z is not N
  P   "Partner's suit, to play"
after 1N (2C) P (P) X (P) 2N (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  3N  "Accepts: a maximum"             shows hcp>=16
      priority 1                       # ahead of one-nt.bid's answer to the invitation
  P   "Declines: a minimum"            shows hcp<=15
      priority 1

# ── Their conventional overcalls (2026-09-28, vs-1nt.notes.md) ───────
# The rules above read 2♦/2♥/2♠ as natural: they apply when the
# overcaller has shown four or more of the suit bid and not both majors.
# The opponents' defence (their card: cappelletti.bid, dont.bid,
# meckwell.bid, multi-landy.bid) can show something else:
#
# - both majors (Cappelletti 2♦, DONT 2♥): the double shows values and
#   says we can defend; a minor at the three level is natural and forcing
#   to game; 3NT is game with both majors held. Afterwards a double of
#   their major is for penalties.
# - an unknown major (Multi-Landy 2♦): the double shows values; 3NT game.
# - their 2♣ is left to the systems-on rules (Stayman by double), and
#   their double to the rules at the top.
after 1N (2y) when y is not C, rho.H>=4, rho.S>=4
  X   "Values: 8+ HCP"                shows hcp>=8
  3C  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more clubs"      shows C>=5, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
  3D  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more diamonds"   shows D>=5, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
  3N  "Game: 10+, both majors held"                   shows hcp>=10, stop(H), stop(S)
  P   "No bid over their overcall"
      priority -10
after 1N (2y) when y is not C, (maybe rho.y<=3), (maybe rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3)
  X   "Values: 8+ HCP"                shows hcp>=8
  3N  "Game: 10+ HCP"                                shows hcp>=10
  P   "No bid over their overcall"
      priority -10

# Responder after a transfer that they interrupted (2026-09-28): with a
# hand no transfer continuation describes (5-4 in the majors and a
# singleton, which uncontested goes through Stayman first) he passes.
# A gap to fill, not a treatment: nt-interference.notes.md.
when answered transfer(M), they.bid
  P   "No further bid"                         priority -10
      when  !passes_out_artificial   # never pass out my own transfer, doubled (base.bid)

# Their relay over our Stayman double (Cappelletti 2♣, X, 2♦): opener
# still shows a major, doubles 2♦ with four of them, else passes.
after 1N (2C) X (2D) when vs_2c
  2H  "4+ hearts"                                shows H>=4
  2S  "4 spades, not 4 hearts"                   shows S>=4, H<=3
  X   "Penalty: four or more diamonds, no major"  shows D>=4, H<=3, S<=3
  P   "No 4-card major"                          shows H<=3, S<=3
      priority -1

# Opener after responder's game-forcing minor over their majors: 3NT,
# the game our side can make with both majors held by one of us.
after 1N (2y) 3z (P) when y is not C, lho.H>=4, lho.S>=4, z is C | z is D
  3N  "Game in notrump"

# Opener after the value-showing double: pass unless they run; a double
# of the suit they run to is for penalties. Responder the same after
# opener's pass: game with 10+ and their suit held.
after 1N (2y) X (P) when y is not C, (lho.H>=4, lho.S>=4) | ((maybe lho.y<=3), (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3))
  P   "Defending their artificial overcall"

# Whatever their overcall, once their advancer bids over our double
# opener has said what he has; the rules above add what he can (a
# penalty double). 2026-09-28: 110 no-rule boards, 1N 2♠ X 2NT and alike.
after 1N (2y) X (*) when !rho.last=P, !rho.last=X
  P   "No further bid"                          priority -10
after 1N (2y) X (2z) when y is not C, (lho.H>=4, lho.S>=4) | ((maybe lho.y<=3), (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3))
  X   "Penalty: four or more {z}"                    shows z>=4
  P   "No further bid"                          priority -5
after 1N (2y) X (2z) X (P) when y is not C, (rho.H>=4, rho.S>=4) | ((maybe rho.y<=3), (maybe rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3))
  P   "Partner doubled for penalties: defend"
after 1N (2y) X (2z) P (P) when y is not C, (rho.H>=4, rho.S>=4) | ((maybe rho.y<=3), (maybe rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3))
  X   "Penalty: four or more {z}"                    shows z>=4
  3N  "Game: 10+, {z} held"                          shows hcp>=10, stop(z)
  P   "No further bid"                          priority -5

# ── Their 2NT: both minors (Cappelletti, Meckwell, Multi-Landy) ─────
after 1N (2N)
  X   "Values: 8+ HCP"                shows hcp>=8
  3H  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more hearts"     shows H>=5, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
  3S  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more spades"     shows S>=5, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
  4H  "Game: six or more hearts"                     shows H>=6, hcp>=10
      when  !texas_1nt
      priority 1
  4S  "Game: six or more spades"                     shows S>=6, hcp>=10
      when  !texas_1nt
      priority 1
  3N  "Game: 10+ HCP"                                shows hcp>=10
  P   "No bid over their 2NT"
      priority -10
after 1N (2N) 3z (P) when z is H | z is S
  4{z}  "Three-card support: game in the major"      shows z>=3
  3N    "Game in notrump"
        priority -1

# Responder passed their overcall: opener has shown his hand.
after 1N (2y) P (P)
  P   "No further bid"

# ── They preempted over our 1NT (a three-level suit) ─────────────────
# No rule existed (2026-09-25: 1NT (3H) in Basic_NT and What_To_Open).
# Game in notrump with their suit held, four of a five-card major, a
# double with game values and no stopper, short in their suit (opener
# passes it with four of theirs); otherwise pass.
after 1N (3y) when y is not N
  3N  "Game: 9+, a stopper in {y}"         shows hcp>=9, stop(y)
  4H  "Game: five or more hearts, 9+"      shows H>=5, hcp>=9
      when  y is not H, !texas_1nt | y is S   # over 3♣/3♦ 4♥ is Texas
  4S  "Game: five or more spades, 9+"      shows S>=5, hcp>=9
      when  y is not S
  X   "Takeout: 9+, no stopper in {y}"     shows hcp>=9, y<=2
      priority -1
  P   "No bid over their preempt"
      priority -10
after 1N (3y) X (P) when y is not N
  P   "Four of their suit: defends"        shows y>=4
      priority 1
  3N  "A stopper in {y}"                   shows stop(y)
  cheapest(S) "Four or more spades"        shows S>=4   when y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Four or more hearts"        shows H>=4   when y is not H
  cheapest(D) "Four or more diamonds"      shows D>=4   when y is not D
      priority -1
  cheapest(C) "Four or more clubs"         shows C>=4   when y is not C
      priority -1
  3N  "Game in notrump"
      priority -5
after 1N (3y) P (P) when y is not N
  P   "No further bid"
files.rules/notrump/nt-splinter.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Splinters over 1NT (nt-splinter.notes.md): 1NT–3♦ with
# `notrump.three_d_response = splinter`, 1NT–3♥/3♠ with
# `notrump.three_major_splinter`. The bid suit is a singleton or void,
# with four or more in each other suit (4-4-4-1, 5-4-4-0 and alike,
# no five-card major) and game values; not with a singleton A, K or Q
# (BBA bids Stayman with those). Opener bids game in a four-card
# major he shares, else 3NT.

module nt-splinter "Splinters over 1NT"
  kind   convention
  needs  notrump-base
  param  three_d  = notrump.three_d_response default natural
  param  major_splinter = notrump.three_major_splinter default false

after 1N (P)
  3D  "Splinter: 0-1 ♦, 4+ in each other suit, game values"  alert
      shows D<=1, !has(A,D), !has(K,D), !has(Q,D), H=4, S=4, C>=4, strength>=game
      when  three_d is splinter
      sets  forcing=game, ask=nt_splinter
      artificial
      priority 2                           # ahead of Stayman
  3H  "Splinter: 0-1 ♥, 4+ in each other suit, game values"  alert
      shows H<=1, !has(A,H), !has(K,H), !has(Q,H), S=4, D>=4, C>=4, strength>=game
      when  major_splinter
      sets  forcing=game, ask=nt_splinter
      artificial
      priority 2
  3S  "Splinter: 0-1 ♠, 4+ in each other suit, game values"  alert
      shows S<=1, !has(A,S), !has(K,S), !has(Q,S), H=4, D>=4, C>=4, strength>=game
      when  major_splinter
      sets  forcing=game, ask=nt_splinter
      artificial
      priority 2

when asked nt_splinter
  4S  "Four spades: game in the fit"        shows S>=4
      when  partner.last=3D | partner.last=3H
      sets  trump=S
  4H  "Four hearts: game in the fit"        shows H>=4, S<=3 | partner.last=3S
      when  partner.last=3D | partner.last=3S
      sets  trump=H
  3N  "No major fit: 3NT"
      priority -1
files.rules/notrump/one-nt.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.

module notrump-base "1NT opening and natural responses"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  skill  basic_bidding/notrump_openings
  param  nt_min   = notrump.one_nt.range_min default 15
  param  nt_max   = notrump.one_nt.range_max default 17
  param  nt_min_plus  = notrump.one_nt.range_min_plus default false
  param  nt_max_minus = notrump.one_nt.range_max_minus default false
  param  alt_min  = notrump.one_nt_alt.range_min
  param  alt_max  = notrump.one_nt_alt.range_max
  param  alt_min_plus  = notrump.one_nt_alt.range_min_plus default false
  param  alt_max_minus = notrump.one_nt_alt.range_max_minus default false
  param  alt_where = notrump.one_nt_alt.seat_vul
  param  one_less = notrump.one_nt.allow_one_less default false
  param  minors   = bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers:style default relay
  param  mtp      = bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers:over_1nt default true
  param  three_c_transfer = bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers:three_c_diamonds default false
  param  three_d  = notrump.three_d_response default natural
  param  systems_on = nt_overcalls.direct.systems_on default true
  param  vs_2c   = bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers:vs_2c default false
  param  style   = general.style
  param  five_major = notrump.one_nt.five_card_major default sometimes
  param  jacoby  = bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers default true
  param  puppet_1nt = bidding_conventions/puppet_stayman:over_1nt default false
  param  allow_5422 = notrump.one_nt.allow_5422 default false
  param  allow_4441 = notrump.one_nt.allow_4441 default false

# ── Systems on (Rick, 2026-10-05) ────────────────────────────────────
# One notion: partner's last call is a natural notrump showing a
# balanced range, and our notrump system answers it at that level: at
# 1NT the two-level structure (Stayman, transfers, ...), at 2NT the
# three-level one (two-nt-responses.bid, two-nt-minors.bid). Each piece
# only as the card plays it. Opener's range is whatever the auction
# showed (1NT 15-17, 2NT 20-21, 2♣–2♦–2NT 22-23, Kokish 24-25, a 1NT
# overcall 15-18 ...), and the responses count strength bands against it.
#
# Where (Rick, 2026-10-05; one-nt.notes.md, "Systems on"): our side has
# not bid a suit naturally before the notrump. Artificial calls do not
# count (2♣ strong, 2♦ waiting, the 2♥ bust, Kokish's relays: rules mark
# them `artificial`), nor do the opponents' calls (2♣ (2♠) P (P) 2NT is
# on). One exception, Rick's list: a positive response to our artificial
# opening (2♣–2♠–2NT, 2♣–2♥–2NT) is on too; BBA's treatment
# (`general.style = bba`) keeps its natural rebids there instead. Not
# when the notrump answers partner's opening (1♥–1NT, 2♣–2NT), or when it
# is our second natural notrump. Our notrump overcall or balancing
# notrump: as the card says (`nt_overcalls.direct.systems_on`).
systems on when call = 1N | call = 2N, maybe shown.balanced, shown.second_longest.min <= 4
  !me.named(C), !me.named(D), !me.named(H), !me.named(S), !me.named(N)
  !partner.opened, !partner.named(N), !(lho.opened | rho.opened) | systems_on
  (me.opened, style is not bba) | (!partner.named(C), !partner.named(D), !partner.named(H), !partner.named(S))

# The 1NT system's ways in (LANGUAGE.md §4, named auction patterns):
# our 1NT where the system came on, RHO passing; with `nt1` also RHO's
# double of our 1NT overcall or balancing 1NT (a double of the 1NT
# opening has its own rules: `after 1N (X)` in stayman.bid and
# jacoby-transfers.bid). A context that starts `after nt1` reaches the
# responses from all of them.
define auction nt1_undoubled = systems 1N (P)
define auction nt1 = nt1_undoubled
  systems 1N (X)   when lho.opened | rho.opened

# The range is in HCP, as BBA plays it (15-17 HCP exactly, whatever the
# tens or length). With the card option "1NT may be 1 HCP light", a hand one
# HCP short opens 1NT when its extras bring it to the range in total points.
# A five-card major only as the card allows (`one_nt.five_card_major`):
# BBA opens 1NT with one only with "1NT opening shape 5 major"; its bare
# SAYC card (probe 2026-09-30) opens the major.
#
# The card's qualifiers (one-nt.notes.md, "Range qualifiers"). A plus on
# the minimum ("14+") is a good 14: the range is judged, in total points,
# so 14 HCP opens only with a point more (a five-card suit, two tens) and,
# the same judgment at the top, a 17 that is worth 18 does not. A minus on
# the maximum ("15-17-", a poor 17) judges the top only. The plus on the
# maximum and the minus on the minimum change nothing: the HCP range
# already takes every hand at those counts. Partner reads the judged range
# (total points 15-17 for "14+-17") and counts against it.
#
# The alternate range (`notrump.one_nt_alt`) is in force where its
# seat/vulnerability text covers the opener's seat and vulnerability
# (`seat_vul`: "Not Vul", "3rd/4th", "NV 1st/2nd"), the main range
# everywhere else. Partner and the opponents read the 1NT by the same
# rules, so every count against opener's range (responses, slam, our
# defence's reading) sees the range in force. The responses are the same
# either way (`one_nt_alt.same_responses`; a separate system for the
# other range is not modelled).
define nt_alt = alt_min is not none, alt_max is not none, seat_vul(alt_where)
define nt_main_range = hcp=nt_min..nt_max, points>=nt_min+1 | !nt_min_plus, points<=nt_max | !(nt_min_plus | nt_max_minus)
define nt_alt_range = hcp=alt_min..alt_max, points>=alt_min+1 | !alt_min_plus, points<=alt_max | !(alt_min_plus | alt_max_minus)
# Opener has shown more than the 1NT range in force (a 2NT, 2♣ then
# notrump): the quantitative answers below.
define above_1nt = (!nt_alt, shown.hcp.min>=nt_max+1) | (nt_alt, shown.hcp.min>=alt_max+1)
# A weak notrump in force (the range in force tops at 14 or less: Rick's
# 11+-14 not vulnerable). Opener's balanced hands too strong for it open
# a suit, and the rebids show them (Rick, 2026-11-07; rebids.bid, "With
# a weak notrump"): after a one-level response 1NT from the top of the
# range up to 17 (`above_weak_nt`: a good 14 to 17 opposite 11+-14),
# 2NT 18-19; after a 2/1 the jump to 3NT the same, 2NT 12-14 or 18+.
# The opener's own seat and vulnerability decide it (`seat_vul` reads
# the actor).
define weak_nt = (!nt_alt, nt_max <= 14) | (nt_alt, alt_max <= 14)
# The top of the weak range judged out of it (a 14 worth 15 total points
# where the range is "11+-14", one-nt.notes.md "Range qualifiers")
# belongs with the hands above the range. Partner reads the 14 in: a
# 14-17 reading measured better than 15-17 (rebids.notes.md).
define weak_nt_top_out = (!nt_alt, hcp=nt_max, points>=nt_max+1) | (nt_alt, hcp=alt_max, points>=alt_max+1)
define above_weak_nt = (!nt_alt, hcp>=nt_max+1, hcp<=17) | (nt_alt, hcp>=alt_max+1, hcp<=17) | weak_nt_top_out
when opening, !nt_alt
  1N  "Notrump opening: {nt_min}-{nt_max} HCP, balanced"  announce "{nt_min} to {nt_max}"
      shows nt_main_range, balanced, five_major is not never | (H<=4, S<=4)
  1N  "Notrump opening: {nt_min}-{nt_max} HCP, balanced"  announce "{nt_min} to {nt_max}"
      shows hcp=nt_min-1, points>=nt_min, balanced, five_major is not never | (H<=4, S<=4)
      when one_less
  # The card's shape options (one-nt.notes.md, "5-4-2-2 and 4-4-4-1").
  # 5-4-2-2 with a five-card minor and four hearts or four of the other
  # minor, both doubletons headed by the ace or king (BBA: never with
  # four spades, always with both doubletons stopped). 4-4-4-1 only with
  # a singleton ace or king.
  1N  "Notrump opening: {nt_min}-{nt_max} HCP, 5-4-2-2"  announce "{nt_min} to {nt_max}"
      shows nt_main_range, shape 5-4-2-2, C=5 | D=5, S=2, H>=2, D>=2, C>=2, has(A,S) | has(K,S), H>=3 | has(A,H) | has(K,H), D>=3 | has(A,D) | has(K,D), C>=3 | has(A,C) | has(K,C)
      when allow_5422
  1N  "Notrump opening: {nt_min}-{nt_max} HCP, 4-4-4-1"  announce "{nt_min} to {nt_max}"
      shows nt_main_range, shape 4-4-4-1, S>=2 | has(A,S) | has(K,S), H>=2 | has(A,H) | has(K,H), D>=2 | has(A,D) | has(K,D), C>=2 | has(A,C) | has(K,C)
      when allow_4441
# The alternate range, where it is in force: the same rules on its range.
when opening, nt_alt
  1N  "Notrump opening: {alt_min}-{alt_max} HCP, balanced"  announce "{alt_min} to {alt_max}"
      shows nt_alt_range, balanced, five_major is not never | (H<=4, S<=4)
  1N  "Notrump opening: {alt_min}-{alt_max} HCP, 5-4-2-2"  announce "{alt_min} to {alt_max}"
      shows nt_alt_range, shape 5-4-2-2, C=5 | D=5, S=2, H>=2, D>=2, C>=2, has(A,S) | has(K,S), H>=3 | has(A,H) | has(K,H), D>=3 | has(A,D) | has(K,D), C>=3 | has(A,C) | has(K,C)
      when allow_5422
  1N  "Notrump opening: {alt_min}-{alt_max} HCP, 4-4-4-1"  announce "{alt_min} to {alt_max}"
      shows nt_alt_range, shape 4-4-4-1, S>=2 | has(A,S) | has(K,S), H>=2 | has(A,H) | has(K,H), D>=2 | has(A,D) | has(K,D), C>=2 | has(A,C) | has(K,C)
      when allow_4441

# Responder. Strength bands are total points measured against opener's
# range, so they follow the card: with 15-17, invite is 8-9 and game 10-15.
after nt1 when !they.bid | systems_on
  6N  "To play: slam values"
      shows balanced, points>=32-partner.hcp.min, H<=4, S<=4   # with five, transfer first
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      shows balanced, strength=slam_invite, points<=31-partner.hcp.min, H<=4, S<=4   # with five, transfer first
      when  style is not bba
      sets  ask=quant
      # Rick: 17 opposite 15-17 jumps to 6NT (BBA: 10 of 12 hands; 16
      # mostly invites). BBA's choices at 16-17 do not follow controls.
  3N  "To play: {game} total points"
      shows strength=game, H<=4, S<=4                   # with five, transfer first
      when  style is not bba
  2N  "Invitational: {invite} total points"
      shows strength=invite, H<=4, S<=4, C<=5, D<=5     # a long suit has its own route
      when  !(mtp, minors is four_way), !(mtp, minors is four_way_reversed), style is not bba   # 2NT is a transfer
      when  !(mtp, minors is two_nt_three_c)                # 2NT is a transfer
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  2N  "Invitational: {invite} total points, a long minor"
      shows strength=invite, H<=4, S<=4, (C>=6 | D>=6)
      when  !mtp | minors is relay         # no minor route for invitations
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  # A slam try in the minor: six cards, or five in an unbalanced hand
  # (2026-09-27: 15-18 counts with a five-card minor bid 3NT opposite
  # 15-17; a nine-card fit makes slam double dummy 72% of the time at 29
  # HCP between the hands, an eight-card fit 71% at 30).
  3C  "Slam try: six or more clubs, or five and unbalanced"
      shows C>=6 | (C>=5, !balanced), strength>=slam_invite, H<=4, S<=4
      when  !three_c_transfer, !(mtp, minors is bba), !puppet_1nt
  3D  "Slam try: six or more diamonds, or five and unbalanced"
      shows D>=6 | (D>=5, !balanced), strength>=slam_invite, H<=4, S<=4
      when  three_d is natural
  3N  "No better call: {game} total points or more"
      shows strength>=game
      priority -5                      # a strong hand never passes 1NT
  P   "No game interest: {signoff} total points"
      shows strength=signoff
      when  style is not bba
      priority -10                     # only if nothing else fits

  # The BBA treatment (probed 2026-09-24, one-nt.notes.md). Total points
  # are HCP + ½ per ten (the `bba` valuation), with two exceptions: with
  # 4-4 in the minors the tens do not count, and 8 HCP 4-3-3-3 without a
  # ten passes. At IMPs game comes a point earlier (9 opposite 15-17).
  # The slam invitation needs 16 HCP: 15 and tens bids 3NT.
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      shows balanced, strength=slam_invite, hcp>=33-partner.hcp.max, points<=31-partner.hcp.min, H<=4, S<=4
      when  style is bba
      sets  ask=quant
  3N  "To play: {game} total points"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, bba_nt_game_points>=10, strength<=game
      when  matchpoints
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min>=15, partner.hcp.max<=17
  3N  "To play: game values"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, bba_nt_imp_game_points>=10, strength<=game
      when  imps
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min>=15, partner.hcp.max<=17
  # Opposite a 1NT that is not 15-17 (Precision, our 1NT overcall), the
  # earlier rules, measured against partner's range: the counts below were
  # fitted opposite 15-17.
  3N  "To play: {game} total points"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, (strength=game, C<=3 | D<=3 | C>=5 | D>=5) | (C=4, D=4, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.min, hcp<=32-partner.hcp.max)
      when  matchpoints
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min<=14 | partner.hcp.max>=18
  3N  "To play: game values"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, (points>=24-partner.hcp.min, points<=32-partner.hcp.max, C<=3 | D<=3 | C>=5 | D>=5) | (C=4, D=4, hcp>=24-partner.hcp.min, hcp<=32-partner.hcp.max)
      when  imps
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min<=14 | partner.hcp.max>=18
  2N  "Invitational: {invite} total points"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, C<=5, D<=5, (strength=invite, C<=3 | D<=3 | C>=5 | D>=5, !shape 4333 | hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max | hcp>=26-partner.hcp.max | has(T,S) | has(T,H) | has(T,D) | has(T,C)) | (C=4, D=4, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max, hcp<=24-partner.hcp.min)
      when  !(mtp, minors is four_way), !(mtp, minors is four_way_reversed), matchpoints
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min<=14 | partner.hcp.max>=18
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  2N  "Invitational"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, C<=5, D<=5, (points>=25-partner.hcp.max, points<=23-partner.hcp.min, C<=3 | D<=3 | C>=5 | D>=5, !shape 4333 | hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max | hcp>=26-partner.hcp.max | has(T,S) | has(T,H) | has(T,D) | has(T,C)) | (C=4, D=4, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max, hcp<=23-partner.hcp.min)
      when  !(mtp, minors is four_way), !(mtp, minors is four_way_reversed), imps
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min<=14 | partner.hcp.max>=18
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  P   "No game interest"
      shows (strength=signoff, C<=3 | D<=3 | C>=5 | D>=5) | (C=4, D=4, hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max) | (shape 4333, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max, hcp<=25-partner.hcp.max, !has(T,S), !has(T,H), !has(T,D), !has(T,C))
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min<=14 | partner.hcp.max>=18
      priority -10
  # At matchpoints BBA's lines between pass, 2NT and 3NT are its own
  # counts (bba_nt_points, bba_nt_game_points: one-nt.notes.md, "BBA's
  # count"): shape-dependent weights, a ten worth 0-0.9, a doubleton major
  # without A or K charged. Calibrated opposite 15-17.
  2N  "Invitational: {invite} total points"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, C<=5, D<=5, bba_nt_points>=8, bba_nt_game_points<=9, points>=25-partner.hcp.max
      when  !(mtp, minors is four_way), !(mtp, minors is four_way_reversed), matchpoints
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min>=15, partner.hcp.max<=17
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  2N  "Invitational"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, C<=5, D<=5, bba_nt_imp_points>=8, bba_nt_imp_game_points<=9, points>=24-partner.hcp.max
      when  !(mtp, minors is four_way), !(mtp, minors is four_way_reversed), imps
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min>=15, partner.hcp.max<=17
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  P   "No game interest"
      shows bba_nt_points<=7
      when  matchpoints, style is bba, partner.hcp.min>=15, partner.hcp.max<=17
      priority -10
  P   "No game interest"
      shows bba_nt_imp_points<=7
      when  imps, style is bba, partner.hcp.min>=15, partner.hcp.max<=17
      priority -10

# Natural major-suit responses when the card plays no transfers
# (`notrump.jacoby_transfers.play` off; one-nt.notes.md, "Natural majors
# without transfers", probes/nt-van-*.toml). 2M is to play with five or
# more and no game interest; 3M is five or more and game values, forcing:
# opener raises to 4M with three or more, else bids 3NT. With 5-5 the
# higher suit. 5-4 in the majors goes through Stayman (stayman.bid), and
# bids 3M over the 2♦ denial.
after nt1 when !they.bid | systems_on
  3S  "Five or more spades, game forcing"
      shows S>=5, S>=H, strength>=game
      when  !jacoby
      sets  forcing=game, ask=choose_game(S)
  3H  "Five or more hearts, game forcing"
      shows H>=5, H>S, strength>=game
      when  !jacoby
      sets  forcing=game, ask=choose_game(H)
  4S  "To play: seven or more spades, short of a game force"
      shows S>=7, S>=H, strength=invite
      when  !jacoby
      priority 1                       # ahead of the invitational Stayman (stayman.bid)
  4H  "To play: seven or more hearts, short of a game force"
      shows H>=7, H>S, strength=invite
      when  !jacoby
      priority 1
  2S  "To play: five or more spades, no game interest"
      shows S>=5, S>=H, strength=signoff | (strength=invite, hcp<=6)
      when  !jacoby
  2H  "To play: five or more hearts, no game interest"
      shows H>=5, H>S, strength=signoff | (strength=invite, hcp<=6)
      when  !jacoby

# Opener after the signoff: pass (BBA passed 641 of 642 on the vanilla set).
after nt1 2H (P) | nt1 2S (P) when !jacoby
  P   "Partner's signoff"

# Opener chooses the game: four of the major with three or more (an
# eight-card fit), 3NT with two, whatever the strength (BBA, every one of
# 800 probe hands: probes/nt-van-3h-opener.toml, nt-van-3s-opener.toml).
when asked choose_game(M)
  4M  "Three or more {M}: game in the fit"   shows M>=3
  3N  "Two {M}: 3NT"                         shows M<=2

# Responder after the choice: with six, 3NT goes back to the major (an
# eight-card fit again); slam values bid it.
when answered choose_game(M), partner.last=3N
  6M  "Slam: six or more {M}, slam values"   shows M>=6, strength>=slam
  6N  "Slam values, no fit"                  shows M<=5, strength>=slam
  4N  "Quantitative, no fit"                 shows M<=5, balanced, strength=slam_invite
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      sets  ask=quant
  4M  "Six or more {M}: game in the fit"     shows M>=6, strength<=slam_invite
  P   "No fit: play 3NT"                     shows M<=5, strength<=slam_invite
when answered choose_game(M), partner.last=4{M}
  6M  "Slam in the fit"                      shows strength>=slam
  # The same slam, counting shortness (support points).
  6M  "Slam in the fit"  shows tp(M)>=33-partner.points.min
  P   "Game in the fit"                      shows strength<=slam_invite
      priority -1

# Opener answers the natural 3m slam try (six of the minor, slam-invite
# values): slam with a fit and a maximum, else 3NT (it had no rule;
# Basic_What_To_Open 320).
after 1N (P) 3C (P) when !three_c_transfer, !(mtp, minors is bba), !puppet_1nt
  6C  "Accepts: a club fit and a maximum"   shows C>=3, hcp>=17
  4C  "A club fit, not a maximum: responder decides"   shows C>=3, hcp<=16
      sets  trump=C, forcing=game
  3N  "Declines: no club fit"               shows C<=2
after 1N (P) 3D (P) when three_d is natural
  6D  "Accepts: a diamond fit and a maximum"   shows D>=3, hcp>=17
  4D  "A diamond fit, not a maximum: responder decides"   shows D>=3, hcp<=16
      sets  trump=D, forcing=game
  3N  "Declines: no diamond fit"               shows D<=2
# Responder after the answer: with the fit known, slam from 17 total
# points (32+ between the hands); without it, 6NT only with slam values.
after 1N (P) 3C (P) 4C (P) | 1N (P) 3D (P) 4D (P)
  6{trump} "Slam in the fit: 17+"          shows points>=17
  5{trump} "Game in the fit"               shows points<=16
after 1N (P) 3C (P) 3N (P) | 1N (P) 3D (P) 3N (P)
  6N  "No fit, but slam values: {slam} total points"   shows strength>=slam
  P   "No fit: 3NT"
      priority -5

# Opener answers the invitation: accept only when game is certain (17
# opposite 8-9). With a 4-4 major fit found through Stayman, play there.
when asked nt_invite
  4H  "Accepts, in the 4-4 heart fit"   shows H>=4, strength>=game    when partner.H>=4
  4S  "Accepts, in the 4-4 spade fit"   shows S>=4, strength>=game    when partner.S>=4
  3H  "Declines, in the 4-4 heart fit"  shows H>=4, strength<=invite  when partner.H>=4
  3S  "Declines, in the 4-4 spade fit"  shows S>=4, strength<=invite  when partner.S>=4
  3N  "Accepts the invitation"          shows strength>=game
  P   "Declines: not a maximum"         shows strength<=invite

# Responder after a decline in the fit: the invitation was answered.
# (bba: over 3S responder bids game with the top of the invitation;
# stayman.bid.)
when answered nt_invite, partner.last=3H | partner.last=3S, style is not bba
  P   "Partner declined: play three of the major"

# Opener answers the quantitative 4NT: slam with 32 combined.
when asked quant
  6N  "Accepts the slam invitation"     shows points>=32-partner.points.min
      when  style is not bba | above_1nt
  P   "Declines: not enough for slam"   shows points<=31-partner.points.min
      when  style is not bba | above_1nt
  # BBA, over its 1NT: 17 HCP accepts, 16 declines whatever its tens
  # (1N_Balanced_Raise, Basic_NT).
  6N  "Accepts the slam invitation"     shows hcp>=33-partner.hcp.min
      when  style is bba, !above_1nt
  P   "Declines: not enough for slam"   shows hcp<=32-partner.hcp.min
      when  style is bba, !above_1nt

# Responder over a 2♣ overcall of our 1NT, when the card keeps the
# structure on (`notrump.jacoby_transfers.vs_2c`). The natural notrump calls
# are unchanged — 2♣ takes nothing away from them — and the double
# replaces the 2♣ Stayman call (stayman.bid). BBA plays it this way on
# every card in the corpus that sets the switch.
after 1N (2C) when vs_2c
  6N  "To play: {slam} total points"
      shows balanced, strength=slam, H<=4, S<=4
  4N  "Quantitative: {slam_invite} total points, invites 6NT"
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      shows balanced, strength=slam_invite
      sets  ask=quant
  3N  "To play: {game} total points"
      shows strength=game, H<=4, S<=4                   # with five, transfer first
  2N  "Invitational: {invite} total points"
      shows strength=invite, H<=4, S<=4, C<=5, D<=5     # a long suit has its own route
      when  !(mtp, minors is four_way), !(mtp, minors is four_way_reversed)
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  3N  "No better call: {game} total points or more"
      shows strength>=game
      priority -5
  P   "No bid over their 2♣"
      priority -10
files.rules/notrump/puppet-1nt.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Puppet Stayman over 1NT (`notrump.stayman.puppet_1nt`; puppet-1nt.notes.md):
# 1NT–3♣ asks for a four- or five-card major, forcing to game. Responder
# bids it with game values, no five-card major and a three- or
# four-card major. Opener's answers and everything after them are the
# Puppet rules over 2NT (two-nt-responses.bid, `when asked puppet`):
# 3♥/3♠ five cards, 3♦ a four-card major, 3NT neither; after 3♦
# responder names the major he does not hold, 4♦ both, 4♣ both with
# slam interest. 2♣ Stayman stays for invitational hands.

module puppet-1nt "Puppet Stayman over 1NT"
  kind   convention
  card   bidding_conventions/puppet_stayman:over_1nt
  needs  two-nt-responses
  skill  bidding_conventions/puppet_stayman

after 1N (P)
  3C  "Puppet Stayman: asks for a four- or five-card major"  alert
      shows strength>=game, H<=4, S<=4, H>=3 | S>=3
      sets  forcing=game, ask=puppet
      artificial
      priority 2                           # ahead of 2♣ Stayman with game values

after 1N (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) 3N (P)
  P   "No fit: 3NT"
files.rules/notrump/super-accept.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.

module super-accept "Super-accepting a Jacoby transfer"
  kind   convention
  card   bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers:super_accept
  needs  jacoby-transfers
  skill  bidding_conventions/super_accept
  param  system = general.system   # `brill`: the Brill card's treatments

# Four-card support and 16-17 (2026-09-25: any four-card super-accept cost
# 1,517 IMPs to our side against 16+; see jacoby-transfers.notes.md): jump in
# the major. With superaccept-doubleton on as well,
# maximums with a doubleton choose the more descriptive doubleton bids, so
# this is left for maximums without one (4-3-3-3).
after nt1 2D (P) when system is not brill
  3H  "Super-accept: 4+ hearts, a maximum"   shows H>=4, hcp>=16
after nt1 2H (P) when system is not brill
  3S  "Super-accept: 4+ spades, a maximum"   shows S>=4, hcp>=16

# brill (the Brill card): the jump is the minimum with four trumps (a
# 4-3-3-3 minimum completes, jacoby-transfers.bid); maximums with four
# go through 2NT or the doubleton (superaccept-doubleton.bid). Brill
# /explain, 2026-10-15, "4+ hearts, min": `hearts > 3 and not max`;
# "4+ spades, min": `spades > 3 and not max`.
after nt1 2D (P) when system is brill
  3H  "Four or more hearts, a minimum"   shows H>=4, hcp<=15, shortest<=2
after nt1 2H (P) when system is brill
  3S  "Four or more spades, a minimum"   shows S>=4, hcp<=15, shortest<=2
files.rules/notrump/superaccept-doubleton.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.

module superaccept-doubleton "Superaccept doubleton"
  kind   convention
  card   bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers:super_accept_doubleton
  needs  super-accept
  skill  bidding_conventions/super_accept
  param  system = general.system   # `brill`: the Brill card's treatments

# Four-card support, a maximum and a doubleton: bid the doubleton when it is
# cheaper than 2NT, otherwise 2NT. (BBA calls this "Extended acceptance".)
# With the queen in a spade doubleton BBA bids 2NT: the queen is worth
# more as a stopper than the shortness is for ruffs.
after nt1 2D (P)
  2S  "Super-accept: 4+ hearts, maximum, doubleton spade"  alert
      shows H>=4, hcp>=16, S=2, !has(Q,S)      # with Qx, KQ or AQ: 2NT, as BBA
      artificial
  2N  "Super-accept: 4+ hearts, maximum, a doubleton"      alert
      shows H>=4, hcp>=16, shortest=2
      artificial
after nt1 2H (P)
  2N  "Super-accept: 4+ spades, maximum, a doubleton"      alert
      shows S>=4, hcp>=16, shortest=2
      artificial

# brill (the Brill card): a maximum 4-3-3-3 bids 2NT too, as the jump to
# three of the major is the minimum (super-accept.bid). Brill /explain,
# 2026-10-15: "Superaccept, no doubleton" `max and ExplicitShape ==
# '3=4=3=3'`; "Superaccept, max" (over 2H) `max and ExplicitShape ==
# '4=3=3=3'`; "Superaccept, doubleton" `max and S <= 2 and hearts > 3`.
after nt1 2D (P) when system is brill
  2N  "Super-accept: 4 hearts, maximum, 3=4=3=3"   alert
      shows H=4, S=3, D=3, C=3, hcp>=16
      artificial
after nt1 2H (P) when system is brill
  2N  "Super-accept: 4 spades, maximum, 4=3=3=3"   alert
      shows S=4, H=3, D=3, C=3, hcp>=16
      artificial
files.rules/notrump/two-nt-minors.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# The minors over a 2NT opening (two-nt-minors.notes.md):
#
# - `notrump.minor_transfers.over_2nt`: 3♠ relays to 4♣ with a long minor
#   (BBA's "Minor Suit Transfers after 2NT": one relay for either minor).
#   Too weak for game opposite opener's range (0-3 HCP opposite 20-21)
#   responder passes or bids 4♦ to play, five of the minor for game. Slam
#   hands keep the natural 4♣/4♦ tries (or Gerber). Not in a game force
#   (2♣–2♦–2NT, Kokish's 2NT): there the weak hands bid 3NT.
# - `notrump.minor_suit_stayman.over_2nt`: 3♠ is Minor Suit Stayman, five-four
#   or better in the minors and slam interest (game hands bid 3NT). Opener bids 4♣ with four
#   clubs, 4♦ with four diamonds and not four clubs, 3NT with neither.
#
# The 4♣/4♦ natural slam tries of two-nt-responses.bid stay.

module two-nt-minors "Minor-suit transfers and Minor Suit Stayman over 2NT"
  kind   convention
  needs  two-nt-responses
  skill  bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers
  skill  bidding_conventions/minor_suit_stayman
  param  mst = bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers:over_2nt default false
  param  mss = bidding_conventions/minor_suit_stayman:over_2nt default false
  param  rkcb   = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard default false
  param  gerber = bidding_conventions/gerber default false

# ── Minor-suit transfer: 3♠ relays to 4♣ ────────────────────────────
after nt2 when mst, !mss
  3S  "Relay to 4♣: six or more of a minor, weak"  alert
      shows C>=6 | D>=6, H<=3, S<=3, hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max
      when  !(we.forcing = game)
      sets  forcing=round, ask=minor_relay
      artificial
      priority 1                           # ahead of 3NT with shortness
after nt2 3S (P) when mst, !mss
  4C  "Completes the relay"  alert
      artificial
after nt2 3S (P) 4C (P) when mst, !mss
  P   "To play: clubs"                     shows C>=6, hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max
  4D  "To play: diamonds"                  shows D>=6, D>C, hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max
  5C  "Game: clubs"                        shows C>=6, C>=D, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max
      priority -1
  5D  "Game: diamonds"                     shows D>=6, D>C, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max
      priority -1
after nt2 3S (P) 4C (P) 4D (P) when mst, !mss
  P   "Partner's diamonds, to play"

# ── Minor Suit Stayman: 3♠ asks for a four-card minor ────────────────
after nt2 when mss
  3S  "Minor Suit Stayman: 5-4+ in the minors, slam interest"  alert
      shows C>=4, D>=4, C+D>=9, H<=3, S<=3, strength>=slam_invite
      sets  forcing=game
      artificial
      priority 1
after nt2 3S (P) when mss
  4C  "Four or more clubs"                 shows C>=4
  4D  "Four or more diamonds, not four clubs"  shows D>=4, C<=3
  3N  "No four-card minor"                 alert  shows C<=3, D<=3
      artificial
# With a fit and slam values, keycard for the minor when the card plays
# it (BBA: "Blackwood 1430, for ♣/♦"; the grand comes from the answers),
# else six.
after nt2 3S (P) 4m (P) when mss
  4N  "Keycard ask in {m}"                 alert
      when  rkcb
      shows tp(m)>=33-partner.hcp.min
      sets  trump=m, ask=keycards(m)
      artificial
      priority 1
  6m  "Slam in the minor fit"              shows tp(m)>=33-partner.hcp.min
      sets  trump=m
  5m  "Game in the minor fit"
      priority -1
# No fit: with slam values check the aces first when the card plays
# Gerber (partner's 3NT is natural, no suit agreed; BBA does not, but
# the same hands without the convention ask over 2NT and reach the
# grands).
after nt2 3S (P) 3N (P) when mss
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"             alert
      when  gerber
      shows points>=32-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1
  6N  "No fit: slam values"                shows points>=32-partner.hcp.min
  6C  "Slam in my long clubs"              shows C>=6, points>=32-partner.hcp.min
  6D  "Slam in my long diamonds"           shows D>=6, points>=32-partner.hcp.min
  4N  "No fit: quantitative, invites 6NT"    shows strength=slam_invite, points<=31-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=quant
  P   "No fit: 3NT"
      priority -5
files.rules/notrump/two-nt-responses.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Responses to a 2NT opening: the 1NT structure one level up, which is
# what BBA plays on this card — 3♣ Stayman, 3♦ and 3♥ transfers, 3NT to
# play, 4NT quantitative. With `notrump.stayman.puppet_2nt` 3♣ is Puppet
# Stayman instead (at the end of the file).
#
# The same system answers every natural, balanced 2NT (Rick, 2026-10-05:
# "the Kokish system should be all the same responses as after 2C/2NT,
# but just with modified HCP range for opener"), wherever systems are on
# (one-nt.bid, `systems on`): the 2NT opening (20-21), 2♣–2♦–2NT
# (22-23), Kokish's 2♣–2♦–2♥–2♠–2NT (24-25), 2♣ and a positive then
# 2NT, 2♣ (2♠) P (P) 2NT, a natural 2NT overcall. `nt2` below names
# them; every context of the system starts `after nt2`. Opener's
# range comes from what the auction showed, so every count here is a
# strength band or measured against partner's range (`hcp>=25-partner.
# hcp.min`), never an absolute number.
#
# Only the asking calls and opener's answers are here. What follows is
# already written against the question in `stayman.bid` and
# `jacoby-transfers.bid` (`when answered majors`, `when answered
# transfer(M)`), and the strength bands read opener's range, so the same
# rules invite and bid game at the right level. After 2♣ the side is in a
# game force (strong-openings.bid), so the passes here are not available
# there and the weakest hands bid game.
#
# Without these rules responder passed a 2NT opening whatever he held:
# 4,345 boards across the corpus, 123 of them in the Basic_* scenarios.

module two-nt-responses "Responses to a 2NT opening"
  kind   system
  needs  notrump-base
  skill  bidding_conventions/stayman
  skill  bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers
  param  stayman = bidding_conventions/stayman default true
  param  jacoby  = bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers default true
  param  puppet  = bidding_conventions/puppet_stayman:over_2nt default false
  param  gerber  = bidding_conventions/gerber default false
  param  tu      = bidding_conventions/texas:two_under default false
  param  style   = general.style

# The 2NT system's way in: our 2NT where the system came on (`systems on`
# in one-nt.bid), RHO passing.
define auction nt2 = systems 2N (P)

after nt2
  3C  "Stayman: asks for a four-card major"  alert
      shows H=4 | S=4, strength>=game
      when  stayman, !puppet, !shape 4333
      when  style is not bba
      sets  forcing=round, ask=majors
      artificial
      priority 1                           # ahead of a transfer with 5-4
  3D  "Transfer to hearts"  announce "Transfer"
      shows H>=5
      when  jacoby
      sets  forcing=round, ask=transfer(H)
      artificial
  3H  "Transfer to spades"  announce "Transfer"
      shows S>=5
      when  jacoby
      sets  forcing=round, ask=transfer(S)
      artificial
  3N  "To play: {game} total points"       shows strength>=game, H<=4, S<=4
      when  style is not bba
  # With a five-card major and transfers, transfer first and bid 4NT or
  # 6NT next (jacoby-transfers.bid), as over 1NT: opposite Kokish's 24-25
  # a 7-count with five hearts is a slam invitation, and 4NT here hid the
  # suit (2026-11-07).
  4N  "Quantitative: {slam_invite} total points, invites 6NT"
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      shows balanced, strength=slam_invite, (H<=4, S<=4) | !jacoby   # with five, transfer first
      when  style is not bba
      sets  ask=quant
  6N  "Slam: {slam} total points"          shows balanced, strength=slam, (H<=4, S<=4) | !jacoby
      when  style is not bba
  # A 4-count is the invitational band opposite 20-21, and there is no
  # invitation over 2NT short of 4NT: pass (BBA passes with 4 too).
  P   "No game: {signoff}-{invite} total points"    shows strength<=invite
      when  style is not bba
      priority -10

  # The BBA treatment (probed 2026-09-24, two-nt-responses.notes.md): in
  # HCP, tens aside. Pass with 4 or less, even with a four-card major;
  # from 5 Stayman (4-3-3-3 too) or 3NT; 4NT with 11, 6NT with 12 (or 11
  # and two tens). With 5-5 in the majors, transfer to spades first.
  3C  "Stayman: asks for a four-card major"  alert
      shows hcp>=25-partner.hcp.min, H=4 | S=4
      when  stayman, !puppet
      when  style is bba
      sets  forcing=round, ask=majors
      artificial
      priority 1
  3H  "Transfer to spades, 5-5 in the majors"  announce "Transfer"
      shows S>=5, H>=5
      when  jacoby
      when  style is bba
      sets  forcing=round, ask=transfer(S)
      artificial
  3N  "To play: game values"               shows hcp>=25-partner.hcp.min, H<=4, S<=4
      when  style is bba
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      shows balanced, hcp>=32-partner.hcp.max, points<=31-partner.hcp.min, H<=4, S<=4   # with five, transfer first
      when  style is bba
      sets  ask=quant
  6N  "Slam"                               shows balanced, points>=32-partner.hcp.min, H<=4, S<=4
      when  style is bba
  P   "No game: 4 HCP or less"             shows hcp<=24-partner.hcp.min
      when  style is bba
      priority -10

# A slam try in a minor (2026-09-27; 483 boards stopped at 2NT-3NT where
# BBA bid slam, half of them in a minor): four of the minor with six, or
# five in an unbalanced hand, and slam-invite values. Opener bids six
# with three-card support (20-21 and a fit is enough), else 4NT, no fit;
# responder then bids 6NT with slam values.
# With Gerber on the card 4♣ asks for aces instead (gerber.bid): the club
# hands ask and bid 6♣. The diamond try stays.
after nt2 when style is not bba
  4C  "Slam try: six or more clubs, or five and unbalanced"
      shows C>=6 | (C>=5, !balanced), strength>=slam_invite, H<=4, S<=4
      when  !gerber, !tu                          # 4♣ is 2-under Texas
  4D  "Slam try: six or more diamonds, or five and unbalanced"
      shows D>=6 | (D>=5, !balanced), strength>=slam_invite, H<=4, S<=4
      when  !texas_2nt                                # 4♦ is Texas (texas-transfers.bid)
after nt2 4x (P) when (x is C, !gerber, !tu) | (x is D, !texas_2nt), style is not bba
  6{x}  "A fit: slam"                       shows x>=3
  4N    "No fit"                            shows x<=2
after nt2 4x (P) 4N (P) when (x is C, !gerber, !tu) | (x is D, !texas_2nt), style is not bba
  6N  "No fit, but slam values"                  shows strength>=slam
  P   "No fit: 4NT"
      priority -5

# Opener answers Stayman. 3♦ is the negative, as over 1NT.
after nt2 3C (P) when !puppet
  3H  "4+ hearts"                 shows H>=4
  3S  "4 spades, not 4 hearts"    shows S>=4, H<=3
  3D  "No four-card major"        shows H<=3, S<=3

# Opener completes the transfer.
after nt2 3D (P)
  3H  "Completes transfer"
after nt2 3H (P)
  3S  "Completes transfer"

# Responder after the completed transfer. The generic rules after a
# transfer (jacoby-transfers.bid) left weak and unbalanced hands with no
# call opposite 20-21: 408 boards across the corpus. BBA: pass with 0-3;
# from 4 (25 combined), 3NT with five of the major, balanced or not, and
# game in the major with six. Fallbacks under the generic rules.
after nt2 3D (P) 3H (P)
  P   "Weak: play here"                        shows hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max
      priority -1
  3N  "Choice of games: five hearts, game values"  shows H=5, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max
      sets  ask=choice
      priority -1
  4H  "Game, six or more hearts"                  shows H>=6, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max
      priority -1
after nt2 3H (P) 3S (P)
  P   "Weak: play here"                        shows hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max
      priority -1
  3N  "Choice of games: five spades, game values"  shows S=5, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max
      sets  ask=choice
      priority -1
  4S  "Game, six or more spades"                  shows S>=6, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max
      priority -1

# ── Puppet Stayman (`notrump.stayman.puppet_2nt`, 2026-09-28) ──────────────
# 3♣ asks for a four- or five-card major. Responder bids it with game
# values, a three- or four-card major and no five (a five-card major
# transfers, 5-4 included); opener shows a five-card major (3♥/3♠), a
# four-card one (3♦) or neither (3NT). After 3♦ responder bids the
# major he does NOT hold, so the strong hand declares the 4-4 fit; 4♦
# is both majors, 4♣ both with slam interest. BBA plays it this way,
# after 2♣–2♦–2NT too (probed: two-nt-responses.notes.md, "Puppet
# Stayman over 2NT"). Only the ask names an auction; the rest follows
# the questions and answers.
after nt2 when puppet
  3C  "Puppet Stayman: asks for a four- or five-card major"  alert
      shows strength>=game, H<=4, S<=4, H>=3 | S>=3
      when  style is not bba
      sets  forcing=game, ask=puppet
      artificial
      priority 2                           # ahead of 3NT, 4NT, 6NT and Gerber
  3C  "Puppet Stayman: asks for a four- or five-card major"  alert
      shows hcp>=25-partner.hcp.min, H<=4, S<=4, H>=3 | S>=3
      when  style is bba
      sets  forcing=game, ask=puppet
      artificial
      priority 2

when asked puppet
  3H  "Five hearts"                           shows H>=5
  3S  "Five spades"                           shows S>=5, H<=4
  3D  "A four-card major, no five"            shows H=4 | S=4, H<=4, S<=4
      artificial
  3N  "No four- or five-card major"           shows H<=3, S<=3

# Opener has a four-card major. Responder names the one he does not hold.
# Without one, the no-fit counts after Stayman (stayman.bid): 6NT from
# 32 total points on opener's minimum.
when answered puppet, partner.last=3D
  3H  "Four spades, not four hearts"          alert
      shows S=4, H<=3
      sets  ask=puppet_fit(S)
      artificial
  3S  "Four hearts, not four spades"          alert
      shows H=4, S<=3
      sets  ask=puppet_fit(H)
      artificial
  4D  "Both majors, no slam interest: opener chooses"  alert
      shows H=4, S=4, strength<=game
      sets  ask=puppet_both
      artificial
  4C  "Both majors, slam interest: opener chooses"     alert
      shows H=4, S=4, strength>=slam_invite
      sets  ask=puppet_both
      artificial
  7N  "No four-card major: grand slam"        shows H<=3, S<=3, points>=37-partner.hcp.min
  6N  "No four-card major: slam"              shows H<=3, S<=3, points>=32-partner.hcp.min
  4N  "No four-card major: quantitative, invites 6NT"
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      shows H<=3, S<=3, balanced, strength=slam_invite, points<=31-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=quant
  3N  "No four-card major: game"              shows H<=3, S<=3, strength>=game
      priority -1

when asked puppet_fit(x)
  4{x}  "Four {x}: game in the fit"           shows x=4   sets trump=x
  3N    "No four {x}"                         shows x<=3
when asked puppet_both
  4S  "Four spades"                           shows S=4   sets trump=S
  4H  "Four hearts, not four spades"          shows H=4, S<=3   sets trump=H
after nt2 3C (P) 3D (P) 3N (P) when puppet
  P   "No fit: 3NT"

# Responder once opener has placed the contract in the 4-4 fit.
when answered puppet_fit(x), partner.last=4{x}
  6{x}  "Slam in the fit"                     shows tp(x)>=33-partner.hcp.min
        priority -1                           # behind the keycard ask (slam/rkcb-1430.bid)
  P     "Game in the fit"
        priority -5
when answered puppet_both, we.trump is suit
  6{trump}  "Slam in the fit"                 shows tp(trump)>=33-partner.hcp.min
        priority -1                           # behind the keycard ask (slam/rkcb-1430.bid)
  P         "Game in the fit"
            priority -5

# Opener has a five-card major.
when answered puppet, partner.last=3H
  6H  "Slam in the five-three fit"            shows H>=3, tp(H)>=33-partner.hcp.min
      sets  trump=H
  4H  "Game in the five-three fit"            shows H>=3
      sets  trump=H
      priority -1                             # slam first when there
  6N  "No fit: slam"                          shows H<=2, points>=32-partner.hcp.min
  4N  "No fit: quantitative, invites 6NT"     shows H<=2, balanced, strength=slam_invite, points<=31-partner.hcp.min
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      sets  ask=quant
  3N  "No fit: game"                          shows H<=2
      priority -1
when answered puppet, partner.last=3S
  6S  "Slam in the five-three fit"            shows S>=3, tp(S)>=33-partner.hcp.min
      sets  trump=S
  4S  "Game in the five-three fit"            shows S>=3
      sets  trump=S
      priority -1
  6N  "No fit: slam"                          shows S<=2, points>=32-partner.hcp.min
  4N  "No fit: quantitative, invites 6NT"     shows S<=2, balanced, strength=slam_invite, points<=31-partner.hcp.min
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      sets  ask=quant
  3N  "No fit: game"                          shows S<=2
      priority -1
# Opener has no major.
when answered puppet, partner.last=3N
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"                 alert
      when  gerber
      shows points>=32-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1                              # ahead of 6NT: check the aces first
  6N  "No fit: slam"                          shows points>=32-partner.hcp.min
  4N  "No fit: quantitative, invites 6NT"     shows balanced, strength=slam_invite, points<=31-partner.hcp.min
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      sets  ask=quant
  P   "No fit: 3NT"
      priority -20                            # behind slam/over-3nt.bid (minor-suit slam tries)
# After a 3NT that denies the 4-4 fit: the same counts.
when answered puppet_fit(x), partner.last=3N
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"                 alert
      when  gerber
      shows points>=32-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1                              # ahead of 6NT: check the aces first
  6N  "No fit: slam"                          shows points>=32-partner.hcp.min
  4N  "No fit: quantitative, invites 6NT"     shows balanced, strength=slam_invite, points<=31-partner.hcp.min
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      sets  ask=quant
  P   "No fit: 3NT"
      priority -20
files.rules/openings/reverse-flannery.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Reverse Flannery (Dural Bridge, "Flannery and Reverse Flannery";
# Practice-Bidding-Scenarios `Reverse_Flannery`): responder's jumps to
# 2♥ and 2♠ over partner's 1♣/1♦ show five spades and four or five
# hearts, below a game try:
#
#   1m–2♥   5♠ and 4-5♥, 5-8 HCP     (card `two_level.reverse_flannery.two_h`)
#   1m–2♠   5♠ and 4♥, 9-10 HCP      (card `two_level.reverse_flannery.two_s`)
#
# Over 2♥ opener passes or bids 2♠ to play, or asks with 2NT: 3♣ 5-4 and
# 5-6, 3♦ 5-4 and 7-8, 3♥ 5-5 and 5-6, 3♠ 5-5 and 7-8. Both outrank a
# jump shift of either kind. See reverse-flannery.notes.md.

module reverse-flannery "Reverse Flannery"
  kind   convention
  needs  responses
  skill  bidding_conventions/reverse_flannery
  param  rf_2h = bidding_conventions/reverse_flannery:two_h default false
  param  rf_2s = bidding_conventions/reverse_flannery:two_s default false

# Read by responses.bid: a jump Reverse Flannery takes is not a strong jump
# shift, which is only what the jump means when nothing else claims it.
define rf_2h_on = rf_2h
define rf_2s_on = rf_2s

# ── Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1m (P)
  2H  "Reverse Flannery: five spades, four or five hearts, 5-8 HCP"   alert
      shows S=5, H=4..5, hcp=5..8
      when  rf_2h
      priority 2
  2S  "Reverse Flannery: five spades, four hearts, 9-10 HCP"   alert
      shows S=5, H=4, hcp=9..10
      when  rf_2s
      priority 2

# ── Opener after 2♥ (5-8) ────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1m (P) 2H (P) when rf_2h
  P   "To play in hearts: hearts longer than spades"
      shows H>S, S<=2, hcp<=15
  2S  "To play in spades"
      shows hcp<=15
      priority -1
  3m  "Six or more of my minor: to play"
      shows m>=6, S<=1, H<=2, hcp<=15
  2N  "Asks: which shape and which half of the range?"   alert
      shows hcp>=16
      sets  forcing=round, ask=reverse_flannery
      artificial
      priority 1
  4S  "Game in spades"   shows S>=3, hcp>=18
      priority 1
  4H  "Game in hearts"   shows H>=4, H>S, hcp>=18
      priority 1

when asked reverse_flannery
  3C  "5-4 in the majors, 5-6 HCP"   shows H=4, hcp<=6   artificial   priority 2
  3D  "5-4 in the majors, 7-8 HCP"   shows H=4, hcp>=7   artificial   priority 2
  3H  "5-5 in the majors, 5-6 HCP"   shows H=5, hcp<=6   priority 2
  3S  "5-5 in the majors, 7-8 HCP"   shows H=5, hcp>=7   priority 2

# Opener places the contract: game with 23 between us counting partner
# at the floor of his answer, else the cheapest call in the better major.
when answered reverse_flannery
  4S  "Game in spades"   shows S>=3, S>=H | partner.H.max<=4, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 23
      priority 1
  4H  "Game in hearts"   shows H>=4, H>S, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 23
      priority 1
  3N  "Game in notrump: no major fit"   shows S<=2, H<=3, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 23
  P   "Partner's 3♠: play there"
      when  partner.last=3S
  3S  "Sign off in spades"
      when  !partner.last=3S
      priority -1
  4H  "Sign off: hearts are the fit"   shows H>=4, H>S
      when  partner.last=3S
      priority -1

# ── Opener after 2♠ (9-10) ───────────────────────────────────────────
after 1m (P) 2S (P) when rf_2s
  P   "A minimum with two spades: play 2♠"
      shows S=2, hcp<=14
  3S  "Three or more spades, a minimum: invites game"
      shows S>=3, tp(S)<=14
  2N  "Short spades, a minimum: no fit"
      shows S<=1, hcp<=14
      priority -1
  3H  "Four hearts, short spades: to play"
      shows H>=4, S<=1, hcp<=14
  3m  "Six or more of my minor, short spades: to play"
      shows m>=6, S<=1, hcp<=14
  4S  "Game in spades"   shows S>=3, tp(S)>=15
      priority 1
  4H  "Game in hearts"   shows H>=4, S<=2, hcp>=15
      priority 1
  3N  "Game in notrump: no fit"   shows S<=2, H<=3, hcp>=15

# Responder after opener's invitation: game with the top of the range.
after 1m (P) 2S (P) 3S (P) when rf_2s
  4S  "Accepts: 10 HCP"   shows hcp>=10
      priority 1
  P   "Declines: 9 HCP"
      priority 1

# Responder after opener's sign-offs: pass.
after 1m (P) 2S (P) 3x (P) when rf_2s, x is not S
  P   "No further bid"
      priority 1
after 1m (P) 2S (P) 2N (P) when rf_2s
  # Partner is minimum without a fit: 2NT is high enough.
  P   "No game: play 2NT"   shows hcp<=9
      priority 1
  3N  "10 HCP: game"
      priority 1
after 1m (P) 2H (P) 3m (P) | 1m (P) 2H (P) 2S (P) when rf_2h
  P   "No further bid"
      priority 1
files.rules/openings/vs-multi.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Defence to their Multi 2♦ (Bridge Bum, "Defense to Multi 2D", option
# 2). Their 2♦ is read with their card: when it is a Multi, the opener
# may hold six hearts or six spades (`maybe lho/rho.H>=6, maybe ...S>=6`;
# `maybe ...D<=3`; a natural weak 2♦ shows six diamonds and Flannery
# five hearts, so neither matches). In the direct seat:
#
#   X     13-15 balanced, or 16+ any shape
#   2♥/2♠ natural, five or more, not forcing
#   2NT   16-18 balanced
#   3♣/3♦ natural, six or more
#   3♥/3♠ natural, six or more, better than a two-level overcall
#
# After (2♦) P (2♥/2♠), pass or correct: a double is takeout of the suit
# bid, other calls natural, 2NT 15-18. Everything else passes. These
# outrank the defence to a natural 2♦ (competitive/vs-preempts.bid).
# See vs-multi.notes.md.

module vs-multi "Defence to a Multi 2♦"
  kind   defence
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/multi_2d

# ── Direct seat ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after (2D) when maybe rho.H>=6, maybe rho.S>=6, maybe rho.D<=3
  X   "13-15 balanced, or 16+ any shape"
      shows (balanced, hcp=13..15) | hcp>=16
      priority 2
  2H  "Natural: five or more hearts, not forcing"   shows H>=5, hcp=10..15
      priority 2
  2S  "Natural: five or more spades, not forcing"   shows S>=5, hcp=10..15
      priority 2
  2N  "16-18 balanced"                              shows balanced, hcp=16..18
      priority 3
  3C  "Natural: six or more clubs"                  shows C>=6, hcp=10..15
      priority 2
  3D  "Natural: six or more diamonds"               shows D>=6, hcp=10..15
      priority 2
  3H  "Natural: six or more hearts, a good overcall"   shows H>=6, hcp=13..16
      priority 3
  3S  "Natural: six or more spades, a good overcall"   shows S>=6, hcp=13..16
      priority 3
  P   "No overcall"
      priority 1

# ── Fourth seat, after their pass-or-correct response ────────────────
after (2D) P (2H) when maybe lho.H>=6, maybe lho.S>=6, maybe lho.D<=3
  X   "Takeout of hearts: 13+"                       shows H<=2, S>=3, hcp>=13
      priority 2
  2S  "Natural: five or more spades"                 shows S>=5, hcp=10..15
      priority 2
  2N  "15-18 balanced"                               shows balanced, hcp=15..18
      priority 3
  3C  "Natural: six or more clubs"                   shows C>=6, hcp=10..15
      priority 2
  3D  "Natural: six or more diamonds"                shows D>=6, hcp=10..15
      priority 2
  P   "No overcall"
      priority 1
after (2D) P (2S) when maybe lho.H>=6, maybe lho.S>=6, maybe lho.D<=3
  X   "Takeout of spades: 13+"                       shows S<=2, H>=3, hcp>=13
      priority 2
  2N  "15-18 balanced"                               shows balanced, hcp=15..18
      priority 3
  3C  "Natural: six or more clubs"                   shows C>=6, hcp=10..15
      priority 2
  3D  "Natural: six or more diamonds"                shows D>=6, hcp=10..15
      priority 2
  3H  "Natural: five or more hearts"                 shows H>=5, hcp=11..15
      priority 2
  P   "No overcall"
      priority 1
files.rules/slam/dopi-ropi.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# DOPI and ROPI: answering an ace or keycard ask after the opponents
# interfere. The answers keep their steps, the first two replaced:
#
#   they bid a suit (DOPI)    double = first step, pass = second step,
#                             then the next two bids are steps three
#                             and four;
#   they double (ROPI)        redouble = first step, pass = second step,
#                             then 5♣ and 5♦.
#
# So with 1430 a double shows one or four keycards and a pass none or
# three; with standard Blackwood a double shows none or four aces, a pass
# one. The asker then places the contract, and with two keycards (aces)
# missing defends: passes partner's double, or doubles himself over
# partner's pass. Notes: dopi-ropi.notes.md.

module dopi-ropi "DOPI and ROPI: answering an ace or keycard ask over interference"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/dopi_ropi
  param  dopi   = bidding_conventions/dopi_ropi:dopi default false
  param  ropi   = bidding_conventions/dopi_ropi:ropi default false
  param  depo   = bidding_conventions/depo default false
  param  gstyle = general.style
  param  rkcb   = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard default false
  param  rstyle = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard:style default 1430
  param  m0314  = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard:minor_0314 default false

# The first step of the keycard answers is "1 or 4" (1430) unless the
# card plays 0314 (`slam.rkcb.style`), or its `minor_0314` treatment
# applies with a minor as trumps (Rick, 2026-11-09: follow the card's
# keycard order). Shared by rkcb-1430.bid and minorwood.bid.
define kc_first_14(t) = !(rkcb, rstyle is 0314), !m0314 | t is H | t is S

# They bid a suit over the ask, below six (DOPI); they doubled it (ROPI).
# A bid, not a pass, double or redouble: checked first, as only bids can
# be ordered (`<=` on a pass is an error).
define rho_bid = !(rho.last = P), !(rho.last = X), !(rho.last = XX)
define lho_bid = !(lho.last = P), !(lho.last = X), !(lho.last = XX)
define partner_bid = !(partner.last = P), !(partner.last = X), !(partner.last = XX)
define dopi_bid  = rho_bid, rho.last <= 5S
define ropi_dbl  = rho.last = X

# ── Keycards ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

when dopi, !depo, asked keycards(t), dopi_bid
  X   "DOPI: 1 or 4 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial
      when  kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5
  P   "DOPI: 0 or 3 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial
      when  kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5
  X   "DOPI: 0 or 3 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial
      when  !kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5
  P   "DOPI: 1 or 4 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial
      when  !kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5

when ropi, asked keycards(t), ropi_dbl
  XX  "ROPI: 1 or 4 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial
      when  kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5
  P   "ROPI: 0 or 3 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial
      when  kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5
  XX  "ROPI: 0 or 3 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial
      when  !kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5
  P   "ROPI: 1 or 4 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial
      when  !kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5
  5C  "ROPI: 2 keycards, no {t} queen"     shows keycards(t)=2, !has(Q,t)   artificial
      priority 5
  5D  "ROPI: 2 keycards and the {t} queen" shows keycards(t)=2, has(Q,t)    artificial
      priority 5

# Steps three and four over their bid: the next two bids.
when dopi, !depo, asked keycards(t)
  5D  "DOPI: 2 keycards, no {t} queen"     shows keycards(t)=2, !has(Q,t)   artificial
      when  rho.last = 5C
      priority 5
  5H  "DOPI: 2 keycards and the {t} queen" shows keycards(t)=2, has(Q,t)    artificial
      when  rho.last = 5C
      priority 5
  5H  "DOPI: 2 keycards, no {t} queen"     shows keycards(t)=2, !has(Q,t)   artificial
      when  rho.last = 5D
      priority 5
  5S  "DOPI: 2 keycards and the {t} queen" shows keycards(t)=2, has(Q,t)    artificial
      when  rho.last = 5D
      priority 5
  5S  "DOPI: 2 keycards, no {t} queen"     shows keycards(t)=2, !has(Q,t)   artificial
      when  rho.last = 5H
      priority 5
  5N  "DOPI: 2 keycards and the {t} queen" shows keycards(t)=2, has(Q,t)    artificial
      when  rho.last = 5H
      priority 5
  5N  "DOPI: 2 keycards, no {t} queen"     shows keycards(t)=2, !has(Q,t)   artificial
      when  rho.last = 5S
      priority 5
  6C  "DOPI: 2 keycards and the {t} queen" shows keycards(t)=2, has(Q,t)    artificial
      when  rho.last = 5S
      priority 5

# ── DEPO (`slam.depo`) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Played instead of DOPI: over their suit bid a double shows an even
# number (0, 2 or 4), a pass an odd number (1 or 3), of keycards or aces.
# No steps above: with the values for slam, partner's even or odd and my
# own count decide.
when depo, asked keycards(t), dopi_bid
  X   "DEPO: 0, 2 or 4 keycards"   shows keycards(t) in 0|2|4   artificial
      priority 5
  P   "DEPO: 1 or 3 keycards"       shows keycards(t) in 1|3|5   artificial
      priority 5

when depo, asked aces, dopi_bid
  X   "DEPO: 0, 2 or 4 aces"       shows keycards(N) in 0|2|4   artificial
      priority 5
  P   "DEPO: 1 or 3 aces"           shows keycards(N) in 1|3     artificial
      priority 5

# ── Aces (standard Blackwood) ─────────────────────────────────────────

when dopi, !depo, asked aces, dopi_bid
  X   "DOPI: 0 or 4 aces"   shows keycards(N) in 0|4   artificial
      priority 5
  P   "DOPI: 1 ace"         shows keycards(N)=1        artificial
      priority 5

when ropi, asked aces, ropi_dbl
  XX  "ROPI: 0 or 4 aces"   shows keycards(N) in 0|4   artificial
      priority 5
  P   "ROPI: 1 ace"         shows keycards(N)=1        artificial
      priority 5
  5C  "ROPI: 2 aces"        shows keycards(N)=2        artificial
      priority 5
  5D  "ROPI: 3 aces"        shows keycards(N)=3        artificial
      priority 5

when dopi, !depo, asked aces
  5D  "DOPI: 2 aces"        shows keycards(N)=2   artificial   when rho.last = 5C   priority 5
  5H  "DOPI: 3 aces"        shows keycards(N)=3   artificial   when rho.last = 5C   priority 5
  5H  "DOPI: 2 aces"        shows keycards(N)=2   artificial   when rho.last = 5D   priority 5
  5S  "DOPI: 3 aces"        shows keycards(N)=3   artificial   when rho.last = 5D   priority 5
  5S  "DOPI: 2 aces"        shows keycards(N)=2   artificial   when rho.last = 5H   priority 5
  5N  "DOPI: 3 aces"        shows keycards(N)=3   artificial   when rho.last = 5H   priority 5
  5N  "DOPI: 2 aces"        shows keycards(N)=2   artificial   when rho.last = 5S   priority 5
  6C  "DOPI: 3 aces"        shows keycards(N)=3   artificial   when rho.last = 5S   priority 5

# ── The asker over a DOPI or ROPI answer ─────────────────────────────
#
# Two keycards (aces) missing: defend rather than bid on. Partner's double
# was the answer and also penalty: pass it. Over partner's pass, double.
# Over ROPI's redouble the asker always bids: 4NT redoubled is ours.
# With the values the slam rules of the ask's own module apply.
define kc_two_missing(t) = we.keycards(t).max <= 3

when (dopi | ropi | depo), answered keycards(t), rho.last = P
  P   "Defend doubled: two keycards missing"
      when  partner.last = X, kc_two_missing(t), lho_bid, lho.last <= 5S
      priority 5
  # Over partner's pass a count still open ("0 or 3" facing my two) is
  # read low, as the sign-off in rkcb-1430.bid is: partner bids six over
  # the double with the higher count.
  X   "Penalty: two keycards missing"
      when  partner.last = P, we.keycards(t).min <= 3, lho_bid, lho.last <= 5S
      sets  ask=keycard_correct(t)
      priority 5

when (dopi | ropi | depo), answered aces, rho.last = P
  P   "Defend doubled: two aces missing"
      when  partner.last = X, we.keycards(N).max <= 2, lho_bid, lho.last <= 5S
      priority 5
  X   "Penalty: two aces missing"
      when  partner.last = P, we.keycards(N).max <= 2, lho_bid, lho.last <= 5S
      priority 5
files.rules/slam/kickback.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Kickback: with a suit agreed, the keycard ask is the bid one step above
# four of the trump suit instead of 4NT: 4♦ with clubs, 4♥ with
# diamonds, 4♠ with hearts. With spades it is 4NT, which rkcb-1430.bid
# already is. The answers are the four 1430 steps above the ask (0314 by
# `slam.kickback.rkcb_0314`), so the fourth step is five of the trump
# suit and every answer leaves the sign-off in five. Notes:
# kickback.notes.md.

module kickback "Kickback: the step above four of the trump suit asks for keycards"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/kickback
  param  kbplay = bidding_conventions/kickback default false
  param  kb1430 = bidding_conventions/kickback:rkcb_1430 default false
  param  kb0314 = bidding_conventions/kickback:rkcb_0314 default false
  param  kstyle = slam.king_ask.style default five_nt   # five_nt | next_step | none (convention-card 0.28); a card that is silent plays 5NT (2026-10-29)

# The card plays Kickback when any of its three fields is on.
define kickback_on = kbplay | kb1430 | kb0314

# The ask is four of the next suit, while the auction is below it
# (`cheapest_rank`: 4♦ 21, 4♥ 22, 4♠ 23). Once
# the auction has passed it, 4NT is the ask again (rkcb-1430.bid).
define kb_room(t) = (t is C, cheapest_rank(D) <= 21) | (t is D, cheapest_rank(H) <= 22) | (t is H, cheapest_rank(S) <= 23)
define kb_asks(t) = kickback_on, kb_room(t)

# Hearts as trumps: 4♠ is the ask, not a control bid (control-bids.bid).
