define kb_spade_ask = kb_asks(H), trump is H

# The first step: "1 or 4" (1430), else "0 or 3".
define kb_first_14 = !kb0314

# ── The ask ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The values are rkcb-1430.bid's: 33 facing a limited partner's maximum
# with no two bare side suits, or 33 on a game-forcing partner's floor.
# Priority 11: the call must read as the ask whatever else could claim
# it (the engine reads a call by its highest-ranked rule), so it ranks
# above the descriptive calls, but below a control bid (12), which comes
# first when a side suit is uncontrolled.

when kickback_on, we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked, we.forcing = none | we.forcing = round
  4D  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♣"  alert
      when  trump is C, kb_room(C)
      when  slam_values_limited, !two_bare_suits
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11
  4H  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♦"  alert
      when  trump is D, kb_room(D)
      when  slam_values_limited, !two_bare_suits
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11
  4S  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♥"  alert
      when  trump is H, kb_room(H)
      when  slam_values_limited, !two_bare_suits
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11

when kickback_on, we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked, we.forcing = game, !answered control
  4D  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♣"  alert
      when  trump is C, kb_room(C)
      when  slam_values
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11
  4H  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♦"  alert
      when  trump is D, kb_room(D)
      when  slam_values
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11
  4S  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♥"  alert
      when  trump is H, kb_room(H)
      when  slam_values
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11

# After a control-bid exchange in hearts (control-bids.bid), as the 4NT
# ask there: once every side suit is covered.
when kickback_on, we.trump is suit, asked control(t), trump is H
  4S  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♥"  alert
      when  kb_room(H), all_covered
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11

when kickback_on, we.trump is suit, answered control(t), partner.last = 4H, trump is H
  4S  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♥"  alert
      when  kb_room(H), all_covered_by_us
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 15

# ── The answers: four steps above the ask ─────────────────────────────

when kickback_on, asked kickback(t), rho.last = P
  4H  "Kickback: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is C, kb_first_14
  4H  "Kickback: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is C, !kb_first_14
  4S  "Kickback: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is C, kb_first_14
  4S  "Kickback: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is C, !kb_first_14
  4N  "Kickback: 2 or 5 keycards, no {t} queen"    shows keycards(t) in 2|5, !has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is C
  5C  "Kickback: 2 or 5 keycards and the {t} queen"  shows keycards(t) in 2|5, has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is C

  4S  "Kickback: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is D, kb_first_14
  4S  "Kickback: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is D, !kb_first_14
  4N  "Kickback: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is D, kb_first_14
  4N  "Kickback: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is D, !kb_first_14
  5C  "Kickback: 2 or 5 keycards, no {t} queen"    shows keycards(t) in 2|5, !has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is D
  5D  "Kickback: 2 or 5 keycards and the {t} queen"  shows keycards(t) in 2|5, has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is D

  4N  "Kickback: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is H, kb_first_14
  4N  "Kickback: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is H, !kb_first_14
  5C  "Kickback: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is H, kb_first_14
  5C  "Kickback: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is H, !kb_first_14
  5D  "Kickback: 2 or 5 keycards, no {t} queen"    shows keycards(t) in 2|5, !has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is H
  5H  "Kickback: 2 or 5 keycards and the {t} queen"  shows keycards(t) in 2|5, has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is H

# ── The asker places the contract ─────────────────────────────────────
#
# The queen: mine, or partner's fourth step, which is always five of our
# suit (`partner.has(Q,t)` is never known: the engine does not track
# another hand's honours; 2026-10-07, as rkcb-1430.bid's 5♠).
#
# As after 4NT (rkcb-1430.bid): `we.keycards(t)` combines my count with
# the answer, within the deck's five. The fourth step is five of our
# suit: pass it with two keycards missing.

when kickback_on, answered kickback(t)
  7{t}  "Grand slam"
        when  we.keycards(t)=5, has(Q,t) | partner.last = 5{t}, grand_try, kstyle is not five_nt   # with the king ask, ask first (2026-10-07)
  # The king ask, as after 4NT (rkcb-1430.bid answers it); the self A/B
  # (2026-10-05) lost the grands that 4NT-5NT found.
  5N    "King ask: all keycards and the {t} queen held"
        when  kstyle is five_nt, we.keycards(t)=5, has(Q,t) | partner.last = 5{t}
        sets  ask=kings(t)
        artificial
  6{t}  "Small slam"
        when  we.keycards(t)>=4
  # The count that fits (rkcb-1430.bid, `kc_high`): with 30 HCP between
  # us the low count of an open answer is impossible.
  7{t}  "Grand slam"
        when  kc_high(t), we.keycards(t).max=5, has(Q,t) | partner.last = 5{t}, grand_try, kstyle is not five_nt   # with the king ask, ask first (2026-10-07)
  5N    "King ask: all keycards and the {t} queen held"
        when  kstyle is five_nt, kc_high(t), we.keycards(t).max=5, has(Q,t) | partner.last = 5{t}
        sets  ask=kings(t)
        artificial
  6{t}  "Small slam"
        when  kc_high(t)
  P     "To play"
        when  partner.last=5{t}, we.keycards(t).max<=3
  5{t}  "Signoff"
        when  we.keycards(t).max<=3
        sets  ask=kb_correct(t)
  5{t}  "Signoff"
        when  maybe we.keycards(t)>=4
        sets  ask=kb_correct(t)

when kickback_on, asked kb_correct(t)
  6{t}  "Corrects to six: the higher count"   shows keycards(t) in 3|4|5
  P     "Accepts the sign-off"
files.rules/slam/minorwood.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Minorwood: with a minor agreed, four of that minor asks for keycards
# instead of 4NT, so every answer stays below five of the minor: over
# 4♣ the steps are 4♦ 4♥ 4♠ 4NT, over 4♦ they are 4♥ 4♠ 4NT 5♣ (1430,
# or 0314 as the card's keycard treatment says). Kickback, when the card
# plays it, is the ask instead (kickback.bid). Notes: minorwood.notes.md.

module minorwood "Minorwood: four of the agreed minor asks for keycards"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/minorwood
  param  mwplay = bidding_conventions/minorwood default false
  param  kstyle = slam.king_ask.style default five_nt   # five_nt | next_step | none (convention-card 0.28); a card that is silent plays 5NT (2026-10-29)

# Four of the minor is still available (`cheapest_rank`: 4♣ 20, 4♦ 21).
define mw_room(t) = (t is C, cheapest_rank(C) <= 20) | (t is D, cheapest_rank(D) <= 21)
define mw_asks(t) = mwplay, !kickback_on, mw_room(t)

# ── The ask ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# A game force with the minor agreed, or (uncontested) a forcing or
# limited auction where four of the minor cannot be weak: "if there is
# any question, 4m is Minorwood" (the source). The values are the 4NT
# ask's (rkcb-1430.bid). Priority 11, as Kickback's: the call must read
# as the ask whatever else could claim it.

when mwplay, !kickback_on, we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked, we.forcing = game, !answered control
  4C  "Minorwood: keycard ask in ♣"  alert
      when  trump is C, mw_room(C)
      when  slam_values
      sets  ask=minorwood(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11
  4D  "Minorwood: keycard ask in ♦"  alert
      when  trump is D, mw_room(D)
      when  slam_values
      sets  ask=minorwood(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11

when mwplay, !kickback_on, we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked, !they.bid, we.forcing = none | we.forcing = round
  4C  "Minorwood: keycard ask in ♣"  alert
      when  trump is C, mw_room(C)
      when  slam_values_limited, !two_bare_suits
      sets  ask=minorwood(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11
  4D  "Minorwood: keycard ask in ♦"  alert
      when  trump is D, mw_room(D)
      when  slam_values_limited, !two_bare_suits
      sets  ask=minorwood(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11

# ── The answers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The first two steps as the card's keycard ask has them in a minor
# (`kc_first_14`, dopi-ropi.bid: 1430 unless the card says 0314 or its minor treatment applies).

when mwplay, asked minorwood(t), rho.last = P
  4D  "Minorwood: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is C, kc_first_14(t)
  4D  "Minorwood: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is C, !kc_first_14(t)
  4H  "Minorwood: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is C, kc_first_14(t)
  4H  "Minorwood: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is C, !kc_first_14(t)
  4S  "Minorwood: 2 or 5 keycards, no {t} queen"    shows keycards(t) in 2|5, !has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is C
  4N  "Minorwood: 2 or 5 keycards and the {t} queen"  shows keycards(t) in 2|5, has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is C

  4H  "Minorwood: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is D, kc_first_14(t)
  4H  "Minorwood: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is D, !kc_first_14(t)
  4S  "Minorwood: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is D, kc_first_14(t)
  4S  "Minorwood: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is D, !kc_first_14(t)
  4N  "Minorwood: 2 or 5 keycards, no {t} queen"    shows keycards(t) in 2|5, !has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is D
  5C  "Minorwood: 2 or 5 keycards and the {t} queen"  shows keycards(t) in 2|5, has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is D

# ── The asker places the contract ─────────────────────────────────────
#
# The queen: mine, or partner's fourth step (4NT in clubs, 5♣ in
# diamonds); `partner.has(Q,t)` is never known (2026-10-07).

when mwplay, answered minorwood(t)
  7{t}  "Grand slam"
        when  we.keycards(t)=5, has(Q,t) | (t is C, partner.last = 4N) | (t is D, partner.last = 5C), grand_try, kstyle is not five_nt   # with the king ask, ask first (2026-10-07)
  # The king ask, as after 4NT (rkcb-1430.bid answers it; 2026-10-05).
  5N    "King ask: all keycards and the {t} queen held"
        when  kstyle is five_nt, we.keycards(t)=5, has(Q,t) | (t is C, partner.last = 4N) | (t is D, partner.last = 5C)
        sets  ask=kings(t)
        artificial
  6{t}  "Small slam"
        when  we.keycards(t)>=4
  # The count that fits (rkcb-1430.bid, `kc_high`): with 30 HCP between
  # us the low count of an open answer is impossible.
  7{t}  "Grand slam"
        when  kc_high(t), we.keycards(t).max=5, has(Q,t) | (t is C, partner.last = 4N) | (t is D, partner.last = 5C), grand_try, kstyle is not five_nt   # with the king ask, ask first (2026-10-07)
  5N    "King ask: all keycards and the {t} queen held"
        when  kstyle is five_nt, kc_high(t), we.keycards(t).max=5, has(Q,t) | (t is C, partner.last = 4N) | (t is D, partner.last = 5C)
        sets  ask=kings(t)
        artificial
  6{t}  "Small slam"
        when  kc_high(t)
  5{t}  "Signoff"
        when  we.keycards(t).max<=3
        sets  ask=mw_correct(t)
  5{t}  "Signoff"
        when  maybe we.keycards(t)>=4
        sets  ask=mw_correct(t)

when mwplay, asked mw_correct(t)
  6{t}  "Corrects to six: the higher count"   shows keycards(t) in 3|4|5
  P     "Accepts the sign-off"
files.rules/slam/over-3nt.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Slam after partner's 3NT (2026-09-27). The slam work's third group:
# 1,433 boards where BBA bid slam and our auction stopped in a 3NT that
# one partner bid with 15-18 balanced while the other, often with 15-17
# and a long suit, passed. Nothing looked past 3NT.
#
# Partner's 3NT has shown a range, and I add my HCP to his minimum: 6NT
# with 34 or more; a quantitative 4NT with 32-33 (answered by `when asked
# quant`, one-nt.bid); with a six-card minor and 31+, four of it as a
# slam try. Counting partner at his minimum, one point above the
# textbook 33/31 measured best (notes).

module over-3nt "Slam after partner's 3NT"
  kind   judgement
  needs  base
  skill  partnership_bidding/slam_bidding
  param  q4n   = bidding_conventions/quantitative_4nt default true
  param  tu    = bidding_conventions/texas:two_under default false
  param  o23   = bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers:over_2c_3nt default true
  param  system = general.system   # `brill`: Gerber here instead (gerber.bid)

# After 2♣–2♦–3NT (24+ shown, opener's second bid) Texas uses 4♦/4♥, or
# 4♣/4♦ for 2-under (texas-transfers.bid): the tries and natural bids
# below give way there, or partner would read them as transfers. Only
# when the card plays transfers there (`notrump.jacoby_transfers.over_2c_3nt`,
# default on, Rick 2026-11-07); off, 4♦ and 4♥ are natural.
define big_3n = partner.hcp.min>=24, partner.bids>=2
define texas_3n = big_3n, o23

when partner.last=3N, !they.bid, we.trump is none
  # Without Texas over 2♣–2♦–3NT, a six-card major goes to game
  # naturally: the same hands that Texas carries there (texas-transfers.bid).
  4H  "To play: six or more hearts"
      shows H>=6, points>=25-partner.points.min, suit_points<=32-partner.points.min
      when  big_3n, !(texas_2nt, o23)
      priority -10
  4S  "To play: six or more spades"
      shows S>=6, points>=25-partner.points.min, suit_points<=32-partner.points.min
      when  big_3n, !(texas_2nt, o23)
      priority -10
  6N  "Small slam"
      shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 34
      priority -10
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  q4n                            # the card plays a quantitative 4NT
      shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 32, hcp + partner.hcp.max <= 35
      sets  ask=quant
      priority -10
  4C  "Slam try: six or more clubs"
      shows C>=6, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 31
      when  !(texas_3n, tu)
      sets  ask=slam_try(C)
      priority -10
  4D  "Slam try: six or more diamonds"
      shows D>=6, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 31
      when  !(texas_3n, texas_2nt | tu)
      sets  ask=slam_try(D)
      priority -10

  # A standalone major, six to the AKQJ or seven to the AKQ, plays in
  # game without help from partner, and a short suit with no stopper is
  # a risk in notrump (Rick, 2026-09-27, ticket b194: 1S 2D 2S 3NT with
  # AKQJ63 and 32 in hearts; BBA bids 4S).
  4S  "To play: a self-sufficient ♠ suit"
      shows (S>=6, quality(S)=3, top5(S)>=4) | (S>=7, quality(S)=3)
      shows (H<=2, !stop(H)) | (D<=2, !stop(D)) | (C<=2, !stop(C))
      priority -10
  4H  "To play: a self-sufficient ♥ suit"
      shows (H>=6, quality(H)=3, top5(H)>=4) | (H>=7, quality(H)=3)
      shows (S<=2, !stop(S)) | (D<=2, !stop(D)) | (C<=2, !stop(C))
      when  !(texas_3n, texas_2nt, !tu)
      priority -10

# The same after their overcall of our 2♣ (2♣ (2♥) P (P) 3NT, 2♣ P 2♦
# (2♥) 3NT), where the block above stops at `!they.bid`. 4♣ is not a
# jump over 3NT, so it is the club slam try, not Gerber (Rick,
# 2026-10-31: Gerber needs a jump; without one 4♣ is a slam try).
# Texas is off after interference, so the tries do not give way to it.
after 2C (*) P (P) 3N (P) | 2C (P) 2D (*) 3N (P) when they.bid, system is not brill
  6N  "Small slam"
      shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 34
      priority -10
  4C  "Slam try: six or more clubs"
      shows C>=6, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 31
      sets  ask=slam_try(C)
      priority -10
  4D  "Slam try: six or more diamonds"
      shows D>=6, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 31
      sets  ask=slam_try(D)
      priority -10

when asked slam_try(m), partner.last=4{m}, we.trump is none
  6{m}  "Small slam: a fit"                       shows m>=3
  4N    "No fit"                            shows m<=2
when answered slam_try(m), partner.last=4N
  6N  "Small slam"    shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 34
  P   "To play"
      priority -5

# The same count for responder when opener's rebid is a new suit
# (2026-09-27): responder bid 3NT with 33+ between the hands
# (1a–1b–2c–3NT, 772 boards short of slam). Counted in points: after a
# jump shift the HCP floor is only 10 (it shows suit points), the
# points floor 18. The textbook 33/31 is kept although lower thresholds
# score better on the slam-rich corpus (notes).
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) when z is not x, z is not y
  6N  "Small slam"
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 33, !shortest<=1
      priority 1
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  q4n                            # the card plays a quantitative 4NT
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 31, points + partner.points.max <= 36, !shortest<=1
      when  no_ask                         # with Blackwood or RKCB, keycard in the last suit (Rick, 2026-10-03)
      sets  ask=quant
      priority 1
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 1z (P)
  6N  "Small slam"
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 33, !shortest<=1
      priority 1
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  q4n                            # the card plays a quantitative 4NT
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 31, points + partner.points.max <= 36, !shortest<=1
      when  no_ask                         # with Blackwood or RKCB, keycard in the last suit (Rick, 2026-10-03)
      sets  ask=quant
      priority 1
after 1x (P) 2y (P) 2z (P) when z is not x, z is not y
  6N  "Small slam"
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 33, !shortest<=1
      priority 1
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  q4n                            # the card plays a quantitative 4NT
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 31, points + partner.points.max <= 36, !shortest<=1
      when  no_ask                         # with Blackwood or RKCB, keycard in the last suit (Rick, 2026-10-03)
      sets  ask=quant
      priority 1

# Opener over responder's 15-17 jump to 3NT after a game-forcing 2/1
# and opener's two-level rebid (responder-rebids.bid; Rick, 2026-11-06,
# #91). The count above (34 / 32 on partner's minimum) lost slams
# opener had bid over the old 16+ 2NT; Rick, 2026-11-07: opener should
# be more aggressive here. The textbook 33/31 on responder's minimum, in
# HCP: 18+ bids 6NT, 16-17 a quantitative 4NT. Counting points or
# partner at mid-range lost (notes).
after 1y (P) 2x (P) 2z (P) 3N (P) when x is not y, we.gf
  6N  "Small slam"
      shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 33
      priority 1
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  q4n                            # the card plays a quantitative 4NT
      shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 31, hcp + partner.hcp.min <= 32
      sets  ask=quant
      priority 1
# Responder answers it in HCP too: 16-17 accepts, 15 declines (31-32
# between the hands). one-nt.bid's answer counts points on opener's
# floor, and his five-card suit made it accept with every 15.
after 1y (P) 2x (P) 2z (P) 3N (P) 4N (P) when x is not y, we.gf
  6N  "Accepts the slam invitation: 16-17"   shows hcp>=16
      priority 1
  P   "Declines: 15"                          shows hcp<=15
      priority 1
files.rules/slam/rkcb-1430.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# No auction patterns here. These rules key off auction state that other
# modules set (trump agreed, game forcing), so they work after any auction
# that reaches that state.

module rkcb-1430 "Roman Keycard Blackwood (1430 or 0314, as the card says)"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/roman_keycard
  param  rkcb   = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard default false
  param  rstyle = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard:style default 1430
  param  m0314 = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard:minor_0314 default false
  param  gstyle = general.style
  param  style = bidding_conventions/control_bids:style default first_or_second_round
  param  kstyle = slam.king_ask.style default five_nt   # five_nt | next_step | none (convention-card 0.28); a card that is silent plays 5NT (2026-10-29)
  param  kspec  = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard:king_ask_specific default false

# ── The ask ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Rick's ruling:
#
#   Slam asks isn't about 18 -- what has partner shown? It's more about
#   33+ combined points, where in a suit contract the player with fewer
#   trumps gets to switch to short-suit points -- 1 for a doubleton, 3
#   for a singleton, 5 for a void, capped by number of trumps held. When
#   the slam asker has unprotected suits, we will normally use control
#   bids before keycard, and stop in game if there is a suit unprotected
#   in both hands.
#
# So the test is **33 combined support points with the agreed suit as
# trump**, `we.tp(trump)`: my exact count plus the range a raise recorded
# for partner. It replaces `tp(trump) + partner.hcp.max`, which was a
# workaround from before raises showed support points. The evidence
# behind the boundaries is in slam-catch.notes.md.
#
# Two branches, because partner's range is read from a different end.
#
# 1. **Partner is limited** (a raise, a limit raise) and nothing has
#    forced us to game. Partner has shown a top as well as a bottom, and
#    the only other call on offer is game, so the ask carries the whole
#    decision and 33 is measured against partner's maximum:
#    `we.tp(trump).max >= 33`. With it, the hand must play for twelve
#    tricks opposite a minimum (`losers <= 4`) and must not have **two
#    bare side suits** -- two or more cards with neither the ace nor the
#    king, where the first two tricks can go. That last test replaces
#    `controls >= 7`: it says which suit is the problem rather than
#    counting. One bare suit is allowed, because a raise facing it will
#    usually hold something there; two is where partner cannot cover
#    both. BBA draws the same line: over `1S P 2S P` and `1S P 3S P` on
#    the Basic-Bridge card it asks with none or one bare suit (272
#    boards) and never with two.
#
# 2. **We are already forced to game.** Partner's range has no top, so
#    `we.tp(trump).max` says nothing; what is known is partner's floor.
#    33 between us on that floor is the test, and where the trump
#    agreement recorded no support points for partner the fallback is my
#    own 18, a game force being worth about 13 (`slam_values`, named in
#    slam-entry.bid with the other shared conditions). Here the
#    ask ranks *behind* the system's descriptive calls: shortness, a
#    second suit and a control bid all say more than 4NT does, and the
#    ask is what is left when they are used up.
#
# When the card plays control bids (`slam.cue_bids.play`), a hand with a
# bare suit goes to `control-bids.bid` first and comes back here only
# once partner has shown a control.

when rkcb, we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked, we.forcing = none | we.forcing = round, !kb_asks(trump), !mw_asks(trump)   # Kickback, Minorwood: their own ask
  4N  "Keycard ask in {trump}"
      when  slam_values_limited     # 33 facing partner's maximum
      when  !two_bare_suits  # and no two bare side suits
      sets  ask=keycards(trump)
      artificial
      priority 1

when rkcb, we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked, we.forcing = game, !answered control, !kb_asks(trump), !mw_asks(trump)   # after a control dialogue its own rules decide
  4N  "Keycard ask in {trump}"
      when  slam_values  # 33 on partner's floor, or 18 of my own
      sets  ask=keycards(trump)
      artificial

# A fit known but not agreed (docs/JUDGMENT-LAYER.md, Phase 1): partner's
# game raise, his preempt, a transfer completed. No rule set `trump`, so
# the asks above never saw it. The ask agrees the major on the way.
# Majors only for now: the sign-offs after an answer are awkward in a
# minor.
when rkcb, we.trump is none, !asked, !they.bid   # uncontested for now: in competition it cost
  4N  "Keycard ask in ♠"
      when  shown_fit(S), we.fit(S).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(S), !two_bare_beside(S)
      sets  trump=S, ask=keycards(S)
      artificial
      priority 1
  4N  "Keycard ask in ♥"
      when  shown_fit(H), we.fit(H).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(H), !two_bare_beside(H)
      sets  trump=H, ask=keycards(H)
      artificial
      priority 1

# The keycard suit when no rule has set the one we play in (Rick,
# 2026-10-03; `kc_open`, slam-entry.bid): a suit agreed by what we have
# shown, else, with no notrump bid by us, the last suit we bid
# (1H-1S-2H-4NT asks in hearts). The ask sets it as trump. The majors
# agreed publicly, and partner's own six-card major, are the rules above.
# The ask needs the fit and the values, as above.
when rkcb, we.trump is none, !asked, !they.bid
  4N  "Keycard ask in ♠"
      when  kc_open(S), !shown_fit(S), !shown_fit(H), we.fit(S).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(S), !two_bare_beside(S)
      sets  trump=S, ask=keycards(S)
      artificial
      priority -1
  4N  "Keycard ask in ♥"
      when  kc_open(H), !shown_fit(S), !shown_fit(H), we.fit(H).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(H), !two_bare_beside(H)
      sets  trump=H, ask=keycards(H)
      artificial
      priority -1
  4N  "Keycard ask in ♦"
      when  kc_open(D), !shown_fit(S), !shown_fit(H), we.fit(D).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(D), !two_bare_beside(D)
      when  hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 30   # a minor slam needs the high cards (rebids.test: 17 facing a preference)
      sets  trump=D, ask=keycards(D)
      artificial
      priority -1
  4N  "Keycard ask in ♣"
      when  kc_open(C), !shown_fit(S), !shown_fit(H), we.fit(C).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(C), !two_bare_beside(C)
      when  hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 30   # a minor slam needs the high cards (rebids.test: 17 facing a preference)
      sets  trump=C, ask=keycards(C)
      artificial
      priority -1

# The same 4NT in competition, for reading only (2026-10-05, DOPI and
# ROPI): the asks above are off once they have bid, but partner's 4NT is
# still keycard for the suit we play in, and the answer comes by DOPI or
# ROPI (dopi-ropi.bid). Never chosen: `read_only` is a condition on the
# caller's hand that no hand meets, and that a reader cannot judge, so
# it stays possible when the call is read (docs/LANGUAGE.md, section 8).
# Low priority as well, so any other meaning of 4NT comes first.
define read_only = bare(C), !bare(C)

when rkcb, we.trump is none, !asked, they.bid
  4N  "Keycard ask in ♠"
      when  kc_open(S) | shown_fit(S)
      sets  trump=S, ask=keycards(S)
      artificial
      when  read_only
      priority -60
  4N  "Keycard ask in ♥"
      when  kc_open(H) | shown_fit(H), !shown_fit(S)
      sets  trump=H, ask=keycards(H)
      artificial
      when  read_only
      priority -60
  4N  "Keycard ask in ♦"
      when  kc_open(D), !shown_fit(S), !shown_fit(H)
      sets  trump=D, ask=keycards(D)
      artificial
      when  read_only
      priority -60
  4N  "Keycard ask in ♣"
      when  kc_open(C), !shown_fit(S), !shown_fit(H)
      sets  trump=C, ask=keycards(C)
      artificial
      when  read_only
      priority -60

# A trump suit agreed and partner's jump to game in competition
# (total-tricks.bid's `ask=signoff`, 1H-2NT-(3C)-4H): 4NT over the
# sign-off is still keycard. For reading, as above.
when rkcb, we.trump is suit, they.bid, asked signoff
  4N  "Keycard ask in {trump}"
      sets  ask=keycards(trump)
      artificial
      when  read_only
      priority -60

# A minor set as trump, and a major agreed since (Rick, 2026-10-03:
# "normally a major fit will replace a minor fit"; 1S-2C-3C-4S-4NT): the
# ask is in the major, and makes it trump.
when rkcb, minor_given_way, !asked
  4N  "Keycard ask in ♠"
      when  major_over_minor(S), fit_slam_values(S), !two_bare_beside(S)
      sets  trump=S, ask=keycards(S)
      artificial
      priority 1
  4N  "Keycard ask in ♥"
      when  major_over_minor(H), !major_over_minor(S), fit_slam_values(H), !two_bare_beside(H)
      sets  trump=H, ask=keycards(H)
      artificial
      priority 1

# After a control-bid exchange (`control-bids.bid`, when the card plays
# them). `asked control(t)` is partner's control bid; `answered control(u)`
# says partner was answering mine, so I am the hand that opened the
# dialogue and the one that takes charge. Above it, the stop-in-game rule
# at priority 20 has already ruled out a suit bare in both hands; below
# it, any control still to show outranks the ask.

# In a control-bid dialogue (control-bids.bid): ask once every side suit
# is covered -- a control of mine, one partner has cued, or one I denied
# that partner has promised by bidding on. A control bid below game still
# comes first (priority 12), the ask before one past game (10).
when rkcb, we.trump is suit, asked control(t), !kb_asks(trump)
  4N  "Keycard ask in {trump}"
      when  all_covered
      sets  ask=keycards(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11
  # Partner's control bid has passed 4NT (a first-round control past
  # game, as over a non-serious 3NT, serious-3nt.bid): with every suit
  # covered and the values, bid the slam rather than go on cueing and
  # stop in five (2026-10-05, Serious boards 17 and 47).
  6{trump}  "Small slam"
      when  all_covered, slam_values, partner.last >= 5C
      priority 11

when rkcb, we.trump is suit, answered control(t), partner.last = 4{trump}, !kb_asks(trump)
  4N  "Keycard ask in {trump}"
      when  all_covered_by_us
      sets  ask=keycards(trump)
      artificial
      priority 15

when rkcb, asked keycards(t)
  # The card's keycard order (Rick, 2026-11-09: "we should follow the
  # card's keycard order"; the 2026-09-27 "1430 whatever the card says"
  # was a misunderstanding): `slam.rkcb.style` 0314 answers 0314 in every
  # suit, as BBA and GIB do; 1430 cards keep the `minor_0314` treatment,
  # which swaps the first two answers when a minor is trumps.
  5C  "1 or 4 keycards"                shows keycards(t) in 1|4  artificial
      when  kc_first_14(t)
  5D  "0 or 3 keycards"                shows keycards(t) in 0|3  artificial
      when  kc_first_14(t)
  5C  "0 or 3 keycards"                shows keycards(t) in 0|3  artificial
      when  !kc_first_14(t)
  5D  "1 or 4 keycards"                shows keycards(t) in 1|4  artificial
      when  !kc_first_14(t)
  # Five keycards answer as two: the steps wrap (0/3, 1/4, 2/5), and the
  # asker, holding none, knows which (Benjamin_2D 222, 2026-10-07: we
  # passed the ask with five).
  5H  "2 or 5 keycards, no {t} queen"     shows keycards(t) in 2|5, !has(Q,t)  artificial
  5S  "2 or 5 keycards and the {t} queen" shows keycards(t) in 2|5, has(Q,t)  artificial

# The asker places the contract. we.keycards(t) combines my exact count
# with partner's answer; the deck limit of 5 keycards resolves "1 or 4".
when rkcb, answered keycards(t)
  7{t}  "Grand slam"
        when we.keycards(t)=5, has(Q,t) | partner.has(Q,t) | partner.last = 5S, grand_try, kstyle is not five_nt   # with the king ask, ask first (2026-10-07)
  # The king ask (`slam.king_ask.style = five_nt`, 2026-10-05): every keycard
  # and the queen are ours, and the grand turns on the side kings.
  5N    "King ask: all keycards and the {t} queen held"
        when kstyle is five_nt, we.keycards(t)=5, has(Q,t) | partner.has(Q,t) | partner.last = 5S
        sets ask=kings(t)
        artificial
  6{t}  "Small slam"
        when we.keycards(t)>=4
  # The count that fits (2026-10-07): with 30 HCP between us the low
  # count of an open answer is impossible (`kc_high`, slam-entry.bid),
  # so no sign-off: on with all five and the queen, else six.
  7{t}  "Grand slam"
        when kc_high(t), we.keycards(t).max=5, has(Q,t) | partner.last = 5S, grand_try, kstyle is not five_nt   # with the king ask, ask first (2026-10-07)
  5N    "King ask: all keycards and the {t} queen held"
        when kstyle is five_nt, kc_high(t), we.keycards(t).max=5, has(Q,t) | partner.last = 5S
        sets ask=kings(t)
        artificial
  6{t}  "Small slam"
        when kc_high(t)
  P     "To play"
        when partner.last=5{t}, we.keycards(t).max<=3
  5{t}  "Signoff"
        when we.keycards(t).max<=3     # filtered out as illegal when the answer
                                       # is already 5{t}; P above covers that
        sets ask=keycard_correct(t)    # partner corrects only with 3-4
  5{t}  "Signoff"
        when maybe we.keycards(t)>=4   # 0 or 3 / 1 or 4 still open
        sets ask=keycard_correct(t)
  # With clubs as trumps every answer but 5♣ passes the sign-off
  # (2026-10-05: we passed partner's artificial 5♦ on ~30 boards). Six
  # then: the answer is never a place to play, and an open count ("0 or
  # 3") is far more often the higher one opposite slam values.
  6{t}  "Small slam"
        priority -1

# The king ask by 5NT: the number of kings outside the trump suit (its
# king is a keycard), by steps from 6♣. As ACBL's SAYC booklet and BBA
# (6♣ 0, 6♦ 1, 6♥ 2, 6♠ 3). Kings are controls less two for each ace.
# The text says "One king", as blackwood.bid's answers do: the trump
# king was counted as a keycard, and these rules also read the answers
# to Blackwood's 5NT (kings(N)), where differing texts left the table
# told only "artificial".
define side_kings(t) = controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) - has(K,t)

when kstyle is five_nt, asked kings(t), !kspec | t is C | t is D
  6C  "No king"     shows side_kings(t) = 0   artificial
  6D  "One king"    shows side_kings(t) = 1   artificial
  6H  "Two kings"   shows side_kings(t) = 2   artificial
  6S  "Three kings" shows side_kings(t) = 3   artificial

# The asker: the grand with every side king between us, or with two, 33
# HCP on partner's floor and a hand that can take care of the missing
# king's suit (a singleton or void, or six trumps in either hand); else six, or 6NT when
# the answer has passed six of a minor. With a flat hand the missing king
# is a finesse for the grand: on Puppet Stayman's 4-4 fits it went down
# as often as it made (2026-10-07, rkcb-1430.notes.md).
define partner_side_kings = (partner.last = 6D) + (partner.last = 6H) + (partner.last = 6H) + (partner.last = 6S) + (partner.last = 6S) + (partner.last = 6S)
define our_side_kings(t) = side_kings(t) + partner_side_kings

when kstyle is five_nt, answered kings(t), !kspec | t is C | t is D
  7{t}  "Grand slam"
        when our_side_kings(t) >= 3
  7{t}  "Grand slam"
        when our_side_kings(t) >= 2, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 33, C<=1 | D<=1 | H<=1 | S<=1 | t>=6 | partner.t.min>=6
  P     "To play"
        when partner.last = 6{t}
  6{t}  "Small slam"
  6N    "Small slam"

# ── Specific kings (`slam.king_ask.specific`, Rick, 2026-10-28) ──────
# 5NT is answered by the cheapest side king below six of trumps, six of
# trumps with none of those. With hearts trumps the spade king is not
# shown; the asker can ask for it with 6♠ (7♥ with it, 6NT without).
# Majors only: with a minor as trumps every side king is above six of
# it, so the count answers stay. A new suit below trumps then asks
# for that king: seven of trumps with it, six of a higher suit below
# trumps with that king instead, six of trumps with neither. The asker
# places the grand: with every side king accounted for (in either hand,
# or the asker short in the suit, at most one card), seven; with one
# missing and askable, he asks; else six.
when kstyle is five_nt, kspec, asked kings(t), t is H | t is S
  6C  "The club king"
      shows has(K,C)
      when  t is not C
      artificial
  6D  "The diamond king, not the club king"
      shows has(K,D), !has(K,C)
      when  t is H | t is S
      artificial
  6H  "The heart king, no club or diamond king"
      shows has(K,H), !has(K,C), !has(K,D)
      when  t is S
      artificial
  6{t}  "No side king below {t}"
      shows !has(K,C), !has(K,D), t is not S | !has(K,H)

define king_held(s) = has(K,s) | partner.last = 6{s}   # partner's answer names its king
# Side kings not accounted for. One of them is still worth the grand
# with the count style's margin (33 HCP, shortness or six trumps).
define kings_unheld(t) = (!(t is C | king_held(C))) + (!(t is D | king_held(D))) + (!(t is H | king_held(H))) + (!(t is S | king_held(S)))
define king_margin(t) = hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 33, C<=1 | D<=1 | H<=1 | S<=1 | t>=6 | partner.t.min>=6

when kstyle is five_nt, kspec, answered kings(t), t is H | t is S
  # Ask when the king asked for is the only one missing, or one of two
  # with the margin for the other (the answer 7 can leave one unknown).
  6D    "Asks for the diamond king"  alert
        when t is H | t is S, !king_held(D), kings_unheld(t) = 1 | (kings_unheld(t) = 2, king_margin(t))
        sets ask=king_in(D)
        artificial
        priority 3
  6H    "Asks for the heart king"  alert
        when t is S, !king_held(H), kings_unheld(t) = 1 | (kings_unheld(t) = 2, king_margin(t))
        sets ask=king_in(H)
        artificial
        priority 3
  # Hearts trumps: the spade king is asked above six of trumps (7♥ with
  # it, 6NT without), after the diamond king is settled.
  6S    "Asks for the spade king"  alert
        when t is H, !king_held(S), king_held(D) | !partner.last = 6C, kings_unheld(t) = 1 | (kings_unheld(t) = 2, king_margin(t))
        sets ask=king_in(S)
        artificial
        priority 2
  7{t}  "Grand slam"
        when kings_unheld(t) = 0 | (kings_unheld(t) = 1, king_margin(t))
        priority 1
  P     "To play"
        when partner.last = 6{t}
  6{t}  "Small slam"
  6N    "Small slam"

when kspec, asked king_in(z)
  7{trump}  "The {z} king"
            shows has(K,z)
  6H        "No diamond king; the heart king"
            shows !has(K,D), has(K,H)
            when  z is D, we.trump is S
            artificial
  6{trump}  "Neither king"
            shows !has(K,z)
  6N        "No spade king"
            shows !has(K,S)
            when  z is S, we.trump is H
            artificial

when kspec, answered king_in(z)
  P         "To play"
            when partner.last = 7{trump} | partner.last = 6{trump} | partner.last = 6N
  6{trump}  "Small slam"

# When the answer was ambiguous the asker signs off in five, and the answerer
# corrects to six holding the higher count (3 or 4 keycards).
when rkcb, asked keycard_correct(t)
  6{t}  "Corrects to six: the higher count"   shows keycards(t) in 3|4|5
  P     "Accepts the sign-off"

# TODO: queen ask (next step after 5C/5D), specific-king ask at 5NT.
files.rules/slam/serious-3nt.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Non-serious 3NT: in a game force with a major agreed at the three
# level (and neither of us shown balanced), the next hand's 3NT is
# artificial: mild slam interest, asking partner to start control bids
# with a good hand. A control bid instead is serious (the slam values of
# control-bids.bid), and four of the major has no interest. Partner
# answers 3NT with a control bid (extras), the keycard ask (slam values
# and every suit controlled), or four of the major. Notes:
# serious-3nt.notes.md.

module serious-3nt "Non-serious 3NT before control bids in a major-fit game force"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/serious_3nt
  param  nsplay = bidding_conventions/serious_3nt default false
  param  cue    = bidding_conventions/control_bids default false
  param  rkcb   = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard default false

# Partner has just agreed (or raised) our major at the three level.
define ns_position = partner.last = 3{trump}, !our_notrump

# ── The 3NT ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Within two points of the slam values that make a control bid serious
# (`slam_count`, slam-entry.bid: 30 for the long hand, 31 short, 32
# equal, on partner's floor), but short of them. The source puts the
# non-serious 3NT about 14-15 opposite a 2/1, the serious control bid
# 16+. Priority 12, level with the control bids: the two never hold on
# the same hand. Partner control-bids over it with a good hand.
define ns_count(t) = (longer(t), count_long(t) >= 28) | (longer(t), count_long_p(t) >= 28) | (shorter(t), count_short(t) >= 29) | (shorter(t), count_short_l(t) >= 29) | (!longer(t), !shorter(t), count_equal(t) >= 30) | (!longer(t), !shorter(t), count_equal_p(t) >= 30)

when nsplay, cue, we.trump is suit, trump is H | trump is S, we.forcing = game, !asked, !answered control
  3N  "Non-serious 3NT: mild slam interest"  alert
      shows ns_count(trump)
      when  ns_position
      when  !slam_values
      sets  ask=ns3nt(trump)
      artificial
      priority 12

# ── Partner over the 3NT ──────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Extras of my own (the count on partner's raised floor): show the
# cheapest control below game, as control-bids.bid's opening. The keycard
# ask with slam values and every side suit controlled. Otherwise game.

when nsplay, cue, asked ns3nt(t)
  cheapest(C)  "Control bid in ♣"  alert
      when  t is not C, under_game(C), slam_interest(t), controlled(C)
      sets  ask=control(C), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(C)
      priority 12
  cheapest(D)  "Control bid in ♦"  alert
      when  t is not D, under_game(D), slam_interest(t), controlled(D)
      sets  ask=control(D), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(D)
      priority 12
  cheapest(H)  "Control bid in ♥"  alert
      when  t is not H, under_game(H), slam_interest(t), controlled(H)
      sets  ask=control(H), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(H)
      priority 12
  4N  "Keycard ask in {t}"
      when  rkcb
      when  slam_values, !side_suit_uncontrolled
      sets  ask=keycards(t)
      artificial
      priority 13
  4{t}  "Signoff: no slam interest"
files.rules/slam/slam-catch.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# The card-independent half of the catch that takes over once a trump suit
# is agreed. There are no auction patterns here: the rules key on
# `we.trump` and `we.forcing`, so the same rule serves a simple raise, a
# limit raise, a Jacoby 2NT, a splinter, a two-over-one and a transfer.
#
# The ask lives in blackwood.bid and rkcb-1430.bid, because which of them
# is active is a card question and the answers differ. The test that
# decides *whether* to ask is the same in both, and is written up in
# slam-catch.notes.md. When the card plays control bids, control-bids.bid
# runs first and this sign-off is what the dialogue falls back to.

module slam-catch "Game or slam once a trump suit is agreed"
  kind   judgement
  needs  base
  skill  partnership_bidding/slam_bidding

# ── The sign-off ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Once a suit is agreed and we are forced to game, game in that suit is
# always a call we can fall back on. Nothing here says anything about the
# hand, so it ranks last: any rule with something to show beats it, and
# the slam tries above it beat it. It exists so that an auction which has
# agreed a trump suit never dies below game for want of a rule.

when we.trump is suit, we.forcing = game, !asked
  4{trump}  "Signoff"
            when trump is H | trump is S
            priority -20
files.rules/slam/slam-entry.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Slam entry: the conditions the slam modules share, named once
# (docs/JUDGMENT-LAYER.md, Phase 0). rkcb-1430.bid, blackwood.bid and
# control-bids.bid used to spell each of them out, up to 1,300 characters
# a line. No rules yet: what decides whether slam is worth looking for
# (Phase 1) will live here, and the modules that ask keep deciding how.
#
# The thresholds are Rick's (rkcb-1430.bid, "The ask"; slam-catch.notes.md):
# 33 support points between us with the agreed suit as trump, or 18 of my
# own facing a game force; the control rulings are control-bids.bid's.

module slam-entry "Slam entry: the conditions the slam modules share"
  kind   judgement
  skill  partnership_bidding/slam_bidding
  param  style = bidding_conventions/control_bids:style default first_or_second_round
  param  bw    = bidding_conventions/blackwood default false
  param  rkcb   = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard default false
  param  q4n   = bidding_conventions/quantitative_4nt default true

# ── The count: declarer points and support points (2026-10-01) ───────
#
# Rick (2026-10-01): "point count for any auction is normally declarer
# points for the hand with longer trumps, and support points for the
# other hand. With 4-4 fits both hands can use support points." The
# long-trump hand counts HCP + length (one a card beyond four, in every
# suit), not its own shortness; the short hand counts HCP + shortness
# (`tp(t)`, capped by its trumps). `we.tp(t)` counted shortness in both
# hands, which double counts.
#
# Trump lengths are compared with what partner has shown (`partner.t.min`):
# longer than that, I am the long hand; shorter, partner is; equal, both
# count support points (4-4, 5-5). A raiser shows the length he raised
# with, so the raiser is the support hand unless I hold no more trumps.

define longer(t)  = t > partner.t.min
define shorter(t) = t < partner.t.min

# The count on partner's floor, by role. Partner as the long hand counts
# his shown points (HCP + length), or his HCP and the length he has shown
# when no call showed points: either is a floor. As the short hand (or
# with equal length) his support points when a raise showed them, else
# the points he showed (`_p`): a call that shows total points leaves
# his HCP floor, and so `partner.tp`, near zero (1S-2D-3C-3S: 13+
# points). Each condition takes the better of the floors.
define count_long(t)    = hcp + length_points + partner.tp(t).min
define count_long_p(t)  = hcp + length_points + partner.points.min
define count_short(t)   = tp(t) + partner.points.min
define count_short_l(t) = tp(t) + partner.hcp.min + partner.length_points.min
define count_equal(t)   = tp(t) + partner.tp(t).min
define count_equal_p(t) = tp(t) + partner.points.min

# The same on partner's maximum.
define count_long_max(t)  = hcp + length_points + partner.tp(t).max
define count_short_max(t) = tp(t) + partner.points.max
define count_equal_max(t) = tp(t) + partner.tp(t).max

# The count at the thresholds the slam conditions use. The textbook 33
# (32 on partner's floor, `slam_values`) holds where both hands count
# support points; the long hand, which no longer counts its shortness,
# needs two less, the short hand one less (calibrated 2026-10-01 on the
# corpus and the 21GF random set: slam-entry.notes.md).
define slam_count_interest(t) = (longer(t), count_long(t) >= 29) | (longer(t), count_long_p(t) >= 29) | (shorter(t), count_short(t) >= 31) | (shorter(t), count_short_l(t) >= 31) | (!longer(t), !shorter(t), count_equal(t) >= 31) | (!longer(t), !shorter(t), count_equal_p(t) >= 31)
define slam_count(t) = (longer(t), count_long(t) >= 30) | (longer(t), count_long_p(t) >= 30) | (shorter(t), count_short(t) >= 31) | (shorter(t), count_short_l(t) >= 31) | (!longer(t), !shorter(t), count_equal(t) >= 32) | (!longer(t), !shorter(t), count_equal_p(t) >= 32)
define slam_count_max(t) = (longer(t), count_long_max(t) >= 31) | (shorter(t), count_short_max(t) >= 32) | (!longer(t), !shorter(t), count_equal_max(t) >= 33)

# ── Values ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Facing a game force: the count on partner's floor (`slam_count`: 32
# with support points in both hands), or 18 of my own. Partner's floor
# understates him, so one point under the textbook 33 (calibrated
# 2026-09-30 on random deals and the corpus: slam-entry.notes.md).
# The 18 of my own only while my range is still open (more than four
# HCP wide): an 18-19 2NT rebid has told partner, and his game bid
# after it is his sign-off, not an invitation (2026-10-05: 1x-1M-2NT-
# 3m(NMF)-...-4M asked with every 18-19 opener).
define slam_values = slam_count(trump) | (tp(trump) >= 18, !(shown.hcp.max - shown.hcp.min <= 4))

# Facing a limited hand (a raise with a top): the count on partner's
# maximum (`slam_count_max`: 33 with support points in both hands), and
# a hand of four losers or fewer.
define slam_values_limited = slam_count_max(trump), losers <= 4

# ── Controls ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# A control in x: the ace or a void, or with `first_or_second_round` the
# king or a singleton. Shortness counts only when partner has not shown
# four of x (a singleton in partner's suit is not a control).
define controlled(x) = has(A,x) | (x<=0, partner.x.min<=3) | (style is first_or_second_round, has(K,x) | (x<=1, partner.x.min<=3))

# First-round control only: past game.
define first_round(x) = has(A,x) | (x<=0, partner.x.min<=3)

# A side suit I cannot control on my own: what sends a hand to control
# bids rather than straight to the keycard ask.
define side_suit_uncontrolled = (trump is not C, !controlled(C)) | (trump is not D, !controlled(D)) | (trump is not H, !controlled(H)) | (trump is not S, !controlled(S))

# Rick's rule for the ask: no two bare side suits (2+ cards, neither the
# ace nor the king).
define two_bare_suits = (bare(C), bare(D)) | (bare(C), bare(H)) | (bare(C), bare(S)) | (bare(D), bare(H)) | (bare(D), bare(S)) | (bare(H), bare(S))

# Going on in the dialogue promises every suit partner denied: it is the
# trump suit, partner did not skip it, or I control it.
define promised(x) = trump is x | !partner.denied(x) | controlled(x)
define denials_promised = promised(C), promised(D), promised(H), promised(S)

# The same past game, with first-round controls.
define promised_first(x) = trump is x | !partner.denied(x) | first_round(x)
define denials_promised_first = promised_first(C), promised_first(D), promised_first(H), promised_first(S)

# Every side suit covered for the keycard ask: my control, one partner
# has cued or shown short in, or one I denied that partner has promised
# by bidding on.
define covered(x) = trump is x | controlled(x) | partner.cued(x) | partner.x.max <= 1 | me.denied(x)
define all_covered = covered(C), covered(D), covered(H), covered(S)

# The same when I opened the dialogue (partner answered me): my control
# or partner's.
define covered_by_us(x) = trump is x | controlled(x) | partner.cued(x) | partner.x.max <= 1
define all_covered_by_us = covered_by_us(C), covered_by_us(D), covered_by_us(H), covered_by_us(S)

# ── Working values opposite a shown shortness (Rick, 2026-11-07) ─────
#
# Rick: "the idea of the relays is it will allow us to find low HCP
# slams when there is a good fit. ... opener had a spade void, i think,
# which means all the combined HCP are 'working', which is the goal of
# this system (and the standard jacoby 2nt, and splinter bids)." Once
# partner has shown a singleton or void (`partner.x.max <= 1`), my K, Q
# and J there are wasted, and opposite a void the ace too (`wasted_hcp`,
# the engine's term; `working_hcp` is `hcp - wasted_hcp`). The working
# count is my support points less the waste, plus partner's floor:
# with nothing wasted it finds slams on fewer high cards than the
# 31-33 above, because partner's shortness, not counted in his floor,
# is worth its full ruffing value opposite my small cards.
define shown_short = partner.C.max <= 1 | partner.D.max <= 1 | partner.H.max <= 1 | partner.S.max <= 1
define working_count(t) = tp(t) - wasted_hcp + partner.points.min

# Slam on the working count: 23 opposite a void, 27 opposite a
# singleton (calibrated 2026-11-07 on the Jacoby and splinter
# scenarios, slam-entry.notes.md "Working values"). Opposite a void
# that is nearly every hand without wasted honours there: the keycard
# ask stops short when two are missing.
define shown_void = partner.C.max <= 0 | partner.D.max <= 0 | partner.H.max <= 0 | partner.S.max <= 0
define working_slam(t) = (shown_void, working_count(t) >= 23) | (shown_short, working_count(t) >= 27)

# The stronger hand by what has been shown (Rick, 2026-11-07: "keycard
# should be the stronger hand"): my HCP at least partner's shown floor.
define stronger_hand = hcp >= partner.hcp.min

# ── A fit known but not agreed (Phase 1, 2026-09-30) ─────────────────

# A suit both hands know we fit: suit agreement (`agreed_fit`,
# fit.bid: eight cards shown between us), or partner's own six-card suit.
# Public, so partner knows what a keycard ask agrees.
define shown_fit(x) = agreed_fit(x) | partner.x.min >= 6

# ── The keycard suit (Rick, 2026-10-03) ──────────────────────────────
#
# "A 4NT with no prior NT bids is normally keycard regardless, and if
# there hasn't been suit agreement, it's for the last bid suit. So
# 1H-1S-2H-4NT would be keycard for H." And: "Normally a major fit will
# replace a minor fit." For the cards that play Blackwood or RKCB; with
# neither (bare SAYC) 4NT stays natural or quantitative. Notes:
# rkcb-1430.notes.md, "The keycard suit".
#
# The suit, in order:
#   1. a trump suit set by a rule, unless it is a minor and a major has
#      since been agreed (`major_over_minor`: 1S-2C-3C-4S-4NT asks in ♠);
#   2. with none set, a suit agreed by what the two hands have shown
#      (eight between us; a major before a minor);
#   3. with no agreement and no notrump bid by us, the last suit our side
#      bid: partner's last call, when it was a bid in a suit that showed
#      two or more cards of it (not an artificial 2♦ waiting bid or a
#      fourth-suit call).
# With notrump bid by us and no agreement, 4NT is quantitative
# (1NT-2D-2H-4NT): the notrump modules' rules.

# Eight cards in x shown between us (fit.bid's `agreed_fit` without the
# trump state).
define shown_eight(x) = shown.x.min + partner.x.min >= 8

# A minor set as trump, and a major agreed since: the major takes over.
define major_over_minor(x) = x is S | x is H, trump is C | trump is D, shown_eight(x)
define minor_given_way = major_over_minor(S) | major_over_minor(H)

# Our side has bid notrump: either of us made a natural notrump bid at
# any point (`we.named(N)`, 2026-10-03; artificial calls such as a 2NT
# feature ask do not count), or either hand has shown a balanced hand.
define our_notrump = we.named(N) | !(maybe !partner.balanced) | !(maybe !shown.balanced)

# Partner's last call was a natural bid in x.
define last_suit(x) = partner_named(x), partner.x.min >= 2

define no_shown_eight = !shown_eight(S), !shown_eight(H), !shown_eight(D), !shown_eight(C)

# 4NT after our side has bid notrump, with no suit agreed, is
# quantitative (Rick, 2026-10-03). The notrump modules write it auction
# by auction; this is the fallback below them, so that a 4NT after, say,
# 1C-1S-1NT-2D (new minor) is read and answered rather than "no rule".
# The answer is one-nt.bid's `when asked quant` (6NT from 32 between us).
#
# `quant_4nt` is the card's switch (`slam.quantitative_4nt.play`, on by
# default and on every stock card), for the quantitative 4NTs the
# notrump and base modules write (2026-10-05).
define quant_4nt = q4n

# Ranked below every pass, so it is for reading: our own 4NT stays with
# the modules that judge it (a higher rank took over their 3NT and pass).
when we.named(N), we.trump is none, !asked, !they.bid, no_shown_eight
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  q4n                            # the card plays a quantitative 4NT
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 31, points + partner.points.min <= 32
      sets  ask=quant
      priority -60

# The keycard suit with no trump set (2 and 3 above), one suit at most.
define kc_shown(x) = shown_eight(x), x is S | !shown_eight(S), x is S | x is H | !shown_eight(H), x is S | x is H | x is D | !shown_eight(D)
define kc_open(x) = kc_shown(x) | (no_shown_eight, !our_notrump, last_suit(x))

# Slam values with x as trump before it is agreed: the count on
# partner's floor (as `slam_values`), or, when he has limited his hand to a
# range of seven points or less (a preempt, a weak two), his top does and
# my hand has four losers or fewer (as `slam_values_limited`).
define fit_slam_values(x) = slam_count(x) | (slam_count_max(x), losers <= 4, partner.points.max - partner.points.min <= 6)

# Two side suits, beside t, of 2+ cards without the ace or king.
define bare_beside(x, t) = x is not t, x>=2, !has(A,x), !has(K,x)
define two_bare_beside(t) = (bare_beside(C,t), bare_beside(D,t)) | (bare_beside(C,t), bare_beside(H,t)) | (bare_beside(C,t), bare_beside(S,t)) | (bare_beside(D,t), bare_beside(H,t)) | (bare_beside(D,t), bare_beside(S,t)) | (bare_beside(H,t), bare_beside(S,t))

# An ambiguous keycard answer ("1 or 4" facing my one: 2 or 5) settled
# by the high cards (2026-10-07, rkcb-1430.notes.md "The count that
# fits"): three keycards missing are at least 11 HCP (two aces and the
# trump king), so with 30 HCP on our floor at most two are missing and
# the low count is impossible. The answers that stay open after the
# deck's limit are 3 apart (2|5, 1|4, 0|3), so the count is the high one.
define kc_high(t) = maybe we.keycards(t) >= 4, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 30

# ── Fast arrival (Phase 1, 2026-09-30) ────────────────────────────────
#
# In a game force with an eight-card fit known and no suit agreed, the
# cheapest bid in the fit agrees it and shows slam interest; jumping to
# game in it (base.bid's fallback) is then the minimum, and denies the
# interest. Once it is agreed, control bids and the keycard ask take over.
# On 20,000 random deals we bid a slam on 15 of 63 boards with a fit and
# 33 HCP between us (BBA 55); the usual path was a jump to game after a
# jump shift or a reverse, where neither hand could count 33 on the
# other's floor.

# Not straight over partner's notrump where systems are on (2♣–2♠–2NT,
# 2026-10-05): there the cheapest bid is the system's (a transfer).
# Slam interest: the count on partner's floor, 31 (29 for the long hand).
define slam_interest(x) = slam_count_interest(x)

when we.forcing = game, we.trump is none, !asked, !game_reached, !they.bid, !we.systems_on
  cheapest(S)  "Agrees ♠: slam interest"
      shows we.fit(S).min >= 8, slam_interest(S)
      when  partner.S.min >= 3, under_game(S)   # public: a raise of partner's suit, never read into a natural bid
      sets  trump=S
  cheapest(H)  "Agrees ♥: slam interest"
      shows we.fit(H).min >= 8, slam_interest(H)
      when  partner.H.min >= 3, under_game(H)   # public: a raise of partner's suit, never read into a natural bid
      sets  trump=H

# ── Slam without an ask (Phase B, 2026-09-30) ─────────────────────────
#
# With no keycard or ace ask on the card, nothing past game read the
# count: on the vanilla SAYC random set the slams BBA bid and we missed
# stopped at base.bid's "Game reached" pass (2,917 boards, -10,007
# IMPs). BBA jumps to slam on support points: my tp plus partner's
# floor, 50% at 31-32 in six made-hand positions (slam-entry.notes.md,
# Phase A), with aces and kings counting a little extra. So, with a suit
# agreed and the values, bid it. Cards that ask (Blackwood, RKCB) keep
# asking: the rule is off for them.
#
# The count is our support points on partner's floor plus my controls
# (A 2, K 1), 35, with at least 29 in support points. Calibrated on the
# vanilla set (notes): 32 in support points alone +1,494 IMPs, 33
# +1,203, 31 +1,413; with controls 37 (tp 30+) +1,962, 36 +2,124, **35
# +2,325**, 34 +1,652; both halves of the set agree. Below BBA's own
# 31-32 because partner's floor understates him (as for slam_values).
#
# Since 2026-10-01 the count is declarer points for the long-trump hand
# and support points for the other (`count_*` above): 28 on partner's
# floor, and 35 with my controls. Par scores it level with the support
# points it replaced (+31 IMPs on the vanilla set, both halves).
#
# It ranks above the descriptive calls (priority 1, 2026-10-01): with the
# values, jump to slam at once, as BBA's "calculated bid" does, rather
# than describe and stop in game. Vanilla +596 IMPs against -10 (below
# every descriptive call), both halves.

# No ace or keycard ask on the card.
define no_ask = !bw, !rkcb

# Slam values for a direct slam: the count 28, and 35 with my controls.
define direct_count(t) = (longer(t), count_long(t) >= 28, count_long(t) + controls >= 35) | (longer(t), count_long_p(t) >= 28, count_long_p(t) + controls >= 35) | (shorter(t), count_short(t) >= 28, count_short(t) + controls >= 35) | (shorter(t), count_short_l(t) >= 28, count_short_l(t) + controls >= 35) | (!longer(t), !shorter(t), count_equal(t) >= 28, count_equal(t) + controls >= 35) | (!longer(t), !shorter(t), count_equal_p(t) >= 28, count_equal_p(t) + controls >= 35)
define direct_slam_values = direct_count(trump)

when we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !they.bid, !asked, no_ask
  6{trump}  "Small slam"
      shows direct_slam_values
      priority 1

# A minor set as trump and a major agreed since: the slam is in the major
# (Rick, 2026-10-03: "normally a major fit will replace a minor fit").
when minor_given_way, !they.bid, !asked, no_ask
  6S  "Small slam"
      shows direct_count(S)
      when  major_over_minor(S)
      sets  trump=S
      priority 1
  6H  "Small slam"
      shows direct_count(H)
      when  major_over_minor(H), !major_over_minor(S)
      sets  trump=H
      priority 1

# ── A fit known but not agreed: the direct slam (2026-10-01) ──────────
#
# 1H-2D-3H (six hearts, 16-18) does not set hearts in standard bidding,
# but responder with two knows the fit (Rick, 2026-10-01); the same when
# a new suit shows me partner's four-card suit (1S-2D-3C with four
# clubs). The hand that sees the fit counts as the role says: the short
# hand support points on partner's declarer points. Bid six on the
# direct count. Reworks the held-back version (branch
# slam-fit-not-agreed, which counted my support points on partner's
# points in every case).
#
# Above the descriptive calls, as the agreed-suit slam: at -10 (only once
# game is reached) +809 IMPs on the vanilla set, at 1 +3,122. Not when my
# own range is four points or less (1NT, 2NT, a jump rebid): partner is
# then the captain (+54). Vanilla calibration (slam-entry.notes.md).
when we.trump is none, !they.bid, !asked, no_ask, !(shown.hcp.max - shown.hcp.min <= 4)
  6S  "Small slam"
      shows we.fit(S).min >= 8, direct_count(S)
      priority 1
  6H  "Small slam"
      shows we.fit(H).min >= 8, direct_count(H)
      priority 1
  6D  "Small slam"
      shows we.fit(D).min >= 8, direct_count(D)
      priority 1
  6C  "Small slam"
      shows we.fit(C).min >= 8, direct_count(C)
      priority 1

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Spiral 2NT: after opener raises responder's major to two (1X-1M-2M),
# responder's 2NT asks for the length of the raise and its strength, so
# responder can judge game, or 3NT opposite three trumps:
#
#   3♣  three trumps, minimum      3♥  four trumps, minimum
#   3♦  three trumps, maximum      3♠  four trumps, maximum
#   3NT 4-3-3-3 with four trumps, maximum
#
# Card field `slam.spiral_cuebids.play`. Opener raises with four in our
# base system, so the three-card answers come from a system that raises
# with three. Notes: spiral.notes.md.

module spiral "Spiral 2NT: how many trumps, minimum or maximum, after 1X-1M-2M"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/spiral
  param  spiral = bidding_conventions/spiral default false

# A maximum for the single raise (12-15 HCP opener): 14 or more.
define sp_max = hcp >= 14

# ── The ask ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The invitational hand that would raise to three (responder-rebids.bid:
# 11-12 support points) asks instead: game opposite a maximum. Priority
# 1 over the natural raise.

after 1x (P) 1M (P) 2M (P) when spiral, x is not M
  2N  "Spiral: how many {M}, minimum or maximum?"  alert
      shows M>=4, tp(M)=11..12
      sets  ask=spiral(M)
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── Opener's answer ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

when spiral, asked spiral(M), rho.last = P
  3C  "Spiral: three {M}, minimum"            shows M=3, !sp_max   artificial
  3D  "Spiral: three {M}, maximum"            shows M=3, sp_max    artificial
  3H  "Spiral: four {M}, minimum"             shows M>=4, !sp_max  artificial
  3S  "Spiral: four {M}, maximum"             shows M>=4, sp_max   artificial
  3N  "Spiral: 4-3-3-3 with four {M}, maximum"  shows M=4, shape 4333, sp_max   artificial

# ── Responder places the contract ─────────────────────────────────────
#
# Game opposite a maximum: 3NT with four of the major facing three and a
# balanced hand, else four of the major; a pass of 3NT when balanced.
# Opposite a minimum, three of the major.

when spiral, answered spiral(M)
  4M  "To play"
      when  partner.last = 3D | partner.last = 3S | partner.last = 3N
  3N  "To play: balanced"
      when  partner.last = 3D, M=4, balanced
      priority 1
  P   "To play: balanced"
      when  partner.last = 3N, M=4, balanced   # with five, the 9-card fit
      priority 1
  3M  "Signoff"
      when  partner.last = 3C | (partner.last = 3H, M is S)
  P   "Signoff"
      when  partner.last = 3H, M is H
